Requirements for the vocabulary layer:

**FR-130 — Vocabularies are data.** Every enum in 5.3 MUST be stored in a versioned vocabulary table, not in application code, and MUST be readable through the API so that exhibits and importers resolve labels from one place.

**FR-131 — Code is the stored value.** Persisted records MUST store the `code`. Storing a `display_label` in a code column MUST fail validation.

**FR-132 — Ordinal integrity.** For every ordered vocabulary the `ordinal` MUST be a dense sequence starting at 1 with no duplicates, enforced by a database constraint.

**FR-133 — Alias resolution is one-way.** `deprecated_aliases` MUST be usable as input by the importer and by search, and MUST NOT be emitted by any read API, exhibit renderer or export.

**FR-134 — Alias uniqueness.** A given alias string MUST NOT appear in more than one code's `deprecated_aliases` within the same vocabulary. Where a string is ambiguous across vocabularies (for example `Managed`, which is level 2 canonically and level 4 in one observed deck vocabulary), the importer MUST NOT auto-resolve it and MUST raise a blocking validation finding (FR-186).

**FR-135 — Anchor rubrics are attached to dimensions.** Each ScoreDimension MUST carry exactly five anchor rows with ordinals 1–5, each with a definition and at least one calibration example, and the system MUST render the anchor text at the point of scoring.

**FR-136 — Band bounds are model data.** Priority band lower bounds MUST be stored on `ScoringModel.band_definitions` and MUST be the only source used by both the calculation engine and every exhibit.

**FR-137 — One canonical horizon name.** The system MUST expose exactly one display label per HorizonBucket code. Any request to create a second active label for a bucket MUST be rejected.

**FR-138 — Declared-but-unpopulated vocabularies.** A vocabulary with no records referencing it MUST be surfaced in the engagement health panel as "declared, unpopulated" with the count of affected records, so the team either populates it or removes it (see FR-172).

**FR-139 — Derived size views are not authorable.** `SpanBand` and `EffortBand` values MUST be computed from `TShirtSize` by the mapping in 5.3 and MUST be rejected on write.

**FR-140 — Anchor label derivation.** `OpportunityScore.anchor_label` MUST be derived from `score` by anchor lookup at read time. The reverse operation, deriving a score from a label, MUST NOT exist anywhere in the codebase.

**FR-141 — Deprecated labels never render.** An exhibit or export that resolves a value to a deprecated alias MUST fail the render with a diagnostic naming the record and field, rather than emit the deprecated string.

### 5.4 Referential integrity and validation rules

Each rule below names the defect in the reference way of working that it exists to prevent. Rules are enforced at the database layer where a constraint can express them and in a shared validation service otherwise, so that the API, the importer and the AI-acceptance path all pass through the same checks.

**FR-145 — One parent initiative per opportunity.** Every Opportunity MUST reference exactly one Initiative through a non-null `initiative_id` foreign key. An Opportunity with no initiative MUST NOT be persistable, and an Initiative MUST NOT be deletable while opportunities reference it.

- `AC-145.1` Attempting to insert an Opportunity with `initiative_id = null` returns HTTP 422 with error code `initiative_required`.
- `AC-145.2` Attempting to delete an Initiative with one or more child opportunities returns HTTP 409 with the child count and requires an explicit reparent operation.

**FR-146 — Theme is never stored on an opportunity.** The Opportunity table MUST NOT contain a `theme_id` or `theme_name` column. Theme MUST be resolved as `Opportunity → Initiative → Theme` at read time.

- `AC-146.1` The API response for an Opportunity includes a read-only `theme` object resolved through the initiative.
- `AC-146.2` A request body containing `theme_id` or `theme` on an Opportunity create or update is rejected with `field_not_writable`.
- `AC-146.3` Reassigning an Opportunity to an initiative under a different theme changes the resolved theme on the next read with no data migration and no second write.

This replaces a denormalised lookup that copied the theme name onto each register row from a table in a *different workbook*. Because the lookup was keyed on the free-text initiative name and returned an empty string on failure rather than an error, any initiative rename produced a silently blank theme, and because the lookup was cross-workbook it also broke on copy. One row bypassed the lookup entirely and pointed at a fixed row number in the external table, so inserting a row above it would have re-pointed that opportunity at a different theme.

**FR-147 — Canonical taxonomy names are unique and trimmed.** Theme, Initiative and Wave names MUST be unique per engagement under `lower(btrim(name))`, and MUST be stored with leading and trailing whitespace and leading punctuation removed.

- `AC-147.1` A unique index on `(engagement_id, lower(btrim(name)))` exists for Theme, Initiative and Wave.
- `AC-147.2` Creating an Initiative named `"eCommerce Platform Consolidation & Scaling"` when `"B2B eCommerce Platform Consolidation & Scaling"` already exists succeeds (they are distinct strings) but triggers a near-duplicate warning listing both, with a one-click merge that reparents children.
- `AC-147.3` Creating a Theme named `" / Stabilize the Core"` normalises to `"Stabilize the Core"` and, if that already exists, is rejected as a duplicate.

The reference taxonomy carried three separate initiative names differing only by a channel prefix (`B2B …`, `B2B2C: …`, and the bare form) for what the canonical table held as one initiative; one theme name carried a stray leading slash; and a fifth theme name appeared in the operating-model sheet spelled with a transposed vowel and paired with a word ("Modernize") that appears in no canonical theme. All four are exactly the class of error this rule blocks.

**FR-148 — Scores are integers; labels are derived.** `OpportunityScore.score` MUST be an integer between `ScoreDimension.min_score` and `max_score` inclusive, stored in a numeric column. The system MUST NOT store a score as a display string and MUST NOT contain any code path that extracts a number from a label.

- `AC-148.1` Posting `score = "4 Material Meaningful revenue growth…"` returns HTTP 422 `score_must_be_integer`.
- `AC-148.2` Posting `score = 6` for a dimension whose `max_score` is 5 returns HTTP 422 `score_out_of_range`.
- `AC-148.3` A repository-wide test asserts that no source file contains a substring-extraction of a numeric prefix from a score or label field.

**FR-149 — Weights sum to one.** A ScoringModel MUST NOT be activated unless the sum of its dimension weights equals 1.000 within a tolerance of 0.0005.

- `AC-149.1` Activating a model whose weights sum to 0.95 returns HTTP 422 `weights_must_sum_to_one` with the computed sum and the per-dimension breakdown.
- `AC-149.2` Deleting a dimension from an active model is prohibited; the model must be cloned to a new version.

**FR-150 — Weights are model data, never formula literals.** Dimension weights MUST be read from `ScoreDimension.weight` at calculation time. No numeric weight literal may appear in calculation code.

The reference workbook held the weights in a spreadsheet row interleaved with rubric prose, so that the weighted-score formula multiplied a five-cell range against a five-cell range in which two cells on each side contained text. The calculation produced the right answer only because the spreadsheet engine treats text as zero in that operation. Worse, the weights were written twice (once in a header row, once in the row the formula actually read), and the operating-model sheet's copy of the formula reached across a workbook boundary to a range **offset by one column** from where the master kept its weights, so the two sheets were not guaranteed to be scoring on the same weights at all.

**FR-151 — One live scoring model per scenario.** A RoadmapScenario MUST reference exactly one ScoringModel version, and every OpportunityScore used in that scenario's calculations MUST belong to that version.

- `AC-151.1` A scenario whose opportunities carry scores from two model versions reports a blocking `mixed_scoring_model` health error and refuses to publish.

**FR-152 — Focus-area name uniqueness is scoped.** MaturityFocusArea names MUST be unique within a capability area and MAY repeat across areas. `MaturityAssessment` MUST be unique per `(focus_area_id, round_label)`.

**FR-153 — Target level bounds.** `current_level` and `target_level` MUST each be null or an integer 1–5. A `target_level` below `current_level` MUST be permitted but MUST raise a non-blocking `target_below_current` warning, since a deliberate de-investment is legitimate but usually a typo.

**FR-154 — Gap is derived only.** `MaturityAssessment.gap` MUST be computed as `target_level − current_level` and MUST be null when either operand is null. It MUST NOT be writable.

**FR-155 — Dependency endpoints differ.** A Dependency MUST have `predecessor_opportunity_id != successor_opportunity_id`, enforced by a check constraint, and `(predecessor, successor, dependency_type)` MUST be unique.

**FR-156 — Cross-scenario referential closure.** A RoadmapItem MUST reference an Opportunity in the same engagement, and every Dependency used by the schedule pass MUST connect two opportunities that both have a RoadmapItem in the scenario being scheduled. Dependencies whose other end is absent from the scenario MUST be reported as `dangling_dependency` warnings and excluded from the schedule, never silently ignored.

**FR-157 — Enum columns reject free text.** Every enum-typed column MUST be constrained to its vocabulary's codes at the database level. Free text MUST NOT be storable in an enum column under any circumstances.

- `AC-157.1` Posting a 200-character paragraph to `Opportunity.status` returns HTTP 422 `invalid_enum_value` listing the permitted codes.
- `AC-157.2` The importer routes any unmappable value found in a source enum column to a quarantine field on the import report rather than to the target column (FR-184).

In the reference register a reviewer's two-sentence question about whether a score should be raised was typed directly into the row's status cell, because the row's values had drifted one column to the left of their headers.

**FR-158 — Column-drift detection on structured input.** For any tabular input, the system MUST validate each column's values against the declared type and vocabulary of that column, and MUST report a `column_offset_suspected` finding when a contiguous block of rows fails type validation in a pattern consistent with a fixed positional shift.

- `AC-158.1` Given a sheet whose rows 7–48 place a numeric score in column `I` and whose row 49 places it in column `H`, the importer reports `column_offset_suspected` for row 49 with the inferred offset of −1 and does not import that row's derived columns.

The reference register's last data row had every formula from one column onward shifted one position left, so that row's business-value figure was computed by the priority-band formula, its urgency figure by the business-value formula, its source text sat in the "so what" column, its status in the source column and a reviewer paragraph in the status column. Every downstream number for that opportunity was wrong, and nothing in the workbook signalled it.

**FR-159 — Declared-but-never-populated fields.** A field that is declared in the schema and populated on zero records across an engagement MUST either be removed from the engagement's active field set or be explicitly marked optional with a recorded reason and an owner.

- `AC-159.1` The engagement health panel lists every such field with its record count of zero.
- `AC-159.2` Marking a field `intentionally_optional` requires a free-text reason of at least 20 characters and records the acting user; the field then no longer appears as a health finding.
- `AC-159.3` Publishing a Deliverable while an unexplained zero-population field exists produces a non-blocking warning listing the fields.

The reference register declared a span column with a documented three-value legend in its header and populated it on none of its 43 rows, while the workshop separately captured a six-value size for the same opportunities on a whiteboard. FR-139 and this rule together make that state impossible to leave undocumented.

**FR-160 — Enum options are complete for every record.** The set of selectable values for an enum field MUST be identical for every record of that entity within an engagement. Per-record restriction of the option list MUST NOT be expressible.

The reference workbook attached its yes/no dropdown to a discontiguous set of cell ranges, leaving nine rows in the middle of the register with no dropdown at all, so those opportunities could not be classified without editing the validation rule itself.

**FR-161 — Hidden data is not a storage location.** The system MUST NOT provide any mechanism by which a field is present in the data but excluded from the schema, the API and the export. Presentation-level hiding MUST be a per-user view preference that never affects stored data, validation or calculation.

- `AC-161.1` Every field returned by the export API is present in the schema documentation, and every schema field is exportable.
- `AC-161.2` A field hidden in the UI still participates in validation and in the calculation engine.

The reference workbooks kept a competing 27-row opportunity register, a second score scale, the only intact copy of the theme-to-initiative taxonomy, and the assessment-status enum list all on sheets marked hidden. The taxonomy case is the sharpest: the visible register in the master workbook depended on a lookup into a table that existed intact only as a hidden sheet in a *different* file.

**FR-162 — No cross-document references.** All calculation inputs MUST resolve within the engagement's own data. The system MUST NOT support a field whose value is a reference into an external file.

**FR-163 — Conditional presentation binds to codes.** Colour rules, heatmap palettes and banding on exhibits MUST bind to vocabulary codes or to numeric ranges resolved from `ScoringModel`, never to display strings.

- `AC-163.1` Renaming a theme's display label changes every exhibit's legend text and leaves every colour assignment unchanged.

The reference workbooks carried conditional-formatting rules keyed to four theme names that had all been retired, so the formatting silently applied to nothing while looking maintained.

**FR-164 — Client-assigned rank coexists with the computed score.** `Opportunity.client_top_priority_rank` MUST be stored as an authored field, MUST be nullable and sparse, MUST NOT influence `weighted_score`, `priority_band`, `business_value_x`, `urgency_y` or `urgency_quadrant`, and MUST be uniquely constrained per engagement.

- `AC-164.1` Two opportunities assigned rank 2 produce HTTP 409 `duplicate_client_rank` naming both records.
- `AC-164.2` An exhibit can sort by client rank, by weighted score, or show both, and the divergence between the two orderings is reported as a first-class metric (see Section 7.2.11).

The reference register carried a client-assigned rank 1–19 taken from the workshop board alongside the calculated score, with the value 2 appearing twice. Preserving both orderings is a feature: the gap between what the model ranks highest and what the room ranks highest is exactly the conversation the workshop exists to have.

**FR-165 — Status vocabularies are not shared across lifecycles.** Inventory provenance (`OpportunityStatus`), assessment review state (`AssessmentReviewStatus`), delivery state (`ActivationStatus`), scenario state (`ScenarioStatus`) and deliverable state (`DeliverableStatus`) MUST be separate vocabularies on separate fields, and no single field may serve two lifecycles.

**FR-166 — Deleting a vocabulary value in use.** Retiring a vocabulary value MUST require either zero referencing records or an explicit remap to another value, executed as one transaction and recorded as a single AuditEvent with the affected record count.

**FR-167 — Cascade rules are explicit.** Deleting an Engagement cascades to all its records. Deleting any other entity is restricted while children reference it, except Evidence (which is retained and orphan-flagged) and AuditEvent and ActualsSnapshot (which are never deleted).

**FR-168 — Every AI write goes through review.** A canonical field MUST NOT be modified by a request whose actor type is `ai`. The only mutation an AI actor may perform is inserting an AISuggestion with status `proposed`.

- `AC-168.1` An update request authenticated as an AI service identity against any entity other than AISuggestion returns HTTP 403 `ai_may_not_write_canonical`.
- `AC-168.2` Accepting a suggestion writes the canonical field, sets `status = accepted`, `reviewed_by`, `reviewed_at`, and emits one AuditEvent per changed field with `suggestion_id` set.

**FR-169 — Suggestion payload validity.** An AISuggestion payload MUST pass the same validation as a human-authored write for its target entity at acceptance time, and MUST be re-validated at acceptance rather than only at creation, because the target record may have changed since.

**FR-170 — Evidence required on factual suggestions.** An AISuggestion whose capability asserts a fact about the client (extraction, scoring, finding generation, dependency inference, cost range) MUST carry at least one EvidenceRef. Suggestions that are purely generative (headline drafting, narrative phrasing) MUST record the entity references they were conditioned on in `payload.conditioned_on`.

**FR-171 — Whitespace and casing normalisation.** All string fields MUST be stored with Unicode NFC normalisation, `btrim` applied, and internal runs of whitespace collapsed to single spaces. Case is preserved as authored; uniqueness comparisons are case-insensitive.

**FR-172 — Engagement health check.** The system MUST expose a health endpoint and panel that runs the full validation rule set across an engagement on demand and on a schedule, returning findings grouped as blocking, warning and informational, each naming the entity, record, field and rule identifier.

- `AC-172.1` The health check covers, at minimum: opportunities without evidence; opportunities without a full set of dimension scores; scoring models whose weights do not sum to one; duplicate client ranks; near-duplicate taxonomy names; dangling dependencies; dependency cycles; unassessed focus areas; unpopulated declared fields; exhibits stale relative to their data; scenarios mixing scoring model versions; unpopulated vocabularies; and quadrants or bands with zero population.

**FR-173 — Publishing gate.** Publishing a Deliverable MUST be blocked while any blocking health finding exists in its scope, and MUST record the full warning list in the published snapshot so the artefact carries its own known-issues manifest.

**FR-174 — Portfolio totals are single-sourced.** Any count or percentage that appears on an exhibit MUST be computed by the calculation engine from the live record set at render time and MUST NOT be authorable.

The reference engagement's theme slides showed opportunity counts of 13, 16, 19 and 8, summing to 56, against a register of 43 technology opportunities plus 12 operating-model opportunities, 55 in total. The one-record discrepancy is small and entirely typical: the numbers were typed onto the slide once and the register moved on.

```json
      "quote": "Identity work is documented as a critical path prerequisite for the partner portal and for single sign-on on the public site.",
      "extracted_at": "2026-08-09T13:11:04Z"
    }
  ],
  "rationale": "Two independent sources state the same prerequisite relationship in directional terms. Lag of 30 days proposed from the stated stabilisation period after identity go-live; lag has lower support than the relationship itself.",
  "model_version": "roadmap-reasoner-2026-07",
  "prompt_version": "dep-infer-v4",
  "created_at": "2026-08-09T13:11:06Z",
  "status": "edited",
  "reviewed_by": "0192f39d-6000-7000-8000-000000000004",
  "reviewed_at": "2026-08-11T15:02:00Z",
  "edit_diff": [
    { "field": "lag_days", "from": 30, "to": 45, "note": "Delivery team advised a 45-day stabilisation window." }
  ]
}
```

### 5.6 Migration and import

The product must be able to start an engagement from an existing workbook of the reference shape, because that is how every in-flight engagement currently exists. Import is a first-class, reviewable, reversible operation, not a one-off script.

#### Import model

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Upload workbook] --> B[Structural scan: every sheet, visible and hidden]
    B --> C[Sheet classification against known archetypes]
    C --> D[Header detection and column mapping proposal]
    D --> E{Consultant confirms mapping}
    E -->|adjust| D
    E -->|confirm| F[Row-level extraction into a staging schema]
    F --> G[Validation pass: types, vocabularies, drift, duplicates]
    G --> H[Validation report]
    H --> I{Consultant resolves blocking findings}
    I -->|fix in staging| G
    I -->|accept| J[Commit to canonical tables in one transaction]
    J --> K[Recalculate all derived values from scratch]
    K --> L[Reconciliation report: imported vs recomputed]
```

**FR-175 — Workbook import.** The system MUST accept an `.xlsx` upload and produce a staged, reviewable import covering, at minimum: the maturity assessment sheet, the opportunity register, the operating-model register, the scoring guide, the theme definitions sheet and the theme-to-initiative taxonomy sheet.

**FR-176 — Every sheet is read, including hidden ones.** The importer MUST enumerate all sheets regardless of visibility state (`visible`, `hidden`, `veryHidden`) and MUST classify each one, because in the reference workbooks the only intact copy of the taxonomy and the only written record of one enum's value set both lived on hidden sheets.

- `AC-176.1` The import report lists every sheet with its visibility state, dimensions, detected archetype and disposition (imported, imported as reference data, quarantined, ignored with reason).
- `AC-176.2` A hidden sheet that the classifier cannot match to an archetype is quarantined with its full contents retained and surfaced for manual mapping, never dropped.
- `AC-176.3` Hidden rows and hidden columns within an imported sheet are imported on the same footing as visible ones, and their hidden state is reported.

**FR-177 — Formulas are read as intent, values as data.** For every formula cell the importer MUST capture the formula text, the cached value and the normalised formula pattern for the column, and MUST compare the column's dominant pattern against the pattern of each cell.

- `AC-177.1` A cell whose formula deviates from its column's dominant pattern is reported as `formula_outlier` with both patterns shown.
- `AC-177.2` A derived column whose formula matches a known engine calculation is mapped to that calculation, and its cached values are retained only for the reconciliation report, never written to a canonical field.
- `AC-177.3` A cell containing a hard-coded positional reference into a lookup table (rather than the column's lookup pattern) is reported as `positional_reference` and its value is not trusted.

**FR-178 — Broken external references.** The importer MUST detect external workbook references (link indices such as `[1]` or `[2]` in a formula) and MUST NOT attempt to resolve them.

- `AC-178.1` Every external reference is listed in the report with the referring cell, the target path fragment and the cached value at the time of last successful resolution.
- `AC-178.2` A derived column that depends on an external reference is imported as **unresolved**: the record is created, the derived field is left null, and a blocking finding requires the source data to be supplied locally before publication.
- `AC-178.3` Where an external reference points at a weights range, the importer MUST NOT infer the weights from cached results; it MUST require the consultant to confirm the weights against the scoring guide sheet, and MUST report any column offset between the referenced range and the range where weights actually sit.

**FR-179 — Prose-in-enum quarantine.** A source cell whose target column is enum-typed and whose value matches no code or alias MUST be quarantined rather than coerced.

- `AC-179.1` The record imports with the enum field null and a `quarantined_values` entry holding the field name, the raw text and the row reference.
- `AC-179.2` A quarantined value longer than 60 characters is additionally classified as `prose_in_enum` and offered for routing to a free-text field, most commonly a note, rationale or open-question field.
- `AC-179.3` No quarantined value is ever discarded; the import cannot be committed while unrouted quarantine entries remain, though "route to notes" and "discard with reason" are both one-click resolutions.

**FR-180 — Column-drift repair.** Where FR-158 detects a positional shift, the importer MUST offer a per-row realignment preview showing each value under its currently mapped header and under the shifted mapping, and MUST require explicit confirmation before applying the shift.

- `AC-180.1` The preview shows both interpretations side by side for every affected column of every affected row.
- `AC-180.2` Applying the shift is recorded as a single AuditEvent with the row references and the offset.
- `AC-180.3` If the consultant declines the shift, the affected rows import with the shifted columns quarantined rather than mis-mapped.

**FR-181 — Score de-stringification.** Where a source column holds a score as a display string with a numeric prefix, the importer MUST extract the integer, match the remaining text against the dimension's anchor rubric, and report any mismatch.

- `AC-181.1` `"4 Material Meaningful revenue growth, cost reduction, or margin improvement…"` imports as `score = 4` with `anchor_code = material` and no stored string.
- `AC-181.2` A string whose numeric prefix and anchor text disagree (for example a leading `3` followed by the level-4 anchor wording) is reported as `score_label_mismatch` and blocks import of that score until resolved.
- `AC-181.3` The importer MUST NOT retain the concatenated display string in any field.

**FR-182 — Taxonomy reconciliation.** The importer MUST build the canonical Theme and Initiative tables from the dedicated taxonomy sheet where one exists, then match every register row's free-text initiative name against it.

- `AC-182.1` Exact matches after normalisation link silently.
- `AC-182.2` Near matches above a configurable similarity threshold are proposed as `AISuggestion` records with `capability = "taxonomy_matching"`, showing both strings and the candidate children affected.
- `AC-182.3` A register row whose initiative name matches nothing imports with a blocking `unmatched_initiative` finding; it MUST NOT be silently assigned a theme, and the empty-string fallback behaviour of the source lookup MUST NOT be reproduced.
- `AC-182.4` Themes named only in the taxonomy sheet's old-name column, or only in a conditional-formatting rule, are imported as `deprecated_aliases` on the matching canonical theme and never as themes in their own right.

**FR-183 — Duplicate detection without auto-merge.** The importer MUST report candidate duplicates across the whole opportunity set, including across the visible register and any hidden or legacy register, and MUST NOT merge any pair automatically.

- `AC-183.1` Candidates are proposed as `AISuggestion` records with `capability = "duplicate_consolidation"`, each showing the two records field by field with differences highlighted.
- `AC-183.2` Accepting a merge preserves both legacy identifiers on the surviving record, unions the evidence and finding references, and requires a single choice for every conflicting scalar field.
- `AC-183.3` Rows that are duplicates by title but carry different scores are flagged `duplicate_with_divergent_scores` and always require human resolution.

**FR-184 — Validation report contents.** The importer MUST produce a machine-readable and human-readable report before commit, containing at minimum:

| Section | Contents |
|---|---|
| Source manifest | File name, size, checksum, author metadata, sheet count, per-sheet visibility, dimensions, detected archetype, disposition |
| Mapping | Per sheet, each source column with its detected header, inferred type, proposed target field, and confidence; unmapped columns listed explicitly |
| Row disposition | Counts of rows imported, quarantined and skipped, per sheet, each with row references |
| Type findings | Every cell whose value failed its target type or vocabulary, with raw value and row reference |
| Quarantine | Every unmappable enum value, with a proposed routing target |
| Drift findings | Suspected column offsets, with affected row ranges and inferred offset |
| Formula findings | Column dominant patterns; per-cell outliers; positional references; external references with target fragments |
| Taxonomy findings | Unmatched initiative and theme names; near-duplicate names; alias assignments made |
| Duplicate findings | Candidate duplicate pairs with similarity scores and score divergence |
| Identifier findings | Legacy identifier schemes detected; codes appearing in more than one scheme; register rows with no legacy code; codes with no register row |
| Vocabulary findings | Values present in the source that map to a deprecated alias; ambiguous aliases requiring human resolution; declared vocabularies with zero population |
| Unpopulated fields | Declared source columns with zero populated cells |
| Validation-rule findings | Every FR-145 to FR-174 rule violated, grouped blocking / warning / informational |
| Reconciliation | For every derived value the source also carried: source cached value, engine-recomputed value, absolute and relative difference, and a verdict of match, rounding difference, or **discrepancy** |
| Sensitive-data findings | Fields matching person-name, email or phone patterns outside the Stakeholder entity (FR-103) |
| Summary | Counts by severity, plus a single go / no-go verdict |

**FR-185 — Reconciliation is mandatory and non-destructive.** After commit the engine MUST recompute every derived value from the imported authored values and MUST report every disagreement with the source's cached values. Source cached values MUST NOT be written into derived fields under any circumstances.

- `AC-185.1` A relative difference above 0.5 percent on any weighted score, band, axis, quadrant, gap or rollup is reported as a discrepancy with both values and the inputs used.
- `AC-185.2` The reconciliation report is attached to the engagement permanently and is retrievable after the fact.
- `AC-185.3` Discrepancies do not block commit, because the whole point is that the recomputed value is the correct one; they block *publication* until reviewed.

**FR-186 — Ambiguous vocabulary values block.** Where a source value matches an alias of two different codes across the vocabularies in play (the maturity-level label collision in 5.3 being the canonical case), the importer MUST NOT guess. It MUST raise a blocking finding naming both candidate codes, and MUST offer resolution per column rather than per cell.

**FR-187 — Legacy score scales are provenance only.** A legacy score on a different scale MUST be imported into `legacy_ids`-adjacent provenance fields and MUST NOT be converted into a score on the canonical scale, because the observed mapping between the two scales was many-to-one and not invertible.

- `AC-187.1` The legacy band value is visible on the record's history panel and in the export, labelled with its scheme.
- `AC-187.2` No calculation reads it, enforced by a test that the legacy field appears in no calculation input set.

**FR-188 — Other-client content detection.** The importer MUST flag any imported content whose client references differ from the engagement's client, because working artefacts in the reference set contained a block of slides belonging to a different client parked inside a live deck.

- `AC-188.1` Detected foreign-client content is quarantined, listed with its location, and requires explicit disposition before commit.

**FR-189 — Deck import is out of MVP scope, structure capture is not.** The MVP MUST NOT attempt to import PowerPoint content into canonical entities. It MUST, however, accept a deck as a SourceDocument so that slide numbers remain citable as `EvidenceRef.locator` values.

**FR-190 — Sensitive data handling on import.** The importer MUST scan every imported text field for email addresses, phone numbers, and named-individual patterns outside the Stakeholder entity, MUST list them in the report, and MUST offer bulk redaction or routing into Stakeholder records before commit.

**FR-191 — Import is reversible.** An import MUST be revertible as a single operation for as long as no record it created has been edited, and MUST report exactly which records block a revert once editing has begun.

**FR-192 — Idempotent re-import.** Re-importing the same workbook checksum MUST be detected and MUST offer either a no-op, or a diff-and-update mode that shows every field that would change before anything is written.

**FR-193 — Import provenance on every record.** Every record created by an import MUST carry `import_batch_id`, source sheet name and source row number, so that any figure can be traced back to the cell it came from for the life of the engagement.

## 6. Functional Requirements by Module

The product is decomposed into modules that map one-to-one onto the phases of the engagement methodology. This section specifies the first four: Charter and Mobilization (Week 0), Fact Base (Weeks 1-2), Maturity Assessment (Weeks 3-4) and the Opportunity Register with scoring and prioritization (Weeks 3-4). Later modules (V1 roadmap, cost and capacity, business alignment, board narrative, activation) are specified elsewhere in this document.

Every module in this section follows the same conventions. AI output never lands in a canonical field; it lands as an `AISuggestion` and is accepted, edited or rejected by a consultant under the propose → review → commit pattern. Every claim carries an `EvidenceRef`. Every enum is a reference to a configured value set, never free text. Every derived number is computed from stored inputs, never typed.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M1["M1 Charter and Mobilization<br/>Week 0"] --> M2["M2 Fact Base<br/>Weeks 1-2"]
  M2 --> M3["M3 Maturity Assessment<br/>Weeks 3-4"]
  M2 --> M4["M4 Opportunity Register<br/>Scoring and Prioritization<br/>Weeks 3-4"]
  M3 --> M4
  M1 -->|"ScoringModel, waves,<br/>t-shirt sizes, objectives"| M4
  M4 --> M5["M5 V1 Roadmap<br/>Week 5"]
```

---

### 6.1 M1 Charter and Mobilization (Week 0) — FR-200 to FR-299

#### 6.1.1 Purpose

M1 turns an unstructured request for help into a configured engagement. It captures the mandate (what leadership wants), the scope (which capability areas are in play), the people (who will be interviewed and who decides), the evidence plan (which documents are needed and which are missing), the testable claims the team is starting from (hypotheses), and the analytical configuration that every later module reads (scoring dimensions, weights, t-shirt sizes, wave labels, priority thresholds).

The configuration point matters more than it appears. In the reference engagement the scoring weights lived inside a formula row on the opportunity sheet, the priority thresholds lived inside a nested `IF` in every one of 43 rows, the t-shirt scale existed only as a table on a workshop slide, and the third-horizon bucket was called three different things across the workbook, the deck and the recap email. M1 exists so that all of those are declared once per engagement, stored as data, and referenced everywhere.

#### 6.1.2 Methodology phase served

Week 0 — Kickoff + Mobilization. Core objective: establish mandate, scope, stakeholders and hypotheses.

#### 6.1.3 Inputs consumed

| Methodology Inputs column | Product representation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Executive goals | `Charter.objective[]` with `source_ref` to a `SourceDocument` | Becomes the Strategic Alignment scoring anchor (FR-203) |
| Known priorities | `Charter.objective[]` with `objective_type = stated_priority` | Distinguished from goals so traceability scoring can tell them apart |
| Existing strategy | `SourceDocument` of `doc_class = strategy` | Referenced by objectives, not retyped into them |
| Stakeholder list | `Stakeholder[]` | Imported from CSV or org chart, or proposed by AI-02 |
| Major programs | `Initiative[]` with `origin = client_inflight` | Fully inventoried in M2 (FR-306); M1 records only what is known at kickoff |
| Initial documents | `SourceDocument[]` with `request_status` | Drives the gap view (FR-208) |

#### 6.1.4 Screens and views

| View | What it shows | Primary actions |
|---|---|---|
| Engagement Setup wizard | Template selection, client name, phase calendar, confidentiality marking | Create engagement, set phase dates |
| Charter | Objectives, success criteria, scope statement, in-scope capability areas | Add or edit objectives, mark charter issued |
| Stakeholder Map | Grid and influence-by-function matrix; role, function, influence, interview status | Add stakeholder, assign to interview, accept AI-02 suggestions |
| Interview Plan | Calendar of slots with interviewer, interviewee, type, guide, status | Schedule, reschedule, generate guide via AI-03 |
| Coverage Completeness | Capability areas x planned interviews, with zero-coverage areas flagged | Add interview to close a gap |
| Document Request List | Requested documents with owner, due date, status, received artefact | Chase, mark received, mark unavailable with reason |
| Hypothesis Board | Testable statements with current status and supporting or contradicting evidence counts | Add hypothesis, review status changes proposed in M2 |
| Engagement Configuration | ScoringModel and weights, priority bands, t-shirt scale, wave labels, quadrant labels, maturity framework selection | Edit before first score is committed; version thereafter |
| Mobilization Readiness | Exit-criteria checklist with computed completion state | Request phase sign-off |

#### 6.1.5 Functional requirements

**FR-200 — Create engagement from methodology template.** The system MUST create an `Engagement` from a stored methodology template that instantiates the eight phases of the methodology as records with a name, a core objective, planned start and end dates, an expected `Deliverable` set and an exit-criteria checklist.
- AC-200.1 The default template contains exactly the eight phases named in the methodology: Week 0 Kickoff and Mobilization; Weeks 1-2 Interviews and Fact Gathering; Weeks 3-4 Current State Maturity and Roadmap Prioritization Build; Week 5 V1 Technology Roadmap; Weeks 6-8 Investment Cost and Capacity Modeling; Weeks 9-10 Business Alignment and Roadmap Refinement; Weeks 10-12 Final Roadmap and Board Narrative; Ongoing Roadmap Activation and Management.
- AC-200.2 Templates are versioned. An `Engagement` records `template_id` and `template_version` and does not change when the template is later edited.
- AC-200.3 Phase dates are editable per engagement and may overlap. The reference engagement ran maturity assessment and prioritization concurrently in the same two-week window, so the model MUST NOT assume phases are sequential and non-overlapping.
- AC-200.4 An engagement carries a `confidentiality_label` (default `Confidential`) that is rendered on every exported artefact.

**FR-201 — Charter record.** The system MUST maintain one `Charter` per `Engagement` holding the mandate statement, scope statement, in-scope `CapabilityArea` references, out-of-scope exclusions, the objective set, the success criteria set, the hypothesis set and the roadmap horizon in years.
- AC-201.1 A `Charter` can be marked issued. Issuing snapshots an immutable version and records who issued it and when.
- AC-201.2 Any edit after issue creates a new version and a `Decision` record is offered so the reason for the change is captured, not inferred.

**FR-202 — Structured executive objectives.** The system MUST store executive goals, known priorities and existing strategy content as discrete objective records rather than as prose, each with `objective_id`, `label` (short name), `statement` (verbatim or lightly edited), `objective_type` (`business_goal` | `stated_priority` | `guiding_principle`), `owner_stakeholder_id`, `evidence[]` of `EvidenceRef`, and `status` (`active` | `superseded`).
- AC-202.1 An objective MUST carry at least one `EvidenceRef` pointing at the source document, page or slide where it appears, or be explicitly flagged `source = verbal_kickoff` with the stakeholder who stated it.
- AC-202.2 The objective set supports two tiers observed in the reference engagement: a set of strategic goals that define the technology journey (the reference had eight) and a set of guiding principles grouped into categories (the reference had three categories: strategic alignment, engineering and architecture, execution and operations). Both are stored as objectives with different `objective_type` values, so both can be cited by a score.
- AC-202.3 Assumption: the shared entity list has no dedicated objective entity, so objectives are modelled as a child collection of `Charter`. If a later revision introduces a `StrategicObjective` entity, this collection is what it replaces.

**FR-203 — Objectives are the Strategic Alignment scoring anchor.** The `ScoreDimension` used for Strategic Alignment MUST be bound to the `Charter` objective set, and an `OpportunityScore` on that dimension MUST record which objectives it traces to.
- AC-203.1 The anchor rubric for that dimension is traceability, not general fit. The reference rubric ran: 5 named explicitly in the strategy document; 4 direct enabler of a named goal; 3 foundational dependency requiring a two-step explanation; 2 thematic fit requiring explanation; 1 not traceable.
- AC-203.2 A score of 5 MUST cite at least one objective by `objective_id`. A score of 4 MUST cite at least one objective. A score of 3 MUST cite the objective at the far end of the two-step chain and the intermediate opportunity or initiative that connects to it. Scores of 2 and 1 require a rationale string but no objective citation.
- AC-203.3 If an objective is later marked `superseded`, every `OpportunityScore` citing it is flagged for re-review and appears in a "stale alignment" queue. The score is not silently changed.

**FR-204 — Stakeholder map.** The system MUST maintain `Stakeholder` records with `name`, `title`, `function`, `business_area` (the executive ownership domain, matching the register's business-area field in M4), `role_in_engagement` (`sponsor` | `steering` | `interviewee` | `deep_dive_participant` | `workshop_participant` | `informed`), `influence` (`decider` | `high` | `medium` | `low`), `interview_status`, and `notes`.
- AC-204.1 `interview_status` is derived from linked `Interview` records and is never typed: `not_planned` | `planned` | `scheduled` | `held` | `synthesized` | `declined`.
- AC-204.2 A stakeholder may be linked to more than one interview (the reference engagement ran leadership interviews and separate functional deep dives with overlapping participants).
- AC-204.3 The map renders as a matrix of `function` by `influence` with interview status shown per cell, so an unspoken-to decider is visible at a glance.

**FR-205 — Interview plan with slots and coverage tracking.** The system MUST maintain `Interview` records with `interview_type` (`leadership` | `functional_deep_dive` | `executive_strategy_session` | `follow_up`), planned datetime and duration, `interviewer[]`, `interviewee[]`, `capability_area_coverage[]`, `objective_coverage[]`, `guide_id`, `status`, and `recording_consent` flag.
- AC-205.1 The plan view aggregates planned counts by type. The reference engagement's plan resolved to 5 leadership interviews plus 10 functional deep dives, and the product MUST show those counts as computed totals rather than as a typed claim on a slide.
- AC-205.2 Each interview declares which capability areas it is expected to cover. Coverage is what FR-206 reports on.
- AC-205.3 Rescheduling an interview MUST NOT clear its guide, its coverage declarations or its linked hypotheses.

**FR-206 — Coverage completeness view.** The system MUST provide a view that lists every in-scope `CapabilityArea` alongside the count of planned interviews covering it, the count held, the count synthesized, and the number of distinct stakeholder functions covered, and MUST flag any capability area with zero planned interviews as a blocking gap.
- AC-206.1 Blocking gaps are counted in the M1 exit criteria (FR-219) and must be either closed or explicitly waived with a reason.
- AC-206.2 The same view flags capability areas covered by exactly one interview as `single_source_risk`, because in M2 a finding supported by one interview is capped at the lowest evidence strength (FR-303).
- AC-206.3 The view also flags any `Charter` objective with no interview declaring coverage of it.

**FR-207 — Document request list.** The system MUST maintain a request list of `SourceDocument` records with `doc_class`, `title`, `requested_from_stakeholder_id`, `requested_at`, `due_at`, `request_status` (`requested` | `chased` | `received` | `partially_received` | `not_available` | `superseded`), `received_artifact_id`, and `not_available_reason`.
- AC-207.1 The default request list is seeded from the methodology's Weeks 1-2 Inputs column: strategy decks, project lists, application landscape, budgets, org charts, architecture documentation, vendor information and prior assessments.
- AC-207.2 A `not_available` status MUST carry a reason string. In the reference engagement several analytical gaps traced directly to artefacts that did not exist, for example the absence of an integration inventory and the absence of any published multi-wave programme roadmap. The product treats "the document does not exist" as a finding-grade fact, so `not_available` records are available to M2 as evidence of a governance gap.
- AC-207.3 The gap view groups outstanding requests by owner and by age, and shows which in-scope capability areas have no received document at all.

**FR-208 — Initial hypotheses as testable statements.** The system MUST record initial hypotheses as `Finding` records with `finding_type = hypothesis`, a single-sentence testable statement, a `confidence_at_kickoff` band (`low` | `medium` | `high`), the capability areas it concerns, the interviews expected to test it, and `hypothesis_status` (`open` | `confirmed` | `disconfirmed` | `inconclusive` | `refined`).
- AC-208.1 A status change away from `open` MUST cite at least one `Evidence` record. AI-04 through AI-07 may propose the status change as an `AISuggestion`; only a consultant commits it.
- AC-208.2 A `refined` hypothesis links to the successor `Finding` that replaced it, so the original claim and its revision are both auditable.
- AC-208.3 The hypothesis board shows, per hypothesis, the count of supporting and contradicting `Evidence` records and the number of distinct sources behind each side.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> open
  open --> confirmed: evidence supports, consultant commits
  open --> disconfirmed: evidence contradicts, consultant commits
  open --> inconclusive: coverage closed, evidence insufficient
  open --> refined: statement restated
  refined --> [*]
  confirmed --> refined: contradicting evidence arrives later
  disconfirmed --> refined: contradicting evidence arrives later
```

**FR-209 — Success criteria.** The system MUST capture engagement success criteria as records with `statement`, `measure`, `target`, `assessed_at_phase`, and an optional link to a `KPI` where the criterion is quantitative and will be tracked into activation.
- AC-209.1 Success criteria are shown on the mobilization readiness view and re-shown at each phase gate with their current assessment.
- AC-209.2 A success criterion may reference a `Deliverable`, which lets the phase gate check "the deliverable exists and was issued" mechanically.

**FR-210 — Configure the scoring model.** The system MUST allow the engagement to define its `ScoringModel` as an ordered set of `ScoreDimension` records, each with `dimension_id`, `name`, `question` (the one-line prompt the scorer reads), `weight`, `scale_min`, `scale_max`, and an anchor rubric of one row per scale point.
- AC-210.1 The default model, taken from the reference engagement, is three dimensions: Financial Impact at weight 0.40, Risk if Deferred at weight 0.35, Strategic Alignment at weight 0.25, each scored 1 to 5.
- AC-210.2 Weights MUST sum to 1.000 within a tolerance of 0.001. The system rejects a save that does not, rather than silently normalizing.
- AC-210.3 Dimensions may be added or removed before the first `OpportunityScore` is committed. After that, changing the dimension set or any weight creates a new `ScoringModel` version, and every existing `OpportunityScore` is re-derived against the new version while the previous derived values remain readable as a snapshot (see FR-527).
- AC-210.4 Weights are stored on the `ScoringModel` and read at derivation time. No requirement in this product permits a weight to be embedded in a formula, a template, a chart definition or an export.

**FR-211 — Configure priority bands.** The system MUST allow the engagement to define priority bands as an ordered list of `{ label, lower_bound_inclusive }` evaluated top down, with a final catch-all band.
- AC-211.1 The default set, from the reference engagement: `Critical` at 4.50 and above; `High` at 3.75 to 4.49; `Medium` at 2.80 to 3.74; `Lower` below 2.80.
- AC-211.2 Band labels are the only labels used anywhere in the product for that concept. The reference workbook wrote `High Priority` in the formula and `High` in the scoring guide and the workshop slide, and the conditional formatting matched on three different casings of the same word. The product MUST render one canonical label per band everywhere, including exports.
- AC-211.3 Bands MUST be contiguous and non-overlapping across the score range. The system validates this on save.

**FR-212 — Configure the t-shirt size scale.** The system MUST allow the engagement to define its effort scale as ordered records of `{ code, effort_description, duration_range, risk_description }`.
- AC-212.1 The default scale, from the reference engagement's Activity 3 material, is six sizes: XS single team well-defined, under 3 months, low risk with proven technology and no legacy touch; S one to two teams with some integration, 3 to 6 months, low to medium; M multi-team with moderate legacy, 6 to 12 months, medium; L cross-functional with significant legacy, 12 to 24 months, medium to high; XL enterprise-wide with deep legacy, 2 to 3 years, high, including core legacy platform change and organizational change; XXL multi-year transformation programme, 3 to 5 or more years, very high with an existential dependency.
- AC-212.2 A second, coarser span scale is also configurable, because the reference register carried a separate three-value span field (multi-year, single year, quarter) distinct from the six-value t-shirt scale. Both are supported; an engagement may enable one or both. If a field is enabled it MUST be populated before phase exit, since the reference workbook declared a span column and left it entirely empty in the master copy while populating it in the derived share copy.

**FR-213 — Configure wave and horizon labels.** The system MUST allow the engagement to define its `Wave` set once, with `sequence_number`, `label`, `horizon_description` and `date_range`, and MUST use that single label set in every view, chart, export and narrative.
- AC-213.1 The default set has four waves, matching the reference engagement's initiative sequence numbers 1 through 4.
- AC-213.2 The quadrant label set is configured in the same place: the default four labels are `Act Now`, `Defend`, `Plan & Fund`, `Sequence Later`, with the quadrant threshold defaulting to 3.5.
- AC-213.3 The system MUST reject the creation of a second label for a concept that already has one. The reference engagement carried three names for one horizon bucket (`Sequence Later` in the workbook formula, `Defer` in the recap email, `Future Horizon` in the same email's next-steps list), which made the workbook, the deck and the client-facing email mutually inconsistent. A single label registry per engagement is the fix, and renaming a label rewrites every rendered surface rather than creating a synonym.
- AC-213.4 Renaming a `Theme`, `Initiative`, `Wave` or band label MUST propagate to every dependent view and stored formatting rule. The reference workbook kept conditional formatting rules keyed to four retired theme names after the themes were renamed, so the colour coding silently stopped matching the data.

**FR-214 — Select the maturity framework.** The engagement configuration MUST include the selection of a maturity framework from the registry defined in M3 (FR-400), defaulting to the CMMI-style five-level framework, and the selection of the capability-area and focus-area set to be assessed.

**FR-215 — Seed the capability area set.** The system MUST create the engagement's `CapabilityArea` records from the selected framework's grouping set, allow additions and removals before assessment begins, and require each area to carry a one-paragraph description of what the area covers and why it is being examined.
- AC-215.1 The default set has eight areas, matching the reference engagement's grouping of the client's business model into eight areas, each with a stated scope sentence and a list of its focus areas.
- AC-215.2 `CapabilityArea` is the join used by the coverage view (FR-206), the maturity heatmap (FR-409), the register's area field (FR-503) and the filters in FR-514, so its identifiers MUST be stable for the life of the engagement.

**FR-216 — AI mobilization assist.** The system MUST expose the three Week 0 AI capabilities from the module hand-off table (6.1.6) as explicit user-invoked actions that produce `AISuggestion` records under propose → review → commit, and MUST NOT run them automatically on upload.

**FR-217 — Mobilization audit trail.** Every create, edit, issue and configuration change in M1 MUST write an `AuditEvent` with actor, timestamp, entity, field-level before and after values, and the originating `AISuggestion` id where the change came from an accepted suggestion.

**FR-218 — Configuration lock and change control.** After the first `OpportunityScore` or `MaturityAssessment` is committed, changes to `ScoringModel`, priority bands, quadrant threshold, t-shirt scale or wave labels MUST require an explicit confirmation that names the downstream impact (count of scores and roadmap items affected) and MUST create a new configuration version rather than mutating the existing one.

**FR-219 — Mobilization exit gate.** The system MUST compute the M1 exit-criteria checklist and MUST NOT allow the engagement to be marked Week 0 complete while any mandatory item is unmet or unwaived. Waivers require a reason and are recorded as `Decision` records.

#### 6.1.6 AI capabilities invoked

| Capability | Purpose in M1 | What M1 hands it | What M1 expects back |
|---|---|---|---|
| AI-01 Document set synthesis and gap identification | Read the initial document set, summarize what it establishes, and name what is missing relative to the methodology's declared inputs | The received `SourceDocument` set, the engagement's in-scope capability areas, the standard request list | Proposed `Charter` objective candidates with `EvidenceRef`, and proposed `SourceDocument` request records for missing artefacts, each with the capability area it would inform |
| AI-02 Stakeholder suggestion from org chart and objectives | Propose who must be interviewed and who is missing from the map | Org chart artefact, existing `Stakeholder` records, `Charter` objectives, in-scope capability areas | Proposed `Stakeholder` records with function, suggested `role_in_engagement`, suggested `influence`, and the objective or capability area that justifies each |
| AI-03 Tailored interview guide generation | Produce a per-interview guide targeted at the interviewee's function, the capability areas assigned to that interview, and the open hypotheses it is meant to test | `Interview` record, interviewee `Stakeholder`, assigned capability areas, open hypotheses, prior findings if any | A guide payload of ordered question blocks, each tagged with the hypothesis or capability area it probes, attached to the interview as an `AISuggestion` |

Guides, stakeholder suggestions and objective candidates are all suggestions. A consultant accepts, edits or rejects each one, and an edited acceptance stores the `edit_diff` so the review load of each capability can be measured (see the AI evaluation section).

#### 6.1.7 Exit criteria

Week 0 is done when all of the following hold, computed by the system rather than asserted by a consultant:

| Exit criterion | Rule |
|---|---|
| Charter issued | `Charter.status = issued` with at least one objective of type `business_goal` |
| Objectives usable as an anchor | Every `active` objective has a label, a statement and at least one `EvidenceRef` or an explicit `verbal_kickoff` flag |
| Stakeholder map complete | Every in-scope capability area has at least one stakeholder with `influence = decider` or `high` identified |
| Interview plan covers scope | Zero capability areas with zero planned interviews, or every such gap explicitly waived |
| Document requests issued | Every seeded request class is either `received`, `not_available` with a reason, or `requested` with a named owner and due date |
| Hypotheses recorded | At least one hypothesis per in-scope capability area, each phrased as a single testable statement |
| Success criteria recorded | At least one success criterion with a measure and a target |
| Configuration complete | `ScoringModel` weights sum to 1.000; priority bands contiguous; t-shirt scale populated; wave labels defined; maturity framework selected |
| Label uniqueness | No duplicate or near-duplicate labels within any configured value set |

---

### 6.2 M2 Fact Base (Weeks 1-2) — FR-300 to FR-399

#### 6.2.1 Purpose

M2 builds the evidence layer that everything downstream cites. Its output is not a document; it is a queryable fact base in which every claim the firm will later make in front of a board is traceable to a source, a locator inside that source and a quote.

The reference engagement's Day 1 findings playback is the concrete specification of what this module must be able to produce: interview themes across people, process, technology and data; survey results with respondent counts by functional area and coded strengths; the maturity heatmap; a "tensions beneath the surface" slide pairing contradictory positions; an external benchmark comparison against best-in-class peers; per-leader deep-dive pages; the client technology leader's strategic goals and guiding principles; and the four investment themes with opportunity counts and percentage shares. Every one of those is a view over structured data in this module or in M3 and M4.

M2 also carries the pain-point register. In the reference workbook, opportunities referenced pain points by number in a comma-separated text field (values such as `26,53,36,37,35,32,33,39,38`). Those numbers were the only link between the diagnosis and the recommendations, and they were unvalidated text. In this product they become real references from `Opportunity` to `Finding`.

#### 6.2.2 Methodology phase served

Weeks 1-2 — Interviews + Fact Gathering. Core objective: build a comprehensive understanding of the organization and transformation context.

#### 6.2.3 Inputs consumed

| Methodology Inputs column | Product representation |
|---|---|
| Interviews | `Interview` with attached audio, transcript or notes artefact |
| Surveys | Survey instrument, responses and coded results (FR-309) |
| Strategy decks | `SourceDocument` `doc_class = strategy` |
| Project lists | `SourceDocument` `doc_class = project_list`, parsed into `Initiative` records with `origin = client_inflight` |
| Application landscape | `SourceDocument` `doc_class = application_inventory` |
| Budgets | `SourceDocument` `doc_class = budget`; consumed for real in M6 but registered here |
| Org charts | `SourceDocument` `doc_class = org_chart`; feeds AI-02 and `Stakeholder` |
| Architecture | `SourceDocument` `doc_class = architecture` |
| Vendor information | `SourceDocument` `doc_class = vendor` |
| Prior assessments | `SourceDocument` `doc_class = prior_assessment`; the reference client had an earlier externally produced roadmap that was never executed, and that fact was itself evidence |
| Firm historical work | `Benchmark` and precedent records retrieved by AI-08 from anonymized prior engagements |

#### 6.2.4 Screens and views

| View | What it shows | Primary actions |
|---|---|---|
| Ingest queue | Uploaded artefacts with type, parse status, extraction status, reviewer | Upload, classify, run AI-04 or AI-05, assign reviewer |
| Interview workspace | Transcript with timestamps beside proposed `Evidence` and `Finding` records | Accept, edit, reject extractions; tag capability area; link to hypothesis |
| Evidence repository | Searchable list of `Evidence` with source, locator, quote, tags, linked findings | Search, filter by source or capability area, open source at locator |
| Finding register | `Finding` records with stable id, statement, capability area, evidence count, distinct-source count, strength, status | Merge, split, promote to theme, link to opportunity |
| Theme board | Clustered findings under candidate `Theme` records with cluster rationale | Accept or reshape clusters, rename, promote to the canonical theme set used by M4 |
| Tensions view | Pairs of contradictory findings side by side with speakers, sources and adjudication state | Adjudicate, record the trade-off, escalate to workshop agenda |
| Initiative inventory | Client in-flight initiatives with owner, status, spend if known, duplicate candidates | Consolidate duplicates, mark superseded, link to opportunities |
| Stakeholder priorities | Per stakeholder, their stated priorities ranked, with evidence | Add, reorder, compare across stakeholders |
| Benchmark library | `Benchmark` records with metric, value, peer definition, source, date | Add, cite in a finding, attach to a capability area |
| Survey results | Respondent counts by functional area, coded strength and opportunity themes, distribution charts | Code responses, publish distribution to playback |
| Findings playback builder | The Day 1 pack assembled from the fact base, section by section | Reorder, include or exclude, export |

#### 6.2.5 Functional requirements

**FR-300 — Interview ingestion in three input modes.** The system MUST accept an interview as audio, as an existing transcript, or as unstructured consultant notes, and MUST produce the same downstream structure in all three cases: a stored artefact, a timestamped or paragraph-indexed body, and a set of proposed `Evidence` records.
- AC-300.1 Audio is transcribed with speaker separation, and the resulting transcript stores per-utterance start and end timestamps so an `EvidenceRef` locator can be a timestamp range.
- AC-300.2 Notes with no timestamps use a paragraph index as the locator, in the form `para:12`.
- AC-300.3 `recording_consent` on the `Interview` MUST be true before audio is accepted for transcription. If consent is false the system accepts notes only.
- AC-300.4 An interview may have more than one artefact (for example audio plus a note-taker's summary), and evidence records identify which artefact they came from.

**FR-301 — Document ingestion and classification.** The system MUST accept the document classes listed in 6.2.3 as PDF, PPTX, XLSX, DOCX, CSV and plain text, extract page, slide, sheet and cell structure, and store `doc_class`, `title`, `author_role`, `document_date` and `provided_by_stakeholder_id`.
- AC-301.1 For spreadsheets, the locator granularity MUST be `sheet!cell`. For decks, `slide:n`. For documents, `page:n`. For CSV, `row:n`.
- AC-301.2 The system MUST record when a spreadsheet contains hidden sheets, external workbook references or formula errors, and surface those as ingest warnings. The reference engagement's own two workbooks were not self-contained: the taxonomy that resolved the theme of every opportunity lived only in a hidden sheet of a derived share copy, and the master's theme column resolved through an external reference that broke when the file was copied. When such an artefact is a client input, the product must tell the consultant what it could not resolve rather than importing blanks.
- AC-301.3 Uploaded content is treated as data, never as instruction. Any imperative text inside an artefact MUST NOT alter system behaviour or AI behaviour.

**FR-302 — Evidence repository.** Every extracted claim MUST be stored as an `Evidence` record carrying an `EvidenceRef` with `source_type`, `source_id`, `locator`, `quote` of at most 300 characters and `extracted_at`, plus `capability_area_refs[]`, `stakeholder_ref` where the source is an interview, and `extraction_method` (`ai` | `manual`).
- AC-302.1 An `Evidence` record MUST resolve to a viewable source location. Clicking it opens the artefact at the locator with the quote highlighted.
- AC-302.2 Quotes longer than 300 characters MUST be truncated at extraction with the full span retained as a locator range, so the source can be read in full without storing long verbatim text on the record.
- AC-302.3 The repository is searchable by full text, source, source type, capability area, stakeholder and date, and supports "show me everything that supports this finding" and "show me every finding this source supports" in one hop.

**FR-303 — Findings with evidence-count strength.** The system MUST store `Finding` records with a stable human-readable id, a one-sentence statement, `capability_area_ref`, `finding_type` (`pain_point` | `strength` | `hypothesis` | `observation` | `constraint`), `evidence[]`, `strength`, `status` (`draft` | `validated` | `retired`), `validated_by`, and `so_what` narrative.
- AC-303.1 `strength` is derived, never typed, from the number of independent sources supporting the finding, where independence is counted by distinct `source_id` and, for interviews, distinct `stakeholder_ref`: `single_source` = 1; `corroborated` = 2; `well_corroborated` = 3 or more; `contested` = has at least one linked contradiction that is unadjudicated, regardless of count.
- AC-303.2 A finding with `strength = single_source` MUST be visibly marked as such in every view and every export, including the playback pack. The reference engagement's strongest claims were explicitly multi-source (for example a delivery constraint independently named by three senior leaders in the same session), and that distinction is exactly what a board narrative needs to be able to make.
- AC-303.3 Finding ids are stable and immutable for the life of the engagement, because `Opportunity` records reference them (FR-503) and the reference engagement's only diagnosis-to-recommendation link was a list of pain-point numbers.
- AC-303.4 Merging two findings redirects all references from the merged id to the survivor and retains the merged id as an alias, so an external citation of the old number still resolves.

**FR-304 — Theme clustering.** The system MUST support clustering findings into candidate `Theme` records, each with `name`, `description` paragraph, `old_name` history, `sequence`, member findings and a cluster rationale.
- AC-304.1 Clustering is proposed by AI-06 and committed by a consultant. A consultant may create, split, merge and rename clusters manually at any time.
- AC-304.2 Renaming a theme retains the previous name in `old_name[]`. The reference engagement renamed all four themes mid-engagement and kept the old names in a column, which is why stale names survived in formatting rules and in a slide-level chart series. The product keeps rename history as data and rewrites every dependent surface (FR-213.4).
- AC-304.3 The canonical theme set that M4 enforces by reference is promoted from this board by an explicit action. Until promotion, clusters are candidates and cannot be referenced by an `Opportunity`.
- AC-304.4 The system MUST reject two themes whose names differ only by case, punctuation or whitespace, and MUST warn on names within a small edit distance of each other. The reference taxonomy contained both a duplicate unmerged theme name and a misspelled variant of another theme name, and both were used as lookup keys.

**FR-305 — Contradiction detection and the tensions view.** The system MUST detect and store contradictions between findings as first-class records and MUST present them in a dedicated tensions view.
- AC-305.1 A `Contradiction` record holds `finding_a`, `finding_b`, `contradiction_type` (`fact_conflict` | `priority_conflict` | `attribution_conflict` | `structural_tension`), `detected_by` (`ai` | `consultant`), `confidence`, and `adjudication`.
- AC-305.2 The tensions view MUST show, for each pair: the two statements; who said each, by name and role, resolved from the evidence; the source and locator of each; the strength of each side; and the adjudication state.
- AC-305.3 `adjudication` is one of `unadjudicated`, `a_holds`, `b_holds`, `both_true_in_different_scopes`, `genuine_tension_to_resolve_with_client`, and carries an adjudication rationale and the consultant who made the call. An unadjudicated contradiction sets both findings to `contested` strength.
- AC-305.4 A contradiction adjudicated as `genuine_tension_to_resolve_with_client` MUST be promotable to the workshop agenda and to the playback pack as a named tension with a headline and a one-paragraph framing. The reference engagement rendered exactly four such tensions on a Day 1 slide, each stated as an "X versus Y" pair with a short explanation of why the tension costs the organization something, and closed the slide with an explicit statement that the trade-off needed client input. The product must produce that slide from data.
- AC-305.5 Contradictions between a client-stated priority and observed evidence MUST be detectable, not only contradictions between two interviews. The reference fact base contained several of these (a published policy with no enforcement, a platform paid for and not used, a plan produced and never executed), and they were the highest-value findings in the deck.

**FR-306 — Initiative inventory with duplicate consolidation.** The system MUST inventory what the client already has running as `Initiative` records with `origin = client_inflight`, capturing `name`, `owner`, `sponsor`, `status`, `start_date`, `expected_completion`, `percent_complete` where stated, `platform_or_vendor`, `funding_state` (`funded` | `partially_funded` | `unfunded` | `unknown`), and `evidence[]`.
- AC-306.1 The inventory MUST support a consolidation workflow: candidate duplicates are surfaced with a similarity score and a shown-side-by-side comparison, and a consultant merges, keeps both with a stated distinction, or rejects the pairing. Rejections are remembered so the same pair is not re-proposed.
- AC-306.2 Merges preserve both source names as aliases and redirect all references. The reference engagement's own workbook comments show this exact conversation happening in threaded comments across two hidden sheets, with two initiatives argued to be the same thing and a third renamed mid-flight, resolved only in prose and never reflected consistently in the data.
- AC-306.3 An in-flight `Initiative` MUST be linkable to the `Opportunity` records that depend on it, protect it or would duplicate it, so the register can answer "are we recommending something the client is already doing".

**FR-307 — Stakeholder priorities.** The system MUST capture priorities per stakeholder as ordered records of `{ stakeholder_ref, rank, statement, capability_area_ref, evidence[] }`, distinct from findings and from charter objectives.
- AC-307.1 A cross-stakeholder comparison view MUST show where priorities converge and where they diverge, ordered by the number of stakeholders naming each priority.
- AC-307.2 Stakeholder priorities are inputs to the stakeholder-specific roadmap views produced in the business-alignment module, and they are the raw material for the priority-conflict class of contradiction in FR-305.

**FR-308 — Benchmark records with source attribution.** The system MUST store `Benchmark` records with `metric`, `value_or_band`, `unit`, `peer_definition`, `peer_set_description`, `source`, `source_date`, `method` (`published` | `firm_prior_engagement` | `analyst` | `estimated`), and `confidence`.
- AC-308.1 Every benchmark rendered in a client-facing artefact MUST show its attribution and, when the value is a judgement rather than a measurement, a visible note saying so. The reference engagement's peer comparison slide carried exactly such a footnote, stating that the client's own position was subjective and derived from interviews and document review, and that the comparator companies were representative industry leaders rather than a measured sample.
- AC-308.2 The system MUST support the comparison shape the reference engagement used: one row per capability area, a lagging-to-leading track with the client's approximate position marked, a named comparator, and a bulleted list of the attributes that define leading practice in that area.
- AC-308.3 Benchmarks tagged to a `CapabilityArea` are available to M3 as the maturity overlay (FR-411) and to M4 as evidence on a Financial Impact or Risk score.

**FR-309 — Survey instrument and results distribution.** The system MUST support a survey with a defined instrument, anonymous or attributed responses, and a results view that renders distributions.
- AC-309.1 The instrument supports Likert-scale items, single and multi select, ranking items and free text.
- AC-309.2 The results view MUST show total respondent count and respondent count by functional area. The reference engagement reported 21 total respondents broken out across eight functional areas with counts including a zero for one area, and the zero was analytically important because it marked a blind spot.
- AC-309.3 Free-text responses MUST be codable to themes and to capability areas, and coded counts MUST be shown as a distribution. The reference engagement coded free text into a strengths view grouped under four headings (people and culture, infrastructure and security, products and platform, innovation and speed) and an opportunities view grouped under modernization, data, infrastructure and governance.
- AC-309.4 Survey items MUST be linkable to findings, so a distribution can serve as an `Evidence` record with `source_type = survey` and a locator of `item:n`.
- AC-309.5 Survey results MUST be able to disagree with the maturity assessment and with interview findings, and such disagreements are candidates for FR-305 contradiction detection. In the reference engagement the survey was the primary source for the tensions slide.

**FR-310 — Per-leader deep-dive views.** The system MUST assemble, per interviewed leader, a view containing that leader's stated priorities, the findings sourced from their interview, the capability areas they own, the contradictions they are party to, and the opportunities that touch their domain.
- AC-310.1 The reference Day 1 playback contained one such page per senior leader, five in total, and each was a synthesis of a single interview against that leader's domain. The product generates the page rather than having a consultant retype it.

**FR-311 — Findings playback pack.** The system MUST assemble a Day 1 playback pack from the fact base, with a configurable section order defaulting to the reference engagement's sequence: engagement framing and why now; how the fact base was built with input counts; interview themes across people, process, technology and data; the eight capability areas with scope statements; assessment strengths; survey results; the maturity framework explainer; the maturity heatmap pages; tensions beneath the surface; external benchmark comparison; client technology leader goals and guiding principles; per-leader deep dives; the four themes with opportunity counts and percentage shares; the opportunity landscape chart; and a themes and initiatives summary.
- AC-311.1 Every number in the pack MUST be bound to its source record and recomputed at build time. No number in the pack is typed.
- AC-311.2 The pack MUST be marked with a draft state where the underlying data is still moving, and the reference engagement's own slides carried a persistent "first draft, will be updated based on additional inputs" banner. The banner state is derived from whether the underlying `ScoringModel` version and register are locked.
- AC-311.3 Sections whose data is incomplete MUST render as explicitly incomplete rather than as empty. Several tables in the reference deck shipped with blank rating columns where the underlying values existed in the workbook.

**FR-312 — Fact base search and retrieval.** The system MUST provide a single search across findings, evidence, stakeholder priorities, benchmarks, initiatives and contradictions, filterable by capability area, source type, strength, status and date, returning results with their locator and one-click source access.

**FR-313 — Provenance completeness report.** The system MUST report, at any time, the count of findings with zero evidence, findings with single-source evidence, evidence records whose source artefact has been deleted or superseded, and claims used in a deliverable that have no evidence at all. Zero unresolved items in the last category is an M2 exit criterion.

**FR-314 — AI fact-base assist.** The system MUST expose the five Weeks 1-2 AI capabilities in 6.2.6 as user-invoked actions producing `AISuggestion` records under propose → review → commit. Extraction may be run in bulk across an artefact set, but acceptance is per suggestion or per reviewed batch, and a batch acceptance records each suggestion individually.

#### 6.2.6 AI capabilities invoked

| Capability | Purpose in M2 | What M2 hands it | What M2 expects back |
|---|---|---|---|
| AI-04 Transcript synthesis and tagging | Turn a transcript into candidate evidence, findings and tags without a consultant reading line by line | Transcript with timestamps, interviewee function, assigned capability areas, open hypotheses | Proposed `Evidence` with timestamp-range locators and quotes, proposed `Finding` statements with `finding_type`, capability-area tags, and proposed hypothesis status changes |
| AI-05 Document extraction to Evidence | Pull claims out of decks, spreadsheets and documents with exact locators | Parsed artefact with page, slide, sheet and cell structure; `doc_class`; capability-area scope | Proposed `Evidence` records with `page:n`, `slide:n` or `sheet!cell` locators and quotes under 300 characters; proposed `Initiative` records from project lists; proposed `Benchmark` records from analyst material |
