| AI-06 Theme clustering | Group findings into candidate themes and name them | The validated finding set with capability areas, strengths and so-what text | Proposed `Theme` clusters with member findings, a name, a description paragraph and a cluster rationale, plus outliers it could not place |
| AI-07 Contradiction detection | Find where sources disagree, including where stated policy disagrees with observed practice | Finding set, evidence set, stakeholder priorities, charter objectives | Proposed `Contradiction` records with type, the two sides, the evidence behind each and a confidence value |
| AI-08 Precedent retrieval from anonymized prior engagements | Surface how the firm handled the same pattern before | Current findings, capability areas, client size band and industry descriptor | Ranked precedent references with the prior pattern, what was recommended, what the outcome was, and a `source_type = prior_engagement` `EvidenceRef`; all client-identifying content removed at the retrieval boundary |

#### 6.2.7 Exit criteria

| Exit criterion | Rule |
|---|---|
| Interview coverage closed | Every planned interview is `held` or explicitly cancelled with a reason; every held interview is `synthesized` |
| Evidence integrity | Zero findings with no evidence; zero evidence records with an unresolvable locator |
| Findings validated | Every finding used in the playback pack is `validated`, and single-source findings are marked as such |
| Themes promoted | A canonical `Theme` set exists, with no duplicate or near-duplicate names, and every finding is either assigned to a theme or explicitly parked |
| Tensions adjudicated | Every detected contradiction is adjudicated, or promoted to the workshop agenda as a genuine tension |
| Initiative inventory clean | Zero unresolved duplicate candidates in the in-flight inventory |
| Stakeholder priorities captured | At least one priority set per interviewed stakeholder with `influence` of `decider` or `high` |
| Benchmarks attributed | Every benchmark has a source, a peer definition and a method |
| Survey closed | Survey closed with respondent counts by functional area published, or explicitly waived |
| Playback pack builds | The pack builds with zero unbound numbers and zero incomplete mandatory sections |

---

### 6.3 M3 Maturity Assessment (Weeks 3-4) — FR-400 to FR-499

#### 6.3.1 Purpose

M3 answers "where is this organization today, against what standard, on what evidence". It produces a per-focus-area current level, a target level, a computed gap, the evidence behind the score, a narrative rationale, and the recommended next steps to advance. It rolls those up to capability areas and to the enterprise, overlays external benchmarks, and hands gaps forward to M4 as candidate opportunities.

The reference engagement did this in a single spreadsheet tab of 28 rows and published it as a four-page heatmap deck. The structure was sound and the mechanics were not. The maturity label was produced by a `CHOOSE` formula with the five level names hard-coded in every row, so the framework could not be changed without editing 28 formulas. The gap was a formula and was reliable; the levels themselves were typed integers with no validation. There was no way to say "we do not have enough evidence to score this", so thin evidence and genuine immaturity both rendered as a 1. Two different capability areas contained a focus area with the identical name, so a focus area could not be identified by name alone. And the deck rendered 27 rows against the workbook's 28, one focus area silently dropped in transcription.

#### 6.3.2 Methodology phase served

Weeks 3-4 — Current State Maturity + Roadmap Prioritization Build. Core objective, first half: diagnose where the organization is today.

#### 6.3.3 Inputs consumed

| Methodology Inputs column | Product representation |
|---|---|
| Fact base | `Finding` and `Evidence` from M2, filtered by capability area |
| Benchmarks | `Benchmark` records tagged to capability areas (FR-308) |
| Stakeholder priorities | Stakeholder priority records, used to set target levels rather than current levels |
| Existing initiatives | In-flight `Initiative` records, which raise or cap a current level (work in flight is managed execution, not defined process) |
| Business objectives | `Charter` objectives, used to justify target levels above the baseline |
| Architecture | `SourceDocument` `doc_class = architecture` evidence |
| Maturity frameworks | The framework registry (FR-400) |

#### 6.3.4 Screens and views

| View | What it shows | Primary actions |
|---|---|---|
| Framework registry | Available frameworks with level count, level names, definitions, grouping sets | Select, clone, define alternative, set engagement default |
| Level definition reference | The selected framework's levels with plain-language definitions and engagement-calibrated meaning | Read; edit the calibration text per engagement |
| Assessment grid | One row per focus area: area, focus area, status, current, target, gap, label, evidence count, priority to fix | Score, attach evidence, write rationale, change status, request validation |
| Focus area detail | Current-state summary, rationale, evidence list with locators, gaps, next steps, threaded review comments, score history | Edit any field, accept or reject an AI-09 proposal, raise a candidate opportunity |
| Heatmap | The paginated deliverable view with current and target markers per focus area and per-area rationale | Paginate, export, toggle benchmark overlay |
| Rollups | Area averages and enterprise average, current and target, with exclusions listed | Drill into an area |
| Benchmark overlay | Peer or band comparison against the assessed levels | Toggle, choose peer set |
| Gap-to-opportunity | Gaps ordered by size and priority-to-fix, with candidate opportunities and their commit state | Generate candidates via AI-11, accept into the register |

#### 6.3.5 Functional requirements

**FR-400 — Configurable maturity framework registry.** The system MUST maintain a registry of maturity frameworks. A framework record holds `framework_id`, `name`, `version`, `description`, `appraisal_method_note`, an ordered `levels[]` collection, and one or more `grouping_sets[]`.
- AC-400.1 A `level` holds `ordinal`, `short_name`, `display_label`, `definition` (framework-standard text) and `calibration_note` (what this level means for an organization of this client's complexity, editable per engagement).
- AC-400.2 A `grouping_set` holds `name`, an ordered list of `CapabilityArea` definitions, and under each area an ordered list of `MaturityFocusArea` definitions. A framework may ship more than one grouping set, for example a distribution-sector set and a generic set.
- AC-400.3 Frameworks support between 3 and 7 levels. The maturity label for a score MUST be resolved as `framework.levels[current_level].display_label` at render time. No level name may be stored on the assessment row, and no level name may appear in a formula, a chart definition or an export template.
- AC-400.4 Assumption: the shared entity list has no framework entity. `MaturityFramework` and its child `level` records are introduced here as the configuration object that `MaturityAssessment` points at, and this is flagged as an addition to that list.

**FR-401 — CMMI-style default framework.** The registry MUST ship a five-level CMMI-style framework as the recommended default, with levels 1 Initial, 2 Managed, 3 Defined, 4 Quantitatively Managed, 5 Optimizing.
- AC-401.1 Each level ships with a plain-language definition. The reference definitions were: level 1, processes are ad hoc and unpredictable and success depends on individual effort rather than repeatable practice, so the process breaks when a key person is unavailable; level 2, processes are planned and tracked at the project level with resources available and status visible to management, but standards are not yet applied consistently across the organization; level 3, standard processes are documented, consistently applied and adapted from a common organizational framework, so a new team member can follow the process without tribal knowledge; level 4, processes are controlled using statistical and quantitative techniques and performance is predictable; level 5, the organization continuously improves based on quantitative understanding of performance and processes self-correct from data.
- AC-401.2 The framework MUST record its appraisal method as a note shown on the level reference view and on every export. The reference assessment declared an informal appraisal method, stated that scores reflected evidence from structured interviews, documentation review and facilitated deep dives across a named date range, and stated explicitly that the scores were the firm's independent judgement and not a formal certification. That disclosure is a required field, not optional boilerplate.
- AC-401.3 The default framework MUST support a per-engagement baseline target note. The reference calibration held that most organizations in the client's revenue band target level 3 as the baseline standard, and that level 4 is appropriate only where the organization has competitive differentiation ambitions, and that level 5 is aspirational and not a near-term target for any domain. Target-level defaults are seeded from this note and are individually overridable.

**FR-402 — Alternative framework shapes.** The registry MUST support at least one alternative framework shape, and a consultant MUST be able to define a new one without engineering work.
- AC-402.1 The system ships a second framework as an alternative: a five-level analyst-style IT capability score in which the levels are expressed as business-outcome stages rather than process-institutionalization stages, and in which each level carries an explicit exit test rather than a descriptive paragraph. Assumption: the reference engagement calibrated its CMMI scores against an analyst maturity descriptor set but did not use that set as its scoring framework, so the alternative's level content here is an illustrative construction, not something observed in the notes. Its purpose is to prove the registry generalizes.
- AC-402.2 Defining a framework requires: name, level count, per-level short name, display label and definition, at least one grouping set, and an appraisal method note. The system validates that ordinals are contiguous from 1 and that display labels are unique within the framework.
- AC-402.3 Switching an engagement's framework after any `MaturityAssessment` is committed MUST require an explicit remap step in which every existing score is mapped to a level in the new framework, or discarded, with the remap recorded as a `Decision`. The system MUST NOT silently reinterpret an ordinal across frameworks.

**FR-403 — Default 28 focus areas under 8 capability areas.** The default grouping set MUST contain 28 `MaturityFocusArea` records grouped under 8 `CapabilityArea` records, matching the reference engagement's structure.

| Capability area | Focus areas | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Core Operations and Fulfillment | Core legacy platform and core systems; ERP implementation; Integration architecture; Warehouse and distribution; Supply chain planning and merchandising; Marketing technology | 6 |
| Data Architecture and Governance | Master data management; Analytics and business intelligence; Data governance; CRM; Talent and organizational capability | 5 |
| Infrastructure, Network and Security | Distribution-centre infrastructure; Identity and access management; Security and risk; IT operations and service management | 4 |
| Digital Commerce | B2B ordering platform; Dealer eCommerce platforms; Loyalty platform | 3 |
| Vendor Enablement | Vendor experience; Product availability and onboarding | 2 |
| Retail Tech | Store point of sale and retail ERP; Owned-estate to enterprise integration; Dealer services commercialization | 3 |
| Organizational Enablement | IT governance and portfolio management; Talent and organizational capability | 2 |
| Enterprise Architecture | Enterprise architecture; IT shared services; Cloud strategy | 3 |
| **Total** | | **28** |

- AC-403.1 A `MaturityFocusArea` MUST be identified by the composite of its capability area and its name, not by name alone. The reference set contains the focus area "Talent and organizational capability" under two different capability areas, assessed separately with different evidence, and a name-keyed model would have collided them.
- AC-403.2 Focus areas may be added, removed or renamed per engagement before assessment begins. Removals after a score is committed require a reason and retain the scored record as `out_of_scope`.

**FR-404 — Per-focus-area assessment record.** The system MUST store one `MaturityAssessment` per focus area per engagement with the following fields.

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `focus_area_ref` | ref | Composite of capability area and focus area |
| `review_status` | enum | `New` \| `In progress` \| `Ready to Review` \| `Reviewed` \| `Final`, the reference workbook's own status set |
| `score_state` | enum | `scored` \| `insufficient_evidence` \| `out_of_scope` (FR-407) |
| `current_level` | int | Within the framework's ordinal range; required when `score_state = scored` |
| `target_level` | int | Within range; MUST be greater than or equal to `current_level` |
| `gap` | derived | `target_level - current_level`, computed, never typed |
| `maturity_label` | derived | `framework.levels[current_level].display_label`, resolved at render |
| `current_state_summary` | text | Pain points and strengths as an ordered list of discrete statements, each linkable to a `Finding` |
| `rationale` | text | Why this level and not the one above or below, in prose |
| `evidence[]` | refs | `Evidence` records with locators; also renders as the deliverable's "evidence and criteria met" cell |
| `gaps[]` | text list | What is missing to reach the target |
| `next_steps[]` | text list | Recommended actions to advance, each promotable to a candidate `Opportunity` |
| `priority_to_fix` | enum | `Critical` \| `High` \| `Medium` \| `Low` |
| `assessed_by` | ref | Consultant of record for the score |
| `validated_by` | ref | Second consultant, required to reach `Reviewed` |

- AC-404.1 `current_state_summary` MUST be stored as discrete statements rather than one delimited string. The reference workbook packed six to twelve separate observations into a single cell using a slash delimiter, which made them uncountable, unlinkable and unsortable.
- AC-404.2 `gap` and `maturity_label` MUST be read-only in every interface.
- AC-404.3 `target_level` MUST carry a justification referencing either a `Charter` objective or a `Benchmark`. A target above the framework's baseline target level requires the justification to name a differentiation ambition.

**FR-405 — Evidence requirement per score.** A `MaturityAssessment` with `score_state = scored` MUST cite at least one `Evidence` record, and reaching `review_status = Reviewed` MUST require at least two independent sources or an explicit single-source waiver recorded on the record.

**FR-406 — Rationale requirement.** A `MaturityAssessment` MUST carry a rationale that states, in prose, the condition that caps the score at its current level. The reference rows did this well and the phrasing is the model: a row scored 1 explained that success depended on individual effort; a row scored 2 explained that execution was managed within defined projects while broader standards did not yet exist. The rationale field is required to reach `Ready to Review`.

**FR-407 — Insufficient evidence as a distinct state.** The system MUST provide `score_state = insufficient_evidence` as a state distinct from a low score, and MUST NOT permit a numeric level to be stored while that state is set.
- AC-407.1 An `insufficient_evidence` record MUST record what evidence would resolve it: the artefact classes or stakeholder functions needed. Those requirements are pushed back into the M1 document request list and the interview plan as open gaps.
- AC-407.2 `insufficient_evidence` records are excluded from all rollup averages, and every rollup MUST display the count and identity of what it excluded (FR-410).
- AC-407.3 In the heatmap the state renders as a visually distinct treatment that cannot be mistaken for level 1, with a legend entry naming it.
- AC-407.4 An `insufficient_evidence` focus area MUST NOT produce a gap and therefore MUST NOT feed the gap-to-opportunity workflow. It produces an evidence-gathering task instead.
- AC-407.5 `out_of_scope` is similarly distinct, excluded from rollups, and requires a reason.

**FR-408 — Level definition reference view.** The system MUST provide a reference view of the selected framework's levels showing ordinal, short name, display label, framework definition and per-engagement calibration note, plus the appraisal method note, and MUST make that view reachable from every scoring surface with one click.
- AC-408.1 The view is exportable as a deliverable page and is the first page of the maturity deliverable, matching the reference deck's ordering of framework explainer before heatmap.
- AC-408.2 While scoring, the definitions for the level below, the level being considered and the level above MUST be visible without leaving the scoring surface.

**FR-409 — Heatmap view with deliverable pagination.** The system MUST render a heatmap view that paginates the assessed set into deliverable pages, and MUST generate the pagination rather than have a consultant lay it out.
- AC-409.1 Each row shows capability area, focus area, a rating track spanning the framework's ordinal range with the current level and the target level marked, and a scoring rationale.
- AC-409.2 A capability area MUST NOT be split across pages. Pagination fills a page up to a configured maximum row count and breaks at the next area boundary. The reference deck used four pages with 9, 4, 7 and 7 rows.
- AC-409.3 The scoring rationale cell is authored once per capability area and spans that area's focus-area rows, as four bulleted observations. That is how the reference deck presented it, and it means the rationale is an area-level narrative field distinct from the per-focus-area `rationale`.
- AC-409.4 Every page carries a key showing the ordinal track, the current-state average across focus areas, and the target marker, matching the reference deck's key row.
- AC-409.5 The page set MUST be complete by construction. The system reports the count of focus areas in scope, the count rendered, and refuses to export while those differ. The reference deck rendered 27 of 28 focus areas, losing one focus area from a two-focus-area capability area, and nothing in the process caught it.
- AC-409.6 A speaker-notes field per page supports assigning a presenter per capability area, which is how the reference deck was delivered.

**FR-410 — Area and enterprise rollups.** The system MUST compute and display, per capability area and for the enterprise: mean current level, mean target level, mean gap, count scored, count `insufficient_evidence`, count `out_of_scope`, and the distribution of `priority_to_fix`.
- AC-410.1 Means are computed over `score_state = scored` records only, and every displayed mean MUST show its denominator.
- AC-410.2 Rollups are recomputed live as scores change and are never stored as typed values in a deliverable.
- AC-410.3 A configurable weighting per focus area is supported for the mean, defaulting to equal weight. Assumption: the reference engagement used an unweighted mean; weighting is an addition and is off by default.

**FR-411 — Benchmark comparison overlay.** The heatmap and the rollups MUST support an overlay showing, per capability area, an external comparator position and the attributes that define leading practice, drawn from `Benchmark` records.
- AC-411.1 The overlay MUST display each comparator's `peer_definition`, `source` and `method`, and MUST render the subjectivity note required by FR-308.1 when the method is `estimated`.
- AC-411.2 The overlay is a separate deliverable page as well as an in-app toggle, matching the reference engagement's separate peer-comparison slide.

**FR-412 — Gap-to-opportunity workflow.** The system MUST provide a workflow in which a maturity gap produces candidate `Opportunity` records for the M4 register, with provenance retained.
- AC-412.1 Candidate generation is available for any focus area with `gap >= 1` and `score_state = scored`. Candidates may be authored manually or proposed by AI-11.
- AC-412.2 A candidate carries a draft opportunity name, a recommended action, the `focus_area_ref` it came from, the `Finding` records behind it, and the gap size, and lands in the register as `origin = maturity_gap` with `status = candidate`.
- AC-412.3 Accepting a candidate into the register creates the `Opportunity` and a permanent bidirectional link. Opening a focus area later MUST show which register entries answer its gap, and opening an opportunity MUST show which gaps it closes.
- AC-412.4 A focus area with `gap >= 2` and `priority_to_fix` of `Critical` or `High` and zero linked opportunities MUST be flagged as an unanswered gap and counted in the M3 exit criteria. In the reference workbook 10 of 28 focus areas carried a Critical priority-to-fix and the connection from those rows to the register existed only as prose in a next-steps cell.
- AC-412.5 The reverse direction is also required: an `Opportunity` whose linked focus areas all show `gap = 0` MUST be flagged for review, since the diagnosis no longer supports the recommendation.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  F["Finding + Evidence<br/>from M2"] --> A["MaturityAssessment<br/>current, target, rationale"]
  A -->|"score_state = scored<br/>gap >= 1"| G["Gap"]
  A -->|"score_state = insufficient_evidence"| E["Evidence-gathering task<br/>back to M1 request list"]
  G --> C["Candidate Opportunity<br/>AI-11 proposes, consultant commits"]
  C --> R["M4 Opportunity Register<br/>origin = maturity_gap"]
  R -->|"bidirectional link"| A
```

**FR-413 — Review and validation workflow.** The system MUST support threaded review comments on any assessment field, addressed to a named consultant, with an open or resolved state and a resolution note.
- AC-413.1 Moving a record to `Reviewed` requires every comment on it to be resolved and requires `validated_by` to differ from `assessed_by`.
- AC-413.2 A comment that proposes a score change MUST offer a one-click path to make that change, so the change is applied through the scoring interface with history rather than negotiated in prose and applied silently. The reference workbook contains exactly this pattern as unresolved threaded comments asking whether a score should move and whether a summary was accurate, sitting in a file whose review status column said the row was reviewed.

**FR-414 — Score history.** Every change to `current_level`, `target_level`, `score_state` or `priority_to_fix` MUST write an `AuditEvent` with before and after values, actor, timestamp, reason string and the `AISuggestion` id if the change originated from an accepted proposal. The focus-area detail view MUST render this history as a timeline.

**FR-415 — AI maturity assist.** The system MUST expose the three Weeks 3-4 maturity AI capabilities in 6.3.6 as user-invoked actions producing `AISuggestion` records under propose → review → commit. No AI-proposed level, gap, rationale or opportunity is ever committed without a consultant action.

#### 6.3.6 AI capabilities invoked

| Capability | Purpose in M3 | What M3 hands it | What M3 expects back |
|---|---|---|---|
| AI-09 Evidence-backed maturity scoring proposal | Propose a current level and a target level per focus area, with the evidence that justifies each | Framework levels with definitions and calibration notes; the findings and evidence tagged to that focus area; in-flight initiatives touching it; the relevant benchmarks | Proposed `current_level`, `target_level`, a rationale naming the condition that caps the score, the specific `Evidence` refs relied on, a confidence band, and an explicit `insufficient_evidence` recommendation where the evidence does not support any level |
| AI-10 Root cause and gap analysis | Explain why the gap exists, not just that it exists | The scored assessment, its evidence, its findings, related focus areas and their scores, contradictions touching the area | Proposed root-cause statements distinguishing capability gaps, ownership gaps, funding gaps and sequencing gaps, each with evidence; proposed `gaps[]` entries; identification of cross-area causes where one area's gap is caused by another's |
| AI-11 Opportunity generation from gaps | Turn a gap into concrete candidate opportunities the register can score | Focus area, gap size, root causes, next steps, priority to fix, existing register entries | Candidate `Opportunity` records with a name, a recommended action written as a directive, the initiative it likely belongs under, the findings it addresses, and a duplicate-check result against the existing register |

#### 6.3.7 Exit criteria

| Exit criterion | Rule |
|---|---|
| Coverage | Every in-scope focus area has a `MaturityAssessment` in `score_state` of `scored`, `insufficient_evidence` or `out_of_scope` |
| No implicit low scores | Zero focus areas scored at the lowest level with fewer than two evidence records and no single-source waiver |
| Evidence and rationale | Every `scored` record has at least one evidence ref and a non-empty rationale |
| Targets justified | Every `target_level` above the framework baseline names an objective or benchmark |
| Review complete | Every record is at `Reviewed` or `Final` with `validated_by` set and all comments resolved |
| Rollups clean | Every rollup displays its denominator and its exclusions |
| Deliverable complete | Heatmap pagination renders 100 percent of in-scope focus areas; page count and row counts reported |
| Gaps answered | Zero focus areas with `gap >= 2` and `priority_to_fix` of `Critical` or `High` and no linked opportunity |
| Framework declared | Framework, version, appraisal method note and calibration notes present on the deliverable |

---

### 6.4 M4 Opportunity Register, Scoring and Prioritization (Weeks 3-4) — FR-500 to FR-599

#### 6.4.1 Purpose

M4 is the heart of the product. It holds the three-level taxonomy (theme, initiative, opportunity), the scored register, the derived priority, the two prioritization charts, the portfolio summary, and the facilitated workshop in which client leaders rank priorities and assign urgency alongside the calculated score.

The reference engagement produced this in a spreadsheet, and the defect list is long enough to be a specification in its own right. Dimension scores were stored as prose strings and converted to numbers by taking the first character with `VALUE(LEFT(cell,1))`, three times per row. Weights were hard-coded into a formula row and referenced by absolute cell address from two sheets, one of which pointed at an external workbook that no longer resolved. The theme of each opportunity resolved through a lookup into a hidden sheet in a different file. From one row down, the derived columns were shifted by one position, so a business-value formula sat in the priority column and a status column held a paragraph of free text. Two opportunity identifier schemes existed side by side, one with no identifiers at all and one with `OPP-nn` codes on a different four-value score scale, and they did not reconcile. A declared effort column was never populated in the master. Data validation ranges skipped rows so some rows could not be set from a dropdown. Conditional formatting still matched retired theme names. And another client's slides sat inside a working copy of the deck.

None of that is a criticism of the analysis. The analysis was good. The point of this module is that the analysis should not be able to be destroyed by its container.

#### 6.4.2 Methodology phase served

Weeks 3-4 — Current State Maturity + Roadmap Prioritization Build. Core objective, second half: translate findings into initial roadmap priorities. Outputs: prioritized initiative backlog and first-cut roadmap logic.

#### 6.4.3 Inputs consumed

| Methodology Inputs column | Product representation |
|---|---|
| Fact base | `Finding` records referenced by each opportunity, replacing the reference workbook's comma-separated pain-point number list |
| Benchmarks | `Benchmark` records cited as evidence on Financial Impact and Risk scores |
| Stakeholder priorities | Stakeholder priority records, used in workshop mode and in reconciliation |
| Existing initiatives | In-flight `Initiative` records, so the register can distinguish new work from protecting work already funded |
| Business objectives | `Charter` objectives, the anchor for Strategic Alignment scoring (FR-203) |
| Architecture | Architecture evidence, used for dependency inference |
| Maturity frameworks | Consumed via M3; gaps arrive as candidate opportunities (FR-412) |

#### 6.4.4 Screens and views

| View | What it shows | Primary actions |
|---|---|---|
| Register tree | Theme, initiative, opportunity hierarchy with counts, scores and bands rolled up | Navigate, add, move, filter |
| Opportunity detail | Every field in FR-503, the three scores with anchors and evidence, links to findings, maturity gaps, dependencies, comments, history | Edit, score, link, comment, raise dependency |
| Bulk scoring and triage | One row per opportunity, three score cells, anchor tooltips, progress and unscored filters | Score at speed, keyboard-only, jump to next unscored |
| Scoring guide | The full rubric: dimension, weight, question, and per-score level label, meaning and calibration example | Read; edit rubric text pre-lock |
| Calibration | Distribution per dimension, mean, mode, share at 4 and above, scorer comparison | Inspect, flag drift, re-open scores |
| Bubble chart | Business value against urgency, bubble size by weighted score, colour by theme | Filter, hover, select, export |
| Quadrant 2x2 | Four labelled quadrants at the configured threshold, with occupancy counts | Filter, drill, export |
| Portfolio summary | Counts and percentage share by theme; per-initiative average weighted score | Export as theme pages |
| Duplicates | Candidate duplicate pairs with similarity and a side-by-side diff | Merge, keep both with distinction, reject |
| Workshop console (facilitator) | Session state, groups, activity timer, board state, reveal controls | Run activities, reveal calculated ranks, capture outputs |
| Workshop board (participant) | Cards with initiative in bold and opportunity in italic, a detail expander, a top-five column and an urgency dropdown | Move cards, set urgency, add notes |
| Reconciliation | Client rank against calculated priority, with disagreement magnitude and required resolution | Resolve per opportunity |
| Change log against issued version | Field-level deltas since a named issued deliverable | Review, annotate, publish a change summary |

#### 6.4.5 Functional requirements

##### Register structure

**FR-500 — Three-level register with taxonomy enforced by reference.** The system MUST hold the register as `Theme` containing `Initiative` containing `Opportunity`, where the parent of each record is a foreign key and never a typed string.
- AC-500.1 An `Opportunity` stores `initiative_ref` only. Its theme is resolved through the initiative. The reference workbook resolved theme by lookup formula from the initiative name, and in three rows the formula's lookup argument pointed at the wrong row, so three opportunities displayed a theme belonging to a different opportunity. Structural containment removes that failure mode.
- AC-500.2 Deleting or renaming a theme or initiative MUST NOT orphan children. Renames propagate; deletions require reassignment of children first.
- AC-500.3 The register enforces the reference engagement's scale as a soft expectation and not a limit: 4 themes, roughly 17 to 20 initiatives, and 40 to 60 opportunities including operating-model entries. The reference set was 4 themes, 17 initiatives, 43 technology opportunities and 12 operating-model opportunities.

**FR-501 — Theme record.** A `Theme` MUST carry `theme_id`, `name`, `description` (one paragraph, board-legible), `old_name[]`, `sequence`, `colour_token`, and derived counts of initiatives and opportunities.
- AC-501.1 The reference theme set is seeded as a template: Stabilize the Core; Assess and Protect Current Investments; Grow the Top Line; Build the Intelligent Enterprise. Each ships with the shape of description the reference used, which states the condition, the consequence and what the theme is therefore about.
- AC-501.2 Theme names MUST be unique after normalization of case, whitespace and punctuation. Near-duplicates within a small edit distance are blocked with an explanatory message. The reference taxonomy carried both an unmerged duplicate of one theme name and a misspelled variant of another, and both were live lookup keys.

**FR-502 — Initiative record.** An `Initiative` MUST carry `initiative_id`, `name`, `theme_ref`, `sequence` (the wave number, referencing the configured `Wave` set), `description` (one paragraph stating the condition and what the initiative does about it), `old_name[]`, `owner_stakeholder_ref`, `origin` (`firm_recommended` | `client_inflight`), and derived counts and score rollups.
- AC-502.1 `sequence` MUST reference a configured wave, defaulting to the four-wave set. In the reference taxonomy all 17 initiatives carried a sequence value of 1 through 4.
- AC-502.2 The initiative description is a required field before an initiative may appear in a client-facing deliverable. In the reference taxonomy 16 of 17 initiatives had a description paragraph and one did not, and that one appeared on a client slide as an empty row.
- AC-502.3 `Initiative` rollups MUST include the mean weighted score across its opportunities, rounded to one decimal, which is the number the reference theme slides displayed per initiative (values such as 4.2, 3.8, 3.7, 3.2 and 2.5).

**FR-503 — Opportunity record.** An `Opportunity` MUST carry the following fields, which together cover every column the reference register used.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `opportunity_id` | string, immutable | Single scheme, `OPP-nnnn`, assigned on create (FR-505) |
| `name` | string | The specific gap or action, unique within its initiative |
| `initiative_ref` | ref | Parent; theme derived through it |
| `capability_area_ref` | ref | The technology or capability area, the register's "tech area" |
| `business_area` | enum | Executive ownership domain, from a configured value set, the register's business-area mapping |
| `recommended_action` | text | Written as a directive, what to do rather than what exists |
| `so_what` | text | Why it matters, in board language |
| `t_shirt_size` | enum | From the configured scale (FR-212) |
| `span` | enum | Coarse duration scale if enabled |
| `objective_refs[]` | refs | Charter objectives this serves; the register's strategy-alignment field |
| `finding_refs[]` | refs | The findings and pain points this addresses, replacing a comma-separated number list |
| `maturity_gap_refs[]` | refs | Focus-area gaps this closes (FR-412) |
| `relationship_type` | enum | `B2B` \| `B2C` \| `B2B2C` \| `Internal` |
| `register_segment` | enum | `technology` \| `operating_model` (FR-519) |
| `origin` | enum | `maturity_gap` \| `interview` \| `workshop` \| `client_inflight` \| `benchmark` \| `consultant_judgement` |
| `foundational` | bool | Whether other work depends on this; the reference register's foundational flag |
| `status` | enum | `New` \| `In progress` \| `Ready to Review` \| `Reviewed` \| `Final`, plus `Existing` \| `Updated` \| `New` as a separate `provenance_state` field |
| `notes_open_items` | text | Working notes and open questions |
| `owner_stakeholder_ref` | ref | Accountable owner once assigned |
| `client_priority_rank` | int, nullable | Client-assigned rank from workshop mode (FR-522) |
| `scores` | child records | One `OpportunityScore` per `ScoreDimension` |
| `weighted_score` | derived | FR-509 |
| `priority_band` | derived | FR-510 |
| `business_value_x` | derived | FR-511 |
| `urgency_y` | derived | FR-511 |
| `quadrant` | derived | FR-512 |

- AC-503.1 The reference register conflated two different status concepts in one column: a review workflow state and a provenance state describing whether the opportunity was pre-existing, updated or newly surfaced. These are separate fields here, because both were needed and one column could only hold one.
- AC-503.2 `foundational` is a real analytical field and MUST be distinguished from `t_shirt_size` and from dependency records. The reference register carried it as a yes-or-no column with a dropdown, but the dropdown's validation range skipped rows, so several rows could not be set from the dropdown at all. Enum validation here is server-side and applies to every row without exception (FR-504).
- AC-503.3 Free-text fields MUST have a defined maximum length and MUST NOT be used to store lists. Lists are lists.

**FR-504 — Enum integrity.** Every enum field on every record in the register MUST be validated server-side against its configured value set on create and on update, for every row, with no per-row exceptions.
- AC-504.1 A write of a value outside the set MUST be rejected with the field name, the offending value and the permitted set. The reference workbook has a paragraph of analytical prose sitting in a status cell whose intended values were three words long, because a spreadsheet cannot refuse a value.
- AC-504.2 Bulk import MUST validate every row before committing any row, and MUST report all violations at once rather than failing on the first.

**FR-505 — Single identifier scheme.** The system MUST assign every `Opportunity` exactly one immutable identifier at creation, and MUST NOT support a second parallel scheme.
- AC-505.1 Identity is never the concatenation of an initiative name and an opportunity name. The reference master register had no identifier column at all, so identity was the text of two fields, and any edit to either changed the identity of the row.
- AC-505.2 Where an engagement inherits opportunity codes from a prior artefact, those codes are stored as `external_ids[]` aliases on the record. They are cross-references, not identifiers. The reference engagement had a hidden sheet using a separate `OPP-nn` scheme on a different four-value score scale that did not reconcile one-to-one with the visible register, and the two sets were never mapped.
- AC-505.3 The system MUST support at most one active `ScoringModel` per engagement per `register_segment`, and MUST NOT allow a second score scale to exist for the same records. Any legacy scale imported as an alias is read-only and clearly labelled as historical.

##### Scoring

**FR-506 — Score against the three dimensions with inline anchors.** The system MUST store one `OpportunityScore` per opportunity per `ScoreDimension`, holding `score` as an integer within the dimension's scale, `anchor_ref` identifying the rubric row chosen, `rationale`, `evidence[]`, `scored_by`, `scored_at`, and `confidence` where proposed by AI-13.
- AC-506.1 The scoring surface MUST display the anchor definitions for the dimension while scoring, so the scorer sees what a 4 means at the moment of choosing 4. The reference workbook achieved this by pasting the full anchor sentence into the cell as the stored value, which is why the numeric score had to be recovered by reading the first character of a string. Here the anchor is shown and the score is stored as an integer with a reference to the anchor row.
- AC-506.2 The stored score MUST be an integer. No parsing of prose into numbers occurs anywhere in this product.
- AC-506.3 The default rubric, from the reference engagement, is:

| Dimension | Weight | Question the scorer answers | 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Financial Impact | 0.40 | Revenue unlocked, cost saved or margin recovered, covering both the upside of acting and the financial cost of not acting. What is the dollar consequence either way? | Transformational: directly enables a new revenue stream, recovers major margin, or eliminates a financial liability that compounds annually, at a magnitude that is material at board level | Material: meaningful revenue growth, cost reduction or margin improvement, quantifiable and significant at operational level, within the configured materiality band, or removes a known annual cost. Named systems or processes must be cited | Moderate: efficiency gains, FTE time savings or cost avoidance that are real but hard to isolate to a single figure. Removing a bottleneck that slows other value-generating work counts here | Indirect: enables other initiatives with higher financial impact but produces no direct dollar outcome itself. Value requires a chain of two or more dependent steps | Hygiene: good practice with negligible direct financial consequence either way. Would not change the investment decision even if absent |
| Risk if Deferred | 0.35 | Not how fragile the system is, but what actually happens if this gap persists. If we defer 12 months, what breaks and what does it cost? | Existential: inaction creates a risk that, if realized, halts operations, triggers a regulatory event, or causes financial harm that cannot be absorbed. Recovery within a normal quarter is not possible without extraordinary intervention | Severe: deferral creates material operational disruption, significant customer or partner impact, or a compounding liability that grows meaningfully each quarter. Recoverable, but costly and externally visible | Compounding: the cost of deferral increases over time. Not a crisis today, but each quarter of inaction makes the fix harder or more expensive. Technical debt with a clear accumulation rate | Latent: risk exists but is not actively accumulating. Could surface as a blocker when a related programme goes live, but current operations are stable and workarounds are sustainable | Negligible: deferral has no meaningful consequence for two or more years. The gap is inconvenient, not risky |
| Strategic Alignment | 0.25 | How directly does this serve a named strategic objective? Scored on traceability. Can you draw a direct line without explanation? | Named explicitly: called out by name, or is the direct enabling action for a stated goal. Removing it would visibly undermine that goal. No inferential leap | Direct enabler: directly enables a named goal even if not named itself. Single-step and obvious to a business leader reading the strategy | Foundational dependency: a prerequisite to a direct enabler. Real but requires a two-step explanation of the form "this enables X, which enables goal Y" | Thematic fit: fits the spirit of the strategy but requires explanation to connect to a specific goal | Not traceable: good practice with no direct or foundational connection to a named goal. Would not appear in a board investment narrative |

- AC-506.4 The rubric's monetary bands are stored as configurable per-engagement values, not as literals in the rubric text, because materiality differs by client. Assumption: the reference rubric stated specific dollar bands; those are represented here as configured bands to avoid a fixed threshold and to avoid reproducing client-specific figures.
- AC-506.5 Every anchor row MUST support a calibration example naming something specific in the engagement, which is how the reference scoring guide made the rubric usable. Examples are engagement-specific text and are shown beside the anchor while scoring.

**FR-507 — Scoring guide view.** The system MUST provide a scoring guide view rendering, for each dimension: the dimension name, weight, the scorer's question, and a table of score, level label, what it means, and the engagement's calibration example. The view MUST also state the weighted-score formula, the maximum possible score and the priority bands.
- AC-507.1 The guide is exportable as a client-facing deliverable page, which the reference engagement shipped in both the internal and the client-shared workbook.
- AC-507.2 The guide is generated from `ScoringModel` configuration. It cannot drift from the model that produced the scores. The reference workbook's guide said the priority threshold was 3.75 while the formula implemented four bands at 4.5, 3.75 and 2.8, and both statements were true of different things and read as contradictory.

**FR-508 — Per-dimension evidence and rationale.** Each `OpportunityScore` MUST support its own `rationale` and its own `evidence[]`, independent of the other dimensions and independent of the opportunity's narrative fields.
- AC-508.1 A score of 5 on any dimension MUST carry at least one rationale sentence, and on Financial Impact and Risk if Deferred MUST carry at least one `EvidenceRef`.
- AC-508.2 Strategic Alignment scores of 4 or 5 MUST cite objectives, per FR-203.2.
- AC-508.3 The opportunity detail view MUST show, per dimension, the score, the chosen anchor, the rationale and the evidence, so a challenge in a workshop can be answered from the screen.

**FR-509 — Derived weighted score.** The system MUST derive `weighted_score` as the sum over dimensions of `weight * score`, using the weights on the engagement's active `ScoringModel` version.
- AC-509.1 The value is stored as a derived field with the `scoring_model_version` that produced it, recomputed on any change to a score or to the model.
- AC-509.2 The value is displayed rounded to two decimals and MUST be computed in a decimal type. The reference workbook surfaced values such as 2.9000000000000004 and 2.6500000000000004 directly into a client-facing sheet.
- AC-509.3 Maximum possible score MUST be computed from the model rather than assumed to be 5.0.
- AC-509.4 An opportunity with any dimension unscored MUST show `weighted_score` as unavailable, not as a partial sum. It appears in the unscored filter and is excluded from distributions and from chart plots, with the exclusion counted and displayed.

**FR-510 — Derived priority band.** The system MUST derive `priority_band` from `weighted_score` against the configured bands (FR-211), evaluated top down, and MUST render the band with its canonical label everywhere.

**FR-511 — Bubble chart.** The system MUST provide a bubble chart with X as business value, Y as urgency, bubble size as weighted score and colour as theme.
- AC-511.1 Business value is derived as the mean of the Strategic Alignment score and the Financial Impact score. Urgency is the Risk if Deferred score. Bubble size is the weighted score. These are the reference engagement's definitions and MUST be stated on the chart itself, as the reference slide did in its subtitle.
- AC-511.2 The derivation MUST be expressed as a named, configurable chart definition referencing dimension identifiers, not as hard-coded column arithmetic. If the engagement changes its dimension set, the chart definition is revalidated and the consultant is asked what business value now means.
- AC-511.3 Points sharing identical coordinates MUST be visibly separated or clustered with a count, since integer scores on a 1 to 5 scale produce heavy overplotting. In the reference chart series, values repeated many times across 56 plotted opportunities.
- AC-511.4 The chart MUST support labelled callout lists beside it, grouped by quadrant, which is how the reference slide made 56 bubbles readable: two lists naming the eight act-now items and the eight plan-and-fund items.

**FR-512 — Quadrant view.** The system MUST provide a 2x2 quadrant view splitting business value and urgency at the configured threshold, defaulting to 3.5, with the four configured labels.
- AC-512.1 The default assignment rule: value at or above threshold and urgency at or above threshold is `Act Now`; value below and urgency at or above is `Defend`; value at or above and urgency below is `Plan & Fund`; otherwise `Sequence Later`. The reference workbook stated the intent of each quadrant in a cell comment, and those statements belong in the product as the quadrant descriptions: act now is high value and high urgency that cannot wait; defend is risk mitigation that must happen regardless of value; plan and fund is the right long-term bet that is not on fire; sequence later is real opportunity that depends on foundations not yet in place.
- AC-512.2 The view MUST display occupancy counts per quadrant, and MUST flag any quadrant with zero occupants as an explicit warning with an explanation of what would have to be true for an opportunity to land there. In the reference register the `Defend` quadrant had no occupants across the entire calculated set, so a labelled box on a client-facing chart described a category the analysis had never produced. A label with no members is either a scoring problem or a framework problem, and the product must say so rather than print an empty box.
- AC-512.3 Quadrant assignment MUST be derived. It MUST NOT be separately editable. Where a consultant disagrees with a quadrant, the path is to change a score or the threshold, both of which are auditable.

**FR-513 — Live derivation.** All derived values (`weighted_score`, `priority_band`, `business_value_x`, `urgency_y`, `quadrant`, initiative and theme rollups, chart positions, distributions) MUST update within 300 milliseconds of a score change, without a page reload, for a register of up to 200 opportunities.

**FR-514 — Filtering.** The register, the bubble chart, the quadrant view and the portfolio summary MUST support combinable filters on theme, initiative, capability area, business area, relationship type, register segment, priority band, quadrant, t-shirt size, foundational flag, origin, status, owner and scored state, and MUST show the active filter set and the filtered count against the total.
- AC-514.1 Every chart and summary MUST state whether it is filtered, and an export of a filtered view MUST carry the filter description.

**FR-515 — Portfolio summary and theme pages.** The system MUST produce a portfolio summary showing, per theme, the count of opportunities, the percentage share of the total, and the mean weighted score, plus per-initiative mean weighted score within each theme.
- AC-515.1 Counts and shares are computed, never typed. The reference engagement's theme distribution slide showed 13, 16, 19 and 8 opportunities at 23, 29, 34 and 14 percent, and those figures had to reconcile against a register on a different sheet in a different file.
- AC-515.2 Percentage shares MUST use a stated rounding rule and MUST reconcile to 100 percent, with any residual shown rather than absorbed silently.
- AC-515.3 The system MUST generate the reference engagement's theme page shape: theme name, a focus sentence, and a table of initiative, mean weighted score and the opportunities within it.
- AC-515.4 The summary MUST state its denominator explicitly, because the reference engagement's totals varied by artefact: 43 technology opportunities in the register, 55 rows including operating-model entries, and 56 plotted points on the landscape chart. One canonical count with a named scope replaces that.

**FR-516 — Bulk scoring and triage view.** The system MUST provide a view for scoring 40 or more opportunities efficiently.
- AC-516.1 One row per opportunity showing name, initiative, capability area, the three score cells, weighted score, band and quadrant, with derived values updating in place.
- AC-516.2 Score entry is keyboard-driven: a number key sets the score, tab moves across dimensions, enter moves to the next opportunity, and a single keystroke opens the anchor definitions for the current dimension as an overlay.
- AC-516.3 Anchor text for the current dimension and score is always visible without a click, as a persistent side panel.
- AC-516.4 The view shows scoring progress as scored, partially scored and unscored counts, and supports jumping to the next unscored dimension anywhere in the register.
- AC-516.5 Rationale may be deferred during a triage pass, but an opportunity cannot reach `Ready to Review` without the rationale required by FR-508.
- AC-516.6 A scoring pass MUST be resumable, and MUST record the scorer per score so FR-518 can compare scorers.

**FR-517 — Duplicate detection and merge.** The system MUST detect candidate duplicate opportunities and provide a merge workflow.
- AC-517.1 Candidates are surfaced with a similarity score computed over name, recommended action, capability area, linked findings and linked maturity gaps, and are proposed by AI-12.
- AC-517.2 The merge screen shows the two records side by side field by field, with differences highlighted, and requires the consultant to choose a surviving value per differing field.
- AC-517.3 Merging retains both identifiers, redirects every reference (dependencies, roadmap items, workshop cards, client ranks, deliverable citations) to the survivor, and writes an `AuditEvent`. The merged identifier resolves to the survivor forever.
- AC-517.4 Where two entries are genuinely distinct despite similarity, the consultant records the distinction on both records and the pair is suppressed from future proposals. The reference workbook contains exactly this unresolved argument in threaded comments, asking whether the same platform consolidation had been counted three times across three different opportunities and whether the attribute scores could distinguish them. The distinction statement is the artefact that answers that question next time.
- AC-517.5 Cross-segment duplicates MUST be detected: a technology opportunity and an operating-model opportunity describing the same work. The reference register carried near-identical governance entries in both the technology sheet and the operating-model sheet.

**FR-518 — Scoring calibration view.** The system MUST provide a calibration view showing, per dimension, the distribution of scores across the register.
- AC-518.1 The view shows a histogram of scores 1 to 5 per dimension, with count and percentage per score, mean, median, mode and standard deviation.
- AC-518.2 The view MUST flag drift conditions: any dimension where more than 60 percent of scores fall on a single value; any dimension whose mean exceeds 4.0; any dimension with fewer than three distinct values used across the whole register; and any dimension where the top two values account for more than 85 percent of scores.
- AC-518.3 The view MUST compare scorers: mean per dimension per `scored_by`, so a systematically generous scorer is visible.
- AC-518.4 The view MUST show band occupancy and quadrant occupancy alongside, so a consultant can see that the score distribution has collapsed the register into two bands before it appears in front of a client.
- AC-518.5 Flagged drift MUST be resolvable by re-opening a filtered scoring pass on the affected dimension, and the calibration state at the time a deliverable is issued MUST be recorded with it.

**FR-519 — Operating-model opportunities as a register segment.** Operating-model opportunities MUST live in the same register as technology opportunities, distinguished by `register_segment`, scored against the same `ScoringModel` version, and included in the same derivations.
- AC-519.1 They MUST be filterable and separately reportable, since the reference engagement presented them separately, but they MUST NOT be a separate sheet with its own copy of the weights. In the reference workbook the operating-model sheet's weighted score formula referenced a weight range in an external workbook, which broke on copy and produced values that could not be recomputed.
- AC-519.2 The reference set had 12 operating-model opportunities under a single operating-model initiative, and they carried the same three-dimension scores and the same priority bands as the technology set.

```mermaid
erDiagram
  Theme ||--o{ Initiative : contains
  Initiative ||--o{ Opportunity : contains
  Wave ||--o{ Initiative : sequences
  Opportunity ||--o{ OpportunityScore : "scored on"
  ScoringModel ||--o{ ScoreDimension : defines
  ScoreDimension ||--o{ OpportunityScore : "rubric for"
  Opportunity }o--o{ Finding : addresses
  Opportunity }o--o{ MaturityAssessment : "closes gap in"
  Opportunity }o--o{ Dependency : "blocks or blocked by"
  Opportunity }o--o{ Charter : "traces to objective in"
  OpportunityScore }o--o{ Evidence : "justified by"
  Opportunity ||--o{ StakeholderFeedback : "ranked in workshop"
  AISuggestion }o--|| Opportunity : "proposes change to"
```

##### Workshop mode

**FR-520 — Facilitated workshop session.** The system MUST provide a workshop mode in which client leaders, working in groups, rank priorities and assign urgency to opportunities, with the facilitator driving activity state from a console.
- AC-520.1 A `WorkshopSession` record holds the engagement, date, participant list, group definitions, the activity sequence with planned durations, and the opportunity subset in scope. Assumption: `WorkshopSession` is introduced here as a container for the session; the individual client judgements it captures are stored as `StakeholderFeedback` records from the shared entity list.
- AC-520.2 Participants are assigned to groups, and each group is dealt a card set. In the reference engagement each group worked from its own set of cards rather than the whole register.
- AC-520.3 Each card MUST render the initiative name in bold and the opportunity name in italic, with a detail expander revealing the recommended action, the so-what, the linked findings and the t-shirt size. That is exactly the card format the reference session used and explained to participants on a slide.
- AC-520.4 Only one participant per group may move that group's cards at a time, with a visible indicator of who holds control and a one-click handover. The reference session enforced this socially by instruction; the product enforces it mechanically to prevent conflicting drags.
- AC-520.5 The facilitator console MUST support an activity timer with the configured duration, a visible countdown for participants, and a facilitator-controlled reveal that shows the firm's calculated ranking beside the group's selection only when the facilitator triggers it. Concealment before reveal is a hard requirement: the reference session deliberately collected client judgement first and revealed the calculated view second.

**FR-521 — Activity 1, establishing top priorities.** The system MUST support a top-priorities activity in which each group selects its top five critical priorities from its card set into a ranked column.
- AC-521.1 The activity MUST work within a 50 minute budget, structured as the reference session structured it: 10 minutes for the group to review cards and move its top five, 5 minutes per group to report out, 5 minutes of room-wide challenge, and 10 minutes of discussion after the calculated ranking is revealed.
- AC-521.2 The top-five column enforces a maximum of five cards and requires them to be ordered.
- AC-521.3 Selections are captured as `StakeholderFeedback` records tied to the group, the session, the activity and the opportunity, with the rank and any spoken rationale the facilitator captures.
- AC-521.4 The reveal MUST show, per card, the calculated `priority_band` and `weighted_score` beside the group's rank, and MUST list where the two disagree in the reconciliation view (FR-523).
- AC-521.5 The priority definitions used in the room MUST be displayable as a reference panel, generated from the configured bands, matching the reference session's definitions slide.

**FR-522 — Activity 2, assigning urgency, and the client rank field.** The system MUST support an urgency activity in which each group assigns an urgency level to its top five, and MUST store client-assigned judgement alongside the calculated values rather than overwriting them.
- AC-522.1 The activity MUST work within a 30 minute budget: 10 minutes to set urgency by dropdown on each card, 5 minutes per group to share selections and rationale, 5 minutes of full-room challenge, and the remainder for discussion after reveal.
- AC-522.2 Urgency values come from the configured quadrant label set, so a client-assigned urgency and a calculated quadrant are directly comparable.
- AC-522.3 `Opportunity.client_priority_rank` stores an integer client-assigned rank across the room's combined selections, unique within a session, and coexists permanently with `weighted_score` and `priority_band`. Neither derives from the other and neither overwrites the other. In the reference engagement this field was added to the register after the workshop, populated by hand from the collaborative board, and ran 1 through 19, with one rank value duplicated across two rows because nothing enforced uniqueness. The product enforces uniqueness within a session and records which session produced the rank.
- AC-522.4 Where the register also carries a separate post-session ranking for the operating-model segment, as the reference workbook did, it MUST be the same field scoped to the same session, not a differently named column on a different sheet.

**FR-523 — Reconciliation of client judgement and calculated priority.** The system MUST provide a reconciliation view that shows where client-assigned rank and calculated priority disagree, and MUST force an explicit resolution for each material disagreement.
- AC-523.1 Disagreement is computed as the difference between the opportunity's rank by `weighted_score` within the session's scope and its `client_priority_rank`, plus a separate flag where client-assigned urgency and calculated quadrant differ. A configurable threshold, defaulting to a rank difference of 5 or more places, marks a disagreement as material.
- AC-523.2 Every material disagreement MUST be resolved by one of exactly three outcomes, each requiring a rationale: `accept_client_rank`, which records that client judgement supersedes the calculation and why, leaving the scores untouched; `revise_scores`, which opens the affected dimension scores for change and records the evidence that justifies the change; `record_disagreement`, which keeps both positions visible and carries the disagreement forward into the roadmap and the decision log.
- AC-523.3 Each resolution writes a `Decision` record with the outcome, the rationale, the participants and the date. A `record_disagreement` outcome also creates an agenda item for the business-alignment phase, which is where the methodology expects key disagreements to be resolved.
- AC-523.4 Unresolved material disagreements MUST block the M4 exit gate.
- AC-523.5 The view MUST be usable live: sortable by disagreement magnitude, resolvable in three clicks plus a rationale, and readable on a projector.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant F as Facilitator
  participant G as Client group
  participant S as System
  F->>S: Start Activity 1 (50 min timer)
  G->>S: Move top five cards, ordered
  S->>S: Store StakeholderFeedback (group, rank)
  F->>S: Trigger reveal
  S->>G: Show calculated band and weighted score per card
  F->>S: Start Activity 2 (30 min timer)
  G->>S: Set urgency per card
  S->>S: Compute client_priority_rank vs calculated rank
  S->>F: Reconciliation list, sorted by disagreement
  F->>S: Resolve each: accept client / revise scores / record disagreement
  S->>S: Write Decision + AuditEvent per resolution
```

**FR-524 — Activity 3, dependencies, milestones and effort.** The system MUST support an activity in which each group adds dependencies, milestones, business value statements and a t-shirt size to its prioritized opportunities.
- AC-524.1 Dependencies are captured as `Dependency` records with `from_opportunity`, `to_opportunity`, `dependency_type` (`blocks` | `enables` | `shares_resource` | `shares_platform`), and a rationale. More than one dependency per opportunity is expected. Selection is from the register by reference, never typed.
- AC-524.2 Milestones are captured as `Milestone` records with a name, a target horizon and the opportunity they belong to.
- AC-524.3 T-shirt size is set from the configured scale, with the scale's effort, duration and risk descriptions visible while choosing.
- AC-524.4 Owners are assigned to items in a full-room pass at the end of the activity, writing `owner_stakeholder_ref`.
- AC-524.5 The system MUST detect and warn on dependency cycles at the moment of creation, and MUST warn where a dependency contradicts the current wave sequencing (an opportunity in wave 1 blocked by one in wave 3).

**FR-525 — Activity 4, roadmap build hand-off.** The system MUST support a facilitated roadmap-placement activity that positions opportunities and initiatives on a timeline using priority, urgency, dependencies, milestones and effort, and MUST persist the result as draft `RoadmapItem` records against `Wave` and `RoadmapScenario` for M5 to refine.
- AC-525.1 The activity MUST show, per placement, which of the six declared sequencing inputs is driving it, and MUST distinguish the four the engagement treats as in-focus (priority, dependencies, t-shirt sizing, business value) from the two it defers (resource constraints, cost). The reference session made this split explicit on a slide, marking four inputs as the focus of the day and two as refine-later, and the product must carry the same distinction so a placement made without cost or capacity data is not later mistaken for a costed commitment.
- AC-525.2 Draft placements are marked provisional until the cost and capacity module has run.

**FR-526 — Live-facilitation performance and resilience.** Workshop mode MUST operate at facilitation speed and MUST NOT lose captured client judgement.
- AC-526.1 Card movements and urgency selections MUST persist within 1 second and MUST be visible to the facilitator console within 2 seconds.
- AC-526.2 The system MUST support at least 8 concurrent groups and 40 concurrent participants per session.
- AC-526.3 A participant losing connectivity MUST retain local state and reconcile on reconnect without losing moves. The facilitator console MUST show per-group connection state.
- AC-526.4 The facilitator MUST be able to enter or correct a group's selections on the group's behalf, since a room can always fall back to paper, and such entries are marked `captured_by_facilitator`.
- AC-526.5 Session state MUST be exportable at any point during the session, so a technical failure never costs a 50 minute activity.

##### Change control

**FR-527 — Change log against issued deliverable versions.** Any change to a score, a derived value, a band, a quadrant, a rank, a taxonomy assignment or a register membership after a deliverable has been issued MUST be visible as a delta against that issued version.
- AC-527.1 Issuing a `Deliverable` snapshots the full register state, the `ScoringModel` version, the derived values and the calibration state, under a version label and a timestamp.
- AC-527.2 The change log view takes an issued version as a baseline and lists, field by field: the entity, the field, the value then, the value now, who changed it, when, why, and whether the change originated from an accepted `AISuggestion` or a workshop resolution.
- AC-527.3 The log MUST summarize at portfolio level as well as row level: how many opportunities changed band, how many changed quadrant, how many entered or left the register, how the theme counts and shares moved, and how the mean score per dimension moved.
- AC-527.4 A client-facing change summary MUST be generatable from the log, because the reference engagement's post-workshop recap email committed in writing that rankings and scoring on the issued deck would shift, that the opportunity inventory was still being cleaned up, that duplicates were still being removed, that foundational and dependent items were still being separated, and that workshop notes were still being incorporated. That promise is a product feature, not an apology: the next issued version must be able to show exactly what moved and why.
- AC-527.5 Any client-facing artefact generated from a register that has changed since the last issue MUST carry a draft marker until re-issued, matching the reference deck's persistent first-draft banner.

**FR-528 — Review comments and open items.** Every register record MUST support threaded comments addressed to a named consultant, with an open or resolved state, a resolution note and an optional linked action.
- AC-528.1 Reaching `Ready to Review` requires zero open comments on the record.
- AC-528.2 Comments that propose a score change MUST offer a one-click path into the scoring interface, so the change carries history. The reference workbook holds several such unresolved questions on rows whose status column claimed the row was updated, including a question about whether a particular opportunity should score higher on financial impact and a question about whether one opportunity duplicated another.
- AC-528.3 The open-items list is a working view across the register, filterable by assignee and age.

**FR-529 — Register integrity report.** The system MUST provide an integrity report that runs on demand and before any deliverable issue, and MUST list every violation of the following, refusing to issue while any unwaived violation stands.

| Check | Rule |
|---|---|
| Orphans | No opportunity without an initiative; no initiative without a theme |
| Enum integrity | No enum field holding a value outside its configured set |
| Identifier integrity | No duplicate identifier; no record whose identity depends on free text |
| Score completeness | Every opportunity in a client-facing view fully scored, or explicitly excluded |
| Evidence completeness | Every score of 5 carries a rationale; financial and risk 5s carry evidence; alignment 4s and 5s cite objectives |
| Derived integrity | Every derived value recomputed under the active `ScoringModel` version |
| Label integrity | No duplicate or near-duplicate labels in any value set; no formatting or chart rule referencing a retired label |
| Count reconciliation | Register count, chart plotted count and summary denominators agree, or differences are declared with scope |
| Duplicate resolution | No unresolved duplicate candidates above the similarity threshold |
| Workshop reconciliation | No unresolved material disagreements from the current session |
| Calibration | No unacknowledged drift flags from FR-518 |
| Foreign content | No artefact in the deliverable set that belongs to another engagement. The reference working deck carried a block of another client's slides inside it, and the product must scope every asset to its engagement and check that scope on export |

**FR-530 — AI prioritization assist.** The system MUST expose the three prioritization AI capabilities in 6.4.6 as user-invoked actions producing `AISuggestion` records under propose → review → commit. An AI-proposed score never becomes an `OpportunityScore` without a consultant accepting or editing it, and an accepted score records the suggestion id so the acceptance rate and the edit distance per capability are measurable.

#### 6.4.6 AI capabilities invoked

| Capability | Purpose in M4 | What M4 hands it | What M4 expects back |
|---|---|---|---|
| AI-12 Duplicate consolidation | Find opportunities that describe the same work, across segments and across origins | The full register with names, recommended actions, capability areas, linked findings and linked maturity gaps | Ranked candidate pairs with a similarity score, the fields that drove the match, a proposed surviving record and a proposed merged field set, or a statement of the distinction if the pair should stay separate |
| AI-13 Score proposal with evidence per dimension | Propose a score per dimension with the anchor it matches and the evidence behind it | The opportunity with its recommended action and so-what; linked findings and their evidence; linked maturity gaps; charter objectives; benchmarks; the dimension rubric with anchors and calibration examples | Per dimension: a proposed integer score, the `anchor_ref` matched, a rationale in the anchor's own terms, the `EvidenceRef` list relied on, and a confidence band; plus an explicit abstention where the evidence does not support a score |
| AI-14 Dependency inference | Propose the dependency graph rather than have a room draw it from memory | The register, architecture evidence, in-flight initiative inventory, maturity assessments, t-shirt sizes and wave assignments | Proposed `Dependency` records with type and rationale, cycle warnings, and a list of sequencing conflicts where a proposed dependency contradicts current wave placement |

#### 6.4.7 Exit criteria

| Exit criterion | Rule |
|---|---|
| Taxonomy complete | 100 percent of opportunities have an initiative; 100 percent of initiatives have a theme and a wave; every initiative has a description paragraph |
| Identifiers | Every opportunity has one immutable identifier; zero identity-by-text records; any inherited codes stored as aliases |
| Scoring complete | Every opportunity in scope fully scored under one active `ScoringModel` version, or explicitly excluded with a reason |
| Rubric discipline | Every score references an anchor row; zero prose-valued score fields anywhere |
| Evidence discipline | FR-508 thresholds met across the register |
| Derivation integrity | Weighted score, band, business value, urgency and quadrant all derived and current; zero typed derived values |
| Calibration acknowledged | Distribution reviewed, drift flags resolved or acknowledged, calibration state recorded with the issued version |
| Duplicates resolved | Zero unresolved duplicate candidates above threshold; every kept-both pair carries a stated distinction |
| Portfolio summary reconciles | Theme counts and shares reconcile to the register; one canonical denominator declared |
| Quadrant sanity | Empty quadrants explained; unreachable-label warnings acknowledged |
| Workshop captured | Client ranks and urgency assignments stored against the session; ranks unique within the session |
| Reconciliation complete | Every material client-versus-calculated disagreement resolved with one of the three outcomes and a `Decision` record |
| Dependencies mapped | Every `Critical` and `High` band opportunity has its dependencies either recorded or explicitly stated as none; zero unacknowledged cycles |
| Change control armed | An issued baseline exists; the change log renders deltas against it; the client-facing change summary generates |
| Integrity report clean | FR-529 reports zero unwaived violations |

### 6.5 M5 Roadmap Sequencing and Scenarios (Week 5) — FR-600 to FR-699

#### 6.5.1 Purpose

M5 turns a scored backlog into a defensible sequence. It takes the prioritized Initiative and Opportunity set produced upstream and answers four questions: what runs when, what must precede what, what cannot physically fit, and what the alternative sequences would look like. It is the module where a consultant stops arguing about scores and starts arguing about calendars.

In the reference engagement this work happened on a Miro board across two facilitated activities and then landed in a spreadsheet column and a set of hand-built PowerPoint timelines. The sequence position itself survived as a single integer per initiative in a hidden taxonomy sheet (`Sequence` = 1..4, one value per theme). Dependencies were captured as free selections from a dropdown on a workshop card and were never modelled as edges anywhere. Nothing checked whether the resulting sequence was possible. M5 exists to make sequence a computed, checked, versioned object rather than a number typed into a hidden column.

#### 6.5.2 Methodology phase served

Week 5 — V1 Technology Roadmap. Core objective: turn the diagnosis into the first tangible roadmap for technology leadership. Key Activities served in full: sequence initiatives; group into workstreams; establish waves; define target outcomes; identify major dependencies and decisions. Outputs owned by this module: initiatives, sequencing, dependencies, timing, owners, expected outcomes, major assumptions.

#### 6.5.3 Inputs consumed

| Methodology Inputs column (Week 5) | Concrete input in this product | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| Current-state findings | `Finding`, `MaturityAssessment`, `MaturityFocusArea` gap values | M3 |
| Prioritized initiatives | `Initiative`, `Opportunity`, `OpportunityScore` (weighted score, priority band, quadrant), client-assigned top-priority rank | M4 |
| Constraints | `CapacityProfile` (may be empty at Week 5), in-flight program load, stated blackout periods, fiscal calendar | M6 when available, otherwise consultant-entered |
| Dependencies | `Dependency` edges asserted in workshop, inferred by AI-16, or derived from architecture documents | M2 workshop capture, AI, `SourceDocument` |
| Strategic objectives | `Charter` goals and guiding principles, `Theme` definitions | M1 |
| Existing commitments | Initiatives flagged `in_flight = true` with committed dates and funded status | M2 initiative inventory |

Two of the six declared sequencing inputs (see FR-600) are expected to be absent or thin in Week 5. The module MUST function without them.

#### 6.5.4 Screens and views

| Screen | Primary job | Key affordances |
|---|---|---|
| Sequencing Inputs board | Show, per initiative, the six sequencing inputs and their readiness state | Inline edit, missing-value badges, "decided now" versus "refine later" grouping |
| Wave Designer | Define and order the wave set for a scenario | Add/reorder/rename waves, set dates or relative quarter offsets, set capacity envelope and target outcome |
| Workstream Board | Assign initiatives to workstreams and see workstream load | Owner, capacity envelope, target outcomes, load bar per wave |
| Dependency Graph | See and edit the dependency network | Typed edges, filter by wave/theme/workstream, cycle highlight, conflict overlay |
| Feasibility Panel | List every infeasibility with its minimum resolution | Severity sort, jump-to-fix, dismiss with reason |
| Sequence Alternatives | Compare generated candidate sequences side by side | Objective selector, per-candidate metrics table, "adopt as scenario" |
| Roadmap Gantt | The V1 roadmap itself | Swimlanes by wave and workstream, dependency arrows, owners, milestones, decision diamonds |
| Scenario Manager | Create, clone, status, and diff scenarios | Status lifecycle, premise text, diff against any other scenario |
| Rationale Card | Explain why one initiative sits where it sits | Stored artifact, versioned, exportable |
| Assumption Register | Hold the roadmap's major assumptions | Owner, validation state, impact if wrong, links to affected initiatives |

```mermaid
erDiagram
  RoadmapScenario ||--o{ RoadmapItem : contains
  RoadmapScenario ||--o{ Wave : defines
  RoadmapScenario ||--o{ Assumption : registers
  Wave ||--o{ RoadmapItem : holds
  Workstream ||--o{ RoadmapItem : groups
  Theme ||--o{ Initiative : groups
  Initiative ||--o{ RoadmapItem : scheduled_as
  Initiative ||--o{ Opportunity : contains
  Initiative ||--o{ Dependency : source_of
  Initiative ||--o{ Milestone : has
  Initiative ||--o{ PrioritizationRationale : explained_by
  Initiative ||--o{ Decision : requires
  OpportunityScore ||--|| Opportunity : scores
```

#### 6.5.5 The six sequencing inputs
