**FR-600 — Six sequencing inputs as first-class fields.** The system MUST model all six declared sequencing inputs as named, typed, individually addressable fields rather than as prose. The six are Priority, Dependencies, T-shirt sizing, Business Value, Resource constraints, and Cost.

| Input | Field | Type | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Priority | `Initiative.priority_band`, `Initiative.rolled_score` | enum (Critical, High, Medium, Lower) and decimal 0.00-5.00 | Rolled up from member `OpportunityScore` records (M4) |
| Dependencies | `Dependency[]` | typed edge set | This module, FR-630 |
| T-shirt sizing | `Initiative.tshirt_size`, `Initiative.size_points` | enum (XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL) and integer | Workshop Activity 3, or AI proposal |
| Business Value | `Initiative.business_value` | decimal 1.00-5.00 | Mean of member opportunities' Business Value X axis, `(alignment + financial) / 2` |
| Resource constraints | `ResourceDemand[]`, `CapacityProfile[]` | FTE by role by month | M6 |
| Cost | `CostEstimate` | three-point range by category | M6 |

- AC-600.1 Each of the six MUST expose a `readiness` value of `decided`, `provisional`, or `absent`.
- AC-600.2 The Sequencing Inputs board MUST group the first four under "Decided now" and the last two under "Refine later", matching the engagement's own split of the same six inputs.
- AC-600.3 No sequencing view may hide the readiness state of an input it uses in a calculation.

**FR-601 — Sequence without cost or capacity.** The system MUST allow a `RoadmapScenario` to be created, populated, checked, exported, and marked `candidate` while `CostEstimate` and `CapacityProfile` records are entirely absent.

- AC-601.1 Checks that require cost or capacity MUST return status `not_evaluable` with the named missing input, never a false pass and never a hard error.
- AC-601.2 Every exported artifact from a scenario in this state MUST carry the marker `Cost and capacity not yet modelled` on the face of the artifact, not in a footnote only.
- AC-601.3 A scenario MUST NOT be promoted to `recommended` while any of the six inputs is `absent` for an initiative placed in the first wave.

**FR-602 — Late-arriving input reconciliation.** When cost or capacity data first arrives, or materially changes, the system MUST produce a `LateInputImpact` report against every scenario that was built without it.

- AC-602.1 The report MUST list, per initiative: the previously assumed value (or "none"), the arrived value, and the resulting change to placement feasibility.
- AC-602.2 The report MUST separately list checks whose status changed from `not_evaluable` to `fail`.
- AC-602.3 The report MUST propose a minimum resequencing (via AI-15) as an `AISuggestion` against the scenario, and MUST NOT alter the scenario until a consultant accepts it.
- AC-602.4 "Materially changes" defaults to a shift in expected cost greater than 20 percent or a change in peak role utilisation greater than 0.10, both configurable per engagement.

**FR-603 — Business Value derivation is explicit and stored.** The system MUST store `Initiative.business_value` as a computed field with its formula recorded, derived as the size-weighted mean of member `Opportunity` Business Value values, where each opportunity's Business Value is `(strategic_alignment_score + financial_impact_score) / 2`.

- AC-603.1 A consultant MAY override the rolled value; the override MUST persist the calculated value alongside it and require a reason.
- AC-603.2 Overrides MUST appear in the initiative's `PrioritizationRationale` (FR-690).

**FR-604 — T-shirt ladder and size points.** The system MUST ship the six-rung size ladder observed in the reference engagement as configuration, mapping each size to a duration band, a risk descriptor, and an integer size-point weight used by capacity envelopes and objective functions.

| Size | Effort descriptor | Duration band | Default size points |
|---|---|---|---|
| XS | Single team, well-defined | under 3 months | 1 |
| S | 1-2 teams, some integration | 3-6 months | 2 |
| M | Multi-team, moderate legacy | 6-12 months | 3 |
| L | Cross-functional, significant legacy | 12-24 months | 5 |
| XL | Enterprise-wide, deep legacy | 2-3 years | 8 |
| XXL | Multi-year transformation program | 3-5 or more years | 13 |

- AC-604.1 Duration bands and descriptors are observed in the reference engagement and MUST be the shipped defaults. ASSUMPTION: the size-point weights are invented for this product; they are configuration and MUST be editable per engagement.
- AC-604.2 An unsized initiative MUST render as `size = unknown` and MUST NOT be silently treated as XS or M. This directly addresses the reference engagement's declared-but-never-populated span column, where an empty sizing field was indistinguishable from a deliberate omission.

**FR-605 — Provenance on every sequencing input value.** Each of the six input values per initiative MUST carry `set_by` (user id or `ai`), `set_at`, `method` (workshop_decision, calculated, ai_proposed_accepted, consultant_override), and, where the value came from a workshop, the workshop session identifier.

#### 6.5.6 Waves and horizons

**FR-610 — Waves are a configurable ordered set.** A `RoadmapScenario` MUST own an ordered list of `Wave` records. The system MUST NOT hard-code the number of waves.

**FR-611 — Wave fields.** Each `Wave` MUST carry: `id`, `scenario_id`, `ordinal` (1-based), `label`, `timing_mode` (`absolute` or `relative`), `start_date` and `end_date` when absolute, `start_quarter_offset` and `duration_quarters` when relative, `target_outcome_statement` (required, 1-400 chars), `capacity_envelope` (FR-615), and `theme_id` when theme-aligned.

- AC-611.1 A wave with `timing_mode = relative` MUST resolve to absolute dates against the engagement's fiscal calendar anchor date, and both the relative definition and the resolved dates MUST be visible.
- AC-611.2 Wave ordinals MUST be contiguous with no gaps; reordering MUST renumber atomically.
- AC-611.3 `target_outcome_statement` MUST be non-empty before a scenario can leave `draft`, because "define target outcomes" is a named Week 5 activity and an unstated wave outcome makes the wave unreviewable.

**FR-612 — Theme-aligned waves.** The system MUST support waves bound one-to-one to `Theme` records, reproducing the reference engagement's structure where the canonical taxonomy assigned each of its four themes a single sequence position 1 through 4 (position 1 Stabilize the Core, position 2 Assess and Protect Current Investments, position 3 Grow the Top Line, position 4 Build the Intelligent Enterprise).

- AC-612.1 When a wave is theme-aligned, adding an initiative from a different theme to that wave MUST raise a `theme_wave_mismatch` warning naming both the initiative's theme and the wave's theme, and MUST be permitted after the consultant supplies a reason.
- AC-612.2 Theme-aligned waves are appropriate when the themes were constructed to encode sequencing intent, which is how they were used in the reference engagement, where the theme itself signalled "stabilize first, intelligence last". Guidance text to this effect MUST appear in the Wave Designer.

**FR-613 — Free-form waves.** The system MUST support waves with no theme binding, labelled and dated by the consultant.

- AC-613.1 Free-form waves are appropriate once initiatives from several themes must run concurrently, which happens as soon as dependency and capacity reality is applied. The Wave Designer MUST offer conversion from theme-aligned to free-form waves without losing initiative placements.
- AC-613.2 A scenario MUST NOT mix theme-aligned and free-form waves silently; mixing is allowed but the Wave Designer MUST label each wave's mode.

**FR-614 — One canonical horizon label set.** Horizon and wave labels MUST be defined once per engagement in a single label registry, with optional display aliases recorded against the canonical label.

- AC-614.1 The registry MUST reject two labels that differ only by case or whitespace.
- AC-614.2 Retired labels MUST be stored as aliases of their replacement, and every view MUST render the canonical label.
- AC-614.3 This requirement exists because the reference engagement carried three different names for the same third horizon bucket ("Sequence Later", "Defer", "Future Horizon") across a workbook formula, a workshop deck, and a client email, and carried conditional formatting still keyed to retired theme names. The product MUST make that class of drift impossible rather than detectable.

**FR-615 — Wave capacity envelope.** Each `Wave` MUST carry a `capacity_envelope` object: `max_size_points` (integer, optional), `max_large_initiatives` (integer, optional, where "large" means L, XL, or XXL), `max_concurrent_initiatives` (integer, optional), and `basis` (free text plus `EvidenceRef[]`).

- AC-615.1 An envelope with all limits null MUST render as "no envelope stated" and MUST cause capacity checks to return `not_evaluable`, not pass.
- AC-615.2 The envelope MUST be settable before any `CapacityProfile` exists, since the workshop question the reference engagement actually asked was how many additional programs the team could absorb in a year.

**FR-616 — Wave load readout.** For each wave the system MUST display total size points, count by size, count of in-flight commitments, and utilisation against each stated envelope limit as a ratio to two decimals.

#### 6.5.7 Workstreams

ASSUMPTION: `Workstream` is not in the shared entity list but the methodology's Week 5 Key Activities require grouping into workstreams, and the reference engagement's follow-on execution deck grouped delivery into named squads (for example a channel squad, a marketing-technology squad, and a data-dependencies squad under a single initiative). This module therefore adds `Workstream` as a first-class entity.

**FR-620 — Workstream entity.** The system MUST provide `Workstream` with: `id`, `engagement_id`, `name`, `owner_stakeholder_id`, `mission_statement`, `target_outcomes[]` (each with a text statement and an optional `KPI` reference), `capacity_envelope` (same shape as FR-615), and `status` (proposed, active, retired).

**FR-621 — One theme and one workstream per initiative.** Each `Initiative` MUST carry exactly one `theme_id` and at most one `workstream_id`. The two groupings MUST be independent: theme answers "what kind of investment is this", workstream answers "which standing team delivers it".

- AC-621.1 An initiative with no workstream MUST be listed in an "unassigned delivery ownership" view.
- AC-621.2 Reassigning a workstream MUST NOT change the theme, and reassigning a theme MUST NOT change the workstream.
- AC-621.3 Where an initiative genuinely spans two delivery teams, the supported pattern is to split the initiative, not to add a second workstream. The system MUST offer a split action that carries opportunities, scores, and dependencies to the chosen child.

**FR-622 — Workstream rollups.** For each workstream the system MUST compute and display, per wave: size points, initiative count by priority band, count of initiatives whose dependencies cross into another workstream, and utilisation against the workstream capacity envelope.

**FR-623 — Theme versus workstream divergence report.** The system MUST provide a matrix of `Theme` by `Workstream` with initiative counts, and MUST flag any workstream carrying initiatives from three or more themes as a delivery-focus risk, with the threshold configurable.

#### 6.5.8 The dependency model

**FR-630 — Typed dependency edges.** The system MUST model dependencies as directed `Dependency` records with `type` drawn from exactly this set: `finish_to_start`, `start_to_start`, `enables`, `shares_resource`, `mutually_exclusive`, `supersedes`.

| Type | Semantics enforced by checks | Directionality |
|---|---|---|
| `finish_to_start` | Target MUST NOT start before source completes | directed, hard |
| `start_to_start` | Target MUST NOT start before source starts | directed, hard |
| `enables` | Target's value case depends on source; ordering preferred but not mandatory | directed, soft |
| `shares_resource` | Both draw on the same named role or team; concurrency inflates demand | undirected in effect, soft |
| `mutually_exclusive` | At most one of the pair may be scheduled in any scenario | undirected, hard |
| `supersedes` | Source replaces target; target MUST be excluded or descoped if source is scheduled | directed, hard |

- AC-630.1 Hard types MUST drive feasibility failures. Soft types MUST drive warnings.
- AC-630.2 `shares_resource` MUST name the shared role or team in `shared_resource_ref`.

**FR-631 — Endpoints.** A `Dependency` MUST support endpoints at both `Initiative` and `Opportunity` level, recorded as `source_entity` and `target_entity` with values `initiative` or `opportunity` plus ids.

- AC-631.1 An opportunity-level dependency MUST roll up to an implied initiative-level constraint when the two opportunities sit in different initiatives, and the rollup MUST be labelled `derived_from_opportunity_edge` rather than duplicated as a separate consultant-authored edge.
- AC-631.2 Cross-level edges (initiative to opportunity) MUST be permitted and MUST be evaluated at initiative granularity for feasibility.

**FR-632 — Rationale and confidence.** Every `Dependency` MUST carry `rationale` (required, 1-600 chars, stating what specifically breaks if the order is violated), `confidence` (0.00-1.00), and `confidence_band` (low, medium, high).

- AC-632.1 An edge with no rationale MUST NOT be savable.
- AC-632.2 Edges with `confidence_band = low` MUST render dashed in the graph and MUST be listed separately in the dependency map export.

**FR-633 — Source provenance.** Every `Dependency` MUST carry `source` from: `workshop_assertion`, `ai_inferred`, `architecture_derived`, `client_document`.

| Source | Meaning | Required companion data |
|---|---|---|
| `workshop_assertion` | A person in the room said so | session id, asserting stakeholder id, activity reference |
| `ai_inferred` | Proposed by AI-16 and accepted by a consultant | originating `AISuggestion.id`, model_version, prompt_version |
| `architecture_derived` | Read from an integration or architecture artifact | `EvidenceRef` with document locator |
| `client_document` | Stated in a client plan, contract, or program schedule | `EvidenceRef` with document locator |

- AC-633.1 ASSUMPTION: `client_document` is added by this product; the brief names the first three. It is included because the reference engagement's dependency reasoning cited funded program schedules and vendor go-live dates that exist only in client documents.
- AC-633.2 A `workshop_assertion` edge MUST be visually distinguishable from an `ai_inferred` edge in every view, because these have different standing in a client conversation.
- AC-633.3 Filtering the graph to `workshop_assertion` only MUST be a one-click view, so a consultant can show a client exactly the dependency set the client's own people asserted.

**FR-634 — AI-proposed edges follow propose, review, commit.** A dependency inferred by AI-16 MUST enter the system as an `AISuggestion` with `target_entity = Dependency`. It MUST NOT appear in the graph, in checks, or in any export until accepted or edited by a consultant.

**FR-635 — Multi-select capture and deduplication.** The system MUST support capturing several dependencies for one initiative in a single interaction, mirroring the workshop mechanic where a card's dependency dropdown allowed more than one selection.

- AC-635.1 On save the system MUST detect an existing edge with the same source, target, and type and MUST offer merge rather than creating a duplicate.
- AC-635.2 Reverse duplicates (A finish_to_start B and B finish_to_start A) MUST be reported as a two-node cycle by FR-641, not silently stored as two unrelated facts.

**FR-636 — Exclusive and superseding semantics.** For `mutually_exclusive`, the system MUST prevent both endpoints from holding a `RoadmapItem` in the same scenario and MUST require the consultant to record which endpoint was chosen and why. For `supersedes`, scheduling the source MUST require an explicit disposition on the target: `excluded`, `descoped`, or `retained_with_reason`.

**FR-637 — Dependency evidence.** Every `Dependency` MUST support `evidence: EvidenceRef[]`. Edges sourced from `architecture_derived` or `client_document` MUST have at least one `EvidenceRef`.

#### 6.5.9 Graph, cycles and conflicts

**FR-640 — Dependency graph view.** The system MUST render the dependency network as a directed graph with nodes coloured by wave, node size by size points, edge style by type, and edge opacity by confidence.

- AC-640.1 The view MUST filter by theme, workstream, wave, dependency type, source, and confidence band.
- AC-640.2 Selecting a node MUST show its inbound and outbound edges with rationale text inline.
- AC-640.3 The view MUST handle at least 60 initiatives and 400 edges without pagination, sized against the reference engagement's 17 initiatives and 55 opportunities with headroom.

**FR-641 — Cycle detector.** The system MUST detect all cycles among hard-type edges and MUST list each cycle as an ordered node path.

- AC-641.1 Detection MUST run on every edge create, edge type change, and scenario open, and MUST complete in under two seconds for the FR-640.3 graph size.
- AC-641.2 Each cycle MUST be reported with the specific edges forming it and, for each edge, its source and confidence, so the consultant can see which link is weakest.
- AC-641.3 The system MUST propose the minimum edge removal or type downgrade that breaks the cycle, defined as the lowest-confidence hard edge in the cycle, presented as a suggestion and not applied automatically.

**FR-642 — Conflict detector with minimum resolution.** For a given scenario the system MUST list every dependency violated by the current wave assignment. Each entry MUST state the specific violation and the minimum change that resolves it.

- AC-642.1 A violation entry MUST contain: `dependency_id`, `type`, source initiative name and wave, target initiative name and wave, a violation sentence naming the wave ordinals, and a `minimum_resolution` object.
- AC-642.2 `minimum_resolution` MUST be one of: `move_target_to_wave` with the smallest wave ordinal that satisfies the edge, `move_source_to_wave` with the largest ordinal that still satisfies the edge, `downgrade_edge_type` with the type that would make the current placement legal, or `delete_edge`. Where two options tie on disruption, the system MUST present both.
- AC-642.3 "Disruption" for ranking resolutions is defined as the number of initiatives whose wave would change, then total size points moved, then count of dependent edges affected.
- AC-642.4 Violations MUST be persisted as `ConflictFinding` records with `first_detected_at`, `resolved_at`, and `resolution_action`, so a scenario carries its conflict history rather than a transient screen state.

**FR-643 — Conflict re-evaluation.** The conflict and cycle checks MUST re-run on any change to wave membership, wave dates, dependency set, or size, and the scenario header MUST show a check freshness timestamp and a stale indicator.

**FR-644 — Dependency map export.** The system MUST export the dependency map as an `Exhibit` with three layers selectable: all edges, hard edges only, and workshop-asserted edges only. The export MUST include a legend for type, source, and confidence.

#### 6.5.10 Feasibility checks

**FR-650 — Prerequisite ordering check.** The system MUST flag every initiative scheduled to start before a hard prerequisite completes, or in the same wave where the prerequisite consumes the full wave duration.

- AC-650.1 Severity `blocker`. Message MUST name both initiatives, both waves, and the overlap in months.

**FR-651 — Wave size overload check.** The system MUST flag any wave carrying more large-size initiatives (L, XL, XXL) than its `capacity_envelope.max_large_initiatives`, or total size points above `max_size_points`, or concurrent count above `max_concurrent_initiatives`.

- AC-651.1 Severity `serious`. Message MUST state the limit, the actual value, the excess, and the smallest set of initiatives whose removal clears the limit.
- AC-651.2 When the envelope is unset the check MUST return `not_evaluable` naming the missing envelope.

**FR-652 — Duration overrun check.** The system MUST flag any initiative whose duration, taken from `Initiative.duration_months` or from the t-shirt duration band lower bound when duration is unset, exceeds the span of its assigned wave.

- AC-652.1 Severity `serious`. Message MUST state initiative duration, wave span, and the overrun in months.
- AC-652.2 The system MUST offer three resolutions: extend the wave, move to a longer wave, or split the initiative across waves with an explicit phase boundary.

**FR-653 — Unowned critical path check.** The system MUST compute the critical path over hard edges using each initiative's duration, and MUST flag any initiative on that path with no `owner_stakeholder_id`.

- AC-653.1 Severity `blocker`. The reference engagement's Activity 3 closed with the room assigning owners to items, so an unowned critical-path initiative represents an unfinished workshop rather than a data-entry gap.
- AC-653.2 The critical path MUST be displayed on the Gantt as a distinct visual track.

**FR-654 — Check registry.** All feasibility, cycle, and conflict checks MUST be defined in a single registry with `check_id`, `title`, `severity` (blocker, serious, watch), `trigger` (on_change, on_demand, on_export), `evaluable_when` (the inputs required), and `message_template`.

- AC-654.1 Check results MUST persist per scenario with a run timestamp, and a scenario MUST expose a single pass/fail summary counting blockers and serious items.
- AC-654.2 A consultant MAY dismiss a check result with a mandatory reason; dismissals MUST be recorded as `AuditEvent` and MUST reappear if the underlying data changes.

#### 6.5.11 Sequencing alternatives

**FR-660 — Generate at least three candidate sequences.** On request the system MUST generate at least three candidate sequences for the current initiative set under different stated optimisation objectives, and MUST present them side by side with the consultant's working scenario as a fourth column.

- AC-660.1 Every candidate MUST respect hard dependency edges and `mutually_exclusive` constraints; a candidate that cannot satisfy them MUST be returned with the unsatisfiable constraint named rather than silently violating it.
- AC-660.2 Every candidate MUST state its objective, its objective value, and the constraints it treated as binding.
- AC-660.3 Where cost or capacity is absent, candidates MUST use size points as the proxy load measure and MUST say so.

**FR-661 — Objective: fastest value.** Maximise `sum over initiatives of ( business_value_i * size_points_i * decay^(wave_ordinal_i - 1) )` with `decay` default 0.7 and configurable, subject to hard dependency and envelope constraints.

- AC-661.1 The weighting by size points makes a large high-value initiative count more than a small one; the decay pulls value earlier. Both factors MUST be shown in the candidate's explanation.

**FR-662 — Objective: lowest risk.** Minimise `sum over initiatives of ( risk_if_deferred_i * (wave_ordinal_i - 1) )`, where `risk_if_deferred_i` is the initiative's rolled Risk if Deferred score on the 1-5 scale, which is also the Urgency axis of the priority bubble chart.

- AC-662.1 Initiatives whose priority band is `Critical` MUST be constrained to wave 1 in this candidate, matching the engagement's own band definition that Critical items cannot be deferred.

**FR-663 — Objective: lowest peak resource demand.** Minimise `max over (role, month) of ( demand_fte(role, month) / available_fte(role, month) )` when `CapacityProfile` exists. When it does not, minimise `max over waves of ( total_size_points(wave) )`, which levels load without capacity data.

- AC-663.1 The candidate MUST report which measure was used and the resulting peak value.
- AC-663.2 Ties MUST be broken by the fastest-value objective.

**FR-664 — Objective: foundation-first.** Maximise `sum over initiatives of ( enables_outdegree_i * (max_wave_ordinal - wave_ordinal_i + 1) )`, where `enables_outdegree_i` counts outbound `enables` and `finish_to_start` edges, subject to hard constraints.

- AC-664.1 This objective deliberately front-loads initiatives that unblock others even when their own scores are moderate. The candidate explanation MUST name the top five unblocking initiatives and their outdegree.

**FR-665 — Side-by-side comparison.** The comparison view MUST show, per candidate: objective and objective value, initiative count and size points per wave, count of dependency violations (must be zero for hard edges), peak load measure, count of Critical-band initiatives outside wave 1, earliest wave containing each theme, and the list of initiatives whose wave differs from the working scenario.

**FR-666 — Generated sequences are proposals.** Each candidate MUST be delivered as an `AISuggestion` from AI-15 with `target_entity = RoadmapScenario`, containing the full proposed wave assignment as payload, plus rationale and confidence.

- AC-666.1 Adopting a candidate MUST create a new `RoadmapScenario` cloned from the working scenario with the proposed placements applied, `premise` pre-filled with the objective statement, and lineage recorded to the originating `AISuggestion`.
- AC-666.2 A consultant MUST be able to accept a candidate partially, applying the placement changes for a selected subset of initiatives; the resulting `AISuggestion.status` MUST be `edited` with `edit_diff` recording exactly which placements were and were not taken.
- AC-666.3 The system MUST NOT write a generated placement to a canonical `RoadmapItem` without that acceptance step.

#### 6.5.12 RoadmapScenario as a versioned object

**FR-670 — RoadmapScenario fields.** `RoadmapScenario` MUST carry: `id`, `engagement_id`, `name` (unique per engagement), `version` (integer), `cloned_from_scenario_id`, `premise` (required, 1-1000 chars, stating the assumption set the scenario tests), `owner_user_id`, `status` (draft, candidate, recommended, superseded), `created_at`, `committed_at`, `wave_set`, `roadmap_items`, `assumption_ids`, and `check_summary`.

**FR-671 — Clone.** Cloning MUST copy waves, roadmap items, workstream assignments, dependency snapshot references, and the assumption register, and MUST set `cloned_from_scenario_id` and reset `status` to `draft`.

**FR-672 — Status lifecycle.** Status transitions MUST follow the state machine below, and each transition MUST write an `AuditEvent` with actor and timestamp.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> draft
  draft --> candidate : checks run, no unresolved blockers
  candidate --> recommended : consultant designates, one per engagement
  candidate --> draft : reopened for edit
  recommended --> superseded : another scenario recommended
  candidate --> superseded : abandoned with reason
  superseded --> [*]
```

- AC-672.1 At most one scenario per engagement MAY hold `recommended`; designating a new one MUST move the previous to `superseded` with a recorded reason.
- AC-672.2 Promotion to `candidate` MUST be blocked while any `blocker`-severity check is unresolved and undismissed.
- AC-672.3 A `recommended` or `superseded` scenario MUST be immutable; editing MUST require cloning.

**FR-673 — Diff against any other scenario.** The system MUST diff any two scenarios in the same engagement, regardless of lineage.

**FR-674 — Diff content.** A scenario diff MUST report at minimum:

| Diff section | Content |
|---|---|
| Wave moves | Every initiative whose wave ordinal differs, with from-wave, to-wave, and direction |
| Timing change | Per moved initiative, change in start month and end month in months; count of initiatives whose finish moves later than the roadmap's stated end |
| Membership | Initiatives present in one scenario and absent in the other, with disposition reason |
| Portfolio metrics | Size points per wave, count by priority band per wave, count of Critical items outside wave 1, peak load measure, number of unresolved blockers, number of hard-edge violations |
| Economics | When cost and value exist: expected cost by fiscal year, portfolio net value, simple payback month, discounted measure (see M6). When absent, the section MUST render as "not modelled" rather than zeros |
| Assumptions | Assumptions added, removed, or changed in validation state |

- AC-674.1 The diff MUST be exportable as an `Exhibit` for use in a client conversation.
- AC-674.2 Every number in the diff MUST be attributable to a scenario snapshot, not recomputed from current live data, so a diff shown to a client remains reproducible.

#### 6.5.13 The roadmap view

**FR-680 — Gantt-style roadmap.** The system MUST provide a timeline view of the active scenario with initiatives as bars positioned by start and end date, grouped into swimlanes.

- AC-680.1 Grouping MUST be switchable between wave, workstream, theme, and owner, and MUST support two-level grouping of wave over workstream.
- AC-680.2 Each bar MUST display initiative name, t-shirt size, priority band, and owner name, with the full rationale card reachable in one click.
- AC-680.3 Hard dependency edges MUST be drawn between bars; soft edges MUST be toggleable to reduce clutter.
- AC-680.4 Wave boundaries MUST be drawn with the wave's target outcome statement visible in the lane header.
- AC-680.5 Milestones MUST render as diamonds and decision points as a visually distinct marker with the decision deadline.
- AC-680.6 Bars whose placement violates a check MUST carry a severity marker linking to the Feasibility Panel entry.
- AC-680.7 Dragging a bar MUST re-run checks immediately and show any new violation before the change is saved.

Illustrative output, fictional content for a hypothetical client named ACME Distribution:

```mermaid
gantt
    title ACME Distribution V1 Technology Roadmap (illustrative, fictional)
    dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    axisFormat %b %Y
    section Wave 1 Stabilize the Core
    Core platform continuity (Owner A. Consultant, L)      :w1a, 2026-07-01, 180d
    Identity and access consolidation (Owner B. Director, M) :w1b, 2026-08-01, 150d
    Platform decision gate                                  :milestone, m1, 2026-10-15, 0d
    section Wave 2 Protect Current Investments
    Planning platform go-live readiness (Owner C. Lead, S)  :w2a, after w1a, 120d
    Portfolio governance stand-up (Owner D. PMO, M)         :w2b, 2027-01-05, 180d
    Architecture function stand-up (Owner E. Architect, M)  :w2c, after w1b, 210d
    section Wave 3 Grow the Top Line
    Commerce platform re-architecture (Owner F. Product, XL) :w3a, after w2a, 400d
    Store technology standardization (Owner G. Retail, L)    :w3b, 2027-04-01, 300d
    section Wave 4 Build the Intelligent Enterprise
    Product data consolidation (Owner H. Data, L)            :w4a, after w2c, 330d
    Data and AI governance (Owner J. Governance, M)          :w4b, after w4a, 210d
```

**FR-681 — Roadmap export.** The system MUST export the roadmap view as an `Exhibit` with the grouping, filters, and legend applied, and MUST stamp it with scenario name, version, and export timestamp.

#### 6.5.14 Milestones and decision points

**FR-685 — Milestone records.** `Milestone` MUST carry: `id`, `initiative_id` or `wave_id`, `title`, `type` (`enabling_action`, `go_live`, `gate`, `external_commitment`), `target_date`, `owner_stakeholder_id`, `status` (planned, at_risk, met, missed), `success_criteria` text, and `evidence: EvidenceRef[]`.

- AC-685.1 Milestone capture MUST be available in the same interaction as dependency and size capture, mirroring Activity 3, which asked each group to outline key milestones or actions needed to enable success alongside dependencies and t-shirt sizing.
- AC-685.2 A milestone whose target date falls outside its parent initiative's date span MUST be flagged.

**FR-686 — Decision points.** `Decision` records used at this stage MUST carry `id`, `title`, `question`, `decision_owner_stakeholder_id`, `required_by_date`, `options[]` with pros, cons and cost implication, `blocking_initiative_ids[]`, `status` (open, decided, deferred), and `decided_option_id` with `decided_at`.

- AC-686.1 An open `Decision` with `required_by_date` earlier than the start of any initiative it blocks MUST raise a `watch` check.
- AC-686.2 The system MUST produce a "decisions required" list ordered by `required_by_date`, showing what each decision blocks. The reference engagement's Week 5 equivalent surfaced several near-term decisions of exactly this shape, including a platform selection and a cloud direction question raised in workbook comments.

**FR-687 — Milestone and decision visibility.** Both MUST appear on the Gantt (FR-680.5), in the wave detail view, and in the scenario diff when their date or status differs between scenarios.

#### 6.5.15 Prioritization rationale as a stored artifact

**FR-690 — PrioritizationRationale is a record, not a screen.** For every initiative in a scenario the system MUST store a `PrioritizationRationale` record explaining its placement, versioned per scenario version.

ASSUMPTION: `PrioritizationRationale` is added to the entity set by this module. The methodology names "explain prioritization rationale" as a Week 5 AI enhancement and the reference engagement's recap email shows the explanation being carried into client communication, so the explanation must be durable and quotable rather than regenerated on view.

**FR-691 — Rationale content.** Each record MUST contain all of the following fields, each populated or explicitly marked absent:

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `weighted_score` | The rolled weighted score to two decimals and the three dimension scores that produced it |
| `priority_band` | Critical, High, Medium, or Lower, with the threshold that applied |
| `quadrant` | Act Now, Defend, Plan and Fund, or Sequence Later, with the Business Value and Urgency coordinates and the 3.5 threshold |
| `size` | T-shirt size, size points, and duration basis |
| `dependency_position` | Inbound hard prerequisites with their waves, outbound enables count, and whether the initiative is on the critical path |
| `wave_placement` | Assigned wave, and which constraint bound the placement (dependency, envelope, workshop decision, or objective) |
| `workshop_override` | Any client-assigned rank or workshop decision that moved the initiative away from its calculated placement, with the session reference |
| `narrative` | Two to five sentences, drafted by AI-17, stating in plain language why the initiative sits where it sits |
| `evidence` | `EvidenceRef[]` supporting the narrative |

- AC-691.1 The `narrative` MUST be produced through propose, review, commit as an `AISuggestion` from AI-17, and MUST show as unreviewed until accepted.
- AC-691.2 The record MUST be exportable directly into a deliverable, since this text is what appears in a client readout.

**FR-692 — Workshop override capture.** The system MUST support a client-assigned priority rank that coexists with the calculated score rather than replacing it.

- AC-692.1 `Initiative.client_assigned_rank` MUST be an optional positive integer, unique within its capture session, with `capture_session_id`, `captured_by`, and `captured_at`. In the reference engagement this was a client-assigned "Identified as Top Priority" rank running 1 to 19 that came off the workshop board and sat alongside the calculated weighted score in the same register.
- AC-692.2 When `client_assigned_rank` and `priority_band` disagree, defined as a rank in the top third paired with a band of Medium or Lower, or a rank absent for a Critical item, the system MUST raise a `watch` check and MUST require a reconciliation note on the rationale record.
- AC-692.3 Views MUST never merge the two into a single "priority" number.

**FR-693 — Rationale freshness.** A `PrioritizationRationale` MUST be marked stale when any input named in FR-691 changes, MUST display the stale marker wherever the narrative is shown, and MUST NOT be exported while stale without an explicit consultant acknowledgement recorded as an `AuditEvent`.

#### 6.5.16 Assumption register

**FR-695 — Assumption register per scenario.** Every `RoadmapScenario` MUST own an assumption register, because "major assumptions" is a named Week 5 output.

ASSUMPTION: `Assumption` is added to the entity set by this module.

**FR-696 — Assumption fields.** Each `Assumption` MUST carry: `id`, `scenario_id`, `statement` (1-500 chars), `category` (`capacity`, `cost`, `vendor`, `dependency`, `business_commitment`, `data_quality`, `organizational`), `affected_entity_refs[]`, `confidence_band`, `validation_status` (unvalidated, validating, validated, invalidated), `owner_stakeholder_id`, `validate_by_date`, `impact_if_wrong` (text plus a severity of blocker, serious or watch), and `evidence: EvidenceRef[]`.

**FR-697 — Assumption behaviour.** Assumptions MUST be surfaced wherever the thing they qualify is shown.

- AC-697.1 An initiative with an `invalidated` assumption of severity `blocker` MUST be flagged on the Gantt and in the Feasibility Panel.
- AC-697.2 Assumptions of category `cost` or `capacity` MUST be handed to M6 as the starting list of items to replace with modelled values, and M6 MUST report which ones it retired.
- AC-697.3 Every exported roadmap `Exhibit` and `Deliverable` MUST include the register filtered to severities `blocker` and `serious`.
- AC-697.4 Promotion of a scenario to `recommended` MUST require every `blocker`-severity assumption to be `validated` or explicitly accepted with a recorded reason.

#### 6.5.17 AI capabilities invoked

| Capability | Purpose in this module | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| AI-15 sequence alternative generation | Produce the candidate sequences of FR-660 to FR-664 under stated objectives | `AISuggestion` targeting `RoadmapScenario`, adopted via FR-666 |
| AI-16 dependency conflict and infeasibility detection | Propose `Dependency` edges from findings and architecture material, and narrate detected conflicts and infeasibilities in reviewable language | `AISuggestion` targeting `Dependency`, and annotations on `ConflictFinding` |
| AI-17 prioritization rationale narration | Draft the `narrative` field of `PrioritizationRationale` from the structured placement facts | `AISuggestion` targeting `PrioritizationRationale` |

Deterministic logic stays deterministic. Cycle detection, conflict detection with minimum resolution, and all four objective functions are computed code, not model output. AI-16's role is to propose candidate edges and to explain findings in prose; it does not decide whether a cycle exists.

#### 6.5.18 Exit criteria

M5 is complete for an engagement when all of the following hold for at least one `RoadmapScenario` in status `candidate` or `recommended`:

1. Every initiative in scope holds a wave assignment, an owner, a t-shirt size, and a `PrioritizationRationale` that is not stale.
2. Every wave carries a target outcome statement and either a capacity envelope or a recorded decision that no envelope has been stated.
3. Every initiative carries exactly one theme and at most one workstream, and the unassigned-delivery-ownership view is empty or explicitly accepted.
4. The dependency graph contains zero cycles among hard edges and zero unresolved hard-edge conflicts.
5. All `blocker`-severity feasibility checks are resolved or dismissed with a recorded reason.
6. At least three generated candidate sequences have been reviewed, with the disposition of each recorded.
7. A scenario diff exists between the recommended scenario and at least one alternative.
8. The assumption register holds at least the cost and capacity assumptions that M6 will test, each with an owner and a validate-by date.
9. The roadmap `Exhibit` exports without stale-data acknowledgements outstanding.

---

### 6.6 M6 Investment, Cost and Capacity Model (Weeks 6-8) — FR-700 to FR-799

#### 6.6.1 Purpose

M6 pressure-tests whether the V1 roadmap is financially and operationally realistic. It attaches cost to initiatives, demand to roles, value to outcomes, and then tries to break the roadmap on all three. Its most important output is not a number. It is a ranked list of the specific reasons the roadmap as sequenced cannot be delivered.

#### 6.6.2 Evidence gap, stated plainly

The reference engagement's artifacts contain no developed cost model, no capacity model, and no value model. What they do contain, and all they contain, on this subject is:

| Present in the reference engagement | Where | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| T-shirt sizing ladder XS to XXL with duration and risk bands | Workshop deck, Activity 3 | Relative effort only, no cost |
| A span field with values L, M, S meaning multi-year, single year, quarter | Opportunity register column and its scoring guide | Duration signal, populated in the client-share copy and left empty in the master |
| Cost and Resource Constraints declared as two of the six sequencing inputs | Workshop deck, sequencing-inputs slide | Explicitly parked under "Refine Later"; no values captured |
| Financial Impact scored 1 to 5 against a labelled rubric with weight 0.40 | Opportunity register scoring model | An ordinal impact judgement, not a currency amount |
| Cost as subject matter | Several opportunities, for example IT financial transparency, multi-year budgeting, labour capitalization | Opportunities about the client's cost management, not estimates of initiative cost |
| A commitment to build the value story later | Post-workshop recap, next step 4 | Named as future work |

Therefore this module is derived primarily from the methodology table's Weeks 6-8 Inputs, Key Activities, and Outputs columns. Section 6.6.14 lists every specific that is inferred rather than observed. Cost categories, the four scenario levers, three-point ranges, missing-cost identification, capacity constraints, and value and ROI assumptions are all named in the methodology table. Their internal structure is this product's design.

#### 6.6.3 Methodology phase served

Weeks 6-8 — Investment, Cost and Capacity Modeling. Core objective: pressure-test whether the V1 roadmap is financially and operationally realistic. Key Activities: estimate costs; define ranges; assess internal resource needs; identify capacity constraints; develop value and ROI assumptions; test scenarios. Outputs: investment profile; capacity requirements; initiative-level cost ranges; initial value case; scenario comparisons.

#### 6.6.4 Inputs consumed

| Methodology Inputs column (Weeks 6-8) | Concrete input in this product | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| V1 roadmap | `RoadmapScenario` in status `candidate`, its `Wave` set and `RoadmapItem` placements | M5 |
| Initiative scope | `Initiative` description, member `Opportunity` records, recommended actions, t-shirt size, duration | M4, M5 |
| Labor assumptions | Role taxonomy, blended rates or rate bands, working-days calendar | Firm configuration plus engagement overrides |
| Vendors | Vendor names, quotes, existing contract values where the client supplied them | `SourceDocument`, `Evidence` |
| Tools | Tool and licence inventory, unit pricing basis, seat counts | `SourceDocument` |
| Implementation | Systems-integrator or implementation-partner effort assumptions | Firm precedent, vendor quote |
| Training | Population to train, delivery mode, unit cost basis | Inferred, see 6.6.14 |
| OCM | Change-management scope and duration | Inferred, see 6.6.14 |
| Internal capacity | `CapacityProfile` by role by month, in-flight program load | Client-supplied or consultant-estimated |

#### 6.6.5 Screens and views

| Screen | Primary job |
|---|---|
| Cost Workbench | Build and review a `CostEstimate` per initiative, line item by line item, with method and basis |
| Sizing Configuration | Maintain the t-shirt size to cost-range and duration lookup |
| Completeness Board | Show the six cost categories by initiative with present, deliberately absent, and unexplained absence states |
| Capacity Model | Role-by-month demand against available capacity, with over-allocation heat and constraint statements |
| Investment Profile | Spend by year, wave, theme, category, and cumulative, with low, expected, and high bands |
| Value Case Builder | Benefit streams per initiative with type, measurement basis, ramp, owner, and quantified state |
| Lever Console | Set timing, resources, budget, and ambition levers and see what recomputes |
| Pressure-Test Report | The ranked list of every reason the roadmap is not realistic |
| Basis Inspector | For any number on any screen, show its basis chain down to `EvidenceRef` |

```mermaid
erDiagram
  Initiative ||--o| CostEstimate : costed_by
  CostEstimate ||--o{ CostLineItem : contains
  CostLineItem ||--o{ SpendPhase : phased_as
  Initiative ||--o| ValueCase : valued_by
  ValueCase ||--o{ Benefit : contains
  Benefit ||--o| KPI : measured_by
  Initiative ||--o{ ResourceDemand : requires
  Role ||--o{ ResourceDemand : supplies
  Role ||--o{ CapacityProfile : has
  RoadmapScenario ||--o{ CostEstimate : snapshots
  RoadmapScenario ||--o{ PressureTestReport : produces
```

#### 6.6.6 Cost structure

**FR-700 — CostEstimate per initiative.** Each `Initiative` MUST support at most one active `CostEstimate` per `RoadmapScenario`, carrying `id`, `initiative_id`, `scenario_id`, `currency`, `version`, `status` (draft, reviewed, final), `prepared_by`, `reviewed_by`, `completeness_score`, and `line_items[]`.

- AC-700.1 A `CostEstimate` MUST be snapshotted into the scenario when the scenario leaves `draft`, so scenario economics remain reproducible.

**FR-701 — Cost categories are a closed set.** `CostLineItem.category` MUST be one of exactly these six, which are the categories the methodology names: `internal_labour`, `vendors`, `tools_and_licences`, `implementation`, `training`, `organizational_change_management`.

- AC-701.1 The set MUST NOT be extendable per engagement. Sub-classification MUST use `CostLineItem.subcategory` free text so that portfolio rollups stay comparable across engagements.
- AC-701.2 Every line item MUST carry `description` (1-300 chars) stating what is being bought or staffed.

**FR-702 — One-time versus run-rate.** Each `CostLineItem` MUST carry `cost_nature` of `one_time` or `run_rate`, and for `run_rate` a `recurrence` (`monthly` or `annual`), a `start_month`, and either an `end_month` or `ongoing = true`.

- AC-702.1 Rollups MUST report one-time and run-rate totals separately and MUST NOT sum an ongoing run-rate into a single lifetime figure without a stated horizon.
- AC-702.2 The default reporting horizon for run-rate is the roadmap span plus 24 months, configurable per engagement.

**FR-703 — Fiscal-year phasing of spend.** Each `CostLineItem` MUST decompose into `SpendPhase` records: `fiscal_year`, `fiscal_period` (month or quarter, configurable granularity), `amount_low`, `amount_expected`, `amount_high`.

- AC-703.1 The engagement MUST define its fiscal-year start month; all phasing and annual envelopes MUST use it, never the calendar year by default.
- AC-703.2 The sum of phase amounts MUST equal the line item's three-point totals at each of low, expected, and high, and the system MUST block save on a mismatch greater than a rounding tolerance of one currency unit.
- AC-703.3 The system MUST offer phasing helpers of `even_across_duration`, `front_loaded_40_30_30`, `back_loaded_20_30_50`, and `manual`, and MUST record which was used. ASSUMPTION: these three curve shapes are invented defaults and are configuration.
- AC-703.4 Default phasing MUST derive from the initiative's start and end dates in the active scenario, so that moving an initiative in M5 re-phases spend rather than silently leaving it in the wrong year.

**FR-704 — Rollups.** The system MUST compute cost rollups at opportunity, initiative, workstream, wave, theme, fiscal year, and portfolio level, each preserving low, expected, and high.

- AC-704.1 Aggregation of ranges MUST use simple summation of low, expected, and high, and every displayed aggregate range MUST be labelled `summed range, not probabilistic` so nobody reads the portfolio high as a confidence bound.
- AC-704.2 Any rollup that includes an initiative with no `CostEstimate` MUST show the count of uncosted initiatives beside the total. A missing estimate MUST NOT be treated as zero.

**FR-705 — Opportunity-level estimates are optional.** The system MUST allow a `CostEstimate` at `Opportunity` level where the consultant wants finer granularity, and MUST then derive the initiative estimate as the sum of its opportunity estimates plus any initiative-level line items, showing which mode each initiative uses.

**FR-706 — No silent zeros or hidden scales.** The system MUST distinguish, in storage and in every view, between a value of zero, an absent value, and a not-applicable value.

- AC-706.1 All monetary amounts MUST be stored as numeric types with a single stated currency and unit per engagement. Amounts MUST NEVER be stored as text, and no displayed number may be derived by parsing a string. This is a direct response to the reference engagement, where dimension scores lived as prose strings and were converted with a leading-character text function, and where a second, incompatible score scale survived in a hidden sheet.
- AC-706.2 The system MUST reject a line item whose expected amount is absent while its low or high is present.

**FR-707 — Rates and weights are configuration, never formulas.** Blended labour rates, contractor rate premiums, currency, the fiscal calendar, the discount rate, and all default multipliers MUST be stored as named, versioned configuration records with an effective date, and MUST be referenced by calculations rather than embedded in them.

- AC-707.1 Every computed number MUST record the configuration version used, so a recomputation months later reproduces the original figure.
- AC-707.2 Changing a configuration value MUST NOT retroactively alter a snapshotted scenario; it MUST create a new computation version and flag affected scenarios as recomputable. The reference engagement hard-coded its scoring weights into a formula row, which meant no historical result could be reproduced after an edit.

#### 6.6.7 Three-point estimation

**FR-710 — Three-point per line item.** Every `CostLineItem` MUST carry `amount_low`, `amount_expected`, `amount_high` in the estimate currency.

**FR-711 — Method field.** Every `CostLineItem` MUST carry `method` from exactly: `analogous_prior_engagement`, `parametric_from_tshirt`, `bottom_up`, `vendor_quote`.

| Method | Required companion data |
|---|---|
| `analogous_prior_engagement` | Reference to the precedent record used, the comparability note, and the scaling factor applied |
| `parametric_from_tshirt` | The size used, the lookup version, and any adjustment factor with reason |
| `bottom_up` | The driver quantities (for example FTE-months by role, seat counts, days of training) and the rate configuration version |
| `vendor_quote` | `EvidenceRef` to the quote with its date and validity period |

- AC-711.1 A line item with `method = vendor_quote` and no `EvidenceRef` MUST fail validation.
- AC-711.2 An `analogous_prior_engagement` line item MUST NOT expose client-identifying detail of the precedent; only the comparability note and scaling factor are carried forward.

**FR-712 — Confidence.** Every `CostLineItem` MUST carry `confidence` (0.00-1.00) and `confidence_band` (low, medium, high). Estimate-level confidence MUST be computed as the cost-weighted mean of line-item confidence and displayed alongside every estimate total.

**FR-713 — Range validation and spread flags.** The system MUST enforce `amount_low <= amount_expected <= amount_high` and MUST flag wide ranges.

- AC-713.1 A line item where `amount_high / amount_low` exceeds 3.0 MUST be flagged `wide_range` and MUST require a note explaining the uncertainty driver. ASSUMPTION: the 3.0 threshold is invented and is configuration.
- AC-713.2 An estimate where line items flagged `wide_range` account for more than 30 percent of expected cost MUST be flagged at estimate level and MUST appear in the pressure-test report as a `watch` item.

**FR-714 — Estimate review workflow.** A `CostEstimate` MUST move draft to reviewed to final with a named reviewer distinct from the preparer, recorded as `AuditEvent`. Only `reviewed` or `final` estimates MUST be included in a scenario snapshot used for a client-facing exhibit, and an exhibit built on `draft` estimates MUST be watermarked as such.

#### 6.6.8 T-shirt size lookup

**FR-720 — Size lookup as configuration.** The system MUST provide a configurable lookup keyed by t-shirt size returning: `duration_months_low`, `duration_months_high`, `cost_low_factor`, `cost_expected_factor`, `cost_high_factor`, and a `basis_note`.

- AC-720.1 Duration bands MUST default to the observed ladder in FR-604.
- AC-720.2 The product MUST NOT ship default currency amounts. Cost factors MUST be expressed against an engagement-level or firm-level `reference_unit_cost` that a consultant sets explicitly, and until it is set the lookup MUST return no cost. ASSUMPTION: the factor-times-reference-unit approach is this product's design; nothing in the reference engagement establishes a size-to-cost mapping.
- AC-720.3 Lookup rows MUST be versioned with effective dates so that historical estimates reproduce.

**FR-721 — Indicative estimates from size alone.** For an initiative with a t-shirt size and no line items, the system MUST produce an indicative `CostEstimate` from the lookup, with a single line item per applicable category, `method = parametric_from_tshirt`, and `is_indicative = true`.

- AC-721.1 Indicative estimates MUST be visually marked wherever they appear, MUST be excluded from any total presented as a budget request, and MUST be included in ranges presented as an order of magnitude, with the mode stated on the exhibit.
- AC-721.2 Replacing an indicative estimate with a real one MUST preserve the indicative figures for variance reporting.

**FR-722 — Duration feedback to M5.** The duration bands in the lookup MUST be the same source used by M5's duration overrun check (FR-652), so sizing changes propagate to feasibility without a second data entry.

#### 6.6.9 Missing-cost identification

**FR-730 — Per-initiative completeness check.** For every initiative in the active scenario the system MUST evaluate each of the six cost categories and assign one of: `present`, `absent_deliberate`, `absent_unexplained`.

**FR-731 — Deliberate absence must be stated.** Marking a category `absent_deliberate` MUST require a reason from a controlled list plus free text: `no_such_cost`, `covered_by_another_initiative` (with the initiative named), `funded_outside_roadmap` (with the funding source named), `client_absorbs_internally`, `out_of_scope_for_this_phase`.

- AC-731.1 `covered_by_another_initiative` MUST create a link so the receiving initiative shows the inherited scope, preventing a category from being deliberately absent on both sides of a pair.

**FR-732 — Completeness score and gates.** `CostEstimate.completeness_score` MUST equal the count of categories in state `present` or `absent_deliberate` divided by six, reported to two decimals.

- AC-732.1 An initiative placed in wave 1 with any `absent_unexplained` category MUST raise a `blocker` in the pressure-test report.
- AC-732.2 A scenario MUST NOT be promoted to `recommended` while any wave 1 initiative has `completeness_score` below 1.00.
- AC-732.3 Portfolio completeness MUST be reported as the size-point-weighted mean of initiative completeness, so an incomplete XL initiative is not offset by ten complete XS ones.

**FR-733 — Portfolio missing-cost report.** The system MUST produce a report listing every `absent_unexplained` category by initiative, ordered by the initiative's size points then priority band, with an AI-19 suggestion attached for each.

- AC-733.1 The report MUST state the systematic pattern where one exists, for example "training is absent on 11 of 17 initiatives", because a category missing across the portfolio is a method failure rather than a data-entry omission.

#### 6.6.10 Capacity

**FR-740 — Role taxonomy.** The engagement MUST define a `Role` set with `id`, `name`, `skill_family`, `internal_external_default`, and `rate_config_ref`. Roles MUST be reusable across initiatives.

**FR-741 — Role-based demand per initiative per month.** `ResourceDemand` MUST carry `initiative_id`, `role_id`, `month` (fiscal period), `fte` (decimal, 0.00-9.99), `basis` (`bottom_up`, `parametric_from_tshirt`, `analogous_prior_engagement`), and `confidence_band`.

- AC-741.1 Demand MUST be generatable from an initiative's duration and t-shirt size using a configurable staffing shape, and MUST be editable line by line afterwards.
- AC-741.2 Demand MUST re-phase automatically when the initiative moves wave or its dates change, and the system MUST record that a re-phase occurred.
- AC-741.3 `internal_labour` cost line items and `ResourceDemand` MUST reconcile. A divergence greater than 10 percent in FTE-months MUST be flagged, with the tolerance configurable.

**FR-742 — Capacity profile per role per month.** `CapacityProfile` MUST carry `role_id`, `month`, `available_fte`, `source` (`current_headcount`, `approved_hire`, `open_requisition`, `contractor`, `vendor_delivered`), and `basis` with `EvidenceRef[]`.

- AC-742.1 Available capacity MUST be reducible by a configurable non-project allocation, for example run-the-business load, expressed as a percentage per role per month and stated on the view.
- AC-742.2 In-flight committed programs MUST be enterable as reserved demand so that available capacity reflects the load already on the team. The reference engagement's own workshop framing was how many additional programs the team could absorb with several major programs already in flight, so reserved demand is required, not optional.

**FR-743 — Hire versus contract representation.** Where demand cannot be met by existing capacity, the gap MUST be resolvable through an explicit `SourcingPlan` record rather than by silently raising available capacity.

`SourcingPlan` MUST carry: `role_id`, `mode` (`hire_internal`, `contract`, `vendor_deliver`, `defer_scope`), `fte`, `start_month`, `lead_time_months`, `ramp_months`, `ramp_curve` (`step`, `linear`, `s_curve`), `unit_cost_ref`, `attrition_assumption`, and `owner_stakeholder_id`.

- AC-743.1 `hire_internal` MUST apply `lead_time_months` before any capacity appears and `ramp_months` during which effective capacity is scaled by the ramp curve. Defaults: lead time 3 months, ramp 3 months, linear. ASSUMPTION: these defaults are invented and are configuration.
- AC-743.2 `contract` MUST apply a shorter default lead time of 1 month and a cost premium factor from configuration, and MUST NOT contribute to permanent capacity beyond its end month.
- AC-743.3 Every `SourcingPlan` MUST generate the corresponding `internal_labour` or `vendors` cost line items, so a capacity fix always has a price. A capacity gap closed with no cost consequence MUST be impossible.
- AC-743.4 `defer_scope` MUST link to the initiative or opportunity whose scope is reduced and MUST surface in the pressure-test report.

**FR-744 — Over-allocation view.** The system MUST display utilisation by role and month as `demand_fte / available_fte`, rendered as a role-by-month grid with values to two decimals.

- AC-744.1 Cells above 1.00 MUST be marked as over-allocated. A configurable amber threshold, default 0.85, MUST mark near-capacity.
- AC-744.2 The view MUST pivot to role by wave, role by initiative, and initiative by month.
- AC-744.3 Every cell MUST drill through to the contributing `ResourceDemand` records.

**FR-745 — Constraint identification.** For each over-allocation the system MUST emit a `CapacityConstraint` record naming the specific constraint: which role, which contiguous months, peak excess FTE, cumulative excess FTE-months, and the ranked list of contributing initiatives by excess FTE-months contributed.

- AC-745.1 The record MUST include a resolution set, each option with its cost and schedule consequence: move a named initiative to a named later wave, add FTE through a `SourcingPlan`, extend the initiative duration by N months, or reduce scope.
- AC-745.2 AI-20 MUST narrate the constraint in reviewable prose attached to the record; the arithmetic MUST be computed, not generated.
- AC-745.3 Constraints MUST feed M5's wave overload check so that capacity findings appear in the roadmap view rather than only in this module.

**FR-746 — Capacity absent mode.** When `CapacityProfile` records do not exist for a role, all capacity checks touching that role MUST return `not_evaluable` naming the role, and the Capacity Model MUST list roles with demand but no capacity profile as its first-priority gap list.

#### 6.6.11 Investment profile

**FR-750 — Investment profile view.** The system MUST present portfolio spend across all of these cuts, each showing low, expected, and high, and each split by one-time and run-rate:

| Cut | Requirement |
|---|---|
| By fiscal year | Columns are fiscal years spanning the roadmap plus the run-rate horizon |
| By wave | Wave ordinal and label, with the wave's date span shown |
| By theme | The engagement's themes |
| By cost category | The six categories of FR-701 |
| Cumulative | Running total of expected spend by fiscal period across the roadmap |

- AC-750.1 Every cut MUST reconcile to the same portfolio expected total, and the view MUST display a reconciliation indicator that fails visibly if they do not.
- AC-750.2 Each cut MUST show the count of uncosted and indicatively costed initiatives included.
- AC-750.3 The view MUST support a stacked-by-category view within fiscal year and a wave-over-theme cross-tab.
- AC-750.4 Any annual envelope defined under FR-773 MUST be drawn on the by-year cut, with overage per year stated in currency and in percent.

**FR-751 — Profile export.** The profile MUST export as an `Exhibit` carrying scenario name and version, estimate status mix (draft, reviewed, final counts), currency and units, the summed-range disclaimer of FR-704.1, and the count of unsupported numbers under FR-791.

#### 6.6.12 Value and ROI

**FR-760 — ValueCase per initiative.** Each `Initiative` MUST support at most one `ValueCase` per scenario, carrying `id`, `initiative_id`, `scenario_id`, `summary_statement`, `benefit_ids[]`, `overall_confidence_band`, `status` (draft, reviewed, final), and `evidence: EvidenceRef[]`.

**FR-761 — Benefit fields and types.** Each `Benefit` MUST carry `id`, `value_case_id`, `name`, `type`, `measurement_basis`, `kpi_id`, `ramp`, `owner_stakeholder_id`, `quantification`, `amounts`, `confidence_band`, and `evidence: EvidenceRef[]`.

`Benefit.type` MUST be one of exactly: `revenue_growth`, `cost_reduction`, `cost_avoidance`, `risk_reduction`, `capacity_release`.

**FR-762 — Measurement basis and KPI link.** `measurement_basis` MUST state the observable quantity, its current baseline value, its target value, and the unit, for example "orders shipped without manual intervention, baseline 62 percent, target 90 percent".

- AC-762.1 A benefit MUST reference a `KPI` record where one exists, so that M8 benefits tracking measures the same quantity the value case promised.
- AC-762.2 A benefit with no baseline MUST be flagged `unbaselined` and MUST be excluded from portfolio financial totals until a baseline exists or the benefit is set to directional.

**FR-763 — Ramp curve.** `Benefit.ramp` MUST carry `start_month` (relative to initiative completion, integer, may be negative for benefits that begin during delivery), `months_to_full`, `curve` (`step`, `linear`, `s_curve`), and an optional explicit per-period percentage array that overrides the curve.

- AC-763.1 Benefit amounts by period MUST be computed from the ramp and MUST re-phase automatically when the initiative moves in M5.
- AC-763.2 The system MUST display the phased benefit profile beside the phased spend profile for the same initiative.

**FR-764 — Named accountable owner.** `Benefit.owner_stakeholder_id` MUST reference a `Stakeholder` and is mandatory. A benefit with no named owner MUST NOT be included in portfolio financial totals and MUST appear in the pressure-test report as a `serious` item.

- AC-764.1 The owner MUST be a business stakeholder where the benefit type is `revenue_growth` or `cost_reduction`. A technology-only owner on a revenue benefit MUST raise a `watch` item.

**FR-765 — Quantified versus directional.** `Benefit.quantification` MUST be `quantified` or `directional`, and the distinction MUST be explicit on the record and on every view and export.

- AC-765.1 A `quantified` benefit MUST carry three-point amounts phased by fiscal period, on the same structure as `SpendPhase`.
- AC-765.2 A `directional` benefit MUST carry no amounts and MUST carry a rationale describing the expected direction and its logic.
- AC-765.3 Portfolio financial totals MUST include only `quantified` benefits. Directional benefits MUST be counted and listed separately, never summed into a currency figure. This rule exists so that a value case built largely of judgement cannot present itself as arithmetic.

**FR-766 — Portfolio net value.** The system MUST compute, per fiscal year and cumulatively: total quantified benefit (low, expected, high), total cost (low, expected, high), and net value as benefit minus cost at each of the three points.

- AC-766.1 Net value MUST be reported at portfolio, theme, wave, and initiative level.
- AC-766.2 The count and list of excluded directional benefits and uncosted initiatives MUST be displayed adjacent to every net value figure.

**FR-767 — Simple payback.** The system MUST compute simple payback as the first fiscal period in which cumulative expected quantified benefit equals or exceeds cumulative expected cost, reported as a period label and as months from roadmap start.

- AC-767.1 Where no payback occurs within the reporting horizon, the system MUST report `no payback within horizon` with the horizon stated and the cumulative shortfall, never a blank or an extrapolation.
- AC-767.2 Payback MUST also be computable at initiative level.

**FR-768 — Discounted measure.** The system MUST compute a discounted net value over the reporting horizon using a discount rate held as engagement configuration.

- AC-768.1 The product MUST NOT ship a default rate. The rate MUST be set explicitly, with the setter and date recorded, and MUST be printed on every exhibit showing a discounted figure.
- AC-768.2 Discounting MUST use fiscal-period cash flows at the engagement's phasing granularity, and the formula and period convention MUST be stated in the Basis Inspector.
- AC-768.3 A sensitivity view MUST show the discounted measure at the configured rate and at plus and minus 300 basis points. ASSUMPTION: the plus or minus 300 basis point band is invented and is configuration.

**FR-769 — Value case drafting is a proposal.** AI-22 drafts of `ValueCase` and `Benefit` records MUST arrive as `AISuggestion` records and MUST NOT populate canonical fields until accepted or edited. Every accepted benefit MUST retain its originating suggestion id.

#### 6.6.13 Scenario modelling on four levers

**FR-770 — Lever framework.** The system MUST express scenario modelling as four named levers, which are the four the methodology names: timing, resources, budget, and ambition. Each lever MUST be a parameter set applied to a base scenario to produce a derived scenario, and MUST be inspectable and reversible.

`LeverApplication` MUST carry `id`, `base_scenario_id`, `derived_scenario_id`, `lever` (`timing`, `resources`, `budget`, `ambition`), `parameters` (typed per lever), `applied_by`, `applied_at`, and `recompute_log`.

**FR-771 — Timing lever.** Parameters: `shift_initiative_ids[]` with `shift_months` (signed integer), or `shift_wave_ordinals[]` with `shift_months`, or `compress_initiative_ids[]` with `compression_percent` (1-50).

| What it changes | What recomputes |
|---|---|
| Initiative start and end dates; wave date spans | Spend phasing (FR-703.4), demand phasing (FR-741.2), benefit ramp phasing (FR-763.1), annual envelope compliance, role-month utilisation, dependency conflict checks in M5, payback and discounted measure |

- AC-771.1 Compression MUST increase peak FTE demand for the affected months proportionally, since duration reduction without effort reduction concentrates load, and MUST raise a `watch` item when compression exceeds 25 percent.

**FR-772 — Resources lever.** Parameters: per role, `available_fte_delta` by month range, or a `SourcingPlan` set to add, or `non_project_allocation_percent` change.

| What it changes | What recomputes |
|---|---|
| `CapacityProfile.available_fte` and the sourcing mix | Utilisation grid, `CapacityConstraint` set, `internal_labour` and `vendors` cost line items generated by sourcing (FR-743.3), portfolio cost, net value, payback |

- AC-772.1 Adding capacity MUST always produce the cost of that capacity in the same scenario.

**FR-773 — Budget lever.** Parameters: `annual_envelope` per fiscal year as an amount, `envelope_basis` (`client_stated`, `consultant_assumed`), and `envelope_scope` (`one_time_only` or `one_time_plus_run_rate`).

| What it changes | What recomputes |
|---|---|
| The feasible spend per fiscal year | Envelope overage per year, the constrained-budget selection of FR-776, deferred-initiative set, benefit phasing for deferred initiatives, payback |

**FR-774 — Ambition lever.** Parameters: `include_priority_bands[]` (subset of Critical, High, Medium, Lower), `scope_tier` per initiative (`full`, `reduced`, `minimum`), and `exclude_initiative_ids[]`.

| What it changes | What recomputes |
|---|---|
| Which initiatives are in the roadmap and at what scope | Cost line items scaled by the tier factor, demand scaled by the tier factor, benefits scaled by the tier factor, dependency validity (excluding a prerequisite MUST raise a conflict), completeness gates |

- AC-774.1 Scope tiers MUST carry configurable factors applied to cost, demand, and benefit independently, defaulting to `full` 1.00, `reduced` 0.65, `minimum` 0.40 for cost and demand and `full` 1.00, `reduced` 0.50, `minimum` 0.25 for benefit. ASSUMPTION: these factors are invented and are configuration. Benefit is deliberately reduced faster than cost, because descoping usually surrenders value faster than it saves money, and this asymmetry MUST be visible and editable rather than hidden.
- AC-774.2 Excluding an initiative that is a hard prerequisite for an included one MUST raise a `blocker` naming both.

**FR-775 — Recompute chain is explicit and logged.** Applying any lever MUST execute the recompute chain in a defined order and MUST write a `recompute_log` naming each stage, the number of records changed, and the elapsed time.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Lever applied] --> B[Re-date initiatives and waves]
  B --> C[Re-phase spend]
  B --> D[Re-phase resource demand]
  B --> E[Re-phase benefit ramps]
  C --> F[Recompute cost rollups and envelope compliance]
  D --> G[Recompute utilisation and capacity constraints]
  E --> H[Recompute net value payback and discounted measure]
  F --> I[Re-run feasibility and completeness checks]
  G --> I
  H --> I
  I --> J[Regenerate pressure-test report]
  J --> K[Mark affected rationale and narratives stale]
```

- AC-775.1 A lever application MUST be atomic. A failure mid-chain MUST leave the derived scenario in `draft` with the failure named and MUST NOT partially mutate the base scenario.
- AC-775.2 The base scenario MUST never be mutated by a lever application.

**FR-776 — Constrained-budget scenario.** The system MUST answer the question "if the annual envelope is capped at a stated amount, which initiatives fit and what is deferred".

- AC-776.1 The selection rule MUST be: (1) force-include every initiative flagged `mandatory` (default flag applies to priority band Critical and to initiatives whose sole benefit type is `risk_reduction` with severity blocker); (2) close the dependency set of forced inclusions, adding hard prerequisites even where their own score is low; (3) rank remaining initiatives by value density, defined as `rolled_weighted_score / expected_one_time_cost_in_reference_units`, descending; (4) walk the ranked list, admitting an initiative when its phased spend fits the remaining envelope in every affected fiscal year and its prerequisites are admitted; (5) stop when no remaining initiative fits.
- AC-776.2 Where the forced-include set alone breaches the envelope, the system MUST NOT silently drop a mandatory initiative. It MUST report the breach, by year and amount, as a `blocker`, and MUST offer timing and scope-tier options that would bring it inside.
- AC-776.3 The output MUST list, for every deferred initiative: the year in which it did not fit, the shortfall amount, the earliest year in which it would fit, its priority band, and its deferral consequence taken from its Risk if Deferred rationale.
- AC-776.4 The selection is a proposal. It MUST be delivered as an `AISuggestion` from AI-21 targeting `RoadmapScenario` and MUST NOT become a scenario until a consultant accepts or edits it. AC-666.2's partial-acceptance behaviour applies.
- AC-776.5 The value-density ranking MUST be shown as a table with the numerator, denominator, and resulting ratio per initiative, so the consultant can see and challenge the rule rather than receiving a verdict.

**FR-777 — Scenario comparison across levers.** The system MUST compare two or more scenarios on: expected cost by fiscal year, envelope overage by year, peak role utilisation and the constrained role, count of blockers and serious items, portfolio net value, simple payback, discounted measure, count of initiatives deferred beyond the roadmap horizon, and count of Critical-band initiatives outside wave 1.

- AC-777.1 The comparison MUST reuse the M5 scenario diff surface so a consultant sees sequence changes and economic changes in one artifact.

#### 6.6.14 Pressure-test report

**FR-780 — The pressure-test report.** For a given scenario the system MUST produce a `PressureTestReport` that names every reason the roadmap is not financially and operationally realistic. This is the module's primary deliverable.

- AC-780.1 The report MUST be generated on demand and automatically on any lever application, and MUST be snapshotted with the scenario version.
- AC-780.2 A report with zero findings MUST state the checks that were evaluated and the checks that were `not_evaluable`, so an empty report is never mistaken for a clean bill of health.

**FR-781 — Finding structure and severity ranking.** Each finding MUST carry `check_id`, `severity` (`blocker`, `serious`, `watch`), `title`, `statement`, `subject_refs` (initiative, wave, role, month, fiscal year, or envelope, as applicable), `magnitude` (a number with a unit), `resolution_options[]`, and `first_detected_at`.

- AC-781.1 The report MUST sort by severity, then by magnitude normalised within check type, then by the affected initiative's priority band.
- AC-781.2 Findings MUST be grouped for reading into Cost, Capacity, Value, and Envelope sections while retaining the global severity ordering within each.

**FR-782 — Check catalogue.** The report MUST evaluate at minimum the following, each with the named specificity:

| Check | Severity | Must name |
|---|---|---|
| Wave 1 initiative with unexplained missing cost category | blocker | Initiative, category |
| Mandatory initiative outside the budget envelope | blocker | Initiative, fiscal year, shortfall amount |
| Role over-allocated above 1.00 | blocker if above 1.25, else serious | Role, contiguous months, peak excess FTE, cumulative excess FTE-months, top contributing initiatives |
| Annual envelope exceeded | blocker | Fiscal year, overage amount and percent, initiatives contributing most |
| Capacity gap closed by a hire whose lead time lands after the initiative starts | serious | Role, initiative, months of shortfall |
| Initiative duration exceeding its wave | serious | Initiative, overrun months |
| Quantified benefit with no named owner | serious | Benefit, initiative |
| Quantified benefit with no baseline | serious | Benefit, KPI |
| Estimate spread concentration above threshold | watch | Initiative, share of expected cost in wide-range items |
| Portfolio value carried mainly by directional benefits (above 50 percent of initiatives) | watch | Count and list |
| Run-rate cost with no end month and no ongoing flag | watch | Line item |
| Cost estimate still in draft inside a scenario marked candidate | watch | Initiative, estimate status |
| Value density ranking overridden by consultant edit | watch | Initiative, original and final position |

ASSUMPTION: the specific severities and numeric thresholds in this table are invented for this product and are configuration. The requirement to test realism and the categories being tested come from the methodology.

**FR-783 — Promotion gate.** A `RoadmapScenario` MUST NOT be promoted to `recommended` while the current pressure-test report contains an unresolved, undismissed `blocker`.

- AC-783.1 Dismissal MUST require a reason and MUST be attributed, recorded as `AuditEvent`, and printed in the report.

**FR-784 — Report as deliverable.** The report MUST export as an `Exhibit` and MUST be consumable by M7 so that executive materials inherit the same findings rather than restating them.

#### 6.6.15 Traceability of every number

**FR-790 — Basis required on every cost and value number.** Every stored monetary or FTE figure MUST carry a `basis` object: `basis_type` (`vendor_quote`, `client_stated`, `firm_precedent`, `bottom_up_calculation`, `parametric_lookup`, `consultant_judgement`, `none`), `basis_note`, `evidence: EvidenceRef[]`, `set_by`, `set_at`, and `config_version` where a calculation was involved.

- AC-790.1 `basis_type = none` MUST be storable, because forcing a fake basis is worse than recording that there is none. It MUST trigger FR-791.
- AC-790.2 `consultant_judgement` MUST require a non-empty `basis_note`.

**FR-791 — Unsupported numbers are visibly marked.** Any figure whose `basis_type` is `none`, or whose `basis_type` requires evidence and has none, MUST be rendered with an `unsupported` marker everywhere it appears.

- AC-791.1 The marker MUST be a visible glyph and label, not a hover-only affordance, and MUST be present in tables, charts, and tooltips.
- AC-791.2 The Basis Inspector MUST reach any number's full basis chain in at most two interactions from wherever the number is displayed.

**FR-792 — Unsupported propagates through rollups.** Any aggregate containing an unsupported component MUST itself be marked, showing the count of unsupported components and their share of the aggregate's expected value.

- AC-792.1 The share MUST be shown as a percentage to one decimal.
- AC-792.2 An aggregate whose unsupported share exceeds 25 percent MUST be marked at a stronger level and MUST appear in the pressure-test report as a `watch` item. ASSUMPTION: the 25 percent threshold is invented and is configuration.

**FR-793 — Exports carry the marking.** Every `Exhibit` and `Deliverable` produced from this module, including generated slides, MUST reproduce the unsupported marking on the face of the exhibit and MUST include a basis appendix listing every unsupported figure with its location.
