- AC-793.1 Export MUST NOT be blocked by unsupported figures. It MUST be impossible to produce an export in which they are invisible.
- AC-793.2 The appendix MUST name the scenario, version, currency, units, discount rate, configuration versions, and the estimate status mix.

**FR-794 — Deck and model cannot drift.** Every number placed in an exported deck MUST be bound to its source record and MUST carry the scenario version it came from.

- AC-794.1 Opening an exhibit whose bound scenario has since changed MUST show a staleness banner naming the changed figures.
- AC-794.2 Regenerating an exhibit MUST refresh all bound numbers atomically; partial refresh MUST NOT be possible.
- AC-794.3 Hand-typed numbers in an exhibit MUST be either impossible or explicitly flagged as unbound and listed in the basis appendix. In the reference engagement the deck and the workbook drifted apart, and another client's slides were left sitting inside a working deck; binding numbers to records and exhibits to scenario versions is how this product prevents both.

#### 6.6.16 AI capabilities invoked

| Capability | Purpose in this module | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| AI-18 cost range proposal from firm precedent | Propose three-point ranges by category for an initiative using comparable prior firm work, with comparability note and scaling factor | `AISuggestion` targeting `CostLineItem` or `CostEstimate` |
| AI-19 missing-cost detection | Identify which cost categories are absent, judge whether the absence looks deliberate, and propose the line items that are probably missing | `AISuggestion` targeting `CostEstimate`, feeding FR-733 |
| AI-20 capacity constraint explanation | Narrate a computed `CapacityConstraint` into reviewable prose naming role, months, magnitude, and contributing initiatives | `AISuggestion` targeting `CapacityConstraint` |
| AI-21 scenario generation from levers | Propose lever parameter sets and the constrained-budget selection of FR-776 | `AISuggestion` targeting `RoadmapScenario` and `LeverApplication` |
| AI-22 value case drafting | Draft `ValueCase` and `Benefit` records including type, measurement basis, ramp shape, and a candidate owner role | `AISuggestion` targeting `ValueCase` and `Benefit` |

All five follow propose, review, commit. No AI output writes a monetary amount, an FTE figure, a lever parameter, or a benefit to a canonical field.

The reference engagement contains no cost model, no capacity model, and no value model (see 6.6.2). The following specifics are therefore this product's design. Each is labelled at its point of use.

| Inferred specific | Grounded in | Nature of the inference |

| The six cost categories as a closed enum | Methodology Inputs column names labor, vendors, tools, implementation, training, OCM | The categories are observed in the methodology; making them a closed, non-extendable enum is a design choice |
| `CostEstimate` and `CostLineItem` structure, one-time versus run-rate, `SpendPhase` | Methodology Outputs: initiative-level cost ranges, investment profile | Entirely designed |
| The three phasing curve helpers and their splits (40/30/30, 20/30/50) | Nothing observed | Invented defaults, configuration |
| The four estimation methods enum | Methodology AI enhancement mentions cost ranges using prior firm work | `analogous_prior_engagement` is implied; the other three and the enum shape are designed |
| Wide-range threshold of 3.0 high-to-low | Nothing observed | Invented, configuration |
| Wide-range concentration threshold of 30 percent of expected cost | Nothing observed | Invented, configuration |
| Size-to-cost factors and the `reference_unit_cost` mechanism | T-shirt ladder is observed; no cost mapping exists | Mechanism designed; deliberately ships with no default amounts |
| Size points 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 | Six-rung ladder is observed; weights are not | Invented, configuration |
| Completeness score as categories addressed over six, and the wave 1 gate | Methodology Key Activity names missing-cost identification | Metric and gate designed |
| Deliberate-absence reason enum | Nothing observed | Invented |
| Role taxonomy, `ResourceDemand`, `CapacityProfile` shapes | Methodology Inputs name internal capacity; Key Activities name capacity constraints | Entirely designed |
| Hire lead time 3 months, ramp 3 months linear; contract lead time 1 month | Nothing observed | Invented defaults, configuration |
| Non-project allocation percentage per role | Nothing observed | Invented, configuration |
| Utilisation amber threshold 0.85 and blocker threshold 1.25 | Nothing observed | Invented, configuration |
| The five `Benefit` type values | Nothing observed in the engagement; the scoring rubric's financial-impact anchors describe revenue, margin, cost avoidance, and FTE time in prose | Enum derived from the rubric's own language, then designed |
| Ramp curve shapes and the quantified versus directional split | Methodology Key Activity names value and ROI assumptions | Designed; the exclusion of directional benefits from financial totals is a deliberate product rule |
| Scope tier factors 1.00 / 0.65 / 0.40 for cost and 1.00 / 0.50 / 0.25 for benefit | Nothing observed | Invented, configuration; the asymmetry is a deliberate design position |
| Value density selection rule for the constrained-budget scenario | Methodology Key Activity names scenario testing on budget | Rule designed; presented as an inspectable table rather than a verdict |
| Discount-rate sensitivity band of plus or minus 300 basis points | Nothing observed | Invented, configuration |
| Unsupported-share threshold of 25 percent | Nothing observed | Invented, configuration |
| The severities and thresholds in the FR-782 check catalogue | Methodology core objective is to pressure-test realism | Check subjects derive from the methodology; severities and numbers are invented configuration |
| Default run-rate reporting horizon of roadmap span plus 24 months | Nothing observed | Invented, configuration |

#### 6.6.18 Exit criteria

M6 is complete for an engagement when all of the following hold for the scenario intended to carry into Weeks 9-10:

1. Every initiative in the scenario holds a `CostEstimate` in status `reviewed` or `final`, or an explicitly accepted indicative estimate with the acceptance recorded.
2. Every `CostLineItem` carries three-point amounts, a method, a confidence band, fiscal-period phasing that reconciles to its totals, and a basis.
3. Portfolio completeness, size-point weighted, is 1.00 for wave 1 and at least a consultant-accepted floor for later waves, with every `absent_deliberate` category carrying a reason.
4. Every role with demand has a `CapacityProfile` for every month in which demand exists, or is listed as an accepted evaluation gap.
5. Every `CapacityConstraint` is either resolved, covered by a `SourcingPlan` whose cost has been added to the model, or accepted with a recorded reason.
6. Every initiative holds a `ValueCase` with at least one `Benefit` that has a type, a measurement basis, a ramp, a named owner, and a quantification state.
7. The investment profile reconciles across all five cuts and exports with its basis appendix.
8. At least three scenarios exist that differ on at least two of the four levers, including one constrained-budget scenario, and are comparable side by side.
9. The pressure-test report contains no unresolved, undismissed `blocker`.
10. No number in any export intended for a client is unmarked and unsupported, and the assumption register handed over from M5 shows which cost and capacity assumptions were retired by modelling and which survive.

### 6.7 M7 Business Alignment and Decision Log (Weeks 9-10) — FR-800 to FR-899

#### 6.7.1 Purpose

M7 is where the roadmap stops being the consulting team's artefact and becomes the client leadership team's plan. The costed roadmap produced by M6 is a technology object: initiatives, waves, scores, cost ranges. Business leaders do not accept technology objects. They accept statements about their own function's outcomes, and they accept them only after they have been allowed to challenge sequencing, value and cost, and after they have seen what their challenge would actually cost elsewhere in the plan.

The module therefore does four things. It reframes one roadmap into many audience-specific views without forking the data. It runs structured socialization rounds and captures every response as a typed, targeted record. It computes the consequences of every requested change before that change is allowed to commit. It records the resulting executive trade-offs as durable Decision records that stay linked to the roadmap, so that six months later any viewer can ask why an initiative sits in Wave 3 and get an answer.

The output is the Business-Aligned V2 Roadmap named in the methodology: agreed outcomes and KPIs, revised priorities, stakeholder feedback, a decision log, and the key executive trade-offs.

#### 6.7.2 Methodology phase served

Weeks 9-10, "Business Alignment + Roadmap Refinement". Core objective: translate the technology roadmap into business outcomes and build enterprise leadership alignment. Key activities served: socialize with business leaders, validate value, challenge sequencing, refine priorities, translate technology investments into business outcomes, resolve key disagreements.

The reference engagement ran a compressed version of this phase inside a two-day onsite rather than across two weeks. The Day 1 findings playback ended on a slide that asked the room, in substance, where they agreed, where they would challenge, and what they would reprioritize. Day 2 then converted that challenge into a client-assigned priority rank that came off the facilitated workshop board and was pasted into the workbook as a column ("Identified as Top Priority", values 1 to 19) sitting alongside the calculated weighted score. M7 generalizes that: the client's own view is first-class data, it is captured against specific items, and it never overwrites the analytical score.

| Input | Source | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `RoadmapScenario` (selected), `RoadmapItem`, `Wave` | M5, M6 | The object being socialized |
| `OpportunityScore`, `ScoringModel`, `ScoreDimension` | M4 | Score challenge and re-scoring |
| `CostEstimate`, `CostLineItem`, `ResourceDemand`, `CapacityProfile` | M6 | Cost and capacity impact classes |
| `ValueCase`, `Benefit` | M6 | Value validation and value-shift impact |
| `Dependency` | M5 | Dependency violation detection |
| `Stakeholder` (with function, seniority, relationship) | M1 | Audience definition, review assignment |
| `MaturityAssessment`, `Finding`, `Evidence`, `Benchmark` | M2, M3 | Evidence backing for views and decisions |
| `Theme`, `Initiative`, `Opportunity` | M4 | Scope filtering and framing |
| `Deliverable` records already issued | M8 | Staleness impact class |

#### 6.7.4 Screens and views

| Screen | What it does |
|---|---|
| **View Library** | Lists every saved `StakeholderRoadmapView` with audience, version, last shared date, and the snapshot it resolves against. Create, clone, version, share. |
| **View Builder** | Three-pane editor: scope filter on the left, dimension show/hide checklist in the middle, live preview of the rendered roadmap on the right. |
| **Review Round Console** | One row per `ReviewAssignment`: stakeholder, assigned view, scoped items, status, sent date, responded date, reminders. Bulk send and bulk remind. |
| **Feedback Inbox** | Chronological and by-target list of `StakeholderFeedback`, with type, sentiment and resolution status filters. Each item links straight to its target entity. |
| **Feedback Synthesis Board** | AI-23 proposed `FeedbackTheme` cards ordered by stakeholder count, each expandable to the verbatims and the affected initiatives. |
| **Change Impact Panel** | Modal opened from any change request. Five impact class tabs, before/after side by side, blocking findings pinned to the top, accept / edit / reject footer. |
| **Decision Log** | Filterable register of `Decision` records, with an "open decisions required" tab and an "executive trade-offs" tab. |
| **Outcome and KPI Mapper** | Matrix of Initiative against business outcome and KPI, with a completeness column that drives the M8 export gate. |
| **Version Diff** | V1 against V2 (or any pair), grouped into added, removed, moved, re-scored, re-costed, outcome-changed, with the causing feedback theme or decision on each row. |

#### 6.7.5 Requirements

**Stakeholder-specific roadmap views**

**FR-800 — StakeholderRoadmapView entity.** The system MUST persist audience-specific roadmap views as first-class, named, versioned, shareable entities rather than as ad hoc exports or filter state.

```
StakeholderRoadmapView {
  id
  engagement_id
  name                       // "Supply Chain leadership view"
  audience_type              // function_leader | technology_leader | finance | board | pmo | client_pmo
  audience_stakeholder_ids[] // optional named recipients
  audience_function          // optional, e.g. "Merchandising"
  scope_filter               // ScopeFilter, see FR-801
  shown_dimensions[]         // enum RoadmapDimension, ordered
  hidden_dimensions[]        // enum RoadmapDimension, explicit not implicit
  framing_language           // business_outcome | technology_capability | financial
  grouping                   // theme | wave | function | owner | capability_area
  sort                       // weighted_score_desc | wave_asc | client_rank_asc | cost_desc
  bound_scenario_id
  bound_snapshot_id          // views resolve against a named snapshot, never "now"
  version                    // integer, monotonic
  status                     // draft | issued | superseded
  created_by, created_at
  shared_with[]              // {stakeholder_id, shared_at, access: view|comment}
  share_expires_at
}
```

- **AC-800.1** Creating a view MUST NOT copy roadmap rows. A view is a query plus a presentation contract over the canonical model.
- **AC-800.2** `hidden_dimensions` MUST be stored explicitly rather than inferred as "everything not shown", so that a later schema addition does not silently appear in an already-issued view.
- **AC-800.3** Issuing a view increments `version` and freezes `bound_snapshot_id`. An issued view is immutable; edits produce version n+1.
- **AC-800.4** Every view render MUST display its snapshot label and as-of timestamp in the header.

**FR-801 — Scope filter.** A view's `ScopeFilter` MUST support predicates over at least: `theme_id`, `initiative_id`, `wave`, `priority_band`, `quadrant`, `functions_touched` (many-to-many between Initiative and business function), `owner_stakeholder_id`, `relationship_type` (B2B / B2C / B2B2C / Internal), `t_shirt_size`, `client_top_priority_rank` presence, and `cost_band`. Predicates combine with AND across fields and OR within a field.

- **AC-801.1** `functions_touched` MUST be a stored attribute of Initiative and Opportunity, not derived from text search, because the function-leader view depends on it entirely.
- **AC-801.2** A view whose filter resolves to zero items MUST refuse to issue and MUST name the predicate that emptied it.

**FR-802 — Dimension vocabulary.** The `RoadmapDimension` enum MUST be a closed set covering exactly the dimensions the model holds, and every dimension MUST be independently showable or hideable. The MVP set is: `theme`, `initiative`, `opportunity`, `recommended_action`, `so_what`, `weighted_score`, `financial_impact_score`, `risk_if_deferred_score`, `strategic_alignment_score`, `priority_band`, `business_value_x`, `urgency_y`, `quadrant`, `client_top_priority_rank`, `t_shirt_size`, `span`, `dependencies`, `wave`, `milestones`, `cost_range`, `cost_by_year`, `resource_demand`, `value_case`, `benefit_detail`, `business_outcome`, `kpi`, `owner`, `relationship_type`, `linked_pain_points`, `maturity_gap`, `evidence`, `status`.

- **AC-802.1** This enum is the same vocabulary M8 exhibits query against, so a dimension added here MUST be available to exhibits without a second schema change.

**FR-803 — Default view templates.** The system MUST ship at least the two audience templates the methodology names, pre-configured and cloneable.

| Template | Scope filter | Shown | Hidden | Framing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Functional business leader | `functions_touched contains <their function>` | business_outcome, kpi, initiative, wave, milestones, dependencies (only those crossing their function), owner, so_what | all three raw sub-scores, weighted_score, bubble coordinates, cost_by_year, resource_demand, full opportunity register | `business_outcome` |
| Technology leader | none (full estate) | all dimensions | none | `technology_capability` |

- **AC-803.1** Hiding cost detail from the functional-leader default is an **assumption**: the reference engagement's functional deep-dive slides carried no cost figures while the investment discussion was held with technology and finance leadership, but no explicit rule was documented. The default MUST be overridable per engagement.
- **AC-803.2** A function leader's view MUST still show any dependency where one endpoint is inside their function and the other is outside it, because those are the dependencies they can break.

**FR-804 — Framing language.** Every `Initiative` MUST carry both a `technology_statement` and a `business_outcome_statement`, and every `Opportunity` MUST carry both a `recommended_action` (technology framing) and a `so_what` (consequence framing). A view's `framing_language` selects which field renders as the primary label.

- **AC-804.1** Where a business_outcome_statement is absent, the view MUST render an explicit "outcome not yet agreed" placeholder rather than silently falling back to the technology statement.
- **AC-804.2** AI-26 drafts missing `business_outcome_statement` values as AISuggestions.

**FR-805 — View sharing.** A view MUST be shareable to a named `Stakeholder` by link, with access level `view` or `comment`, an optional expiry, and an access log written as `AuditEvent` records.

- **AC-805.1** A `comment` share MUST let the recipient create `StakeholderFeedback` against items visible in that view, and MUST NOT let them create feedback against items the view filters out.

**Client-facing review sessions**

**FR-806 — ReviewRound entity.** The system MUST model socialization as explicit rounds so that "who has responded" is answerable at any moment.

```
ReviewRound {
  id, engagement_id
  label                  // "V1 socialization", "V2 confirmation"
  purpose                // validate_value | challenge_sequencing | confirm_outcomes | final_signoff
  scenario_id, snapshot_id
  roadmap_version_id
  opened_at, closes_at, closed_at
  facilitator_user_id
  status                 // planning | open | closed | abandoned
}
```

**FR-807 — ReviewAssignment.** Each round MUST hold one `ReviewAssignment` per participating stakeholder, carrying the scoped set of items that stakeholder is being asked about.

```
ReviewAssignment {
  id, round_id, stakeholder_id
  view_id                        // the StakeholderRoadmapView they see
  scoped_entity_refs[]           // explicit list of Initiative / Opportunity / Wave ids in scope
  ask                            // free text: what we need from you
  status                         // not_sent | sent | in_progress | responded | partially_responded | declined | no_response
  sent_at, first_opened_at, responded_at
  reminder_count, last_reminder_at
  session_type                   // async_review | one_to_one | group_workshop
  session_date                   // for facilitated sessions
}
```

- **AC-807.1** Status MUST be per stakeholder per round. A stakeholder who responded in round 1 starts round 2 at `not_sent`.
- **AC-807.2** The console MUST show round-level completion as responded / total and MUST list non-responders by name so the engagement lead can chase them.
- **AC-807.3** A facilitated group session MUST be recordable as one assignment per attendee, so that feedback captured live in the room attributes to individuals rather than to "the workshop".
- **AC-807.4** Closing a round MUST be blocked while any assignment is `in_progress`, with an explicit force-close that records who closed it and why.

**StakeholderFeedback records**

**FR-808 — StakeholderFeedback entity.** Every response MUST be stored as a typed record attached to a specific model entity. Free-floating feedback MUST be rejected by the API.

```
StakeholderFeedback {
  id, engagement_id, round_id, assignment_id
  stakeholder_id                 // who
  captured_at                    // when
  captured_by                    // consultant who transcribed, if not self-service
  target_entity                  // Initiative | Opportunity | OpportunityScore | Wave | RoadmapItem
                                 // | CostEstimate | ValueCase | Dependency | Theme | KPI
  target_id                      // required, must resolve
  comment                        // verbatim, required, unbounded free text
  feedback_type                  // challenges_sequencing | challenges_value | challenges_cost
                                 // | adds_scope | removes_scope | requests_information | endorses
  sentiment                      // supportive | neutral | concerned | opposed
  structured_ask                 // optional, see FR-810
  resolution_status              // open | accepted | rejected | deferred | superseded | answered
  resolution_note
  resolved_by, resolved_at
  resulting_change_request_id     // nullable
  resulting_decision_id           // nullable
  evidence[]                      // EvidenceRef, e.g. session recording timestamp
  classification_source           // human | ai_accepted | ai_edited
}
```

- **AC-808.1** `target_entity` and `target_id` are NOT NULL. A creation request without a resolving target returns 422 with the message naming the missing target.
- **AC-808.2** `feedback_type` and `sentiment` are closed enums. The API MUST reject any value outside the enum and MUST NOT coerce, truncate or store free text in these fields. This is a direct response to a known defect in the reference engagement's workbook, where a free-text paragraph had been typed into a cell whose column was declared as a status enum.
- **AC-808.3** `comment` MUST be stored verbatim and MUST never be overwritten by a classification, a summary or an AI rewrite. Summaries live on `FeedbackTheme`.
- **AC-808.4** One comment that raises two distinct concerns MUST be splittable into two `StakeholderFeedback` records that share a `source_comment_id`, so that counts by type stay honest.
- **AC-808.5** Every create, classify and resolve action writes an `AuditEvent`.

**FR-809 — Feedback capture surfaces.** The system MUST support three capture paths: self-service comment from a shared view; consultant transcription during or after a session; bulk import of a facilitated-board export (CSV or equivalent) mapped to targets.

- **AC-809.1** The bulk import path MUST require every imported row to map to a resolving `target_id` before the import commits, and MUST report unmapped rows rather than creating orphans. The reference engagement's workshop-board output was pasted into a spreadsheet column with no such check, which is how a client-assigned rank ended up coexisting with the calculated score with no recorded linkage.

**FR-810 — Structured ask.** Where a stakeholder is asking for a specific model change, the feedback record SHOULD carry a machine-readable `structured_ask` so the change-impact engine can evaluate it without re-interpretation.

```
structured_ask {
  ask_type      // move_wave | change_score | change_cost | change_size | add_dependency
                // | remove_dependency | add_scope_item | remove_item | change_owner
  field
  proposed_value
  current_value
  justification
}
```

- **AC-810.1** A `structured_ask` MUST NOT mutate anything. It is an input to FR-813.

**FR-811 — Client-assigned priority coexistence.** Where a review session produces a client's own ranking or urgency selection, the system MUST store it as a separate field on the target entity (`client_top_priority_rank`, `client_urgency`) with the round it came from, and MUST NOT overwrite `weighted_score`, `priority_band`, `business_value_x`, `urgency_y` or `quadrant`.

- **AC-811.1** Both values MUST be displayable side by side, and the system MUST compute a divergence list: items where the client rank and the calculated band disagree by more than one band. That list is the agenda for the alignment conversation.
- **AC-811.2** Grounded observation: the reference engagement carried a client-assigned rank of 1 to 19 in the register alongside a calculated 1 to 5 weighted score, with no reconciliation view. The divergence list is the missing view.

**Feedback synthesis**

**FR-812 — FeedbackTheme entity and synthesis.** The system MUST cluster feedback across stakeholders into themes, each carrying the count of distinct stakeholders raising it and the specific entities affected.

```
FeedbackTheme {
  id, engagement_id, round_id
  label                     // short, e.g. "Sequencing of the data foundation is contested"
  description
  stakeholder_count         // distinct stakeholders, not comment count
  feedback_ids[]
  affected_entity_refs[]    // the specific Initiatives / Opportunities / Waves
  dominant_type             // modal feedback_type
  type_distribution         // {type: count}
  sentiment_distribution    // {sentiment: count}
  severity                  // derived: see AC-812.3
  status                    // proposed | accepted | merged | rejected | resolved
  resolution_decision_id    // nullable
  provenance                // AISuggestion id when proposed by AI-23
}
```

- **AC-812.1** `stakeholder_count` MUST count distinct stakeholders. Two comments from one person is one stakeholder.
- **AC-812.2** The board MUST sort themes by `stakeholder_count` descending and MUST show, for each, the named initiatives affected. A theme with no `affected_entity_refs` cannot be accepted.
- **AC-812.3** `severity` = `high` when `stakeholder_count >= 3` and any affected item sits in Wave 1; `medium` when `stakeholder_count >= 3` or any affected item sits in Wave 1; else `low`. Thresholds are configurable; the 3-stakeholder default is an **assumption**.
- **AC-812.4** Every theme MUST expand to the verbatim comments and their authors. Synthesis is never a lossy replacement for the record.
- **AC-812.5** AI-23 proposes themes and AI-24 proposes per-comment type and sentiment, both through propose → review → commit. A consultant may merge, split, relabel or reject.

**FR-813 — Change requests.** Every proposed modification to the roadmap arising from alignment MUST be expressed as a `ChangeRequest` containing one or more typed operations, and MUST pass through impact analysis before it can commit.

```
ChangeRequest {
  id, engagement_id
  origin                 // stakeholder_feedback | consultant | decision | refresh_cycle | resequencing_ai
  origin_ref             // feedback_id / decision_id / suggestion_id
  title, rationale
  operations[]           // ChangeOperation
  requested_by, requested_at
  base_snapshot_id       // the snapshot impact was computed against
  status                 // draft | impact_computed | accepted | rejected | superseded | stale
  impact_report_id
  decision_id            // set when accepted
  resulting_version_id
}

ChangeOperation {
  op_type   // move_initiative_wave | remove_initiative | add_initiative | split_initiative
            // | merge_initiatives | set_score_dimension | set_t_shirt_size | set_cost_estimate
            // | add_dependency | remove_dependency | set_wave_boundary | set_owner
            // | set_client_rank | set_kpi_target
  target_entity, target_id
  field, from_value, to_value
}
```

**Change-impact analysis**

**FR-814 — Change-impact analysis is mandatory and pre-commit.** For any `ChangeRequest`, the system MUST compute and display a complete `ImpactReport` before the change can be accepted. An accept action on a change request with no current impact report MUST fail.

```
ImpactReport {
  id, change_request_id
  computed_at, base_snapshot_id, engine_version
  blocking_count, warning_count, informational_count
  findings[]             // ImpactFinding
  before_after           // paired summary values, see AC-814.5
}

ImpactFinding {
  id
  impact_class           // dependency_violation | wave_capacity_breach | cost_profile_shift
                         // | value_case_shift | deliverable_staleness
                         // | band_membership_change | orphaned_outcome
  severity               // blocking | warning | informational
  entity_refs[]
  description            // deterministic, generated from the computation not by a model
  quantum                // the number that matters: days, FTE, currency, count
  suggested_remedy       // nullable, e.g. "also move Initiative X to Wave 2"
}
```

**FR-815 — Impact class 1: dependency violations created.** The engine MUST re-evaluate every `Dependency` whose either endpoint is touched by the change, and MUST report each violation with both endpoints, the dependency type, and the wave or date gap that violates it.

- **AC-815.1** Violation rules by dependency type: `finish_to_start` violated when the predecessor's wave is greater than or equal to the successor's wave; `must_precede_or_same_wave` violated when the predecessor's wave is greater than the successor's; `blocks` violated when the blocker is unscheduled or cancelled while the blocked item remains scheduled; `enables` reported as a warning rather than a violation when the enabler moves later.
- **AC-815.2** The engine MUST also detect transitive violations, not only direct ones, and MUST report the full chain.
- **AC-815.3** Any created cycle MUST be reported as blocking with the cycle path enumerated.
- **AC-815.4** Dependency violations are always `blocking`.

**FR-816 — Impact class 2: wave capacity breaches.** For every `Wave` whose contents change, the engine MUST recompute aggregate `ResourceDemand` by role or skill and compare it against the matching `CapacityProfile`, reporting each breach with the role, the wave, demand, capacity, and the overage in FTE and in percent.

- **AC-816.1** Breach severity: `blocking` when overage exceeds 20 percent of capacity for any role in any wave; `warning` between 5 and 20 percent; `informational` below 5 percent. The 20 percent and 5 percent thresholds are **assumptions** and MUST be configurable per engagement.
- **AC-816.2** The engine MUST also report parallelism feasibility using `t_shirt_size`, because the reference engagement declared T-shirt sizing as the input that "will inform how many initiatives can run in parallel". Rule: report a warning when the count of `L`, `XL` or `XXL` items scheduled to start in the same wave exceeds the engagement's configured parallel-large-item limit (default 3, an **assumption**).
- **AC-816.3** Where `ResourceDemand` or `CapacityProfile` is absent for an affected role, the finding MUST read as "cannot be evaluated: capacity profile missing for role R" rather than as "no breach".

**FR-817 — Impact class 3: cost profile shift by year.** The engine MUST recompute the investment profile by year and report the before, after and delta for each year in the roadmap horizon, split by `capex` and `opex` and by `run` / `grow` / `transform` where those classifications exist.

- **AC-817.1** Reporting MUST use the estimate's low, base and high range values, not a single point, because the reference engagement's cost thinking was explicitly range-based.
- **AC-817.2** The engine MUST flag a funding cliff: any year where the after-profile exceeds the prior year's base spend by more than 40 percent, or exceeds a declared annual funding envelope. The 40 percent default is an **assumption**; the reference engagement named avoiding funding cliffs as a purpose of the cost input but declared no threshold.
- **AC-817.3** Severity is `warning` for any year-on-year swing above the configured threshold, `blocking` where a declared annual envelope is exceeded.

**FR-818 — Impact class 4: value case shift.** The engine MUST recompute the `ValueCase` and report the change to each affected `Benefit`: benefit start date shift in months, benefit-to-date at each year boundary, total horizon benefit before and after, and the delay cost.

- **AC-818.1** Delay cost formula shape: `delay_cost = Σ_benefits (monthly_benefit_rate × delay_months × discount_factor(month))`. The monthly rate derives from the Benefit's ramp profile, not from a flat division, where a ramp is defined.
- **AC-818.2** Where an initiative is removed rather than moved, the engine MUST report the benefits that are forgone entirely and the KPIs left with no contributing initiative (see FR-820).
- **AC-818.3** Severity is `warning` by default and `blocking` where the change would leave an already-agreed KPI target unreachable inside its `target_date`.

**FR-819 — Impact class 5: deliverable staleness.** The engine MUST identify every already-issued `Deliverable`, `Exhibit` instance and `NarrativeMessage` whose bound model values the change would alter, and MUST list them by name with the specific values that move.

- **AC-819.1** This detection MUST use the same `ModelValueRef` binding machinery specified for M8 (FR-901). Staleness in M7 and staleness in M8 are one mechanism, not two.
- **AC-819.2** For each affected deliverable the finding MUST state its recipients where a distribution list was recorded, because "we have already sent this to the board" changes the calculus of accepting a change.
- **AC-819.3** Severity is `informational`. Stale deliverables never block a correct decision; they create regeneration work, which is what M8 exists to make cheap.

**FR-820 — Impact class 6: band membership and orphaned outcomes.** The engine MUST additionally report every item that crosses a `priority_band` boundary or a quadrant boundary as a result of a score change, and every `KPI` that would be left with no linked initiative.

- **AC-820.1** Band boundaries and quadrant thresholds MUST be read from the active `ScoringModel` version, not hard-coded in the engine. The reference engagement hard-coded weights into a formula row, which is precisely why re-weighting could not be evaluated.

**FR-821 — Before and after presentation.** The impact panel MUST present a side-by-side before and after summary containing at minimum: item count by wave, total cost by year, aggregate weighted score by theme, count of dependency violations, count of capacity breaches, total horizon benefit, and count of stale deliverables.

**FR-822 — Recompute on drift.** If the roadmap's current snapshot differs from the `ImpactReport.base_snapshot_id`, the report MUST be marked `stale` and the accept action MUST be blocked until it is recomputed.

**FR-823 — Blocking findings and override.** A `ChangeRequest` with one or more `blocking` findings MUST NOT be accepted through the normal path. It MAY be accepted through an explicit override that records the overriding user, a justification of at least 40 characters, and the full list of overridden findings, and that automatically creates a `Risk` record referencing them.

**FR-824 — Commit semantics.** Accepting a `ChangeRequest` MUST, in one transaction: apply the operations to the canonical model, create a `Decision` record (FR-825), create a new `RoadmapVersion` (FR-831), mark affected deliverables stale, resolve the originating `StakeholderFeedback` records, and write `AuditEvent` records for each mutation.

- **AC-824.1** Rejecting a change request MUST require a reason, MUST leave the model untouched, and MUST set the originating feedback to `rejected` with that reason visible to the person who raised it.
- **AC-824.2** AI-25 generates a plain-language narration of the impact report as an AISuggestion, for use in the review conversation and later in M8 messaging. The deterministic findings are the source of truth; the narration never replaces them.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Stakeholder
    participant C as Consultant
    participant P as Product
    participant E as Impact Engine
    participant M as Canonical Model
    S->>P: Feedback on Initiative (typed, targeted)
    P->>P: Store StakeholderFeedback
    C->>P: Draft ChangeRequest from structured_ask
    P->>E: Compute impact vs base snapshot
    E->>M: Read dependencies, capacity, cost, value, bindings
    E-->>P: ImpactReport (6 classes, severities, quanta)
    P-->>C: Impact panel, before/after, blocking pinned
    P-->>S: Same impact panel, business framing
    C->>P: AI-25 narration requested
    P-->>C: AISuggestion (proposed narration)
    S->>C: Decide: accept / modify / reject
    alt Accepted
        C->>P: Accept with Decision fields
        P->>M: Apply operations
        P->>M: Write Decision, RoadmapVersion n+1
        P->>M: Mark affected Deliverables stale
        P-->>S: Confirmation + what changed
    else Rejected
        C->>P: Reject with reason
        P-->>S: Reason recorded against your feedback
    end
```

**The Decision record**

**FR-825 — Decision entity.** The system MUST record executive trade-offs explicitly, since the methodology names "key executive trade-offs" as a Weeks 9-10 output.

```
Decision {
  id, engagement_id
  title
  decision_statement           // what was decided, one sentence
  decision_type                // sequencing | scope | investment | ownership
                               // | platform_selection | governance | risk_acceptance
  options_considered[] {
    label, description, pros, cons,
    modelled_effect            // reference to an ImpactReport or RoadmapScenario
  }
  chosen_option_index
  tradeoff_statement           // what we gained, what we gave up
  decided_by                   // stakeholder_id, the accountable decider
  participants[]               // stakeholder_ids present
  decision_forum               // e.g. "steering committee", "CIO one-to-one", "workshop day 2"
  decided_on                   // date
  rationale                    // why this option, in the decider's terms
  evidence[]                   // EvidenceRef
  affected_entity_refs[]       // Initiatives / Opportunities / Waves / KPIs
  resulting_change_request_id
  resulting_version_id         // the model change it produced
  reversibility                // reversible | hard_to_reverse | irreversible
  is_executive_tradeoff        // boolean, drives the M8 trade-off exhibit
  status                       // open | decided | deferred | revisited | reversed
  required_by                  // date, for open decisions
  blocked_entity_refs[]        // what cannot proceed until this is decided
  supersedes_decision_id
}
```

- **AC-825.1** A Decision that produced a model change MUST carry `resulting_change_request_id` and `resulting_version_id`. A Decision that changed nothing (a confirmation) MUST say so explicitly.
- **AC-825.2** `options_considered` MUST contain at least two entries for any Decision of type `sequencing`, `investment` or `platform_selection`. A single-option decision is a confirmation and MUST be typed as such.
- **AC-825.3** `tradeoff_statement` is required when `is_executive_tradeoff` is true.

**FR-826 — Decisions required register.** The system MUST maintain a register of `Decision` records in status `open`, each with a `required_by` date, the entities blocked by it, and the options on the table, and MUST surface overdue open decisions on the engagement dashboard.

- **AC-826.1** Grounded observation: the reference engagement's working register carried open decision questions inside cell comments, for example whether a cloud platform choice was needed and whether an item belonged to one initiative or another. Those are Decision records in draft, and the product MUST hold them as such rather than as marginalia.
- **AC-826.2** An `open` Decision blocking a Wave 1 item MUST appear in the M8 board deck's decisions-and-asks section by default.

**FR-827 — Decision linkage from the roadmap.** Every `RoadmapItem` MUST expose a "why is this here" panel, reachable from any roadmap view including shared client views, showing: the linked `Decision` records with their statements and dates, the top score drivers with their dimension scores and evidence, the dependency chain that constrains its position, and the client rank where one exists.

- **AC-827.1** The panel MUST work for a read-only shared view recipient, subject to the view's dimension visibility rules.
- **AC-827.2** Where an item's wave was set by a Decision that overrode the calculated sequence, the panel MUST say so and name the decider.

**FR-828 — Executive trade-off register.** Decisions flagged `is_executive_tradeoff` MUST be queryable as a set, ordered by decision date, and MUST be renderable as an M8 exhibit input containing option A, option B, what is gained, what is given up, and the model evidence for each.

**Business-outcome translation**

**FR-829 — OutcomeMapping entity.** The system MUST map each technology initiative to business outcomes and agreed KPIs.

```
OutcomeMapping {
  id, engagement_id
  initiative_id
  business_outcome_statement    // in the business's language, not IT's
  function                      // the owning business function
  outcome_owner_stakeholder_id  // the business leader who owns the outcome
  kpi_id
  contribution_type             // primary | contributing | enabling
  contribution_note             // how this initiative moves this KPI
  agreed_in_round_id            // which socialization round agreed it
  agreed_by, agreed_at
  evidence[]
  status                        // proposed | agreed | disputed | retired
  provenance                    // AISuggestion id when drafted by AI-26
}

KPI {
  id, engagement_id
  name, definition              // definition is required: an undefined KPI cannot be measured
  unit                          // currency | percent | count | days | ratio | score
  direction                     // increase | decrease
  baseline_value, baseline_as_of, baseline_source
  baseline_status               // measured | estimated | to_be_established
  target_value, target_date
  interim_targets[]             // {date, value}
  measurement_owner_stakeholder_id
  measurement_source            // named system or report
  measurement_cadence           // monthly | quarterly | annual
  first_measurement_date
  status                        // draft | agreed | active | retired
}
```

**FR-830 — Outcome completeness gate.** Every `Initiative` present in the recommended final roadmap MUST have at least one `OutcomeMapping` in status `agreed` with `contribution_type = primary`, linked to a `KPI` that has a baseline (measured, estimated, or explicitly `to_be_established` with a date), a target value, a target date, and a named measurement owner.

- **AC-830.1** The Outcome and KPI Mapper MUST show a completeness column per initiative and an engagement-level completeness percentage.
- **AC-830.2** This gate is enforced at M8 export time as validation V5 in the pre-export gate (FR-920). An incomplete mapping does not block editing; it blocks issuing a final roadmap.
- **AC-830.3** Where a baseline genuinely is not known, `baseline_status = to_be_established` MUST be accompanied by an `ActivationTask` to establish it and a date. A blank baseline MUST NOT be storable. The reference engagement's workbook carried a declared-but-never-populated column; the product's answer to "we do not know yet" is a named task with an owner and a date, not an empty cell.
- **AC-830.4** AI-26 drafts `business_outcome_statement`, candidate KPIs, and candidate baselines from findings and evidence, as AISuggestions. A KPI never becomes `agreed` without a human accept and a named measurement owner.

**FR-831 — V1 to V2 roadmap versioning.** The system MUST create a labelled, immutable `RoadmapVersion` per socialization round and MUST provide a diff view between any two versions.

```
RoadmapVersion {
  id, engagement_id, scenario_id
  label                    // "V1", "V1.1", "V2", "V2 final"
  round_id                 // the socialization round that produced it, nullable
  snapshot_id              // immutable data snapshot
  created_at, created_by
  status                   // draft | issued | superseded
  is_provisional           // see FR-833
  change_summary           // generated: counts by change class
  change_entries[]         // VersionChangeEntry
  parent_version_id
}

VersionChangeEntry {
  change_class      // added | removed | wave_moved | rescored | recosted
                    // | resized | dependency_changed | outcome_changed | owner_changed | renamed
  entity_ref
  from_value, to_value
  caused_by_feedback_theme_id     // nullable
  caused_by_feedback_ids[]        // nullable
  caused_by_decision_id           // nullable
  change_request_id
}
```

- **AC-831.1** Every `VersionChangeEntry` MUST carry at least one of `caused_by_feedback_theme_id`, `caused_by_feedback_ids` or `caused_by_decision_id`. A change with no recorded cause MUST be flagged in the diff view as unattributed and MUST be resolvable to a cause before the version can be issued.
- **AC-831.2** The diff view MUST group by change class, MUST be filterable by theme and by wave, and MUST produce a narrative summary of the form "N initiatives moved earlier, N moved later, N re-scored, driven by M feedback themes across K stakeholders".
- **AC-831.3** An `issued` version is immutable. Any further change creates a new version.
- **AC-831.4** Version labels MUST be human-assigned (V1, V2) with an auto-incrementing minor for intermediate drafts, so that the client-facing vocabulary matches the methodology's own V1 and V2 language.

**FR-832 — Feedback-to-change traceability report.** For any version pair, the system MUST produce a report that answers, per stakeholder, what they asked for and what happened to it: accepted, accepted with modification, rejected with reason, or deferred.

- **AC-832.1** This report is a shareable artefact. Showing a leader that their challenge was recorded, evaluated and answered is the mechanism by which alignment is actually earned.

**FR-833 — Provisionality flag.** A `RoadmapVersion` MUST carry `is_provisional`, set true automatically while any of the following hold: the version status is `draft`; any in-scope `Opportunity` has status other than validated; any `OpportunityScore` has `confidence_band = low`; any register-hygiene task is open; any Wave 1 initiative has an unresolved blocking `Decision`.

- **AC-833.1** `is_provisional` MUST propagate to every view, exhibit and deliverable built from that version, rendered as a visible statement of what specifically remains provisional.
- **AC-833.2** Grounded observation: the reference engagement's post-workshop recap email carried an explicit warning that the rankings and scoring on the deck would shift, alongside a list of the cleanup work still in progress. That warning was written by hand each time. Here it is a property of the model.

#### 6.7.6 AI capabilities invoked

| ID | Capability | Purpose in M7 |
|---|---|---|
| AI-23 | Feedback synthesis and theme extraction | Cluster `StakeholderFeedback` across a round into `FeedbackTheme` proposals with stakeholder counts and affected entities |
| AI-24 | Sentiment and concern classification | Propose `feedback_type` and `sentiment` per comment, and propose the `structured_ask` where the comment implies one |
| AI-25 | Change-impact narration | Turn a deterministic `ImpactReport` into plain-language consequences for a named audience |
| AI-26 | Business-outcome translation drafting | Draft `business_outcome_statement`, candidate KPIs, baselines and targets per initiative |

All four operate through propose → review → commit. None writes to a canonical field.

#### 6.7.7 Exit criteria

M7 is complete for an engagement when all of the following hold:

1. At least one `StakeholderRoadmapView` is issued per participating audience, each bound to a named snapshot.
2. A `ReviewRound` is closed with every assignment in a terminal status (`responded`, `declined` or an explicitly force-closed `no_response`), and the round's response rate is recorded.
3. Every `StakeholderFeedback` record has a `resolution_status` other than `open`.
4. Every `FeedbackTheme` with severity `high` is linked to a `Decision`.
5. Every accepted `ChangeRequest` has a computed `ImpactReport` with zero unoverridden blocking findings, and every override has a recorded justification and a linked `Risk`.
6. Every `Decision` of type `sequencing`, `investment` or `platform_selection` has at least two `options_considered`, a `tradeoff_statement` where flagged as an executive trade-off, a named decider and a date.
7. Outcome completeness is 100 percent for the recommended initiative set per FR-830.
8. A `RoadmapVersion` labelled V2 exists in status `issued`, with a diff against V1 in which every change entry carries a recorded cause.
9. The feedback-to-change traceability report generates without unattributed entries.

---

### 6.8 M8 Narrative and Deliverable Generation (Weeks 10-12) — FR-900 to FR-999

#### 6.8.1 Purpose

M8 converts the aligned model into the executive story and the decision package. This is the module that replaces PowerPoint as the place where analysis becomes narrative, and it exists to fix one specific and expensive failure: in the reference engagement the story lived in slides while the numbers lived in a workbook, the two were connected only by a consultant retyping figures, and the deck drifted out of sync with the register. Counts on a theme-distribution slide summed to 56 opportunities while the register held 43 technology plus 12 operating-model rows, a total of 55. Nobody caught it, because nothing could.

The product's answer is that a narrative claim is a data object. A headline that asserts something about the model binds to the specific model values it asserts, and when a bound value moves the headline is flagged stale and the export gate refuses to ship it.

Around that core the module provides a storyline model, an exhibit registry whose members are queries rather than drawings, PowerPoint generation with a recorded provenance manifest, three audience detail levels, a confidentiality gate, the 90-day activation plan, and the short written narrative in the shape of the reference engagement's recap email.

#### 6.8.2 Methodology phase served

Weeks 10-12, "Final Roadmap + Board Narrative Development". Core objective: convert the aligned roadmap into an executive-ready transformation story and decision package. Activities served: sharpen executive storyline, validate economics and timing, develop Board-level messages, identify key decisions and asks, prepare the 90-day activation plan. Outputs served: Final Executive Roadmap, Board Deck, 90-Day Activation Plan. The methodology's AI enhancement column for this phase ends with "ensure numbers and roadmap remain synchronized", which is FR-901 and FR-925.

#### 6.8.3 Inputs consumed

| Input | Source | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `RoadmapVersion` (issued V2), `RoadmapScenario`, `RoadmapItem`, `Wave` | M7 | Timeline and mobilization exhibits |
| `Theme`, `Initiative`, `Opportunity` | M4 | Taxonomy exhibits and per-theme slides |
| `OpportunityScore`, `ScoringModel`, `ScoreDimension` | M4 | Scoring explainer, bubble chart, band labels |
| `MaturityAssessment`, `MaturityFocusArea`, `CapabilityArea` | M3 | Paginated heatmap |
| `Benchmark` | M2 | Benchmark positioning (deferred exhibit) |
| `CostEstimate`, `CostLineItem` | M6 | Investment profile by year |
| `ValueCase`, `Benefit`, `KPI`, `OutcomeMapping` | M6, M7 | Value messages and outcome slides |
| `Decision`, `StakeholderFeedback`, `FeedbackTheme` | M7 | Decisions and asks, trade-offs, provisionality |
| `Finding`, `Evidence` | M2, M3 | Message evidence backing |
| `Risk` | M7, M9 | Risk section of board narrative |
| `Stakeholder` | M1 | Audience definition, distribution lists |

#### 6.8.4 Screens and views

| Screen | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Storyline Editor** | Ordered list of `NarrativeMessage` cards in a single column, drag to reorder, arc template picker, per-message status chips (draft / reviewed / approved / stale). |
| **Message Inspector** | One message: headline, supporting argument, so-what, message type, audience tags, evidence list, and the bound `ModelValueRef` table showing each bound value with its resolved figure and drift. |
| **Exhibit Gallery** | The registry of exhibit types with live previews built from the current snapshot, plus instance list showing which storyline positions use each. |
| **Deliverable Builder** | Pick template, storyline, audience level, exhibit set; shows slide budget against the level's limit; export button gated by validation. |
| **Consistency Report** | Pre-export validation results, grouped by check, each row naming the message, exhibit or value at fault with a jump link. |
| **Confidentiality Report** | Cross-engagement, named-client and personal-data findings, each classified must_remove / requires_approval / allowed. |
| **Activation Plan Editor** | The near-term wave rendered as ordered `ActivationTask` rows grouped by initiative and 30/60/90 window, with owner and decision columns. |
| **Written Narrative Editor** | Themes and next steps in the recap-email shape, with the generated provisionality statement pinned and non-removable. |
| **Regeneration Diff** | Number-by-number and message-by-message diff between two exports of the same deliverable. |

#### 6.8.5 Requirements

**The narrative model**

**FR-900 — NarrativeMessage entity.** A narrative message MUST be a first-class model entity, not text inside a slide.

```
NarrativeMessage {
  id, engagement_id
  headline                 // the assertion, <= 140 chars
  supporting_argument      // the reasoning, 1-3 sentences
  so_what                  // the consequence for the audience
  message_type             // situation | finding | implication | recommendation
                           // | ask | trade_off | risk | proof_point
  audience[]               // board | exec_committee | technology_leadership | function_leader | pmo
  storyline_id, position   // ordered position within the storyline
  section                  // storyline section label
  evidence[]               // EvidenceRef[]
  value_bindings[]         // ModelValueRef[], see FR-901
  exhibit_instance_ids[]   // exhibits that carry the same claim visually
  linked_decision_ids[]
  linked_kpi_ids[]
  linked_entity_refs[]     // Initiative / Theme / Wave / Opportunity the message is about
  status                   // draft | reviewed | approved | stale | retired
  staleness {
    is_stale, detected_at,
    drifted_bindings[]     // {binding_id, old_value, new_value, delta, delta_pct}
  }
  author_user_id, approved_by, approved_at
  provenance               // AISuggestion id when generated by AI-27
  is_provisional           // inherited from the bound RoadmapVersion
}
```

- **AC-900.1** `so_what` is a required field for message types `finding`, `implication` and `recommendation`. Grounded observation: the reference engagement's opportunity register carried a dedicated "So What (Why It Matters)" column, and the deck's per-initiative content was built from it. The consequence sentence is a modelled field, not an afterthought.
- **AC-900.2** A `Storyline` is an ordered set of `NarrativeMessage` records: `Storyline { id, engagement_id, name, audience_default, arc_template_id, sections[], message_order[], status, roadmap_version_id }`.
- **AC-900.3** Reordering a storyline MUST NOT change message ids. Positions are storyline properties.

**FR-901 — Value binding: ModelValueRef.** Every claim a message makes about the data MUST bind to the specific model values it claims. This is the fix for deck numbers drifting from the workbook, and the binding is the same mechanism M7's staleness impact class (FR-819) and M9's dashboards (FR-1017) rely on.

```
ModelValueRef {
  id
  entity                // Opportunity | Initiative | Theme | Wave | MaturityFocusArea
                        // | CostLineItem | Benefit | KPI | OpportunityScore | Risk | Decision
  entity_id             // nullable when the ref is an aggregate over a filter
  field_path            // e.g. "weighted_score", "cost.base", "current_level"
  aggregation           // none | sum | avg | count | share | min | max | median
  filter                // the same ScopeFilter grammar as FR-801
  scoring_model_version // when the value depends on a scoring model
  resolved_value
  resolved_at
  snapshot_id
  display_format        // e.g. "0.0", "#,##0", "0%"
  tolerance             // absolute or relative; drift within tolerance is not staleness
}
```

- **AC-901.1** Resolving a `ModelValueRef` MUST be a pure read against a named snapshot. No binding may resolve against "current" implicitly.
- **AC-901.2** `tolerance` exists so that display rounding does not generate false staleness. Default tolerance is half the least significant displayed digit.
- **AC-901.3** A binding whose `filter` returns a different row count than at authoring time MUST be reported as drifted even when the aggregate value is unchanged, because the population changed.

**FR-902 — Numerals require bindings.** The system MUST parse `headline`, `supporting_argument` and `so_what` for numerals, currency amounts, percentages and count words, and MUST refuse to move a message to status `reviewed` while any detected numeral is not covered by a `value_binding`.

- **AC-902.1** Coverage means the numeral's rendered form matches a binding's `resolved_value` under that binding's `display_format`, within tolerance.
- **AC-902.2** Numerals that are genuinely not model values (a year, a wave number, a count of workshop days) MUST be markable as literal with a one-click annotation that is recorded, not silently ignored.
- **AC-902.3** Treating count words ("four themes", "seven initiatives") as bindable is an **assumption** extending the observed practice; the reference engagement's slides carried exactly such counts, hand-typed, and one of them did not reconcile with the register.

**FR-903 — Staleness detection.** When a new snapshot is created, the system MUST re-resolve every `ModelValueRef` on every non-retired `NarrativeMessage` and every exhibit instance, and MUST set `status = stale` on any message with at least one drifted binding.

- **AC-903.1** The staleness record MUST name each drifted binding with old value, new value, absolute delta and percentage delta.
- **AC-903.2** A stale message MUST retain its previous text. The system flags; it does not silently rewrite.
- **AC-903.3** AI-30 proposes a corrected text for each stale message as an AISuggestion, with the drifted values highlighted.
- **AC-903.4** Re-resolution MUST complete for an engagement of the reference engagement's size (55 opportunities, 17 initiatives, 28 maturity focus areas, on the order of 200 messages and 40 exhibit instances) inside 10 seconds, so that the consultant sees staleness immediately after a change rather than at export time. This performance figure is an **assumption**.

**FR-904 — Storyline arc templates.** The system MUST ship reusable arc templates, and the MVP MUST include the arc the reference engagement actually used, so that a consultant starts from a known-good structure rather than a blank storyline.

The observed Day-1 findings-playback arc, generalized:

| # | Section | Message type | Typical exhibit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Why we are here, and the mandate | situation | none |
| 2 | How the fact base was built (inputs and coverage) | situation | inputs and coverage summary |
| 3 | What the interviews said, across people, process, technology, data | finding | interview theme summary |
| 4 | How we grouped the business into capability areas | situation | capability area map |
| 5 | What is working today | finding | strengths list |
| 6 | What the survey said | finding | survey results |
| 7 | How maturity was scored | situation | EX-03-style method explainer |
| 8 | Where maturity actually sits | finding | **EX-01** paginated heatmap |
| 9 | The tensions beneath the surface | implication | tensions pairing |
| 10 | Where peers have got to | finding | benchmark positioning |
| 11 | The client's own strategic goals and guiding principles | situation | goals and principles |
| 12 | Per-leader deep dives | finding | per-leader detail |
| 13 | The investment themes and how the portfolio distributes | finding | **EX-02** theme summary |
| 14 | The three-level taxonomy | situation | taxonomy explainer |
| 15 | How opportunities were scored and weighted | situation | **EX-03** scoring explainer |
| 16 | Theme by theme, what is in it | finding | **EX-04** per-theme initiative slide |
| 17 | The whole portfolio in one picture | implication | **EX-05** opportunity landscape |
| 18 | The initiative summary across all themes | finding | initiative summary matrix |
| 19 | What has to be true for any of this to work | recommendation | foundational elements |
| 20 | What happens next | ask | **EX-09** themes and next steps |

- **AC-904.1** Applying a template MUST create placeholder messages with the section, type and suggested exhibit pre-set, and MUST leave every headline empty for authoring or AI-27 proposal.
- **AC-904.2** Templates are editable per firm. The arc above is a starting structure derived from one observed engagement and MUST NOT be enforced.

**Board-level message generation**

**FR-905 — Headline generation.** AI-27 MUST propose a bounded set of board-level headline messages from the model, each as an AISuggestion carrying a headline, a supporting argument, its value bindings, its evidence, and the message type.

- **AC-905.1** The proposal set MUST default to between 5 and 7 headlines for a board audience. That range is an **assumption**; it is bounded because a board narrative that asserts twenty things asserts nothing.
- **AC-905.2** Every proposed headline MUST arrive with at least one `ModelValueRef` and at least one `EvidenceRef`. A proposal with neither MUST be rejected by the system before it reaches the consultant.
- **AC-905.3** Inputs to AI-27 MUST be the structured model, not prose: theme distribution, weighted scores by band, maturity gaps by capability area, cost by year, benefit by year, dependency chains constraining Wave 1, open decisions, and top risks by exposure.

**FR-906 — KeyMessage, TradeOff and Ask as distinct objects.** The methodology asks for Board-ready headlines, key messages, key decisions and asks. Each MUST be a distinct addressable object, not a formatting variant.

```
TradeOff {                          // NarrativeMessage of type trade_off
  id, message_id
  option_a { label, what_you_gain, what_you_give_up, modelled_effect_ref }
  option_b { label, what_you_gain, what_you_give_up, modelled_effect_ref }
  recommendation                    // which, and why
  linked_decision_id                // the Decision this trade-off resolves or presents
  value_bindings[]
}

Ask {                               // NarrativeMessage of type ask
  id, message_id
  ask_statement                     // what we need from this body
  ask_type                          // funding | decision | resource | mandate | governance
  amount, amount_binding            // where the ask is financial
  by_when
  decision_id                       // the open Decision it unblocks
  consequence_of_no_decision        // bound to the value_case_shift / risk exposure
  owner_stakeholder_id
}
```

- **AC-906.1** Every `Ask` MUST link to an open `Decision` or create one. An ask with no decision behind it is a wish.
- **AC-906.2** Every `TradeOff`'s `modelled_effect_ref` MUST point at a real `RoadmapScenario` or `ImpactReport`, so that "what you give up" is a computed figure rather than a rhetorical one.
- **AC-906.3** `consequence_of_no_decision` MUST bind to a model value: the delay cost from FR-818, the risk exposure from FR-1019, or the capacity breach from FR-816.
- **AC-906.4** The board storyline MUST be renderable as a decisions-and-asks summary listing every `Ask` with amount, by-when and consequence.

**FR-907 — Message approval.** A `NarrativeMessage` MUST move draft → reviewed → approved, with `reviewed` blocked by FR-902 numeral coverage and `approved` recording the approver and timestamp. A stale message MUST drop out of `approved`.

**Exhibit generation**

**FR-908 — Exhibit registry.** Exhibits MUST be defined as registry entries that carry a model query, required inputs, a rendering specification and a pagination rule, and MUST be instantiated by execution against a snapshot. An exhibit is never a drawing with typed numbers.

```
ExhibitType {
  code, name, description
  model_query               // declarative: entities, filter, grouping, aggregations, sort
  required_inputs[]         // entity + field list; missing input blocks instantiation
  rendering                 // table | heatmap_table | bubble_chart | stacked_bar
                            // | gantt_lanes | card_grid | matrix | positioning_table | prose_block
  phase                     // methodology phase the exhibit belongs to
  pagination_rule
  caption_template
  min_data_requirements
  geometry_variants[]       // which template geometries it can render into
}

ExhibitInstance {
  id, exhibit_type_code, deliverable_id, storyline_position
  snapshot_id, resolved_data, value_bindings[]
  caption, caption_provenance
  page_index, rendered_at
}
```

**FR-909 — MVP exhibit set.** The system MUST implement the following nine exhibit types, derived from what the reference engagement actually produced.

| Code | Name | Inputs | Rendering | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EX-01 | Paginated maturity heatmap | `CapabilityArea` (8), `MaturityFocusArea` (28) with current level, target level, gap, scoring rationale; CMMI level label set (1 Initial, 2 Managed, 3 Defined, 4 Quantitatively Managed, 5 Optimizing) | Heatmap table: Technology Function, Focus Area, Rating band with current and target markers, Scoring Rationale; legend row carrying the 5 level labels and a current-state average marker | Weeks 3-4 |
| EX-02 | Theme summary with counts and shares | `Theme` (4) with name and definition paragraph; `Opportunity` count per theme; total opportunity count | Horizontal distribution bar with count and integer percentage share per theme, plus theme definition blocks | Weeks 3-4 |
| EX-03 | Three-dimension scoring explainer | `ScoringModel` with `ScoreDimension` name, definition, weight (0.40 / 0.35 / 0.25), and the score-5 and score-1 anchor text from the rubric | Three weight cards, each with dimension name, definition, and the top and bottom anchor examples | Weeks 3-4 |
| EX-04 | Per-theme initiative slide | One `Theme`; its `Initiative` set with name, average weighted score to one decimal, and the `Opportunity` names under each | Table of Initiative, average weighted score, opportunities, with a proportional score bar per initiative, sorted score descending | Weeks 3-4 |
| EX-05 | Opportunity landscape bubble chart | Per `Opportunity`: business value X = (alignment + financial) / 2, urgency Y = risk score, bubble size = weighted score, series = theme; quadrant threshold 3.5; horizon bucket labels | Bubble chart with quadrant gridlines at 3.5 on both axes, one series per theme, plus side lists of item names grouped by horizon bucket with counts | Weeks 3-4 |
| EX-06 | Wave-based roadmap timeline | `Wave` (1-4) boundaries; `RoadmapItem` per wave with name, t-shirt size, owner; `Dependency` edges; `Milestone` dates | Swimlane timeline, one lane per wave or per workstream, dependency arrows, milestone diamonds | Week 5 |
| EX-07 | Investment profile by year | `CostLineItem` aggregated by year and cost type, with low / base / high range; capex and opex split; run / grow / transform split where present | Stacked bars per year with a range whisker on the total, plus a table of the same figures | Weeks 6-8 |
| EX-08 | Per-initiative mobilization slide | One `Initiative` flagged for near-term mobilization; its why-it-matters statement, first 60-90 day workstreams each with activities and named deliverables, value-created statement, execution squads by domain, takeaway line, `ActivationTask` set | Card grid: why-it-matters banner, parallel workstream columns each with activities and a deliverables list, value-created banner, squad row, takeaway bar | Weeks 10-12 |
| EX-09 | Themes and next steps summary | 4-6 `FeedbackTheme` or narrative themes with a paragraph each; ordered next steps with owner and by-when; provisionality statement | Prose block: theme headings with paragraphs, then a numbered next-steps list, then the provisionality statement | Weeks 10-12 |

- **AC-909.1** EX-01 pagination rule: paginate at 10 table rows per page and never split a `CapabilityArea` across pages unless that single area exceeds one page. Grounded observation: the reference engagement's 28 focus areas across 8 capability areas rendered as a 4-page heatmap.
- **AC-909.2** EX-02 MUST compute counts and shares from the register, never accept typed values, and MUST assert that shares sum to 100 after rounding. Grounded observation: the reference engagement's theme-distribution slide carried counts of 13, 16, 19 and 8 summing to 56, with shares 23, 29, 34 and 14 percent, while the register held 43 technology plus 12 operating-model opportunities, a total of 55. The exhibit MUST make that class of error impossible by construction, and MUST state which population it counted (technology only, operating model only, or both).
- **AC-909.3** EX-04 MUST compute the per-initiative average from its member opportunity scores at render time. Grounded observation: in the reference engagement the per-theme slides carried initiative averages to one decimal (for example 4.2, 3.8, 3.7, 3.2, 2.5) as typed text next to an empty "Avg Weight" table column.
- **AC-909.4** EX-05 MUST read the quadrant threshold and the axis formulae from the active `ScoringModel`, and MUST report any quadrant with zero members as an informational note rather than drawing an empty labelled region without comment. Grounded observation: one of the four quadrants in the reference engagement's model was unreachable given the axis definitions and never contained an item.
- **AC-909.5** EX-05 MUST use exactly one canonical vocabulary for horizon buckets, read from the engagement's configuration. Grounded observation: the reference engagement used three different names for the same third bucket across its workbook and decks.
- **AC-909.6** EX-08 MUST generate one instance per `Initiative` where wave = 1 and `near_term_mobilization = true`. Grounded observation: the reference engagement's execution-planning deck carried exactly this shape, one slide per initiative, for seven initiatives, preceded by a single summary table of Priority, Immediate Readiness Focus and Expertise Required.
- **AC-909.7** Every exhibit instance MUST record its `value_bindings[]` so that FR-903 staleness applies to exhibits exactly as it applies to messages.
- **AC-909.8** An exhibit whose `min_data_requirements` are unmet MUST fail to instantiate with a message naming the missing input, and MUST NOT render a partial or placeholder version into a deliverable.

**FR-910 — Deferred exhibit types.** The following exhibits were observed in the reference engagement but are out of MVP scope. They MUST be registrable later without a schema change, and are listed here so the engineering agent does not treat the nine above as the complete universe.

| Code | Name | Observed as |
|---|---|---|
| EX-D1 | Benchmark positioning table | Capability rows with a lagging-to-leading axis, a current-position marker, a north-star comparator and attribute text |
| EX-D2 | Survey results and tension pairing | Aggregated survey scores, plus paired-tension blocks with an explanatory "what this means" panel |
| EX-D3 | Foundational elements grid | Numbered prerequisite cards, each with a title and a consequence-of-absence sentence |
| EX-D4 | Interview theme summary | Themes grouped across people, process, technology and data |

**FR-911 — Exhibit captions.** AI-28 MUST propose a caption per exhibit instance that states what the exhibit shows and what the reader should conclude, bound to the exhibit's own values. Captions follow propose → review → commit.

**FR-912 — No typed numbers in exhibits.** The exhibit renderer MUST NOT expose any field into which a user can type a numeric value that appears in the rendered output. Annotations and labels are text; figures come from the query.

**Deck generation to PowerPoint**

**FR-913 — Deliverable assembly.** The system MUST assemble a `Deliverable` from a template, a selected storyline, an audience level and a resolved exhibit set, and MUST export it to .pptx.

```
Deliverable {
  id, engagement_id
  name
  deliverable_type        // workshop_deck | board_deck | execution_planning_deck
                          // | maturity_deck | written_narrative | activation_plan | review_pack
  template_id
  storyline_id
  audience_level          // board | exec_committee | technology_leadership
  exhibit_instance_ids[]
  slide_map[]             // {slide_index, source: message_id | exhibit_instance_id | template_static}
  roadmap_version_id, snapshot_id, model_version
  scoring_model_version
  numbers_manifest        // see FR-915
  validation_result_id
  confidentiality_result_id
  override_record_id      // nullable
  is_provisional
  exported_at, exported_by, file_uri, checksum
  distribution_list[]     // stakeholder_ids, required for issued deliverables
  status                  // draft | validated | exported | issued | superseded | stale
}
```

**FR-914 — Template binding by name.** A .pptx template MUST declare named placeholders, and the generator MUST bind content to placeholder names rather than to slide positions or shape indices.

- **AC-914.1** Grounded observation: the reference engagement's decks used consistent named shapes and placeholders, including title placeholders, subtitle text placeholders, a takeaway bar, numbered card headers with key-action and expected-outcome sub-blocks, and legend text. Those names are the binding contract.
- **AC-914.2** A template missing a placeholder that the assigned exhibit or message requires MUST fail validation at build time, naming the template, the slide layout and the missing placeholder.
- **AC-914.3** Templates MUST declare page geometry, and exhibits MUST be geometry-aware. Grounded observation: the reference engagement's workshop deck was authored on a 10.0 by 5.63 inch canvas while its execution-planning deck was authored on a 13.3 by 7.5 inch canvas. An exhibit built for one geometry rendered into the other without adaptation produces overflow.

**FR-915 — Provenance and numbers manifest.** Every export MUST record exactly which model version and snapshot it was built from, and MUST persist a numbers manifest.

- **AC-915.1** The manifest MUST list every `ModelValueRef` used anywhere in the deliverable with its `field_path`, `filter`, `resolved_value`, `display_format` and the slide index where it appears.
- **AC-915.2** The manifest MUST be retrievable for any historic export, so that "where did this number on slide 14 come from" is answerable a year later.
- **AC-915.3** The exported file MUST carry the snapshot label and export timestamp in a footer or notes field on every slide.

**FR-916 — Regeneration diff.** Regenerating a `Deliverable` against a newer snapshot MUST produce a diff report before the new file is issued.

- **AC-916.1** The report MUST contain: every number that changed, with slide index, old value, new value, absolute and percentage delta; every message whose text changed, as a text diff; every exhibit whose underlying data points changed, with the changed rows or series enumerated; and slides added or removed.
- **AC-916.2** The report MUST be exportable alongside the deck, because the first question a recipient of version 2 asks is what changed.
- **AC-916.3** Regeneration MUST NOT silently overwrite the prior export. Prior exports are immutable and remain retrievable with their manifests.

**FR-917 — Native chart objects.** Where an exhibit's rendering is a chart, the generator SHOULD emit a native PowerPoint chart with its data table embedded, rather than a raster image, so that the recipient can inspect the values.

- **AC-917.1** Grounded observation: the reference engagement's decks contained a native bubble chart carrying per-theme series values, alongside a third-party charting add-in's embedded data objects. Emitting native charts is what preserves inspectability; requiring it for all chart exhibits in the MVP is an **assumption** and MAY be relaxed to raster for `gantt_lanes` and `heatmap_table`.

**Audience tailoring**

**FR-918 — Three detail levels.** The same storyline MUST be renderable at three audience levels, each with an explicit and enforced rule for what is dropped.

| Level | Slide budget | Message types kept | Exhibits kept | Explicitly dropped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Board** | 12-15 | situation, implication, recommendation, ask, trade_off | EX-02, EX-05 (quadrant summary only, item lists suppressed), EX-06 (wave level, no item detail), EX-07, EX-09 | Method explainers (EX-03), the maturity heatmap detail (EX-01 reduced to one summary row per capability area), per-theme initiative detail (EX-04), per-leader deep dives, per-opportunity rows, workshop facilitation material, scoring rubric anchors |
| **Executive committee** | 20-25 | all board types plus finding, risk, proof_point | Board set plus EX-01 (paginated), EX-04, EX-08, plus decisions-and-asks summary and next-steps timeline | Scoring rubric anchor detail (EX-03), the full opportunity register, workshop activity instructions, firm qualifications |
| **Technology leadership** | 60-70 | all message types | All nine exhibits at full detail, plus deferred exhibits where registered | Nothing on the basis of level; only items explicitly excluded per deliverable |

- **AC-918.1** The three budgets are grounded in the reference engagement's own artefacts: a 67-slide two-day workshop deck for technology leadership and the wider leadership group, a 23-slide execution-planning deck for the executive audience, and a 2-page written recap. The board level is interpolated below the 23-slide deck and its 12-15 range is an **assumption**.
- **AC-918.2** Exceeding the level's slide budget MUST produce a warning naming the slides above budget and ranked by lowest message priority, not a silent truncation.
- **AC-918.3** The drop rules MUST be declarative configuration per level, editable per firm, not hard-coded in the renderer.

**FR-919 — Audience rewriting.** AI-29 MUST propose level-appropriate rewrites of each retained message: shorter and more consequence-led for board, more mechanism-detail for technology leadership.

- **AC-919.1** A rewrite MUST NOT change any bound value, MUST NOT introduce an unbound numeral, and MUST NOT drop an `EvidenceRef`. The system MUST reject a rewrite suggestion that violates any of these before it reaches the consultant.
- **AC-919.2** Rewrites are AISuggestions against the message, and an accepted rewrite creates a level-specific text variant rather than overwriting the canonical message text: `MessageVariant { message_id, audience_level, headline, supporting_argument, so_what, provenance, approved_by }`.
