| Class | Capabilities | Target acceptance | Target edit rate ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Mechanical extraction and drafting | AI-02, AI-03, AI-04, AI-05 | >= 0.85 | 0.20 |
| B. Synthesis and grouping | AI-01, AI-06, AI-07, AI-08, AI-10, AI-12 | >= 0.70 | 0.35 |
| C. Rubric-bound judgement | AI-09, AI-11, AI-13, AI-14 | >= 0.60 | 0.45 |
| D. Generative options and narrative | AI-15, AI-16, AI-17 | >= 0.65 | 0.50 |

A capability below its class target for two consecutive engagements is demoted: bulk accept is disabled and it is flagged in the queue as "calibrating".

#### 8.1.8 The loop

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Consultant
    participant ING as Ingest and Index
    participant REPO as Evidence Repository
    participant LIB as Precedent Library
    participant CAP as AI Capability
    participant Q as Review Queue
    participant CALC as Calculation Engine
    participant AUD as Audit Log

    C->>ING: upload SourceDocument / Interview recording
    ING->>ING: chunk, content-address, PII classify, injection envelope
    ING->>REPO: store chunks and locators
    ING->>CAP: trigger eligible capabilities
    CAP->>REPO: retrieve scoped to engagement_id
    CAP->>LIB: retrieve anonymised precedent (cross-engagement claims only)
    CAP->>CAP: k-sample, build payload, derive per-field confidence
    alt citation floor met
        CAP->>Q: AISuggestion (proposed) + RetrievalManifest
    else citation floor not met
        CAP->>Q: AISuggestion (insufficient_evidence) -> Charter backlog
    end
    C->>Q: review with evidence drawer
    alt accept or edit
        Q->>CALC: commit transaction carrying suggestion_id
        CALC->>CALC: recompute gap, weighted score, band, quadrant, graph checks
        CALC->>Q: mark dependent suggestions stale
        CALC->>AUD: AuditEvent (before, after, edit_diff)
    else reject
        Q->>AUD: AuditEvent (rejected, reason)
    end
    AUD->>CAP: feed acceptance, edit distance, calibration metrics
```

### 8.2 AI-01 Document set synthesis and information gap identification

**Purpose.** Read the initial document drop at kickoff, produce a structured synthesis of what the materials establish, and produce a ranked register of what is missing before the fact base can be built. Methodology row: Week 0 Kickoff + Mobilization, AI Enhancement "Synthesize initial materials; identify missing information".

**Trigger.** Runs when a consultant marks the Week 0 document drop as complete, and re-runs incrementally whenever a `SourceDocument` is added while `Engagement.phase == "week_0"`. Manually re-runnable at any time.

**Input contract.**

| Input | Detail |
|---|---|
| `SourceDocument[]` | `id, filename, mime_type, page_or_slide_count, ingest_status, classification (strategy \| project_list \| application_landscape \| budget \| org_chart \| architecture \| prior_assessment \| vendor \| policy \| other), chunk_ids` |
| `Charter` (draft) | `objectives[], scope_in[], scope_out[], strategic_objectives[] (name, description), success_criteria[]` if already captured at kickoff |
| Required-input checklist | The methodology's declared Weeks 1-2 input list, seeded as a template: interviews, surveys, strategy decks, project lists, application landscape, budgets, org charts, architecture, vendor information, prior assessments, firm historical work. |
| `MaturityFocusArea[]` template | The 28-focus-area, 8-capability-area default scaffold from the precedent library, used to test document coverage per focus area. |
| Retrieval scope | This engagement only. Precedent library used only to retrieve the expected-document profile for comparable engagements, never to assert a fact about this client. |
| Limits | Max 400 chunks retrieved per invocation, 180k prompt tokens. Documents are summarised hierarchically (chunk summary, then document summary, then corpus synthesis) when the corpus exceeds the budget. `RetrievalManifest.truncated` must be set when any document is excluded. |

**What the model must determine.**

1. For each `SourceDocument`, a one-paragraph statement of what it establishes and its classification, with the page or slide range that carries the substance.
2. Corpus-level synthesis: the organisation's declared strategy, the named strategic objectives it contains, the in-flight major programs it names, and the technology estate it describes, each as discrete claims with evidence.
3. Which of the 8 capability areas and 28 focus areas have documentary coverage, which have partial coverage, and which have none.
4. The information gap register: for each required input in the checklist and each uncovered focus area, whether it is absent, stale (document date older than the engagement's staleness threshold, default 18 months), or contradicted by another document.
5. Ranked criticality of each gap on a three-level enum `blocking | important | nice_to_have`, where `blocking` means a downstream phase deliverable cannot be produced without it.
6. Initial hypotheses: candidate propositions about the organisation that the fact base should test, each stated so that it can be falsified, each with the evidence that suggested it.
7. For each gap, the collection route: document request, interview topic, survey question, or benchmark purchase.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type AI01Payload = {
  document_summaries: {
    source_document_id: string
    classification: string
    establishes: string              // <= 600 chars
    substantive_locator: string      // "slides 4-11" | "pp. 2-6" | "sheet 'Assessment'!A7:M35"
    quality_flags: ("undated" | "draft" | "superseded_by" | "empty" | "other_client_content")[]
    superseded_by_source_document_id: string | null
  }[]
  corpus_synthesis: {
    declared_strategy: { statement: string, evidence: EvidenceRef[] }[]
    strategic_objectives_found: { name: string, description: string, evidence: EvidenceRef[] }[]
    in_flight_programs: { name: string, stated_status: string, evidence: EvidenceRef[] }[]
    estate_observations: { statement: string, capability_area: string, evidence: EvidenceRef[] }[]
  }
  coverage: {
    capability_area: string
    focus_area: string
    coverage: "none" | "partial" | "adequate"
    covering_source_document_ids: string[]
  }[]
  gaps: {
    gap_id: string
    required_input: string           // from the checklist, or "focus area coverage: <focus area>"
    state: "absent" | "stale" | "contradicted"
    criticality: "blocking" | "important" | "nice_to_have"
    blocks: string[]                 // deliverable or phase identifiers
    collection_route: "document_request" | "interview_topic" | "survey_question" | "benchmark"
    suggested_owner_role: string     // role, never a person name
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]          // for "stale" and "contradicted"; may be empty for "absent"
  }[]
  hypotheses: {
    statement: string                // falsifiable
    falsification_test: string
    capability_areas: string[]
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]
  }[]
}
```

**Confidence and evidence.** `evidence_sufficiency` for a document summary requires at least one `EvidenceRef` into that document. For a `contradicted` gap it requires at least two refs from different `source_id`s. For an `absent` gap, evidence is not required and confidence is instead the completeness of the checklist match, which is deterministic, so absent-gap items carry `confidence: 1.0` and are the bulk-acceptable subset. Hypotheses require at least two `EvidenceRef`s from at least two distinct documents, otherwise they abstain. `rubric_fit` is 1.0 except for `criticality`, which is scored against the anchor definitions and reported in `field_confidence["gaps[i].criticality"]`.

**Human actions available.** Accept, edit, reject per item. Bulk accept the `gaps` array where `state == "absent"`. Capability-specific: **promote gap to Charter** (writes a `Charter` document-request or interview-plan line), **merge duplicate gaps**, **mark document as superseded** (which restricts later retrieval to the superseding document), **quarantine document** for the observed case of another client's slides sitting inside a working deck, and **re-run with hint** to focus on a named capability area.

**Downstream dependencies on commit.**

- `Charter.document_requests[]` and `Charter.interview_plan_topics[]` are populated, which is the input to AI-02 and AI-03.
- `Charter.hypotheses[]` are created, which AI-06 later tests against clustered findings and which AI-07 uses as a contradiction target set.
- `Charter.strategic_objectives[]` are seeded. This matters more than it looks: AI-13's Strategic Alignment dimension can only score above the lowest anchor by tracing to one of these objectives.
- `SourceDocument.classification` and `superseded_by` change retrieval eligibility for every later capability.
- The coverage matrix drives the Week 0 readiness gate: an engagement with any `blocking` gap open cannot advance its phase without an override recorded in `AuditEvent`.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

| Failure mode | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Another client's material inside a working deck is synthesised as if it were this client's estate. Observed directly in the reference engagement, where a working deck carried a 10-slide reusable section holding a different client's platform estate. | Cross-document entity-consistency check: organisation names, brand names, and platform names appearing in fewer than a threshold share of documents are flagged. Any document section whose named organisation differs from `Engagement.client_display_name` is emitted as `quality_flags: ["other_client_content"]` and excluded from `corpus_synthesis` until a consultant clears it. |
| Zero-byte, placeholder, or unparseable files are silently skipped and the corpus looks more complete than it is. Observed as an empty placeholder deck in the reference file set. | Ingest emits an explicit `quality_flags: ["empty"]` document summary rather than dropping the file. Coverage counts never include unparseable documents. `RetrievalManifest.truncated` is set. |
| Hallucinated gaps: the model invents required inputs that are not on the checklist, inflating the request list and damaging client trust at kickoff. | `gaps[].required_input` is constrained to the checklist enum plus the generated `focus area coverage: <name>` form validated against the 28-focus-area list. Free-text required inputs are rejected by schema validation. |
| A stale document is treated as current because it carries no date. | `quality_flags: ["undated"]` forces `state: "stale"` unless a consultant sets an effective date. Undated documents may not be the sole evidence for a `corpus_synthesis` claim. |

**Acceptance test.** Load the reference-engagement fixture with the following planted conditions: one zero-byte file, one deck containing a foreign-client section, one strategy document dated 30 months before the engagement start, and the required-input checklist with interviews, surveys, and budgets deliberately absent from the corpus. Assert that: (1) the zero-byte file produces a summary row with `quality_flags` containing `empty` and contributes to no coverage cell; (2) the foreign-client section is flagged `other_client_content` and none of its platform names appear in `corpus_synthesis.estate_observations`; (3) the 30-month-old document yields `state: "stale"`; (4) `gaps` contains `absent` entries for interviews, surveys, and budgets, each with `criticality: "blocking"` and a non-empty `blocks` array; (5) every `hypotheses[i]` has at least two `EvidenceRef`s from two distinct `source_id`s; (6) no `gaps[].required_input` value falls outside the permitted enum; (7) accepting the gap register writes the corresponding `Charter` request lines and one `AuditEvent` per gap.

### 8.3 AI-02 Stakeholder identification and interview-coverage suggestion

**Purpose.** Propose the stakeholders who must be interviewed and detect where the planned interview set leaves a capability area, a business function, or an in-flight program without a voice. Methodology row: Week 0, AI Enhancement "suggest stakeholders".

**Trigger.** On commit of AI-01 output, on upload or edit of an org chart, on any change to `Charter.scope_in[]`, and on any change to the `Interview` plan. Re-runs as a coverage check whenever an `Interview` is scheduled, completed, or cancelled.

**Input contract.**

| Input | Detail |
|---|---|
| `SourceDocument` subset | Documents classified `org_chart`, `project_list`, `strategy`, `application_landscape`, `vendor`. Chunks only. |
| `Stakeholder[]` | Existing rows: `id, role_title, function, capability_areas[], seniority (c_level \| evp_svp \| vp \| director \| manager \| ic), is_client_sponsor, source_evidence[]` |
| `Interview[]` | `id, stakeholder_id, planned_date, status (planned \| completed \| declined \| cancelled), duration_minutes, topics[]` |
| `Charter` | `scope_in[], scope_out[], objectives[], strategic_objectives[], hypotheses[]` |
| `CapabilityArea[]` / `MaturityFocusArea[]` | The 8 and 28 respectively, to test coverage. |
| `Initiative`-like in-flight programs | From AI-01 `in_flight_programs`, to test program-owner coverage. |
| Precedent library | The interview-shape profile for comparable engagements: typical counts by seniority tier and the set of roles that were interviewed. Anonymised role titles only. |
| Limits | Max 150 chunks, 60k prompt tokens. Org chart images must be OCR'd at ingest; the capability does not receive raw images. |

**What the model must determine.**

1. Candidate stakeholders as **roles**, not names, each mapped to the capability areas and focus areas they own, with the evidence that establishes ownership.
2. For each candidate, an interview priority `must_interview | should_interview | optional` and the specific reason: sole owner of a focus area, owner of an in-flight program, named in a hypothesis, holds a decision right, or represents a business function inside scope.
3. Coverage gaps against three axes: capability area coverage, business function coverage, and seniority coverage. A gap is a cell with no `must_interview` stakeholder in a planned or completed `Interview`.
4. Single-point-of-view risk: any focus area whose only planned voice is one stakeholder, which makes later contradiction detection impossible for that area.
5. Suggested interview format per candidate: leadership interview, functional deep dive, or survey-only. The reference engagement's shape was 5 leadership interviews across core technology domains plus 10 functional deep dives, and the precedent library supplies this ratio as a comparison point rather than a target.
6. Where a role appears to be vacant or unfilled, flag it, because an unfilled owner role is itself a finding and cannot be interviewed.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type AI02Payload = {
  candidate_stakeholders: {
    role_title: string                     // role only, never a person name
    function: string
    seniority: "c_level" | "evp_svp" | "vp" | "director" | "manager" | "ic"
    owns_capability_areas: string[]
    owns_focus_areas: string[]
    owns_programs: string[]
    priority: "must_interview" | "should_interview" | "optional"
    reason: "sole_focus_area_owner" | "program_owner" | "named_in_hypothesis"
          | "decision_right_holder" | "in_scope_business_function" | "precedent_pattern"
    suggested_format: "leadership_interview" | "functional_deep_dive" | "survey_only"
    role_status: "filled" | "vacant" | "unknown"
    matched_existing_stakeholder_id: string | null
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]
  }[]
  coverage_gaps: {
    axis: "capability_area" | "business_function" | "seniority"
    key: string
    state: "no_voice" | "single_voice" | "junior_only"
    affected_focus_areas: string[]
    recommended_action: string
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]
  }[]
  plan_shape: {
    planned_leadership_interviews: number       // computed by engine, passed in and echoed
    planned_functional_deep_dives: number
    precedent_median_leadership: number | null
    precedent_median_deep_dives: number | null
  }
}
```

**Confidence and evidence.** A candidate requires at least one `EvidenceRef` establishing the role exists and at least one establishing ownership. Where the role exists but ownership is inferred from the precedent pattern alone, `reason` must be `precedent_pattern`, the evidence must carry `source_type: "prior_engagement"`, and `confidence` is capped at 0.55 so that it lands in the low band and cannot be bulk-accepted. `coverage_gaps` with `state: "no_voice"` are deterministic set differences and carry `confidence: 1.0`. `field_confidence` is reported for `priority`, `owns_focus_areas`, and `role_status` separately, because role existence is usually well evidenced while focus-area ownership frequently is not.

**Human actions available.** Accept, edit, reject. Bulk accept high-confidence candidates and coverage gaps. Capability-specific: **link candidate to an existing `Stakeholder`** rather than creating a duplicate, **split** a candidate role that the model fused (one row proposing "VP infrastructure and security" becomes two), **merge** two candidates that are the same role under different titles, **convert to survey-only**, and **mark role vacant**, which routes the item to the `Finding` backlog instead of the interview plan.

**Downstream dependencies on commit.**

- Creates or updates `Stakeholder` rows and `Interview` plan rows in `Charter.interview_plan`.
- Interview coverage is an input to AI-03, which tailors each guide to the stakeholder's owned focus areas.
- `single_voice` flags cap `source_agreement` for AI-09 proposals on the affected focus areas, so a maturity level resting on one voice cannot present as high confidence.
- Vacant-role flags become candidate `Finding` rows and frequently become `Opportunity` records under organisational enablement, which is the pattern in the reference engagement where multiple unfilled leadership roles were themselves scored opportunities.
- `KPI`-style engagement health: interview coverage percentage by capability area is reported on the engagement dashboard.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

| Failure mode | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| The model proposes person names lifted from an org chart, creating a personal-data leak into a client-facing interview plan. | Schema forbids a `person_name` field. A validator rejects any `role_title` matching the person-name detector or matching a value in the restricted `Stakeholder` name column. Names live only in the restricted table and are attached by the consultant at scheduling time. |
| Duplicate stakeholders accumulate because the same role is titled differently across an org chart and a project list. | `matched_existing_stakeholder_id` is computed by a deterministic matcher (normalised title, function, seniority) before the model runs, and the model may not propose a candidate whose match score exceeds the merge threshold. The queue shows the match for confirmation. |
| Over-proposal: the model suggests 60 interviews, which is unschedulable, and the consultant abandons the capability. | Hard cap of `must_interview` candidates at the number of focus areas with `no_voice` plus program count. Everything else must be `should_interview` or `optional`. The queue sorts by priority and shows a running total of proposed interview hours against a configured Week 0 capacity. |
| Coverage looks complete because a declined or cancelled interview still counts. | Coverage arithmetic counts only `status in (planned, completed)`. A transition to `declined` or `cancelled` re-triggers the capability and marks any dependent AI-09 suggestion stale. |

**Acceptance test.** Seed a fixture with an org chart naming 12 roles across 8 capability areas, a project list naming 5 in-flight programs, an interview plan containing 5 leadership interviews and 10 functional deep dives, and two deliberate holes: no planned interview touching one capability area, and exactly one planned interview touching a second. Assert that: (1) `coverage_gaps` contains a `no_voice` row for the first area and a `single_voice` row for the second; (2) no `role_title` contains a person name from the fixture; (3) every `must_interview` candidate has at least two `EvidenceRef`s; (4) candidates whose only justification is the precedent pattern carry `confidence <= 0.55` and are excluded from bulk accept; (5) cancelling one of the 15 planned interviews re-runs the capability and produces a new `no_voice` or `single_voice` row within the same engagement; (6) a candidate that deterministically matches an existing `Stakeholder` is emitted with `matched_existing_stakeholder_id` populated and does not create a second row on accept.

### 8.4 AI-03 Tailored interview guide generation

**Purpose.** Generate a per-stakeholder interview guide whose questions are specific to that stakeholder's owned focus areas, the engagement hypotheses, and the gaps AI-01 identified, so the interview collects the evidence the later maturity and scoring work will require. Methodology row: Week 0, AI Enhancement "generate tailored interview guides".

**Trigger.** On creation or update of an `Interview` with `status: "planned"`. Re-runs when the stakeholder's owned focus areas change, when `Charter.hypotheses` change, or when a prior interview produces a contradiction that this stakeholder can resolve.

**Input contract.**

| Input | Detail |
|---|---|
| `Stakeholder` | `role_title, function, seniority, owns_capability_areas[], owns_focus_areas[]` |
| `Interview` | `duration_minutes, planned_date, format (leadership_interview \| functional_deep_dive)` |
| `Charter` | `objectives[], strategic_objectives[], hypotheses[] (statement, falsification_test)`, `document_requests[]` |
| AI-01 gaps | Open `gaps` where `collection_route == "interview_topic"` and the gap's focus areas intersect this stakeholder's owned focus areas. |
| `MaturityFocusArea[]` | For each owned focus area: name, definition, and the level-definition text for all five levels, so questions can be written to discriminate between adjacent levels. |
| `Finding[]` and open contradictions | Findings already committed for the owned focus areas, and any `AI-07` contradiction whose parties include this stakeholder's function. |
| Precedent library | Anonymised question banks by focus area from prior engagements, with their historical evidence yield. |
| Limits | Max 120 chunks, 50k prompt tokens. Guide length is bounded by `duration_minutes`: budget 4 minutes per primary question including follow-ups, reserve 10 minutes for opening and close. |

**What the model must determine.**

1. A question set sized to the interview duration, allocated across the stakeholder's owned focus areas in proportion to how many open gaps and untested hypotheses each carries.
2. For each question: which focus area it probes, which maturity level boundary it is designed to discriminate (for example a question that separates level 2 from level 3 by asking whether a process is documented organisation-wide or only per project), and which gap or hypothesis it serves.
3. Follow-up probes for each primary question, written to elicit the specific evidence types that later capabilities need: named systems, counts, frequencies, ownership, documentation existence, and consequence of failure.
4. Questions that will produce the evidence AI-13 needs, distinguished by dimension: financial consequence questions, consequence-of-deferral questions, and questions that trace work to a named strategic objective from the Charter.
5. Contradiction-resolution questions where an open contradiction touches this stakeholder's area, phrased neutrally so the interview does not accuse a colleague.
6. Sensitivity flags: questions touching security incidents, personnel, or vendor disputes must be flagged so the consultant can decide whether to ask them and how.
7. Explicit out-of-scope note per guide, drawn from `Charter.scope_out`, so the interviewer can redirect.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type AI03Payload = {
  interview_id: string
  guide: {
    opening: string                        // <= 500 chars, states purpose and confidentiality
    time_budget_minutes: number
    sections: {
      capability_area: string
      focus_areas: string[]
      allocated_minutes: number
      questions: {
        question_id: string
        text: string
        probes: string[]                   // 1-4 follow-ups
        purpose: "level_discrimination" | "gap_fill" | "hypothesis_test"
               | "contradiction_resolution" | "financial_evidence"
               | "deferral_risk_evidence" | "strategic_traceability"
        discriminates_levels: [number, number] | null   // e.g. [2,3]
        serves_gap_ids: string[]
        serves_hypothesis_ids: string[]
        expected_evidence_type: ("named_system" | "count" | "frequency" | "owner"
                               | "document_existence" | "consequence" | "date")[]
        sensitivity: "none" | "personnel" | "security_incident" | "vendor" | "financial"
      }[]
    }[]
    closing: string                        // ask for documents and referrals
    out_of_scope_note: string
    document_asks: string[]                // drawn from open document_requests
  }
  coverage_assertion: {
    owned_focus_areas: string[]
    focus_areas_covered_by_questions: string[]
    uncovered_focus_areas: string[]        // must be empty or explained
    open_gaps_addressed: string[]
    open_gaps_not_addressed: string[]
  }
}
```

**Confidence and evidence.** Evidence requirements here differ from other capabilities because the output is an artefact rather than a claim. Mandatory: every question with `purpose in (gap_fill, hypothesis_test, contradiction_resolution)` must carry the identifier of the gap, hypothesis, or contradiction it serves, and those identifiers are validated against live records. Every `level_discrimination` question must cite the `MaturityFocusArea` level-definition text it discriminates as an `EvidenceRef` with `source_type: "workbook"` or `"prior_engagement"`. Confidence is dominated by `evidence_sufficiency` measured as the share of the stakeholder's owned focus areas covered by at least one question, and `rubric_fit` measured as the share of `level_discrimination` questions whose target boundary is justified by the level definitions. A guide with `uncovered_focus_areas` non-empty cannot exceed the medium band.

**Human actions available.** Accept, edit, reject the guide as a whole or per question. Bulk accept whole guides at high confidence. Capability-specific: **reorder sections**, **drop question** (recorded, and the dropped question's gap returns to the open pool), **re-allocate time**, **suppress sensitivity class** for this stakeholder, **re-run with hint** ("go deeper on integration ownership"), and **export** to the interview format the consultant uses in the field.

**Downstream dependencies on commit.**

- Writes the guide as a `Deliverable` of type `interview_guide` attached to the `Interview`.
- `question_id` becomes the join key that AI-04 uses to attach each transcript answer to the question that produced it, which is what allows evidence to be traced from a score back to a question and a level boundary.
- `serves_gap_ids` closes AI-01 gaps when the interview completes and the answer is captured, or leaves them open when it does not.
- `expected_evidence_type` drives AI-04's extraction targets and AI-13's per-dimension evidence availability check.
- Unaddressed gaps remain in the `Charter` backlog and are re-offered to the next scheduled interview.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

| Failure mode | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Generic questions that could be asked of any organisation, producing no discriminating evidence. This is the failure that makes AI-09 abstain later. | Validation rejects a guide where fewer than 60 percent of primary questions carry a non-null `discriminates_levels`, a `serves_gap_ids` entry, or a `serves_hypothesis_ids` entry. The harness additionally measures downstream evidence yield per `question_id` and feeds low-yield question templates back into the precedent question bank with reduced rank. |
| Guide over-runs the slot, so the last focus areas are never asked and appear as uncovered evidence later. | Time budget is enforced arithmetically against `duration_minutes` at validation, not suggested in the prompt. A guide whose summed `allocated_minutes` exceeds the budget is rejected before it reaches the queue. |
| A contradiction-resolution question names a colleague or a source, making the interview adversarial and poisoning the engagement relationship. | `sensitivity` classification plus a validator that rejects question text containing any value from the restricted `Stakeholder` name column or a `source_id` display name. Contradiction questions are templated to ask about the mechanism rather than the disagreement. |
| Sensitive topics asked without warning, for example a prior security incident. | `sensitivity != "none"` questions are rendered collapsed in the guide with a reviewer confirmation required before export, and are excluded from bulk accept at the guide level. |

**Acceptance test.** Seed a stakeholder owning 4 focus areas, an `Interview` of 60 minutes, 3 open AI-01 gaps mapped to 2 of those focus areas, 1 open hypothesis, and 1 open contradiction touching the stakeholder's function. Assert that: (1) summed `allocated_minutes` is less than or equal to 50; (2) `uncovered_focus_areas` is empty; (3) all 3 gap ids and the hypothesis id appear in at least one `serves_*` array; (4) at least one question has `purpose: "contradiction_resolution"` and its text contains no stakeholder name from the restricted table; (5) at least one question each for `financial_evidence`, `deferral_risk_evidence`, and `strategic_traceability`, and the `strategic_traceability` question names an objective present in `Charter.strategic_objectives`; (6) every `level_discrimination` question's `discriminates_levels` pair is adjacent and cites the level-definition text; (7) a variant fixture with `duration_minutes: 30` produces a strictly smaller question count with the same gap coverage priority order.

### 8.5 AI-04 Interview transcription, synthesis and tagging

**Purpose.** Turn a recorded or uploaded interview into a diarised, time-located transcript, a synthesis of what was said, and a set of tagged, evidence-linked candidate `Finding` records. Methodology row: Weeks 1-2, AI Enhancement "Interview transcription/synthesis ... automatic tagging".

**Trigger.** On upload of an interview recording or transcript file, or on marking an `Interview` complete with notes attached. Synthesis re-runs if the transcript is corrected.

**Input contract.**

| Input | Detail |
|---|---|
| Media or text | Audio or video file, or a text transcript, or consultant notes. Stored as a `SourceDocument` with `source_type: "interview"`. |
| `Interview` | `id, stakeholder_id, format, planned topics[], guide question_ids[] with text and expected_evidence_type` |
| `Stakeholder` | `role_title, function, owns_capability_areas[], owns_focus_areas[]` |
| Taxonomy for tagging | `CapabilityArea[]` (8), `MaturityFocusArea[]` (28), `Theme[]` candidate set, and the pain-point register if one exists. Tag vocabularies are closed sets. |
| `Charter` | `hypotheses[]`, `strategic_objectives[]` |
| Limits | Diarisation and ASR run as a separate deterministic pipeline, not as part of the reasoning call. Synthesis operates on the transcript in windows of at most 8k tokens with 400-token overlap, then a reduce pass over window summaries. Max 250k transcript tokens per interview; longer recordings are split into parts with explicit part boundaries. |

**What the model must determine.**

1. Speaker attribution mapped to roles, using the interview roster. Unidentified speakers remain `unknown_speaker_n` and their statements may not become `Finding` evidence.
2. Segment boundaries: contiguous transcript spans that address one topic, each with a start and end timestamp.
3. For each segment, the guide `question_id` it answers, or `null` for unprompted content.
4. Candidate `Finding` records: a `Finding` is a single assertion about the organisation, stated as the consultant would state it, with the exact quote that supports it and its timestamp range.
5. Tags per finding from closed vocabularies: capability area, focus areas, tag class (`pain_point | strength | risk | decision | commitment | constraint | aspiration`), and sentiment on a three-point scale.
6. Extraction of the specific evidence types the guide asked for: named systems, counts, frequencies, owners, document existence, dates, and stated consequences. These become structured attributes on the finding rather than prose.
7. Statements that assert a number, so that G-4 can be enforced: every number in a finding must appear in the quote.
8. Statements that contradict the stakeholder's own earlier statements in the same interview, flagged for AI-07.
9. Commitments and decisions stated in the interview, which become candidate `Decision` records.
10. Unanswered guide questions, which return to the gap pool.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type AI04Payload = {
  interview_id: string
  transcript_quality: {
    asr_confidence_mean: number
    diarisation_speaker_count: number
    unknown_speaker_share: number
    inaudible_segment_seconds: number
  }
  segments: {
    segment_id: string
    start_ms: number
    end_ms: number
    speaker_role: string | "unknown_speaker_1" | "unknown_speaker_2"
    answers_question_id: string | null
    topic: string
  }[]
  findings: {
    candidate_finding_id: string
    statement: string                       // <= 400 chars, consultant voice, no person names
    tag_class: "pain_point" | "strength" | "risk" | "decision" | "commitment" | "constraint" | "aspiration"
    capability_area: string                 // closed set of 8
    focus_areas: string[]                   // closed set of 28
    sentiment: "negative" | "neutral" | "positive"
    attributes: {
      named_systems: string[]
      counts: { label: string, value: number, unit: string }[]
      frequencies: string[]
      owner_role: string | null
      documentation_exists: boolean | null
      dates: string[]
      stated_consequence: string | null
    }
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]                 // locator = "hh:mm:ss-hh:mm:ss"
    self_contradiction_of: string | null    // candidate_finding_id within this interview
  }[]
  candidate_decisions: {
    statement: string
    decided_by_role: string
    stated_date: string | null
    reversible: boolean | null
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]
  }[]
  guide_coverage: {
    answered_question_ids: string[]
    unanswered_question_ids: string[]
    unprompted_topics: string[]
  }
}
```

**Confidence and evidence.** Every finding requires exactly one or more `EvidenceRef` with a timestamp-range locator and a quote of at most 300 characters drawn verbatim from the transcript. Validation string-matches the quote against the transcript and rejects the finding if it does not match. `evidence_sufficiency` is 1.0 when the quote validates and the speaker is identified, 0 when the speaker is unknown. `source_agreement` is reduced when `self_contradiction_of` is set. `field_confidence` is reported separately for `statement`, `tag_class`, `capability_area`, `focus_areas`, and each populated `attributes` key, because ASR errors damage numeric extraction far more than they damage topic tagging. Findings whose `attributes.counts` values cannot be located in the quote are rejected, not down-weighted.

**Human actions available.** Accept, edit, reject per finding. Bulk accept tags and segment boundaries at high confidence. `Finding` creation is never bulk-accepted. Capability-specific: **correct speaker attribution** (which re-runs synthesis for that speaker's segments), **split finding** into two assertions, **merge findings**, **re-tag** from the closed vocabulary, **promote to `Evidence`** so the quote becomes citable by scoring capabilities, **mark quote sensitive** to exclude it from client-facing export, and **re-run with hint** on a named segment range.

**Downstream dependencies on commit.**

- Creates `Finding` and `Evidence` rows. These are the atoms every later capability cites. AI-06 clusters them, AI-07 compares them, AI-09 grounds levels in them, AI-11 generates opportunities from them, AI-13 cites them per dimension.
- `Finding.focus_areas` populates the evidence pool per `MaturityFocusArea`, which determines whether AI-09 can propose a level or must abstain.
- `candidate_decisions` become `Decision` records in the decision log.
- `guide_coverage.unanswered_question_ids` reopens the corresponding AI-01 gaps.
- Interview count and coverage per capability area update the engagement dashboard and the "what we did" statement in the findings playback deck, which in the reference engagement was stated as a count of leadership interviews plus a count of functional deep dives.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

| Failure mode | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| ASR mis-hears a number or a system name and the error propagates into a score and then into a Board deck. | Numbers and named systems are extracted only when the token's ASR confidence exceeds a configured floor, default 0.85, and the quote validates. Numbers below the floor are emitted with `attributes.counts` empty and a `verify_numeric` flag that forces individual review. Named systems are matched against the engagement's application landscape where one exists; unmatched names are flagged. |
| Speaker confusion attributes a statement to the wrong role, which corrupts single-voice detection and contradiction detection. | Findings from `unknown_speaker_*` cannot be promoted to `Evidence`. Speaker correction re-runs synthesis for affected segments and marks all dependent suggestions stale. |
| Findings restate the transcript rather than asserting anything, producing hundreds of low-value rows. | Validation rejects a finding whose `statement` has cosine similarity above 0.95 to its own quote, and enforces a per-interview cap computed as `duration_minutes / 2` candidate findings, with the model required to rank and keep the highest-evidence subset. |
| Person names leak into `statement`, which then flows to a deliverable. | `statement` and `owner_role` are validated against the restricted name column and the person-name detector. Names remain only inside `evidence[].quote`, which is internal-only and redacted to roles on export. |

**Acceptance test.** Use a fixture interview of 45 minutes with a known transcript, two speakers, one deliberate self-contradiction, one spoken figure ("we run 30-minute batch cycles"), one unanswered guide question, and one span marked inaudible. Assert that: (1) every `findings[i].evidence[0].quote` is a verbatim substring of the transcript and its timestamp range contains the quote; (2) the spoken figure appears as `attributes.counts` with value 30 and unit "minutes" and the digits appear in the quote; (3) the self-contradiction pair is emitted with `self_contradiction_of` set on one member; (4) the unanswered question appears in `unanswered_question_ids` and reopens its gap on commit; (5) findings attributed to `unknown_speaker_1` cannot be promoted to `Evidence` through the API; (6) `capability_area` and every `focus_areas` entry are members of the closed sets; (7) no `statement` contains a name from the restricted table; (8) correcting the speaker on one segment marks the derived findings stale.

### 8.6 AI-05 Document extraction to Evidence records

**Purpose.** Convert client documents, decks, and workbooks into `Evidence` records with precise locators, so that every later claim can cite a page, slide, or cell rather than a document. Methodology row: Weeks 1-2, AI Enhancement "document extraction".

**Trigger.** On ingest of any `SourceDocument`. Re-runs on re-upload of a new version, which supersedes rather than overwrites prior `Evidence`.

**Input contract.**

| Input | Detail |
|---|---|
| Parsed document structure | For PDFs and text: page-numbered blocks. For decks: slide number, layout name, shape text, speaker notes, and table contents. For workbooks: sheet name, cell address, cell value, cell formula, cached formula value, data-validation lists, conditional-formatting rules, and threaded comments. Extraction of structure is deterministic and happens before the model call. |
| `SourceDocument` | `id, classification, effective_date, quality_flags` |
| Extraction targets | Driven by `classification`: a project list yields initiative inventory rows; an application landscape yields systems and integrations; a budget yields cost lines; a prior assessment yields prior levels and prior scores; an architecture document yields dependencies. |
| Taxonomy | `CapabilityArea[]`, `MaturityFocusArea[]`, and the engagement's system register for entity linking. |
| Limits | Max 300 structural blocks per call, 100k prompt tokens, documents processed in page or sheet batches with the batch boundary recorded in the manifest. Images without extractable text are flagged, not guessed at. |

**What the model must determine.**

1. Which structural blocks carry substance and which are chrome (title slides, agenda, legends, decorative shapes, empty placeholders).
2. For each substantive block, one or more `Evidence` records: a claim the document makes, the verbatim quote, and the exact locator.
3. Entity links: the systems, programs, vendors, roles, focus areas, and existing `Finding` records the evidence relates to.
4. Structured extraction by classification. For a workbook this includes reading the formula rather than only the cached value, so that a scoring model, a weight, or a band threshold is captured as a formula shape rather than a number.
5. Internal inconsistencies inside a single document: a value in a table that disagrees with a value in prose, a cached formula value that disagrees with the formula, a conditional-formatting rule referencing a label that no longer exists in the data, a declared column that is empty, and a validation range that is discontiguous. Each becomes a `data_quality_issue`, not an `Evidence` record.
6. Cross-workbook and cross-file references, including broken external references, recorded with the referenced path so the missing source can be requested.
7. Sensitivity classification per evidence record: personal data, security incident, financial figure, or none.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type AI05Payload = {
  source_document_id: string
  evidence: {
    candidate_evidence_id: string
    claim: string                    // <= 300 chars, what the document asserts
    quote: string                    // <= 300 chars verbatim
    locator: string                  // "p. 14" | "slide 21" | "'Assessment'!F8" | "'Opportunities'!N7"
    block_type: "prose" | "table_cell" | "shape_text" | "speaker_notes" | "formula" | "comment" | "chart_label"
    formula: string | null           // present when block_type == "formula"
    cached_value: string | null
    links: {
      systems: string[]
      programs: string[]
      vendors: string[]
      roles: string[]
      capability_area: string | null
      focus_areas: string[]
      related_finding_ids: string[]
    }
    extracted_structure: object | null   // classification-specific typed payload
    sensitivity: "none" | "personal_data" | "security_incident" | "financial"
    confidence: number
  }[]
  data_quality_issues: {
    issue_type: "value_disagreement" | "formula_vs_cached_mismatch" | "stale_conditional_format"
              | "empty_declared_column" | "discontiguous_validation_range" | "prose_in_enum_cell"
              | "broken_external_reference" | "duplicate_label" | "unreachable_branch"
              | "misaligned_formula" | "competing_id_scheme" | "competing_score_scale"
    locators: string[]
    description: string
    referenced_path: string | null
    severity: "blocking" | "material" | "cosmetic"
  }[]
  chrome_blocks_skipped: number
  unextractable_blocks: { locator: string, reason: "image_only" | "empty" | "parse_error" }[]
}
```

**Confidence and evidence.** This capability is the source of evidence rather than a consumer of it, so the citation floor is satisfied structurally: every record must carry a locator that resolves in the parsed document and a quote that string-matches the block content. Validation rejects any record failing either test. `confidence` per record is the product of parse fidelity (1.0 for text blocks, reduced for OCR), entity-link certainty, and, for `extracted_structure`, schema completeness. `field_confidence` is reported for `claim`, each `links` key, and `extracted_structure`. `data_quality_issues` are detected by deterministic checks wherever possible, and those carry `confidence: 1.0`; only the description and severity are model-generated.

**Human actions available.** Accept, edit, reject. Bulk accept high-confidence evidence records, which is the normal path given volume. Capability-specific: **re-locate** a mis-addressed locator, **split** an evidence record covering two claims, **link to finding**, **reclassify sensitivity**, **suppress chrome pattern** so the same decorative shape type is skipped in future documents from the same template, **request missing external source** for a broken reference, and **promote data-quality issue** into an engagement `Risk` where it affects a deliverable.

**Downstream dependencies on commit.**

- Creates `Evidence` rows keyed by locator, which every scoring, maturity, and narrative capability cites. Without this, `EvidenceRef.locator` cannot be populated for document sources.
- `extracted_structure` seeds the initiative inventory, the system register, prior-assessment levels used as a comparison input to AI-09, and cost lines used later by the cost capabilities.
- Captured formula shapes seed `ScoringModel` configuration when a client or prior engagement supplies one, which is how the product replaces hard-coded weights with a versioned model.
- `data_quality_issues` populate a document-hygiene report and block advancement when `severity: "blocking"`.
- `superseded_by` on re-upload retires the prior evidence and marks all suggestions citing it stale, which is the control that stops deck numbers drifting from workbook numbers.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

| Failure mode | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| A cached formula value is extracted as fact while the formula itself is wrong or misaligned, so a broken calculation is imported as truth. Directly observed in the reference workbooks, where one row's band formula and business-value formula were shifted by one column. | Both `formula` and `cached_value` are captured and compared by a deterministic evaluator. A mismatch, or a formula whose relative references break the column pattern of its neighbours, raises `formula_vs_cached_mismatch` or `misaligned_formula` with `severity: "blocking"`, and the value may not be cited as evidence until resolved. |
| Chrome is extracted as substance, flooding the evidence repository with legends, agenda items, and empty placeholder shapes. | Deterministic pre-filter on block geometry, empty text, and layout name, plus the `chrome_blocks_skipped` count so a reviewer can see how aggressive the filter was. Suppressible chrome patterns are stored per document template. |
| Two competing identifier schemes or score scales inside one workbook are merged into one register, silently reconciling records that do not reconcile. Observed in the reference workbook, where a hidden sheet used a distinct opportunity ID scheme and a different point scale from the visible sheets. | `competing_id_scheme` and `competing_score_scale` are explicit issue types. Extraction keeps each scheme in its own namespace with the sheet name as the namespace key, and refuses to create cross-scheme links. Reconciliation is a human decision recorded as a `Decision`. |
| Person names, email addresses, phone numbers, and security-incident references are extracted into evidence that later flows into a client-facing exhibit. | `sensitivity` classification at extraction time, restricted storage, and export-time redaction to roles. `security_incident` evidence is excluded from generated client-facing text unless individually cleared. |

**Acceptance test.** Run against a fixture workbook and deck reproducing the reference engagement's structural conditions: a maturity sheet with a `gap = target - current` formula column and a `CHOOSE`-based label column, an opportunities sheet with score cells holding prose strings and hidden helper columns parsing the leading character, one row whose band and business-value formulas are shifted by one column, a conditional-formatting rule keyed to a retired theme label, a declared column with no data, a discontiguous validation range, a broken external workbook reference, and a deck containing one empty placeholder slide. Assert that: (1) every `evidence[i].locator` resolves and every `quote` string-matches the parsed block; (2) formula columns are captured with both `formula` and `cached_value`; (3) the shifted row raises `misaligned_formula` with `severity: "blocking"`; (4) the retired-label rule raises `stale_conditional_format`; (5) the empty column raises `empty_declared_column`; (6) the discontiguous range raises `discontiguous_validation_range`; (7) the prose score cells raise `prose_in_enum_cell` and are not extracted as numeric evidence; (8) the broken reference raises `broken_external_reference` with `referenced_path` populated; (9) the empty slide appears in `unextractable_blocks` and not in `evidence`; (10) re-uploading a modified workbook supersedes the prior evidence and marks a suggestion citing an affected cell stale.

### 8.7 AI-06 Theme clustering across findings

**Purpose.** Group the committed `Finding` set into a small number of coherent investment themes and, within each theme, into initiative-level buckets, so that the fact base becomes a communicable structure rather than a list. Methodology row: Weeks 1-2, AI Enhancement "theme clustering".

**Trigger.** Runs when the committed `Finding` count for the engagement crosses a configured minimum, default 40, and re-runs on demand and whenever the finding count grows by more than 10 percent since the last run. Also re-runs after AI-12 consolidation changes the opportunity set, because theme membership and counts are published.

**Input contract.**

| Input | Detail |
|---|---|
| `Finding[]` | All committed findings: `id, statement, tag_class, capability_area, focus_areas[], sentiment, attributes, evidence[]` |
| Survey aggregates | Per-question response distributions and free-text response clusters, as `Evidence` with `source_type: "survey"`. |
| `Charter` | `strategic_objectives[]`, `objectives[]`, `hypotheses[]`. Themes must be expressible as answers to a strategic question, not as technology categories. |
| `Theme[]` seeds | Either an existing engagement theme set, or the anonymised theme archetypes from the precedent library. The reference engagement's four observed themes are Stabilize the Core, Assess & Protect Current Investments, Grow the Top Line, and Build the Intelligent Enterprise, and these are available as archetypes with their descriptions. |
| Existing taxonomy | Any `Initiative` rows already committed, with their `Theme` and wave number, so clustering respects prior human decisions. |
| Limits | Findings are embedded once at commit time and cached. The clustering call receives finding statements plus tags, not full evidence quotes: max 600 findings per call at roughly 60 tokens each, 120k prompt tokens. Above 600 findings the capability clusters per capability area first, then reconciles. |

**What the model must determine.**

1. A theme set of between 3 and 6 themes. The count is a judgement, and the model must state why the chosen count is right rather than defaulting to the archetype count.
2. For each theme: a name, the strategic question it answers, a description of roughly 80 to 120 words in the voice used in client-facing material, and the type of problem it represents.
3. Assignment of every `Finding` to exactly one theme, with a secondary theme allowed as `also_relates_to` for reporting but not for counting.
4. Within each theme, initiative-level buckets: groupings of findings that share a natural dependency or a single owner, each with a name and a paragraph description. The reference engagement produced 17 initiatives across 4 themes, and the precedent library supplies the observed range rather than a target.
5. Findings that resist assignment, which must be emitted as `unassigned` with a reason, never forced into the nearest theme.
6. Overlap and boundary problems: pairs of themes whose descriptions do not cleanly separate, and findings that sit exactly on a boundary.
7. Candidate old-name mappings when a theme replaces or renames a prior theme, so that superseded labels are recorded rather than left to rot.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type AI06Payload = {
  theme_count_rationale: string
  themes: {
    candidate_theme_id: string
    name: string
    strategic_question: string          // "Why should this organisation care about this category of investment now?"
    description: string                 // 80-120 words
    problem_type: "existential_risk" | "protect_committed_investment" | "revenue_growth"
                | "capability_building" | "other"
    replaces_theme_name: string | null  // records the superseded label
    initiative_buckets: {
      candidate_initiative_id: string
      name: string
      description: string               // one paragraph
      finding_ids: string[]
      single_owner_role: string | null
      dependency_rationale: string      // why these findings belong together
    }[]
    finding_ids: string[]               // union of bucket members plus theme-level findings
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]             // representative evidence for the theme narrative
  }[]
  assignments: {
    finding_id: string
    theme_id: string
    initiative_id: string | null
    also_relates_to: string[]
    assignment_confidence: number
    boundary_case: boolean
  }[]
  unassigned: {
    finding_id: string
    reason: "singleton" | "out_of_scope" | "insufficient_specificity" | "spans_all_themes"
  }[]
  boundary_problems: {
    theme_a: string
    theme_b: string
    problem: string
    affected_finding_ids: string[]
  }[]
}
```

**Confidence and evidence.** Cluster membership is a material claim, so every theme requires representative `EvidenceRef`s and every assignment carries an `assignment_confidence` derived from the finding's embedding distance to the theme centroid, normalised against its distance to the runner-up theme. A finding whose margin between best and second-best theme is below a configured threshold, default 0.08 cosine, is marked `boundary_case: true` and forces individual review. `rubric_fit` for the whole suggestion is the mean assignment margin. `self_consistency` is measured as the Adjusted Rand Index across the k samples: an unstable clustering produces low confidence even when each individual run looks plausible. `field_confidence` is reported per theme and per initiative bucket, because a well-evidenced theme can contain a weak bucket.

**Human actions available.** Accept, edit, reject. No bulk accept. Capability-specific: **rename theme**, **merge two themes**, **split a theme**, **move finding** between themes or buckets, **split an initiative bucket**, **merge buckets**, **pin** a theme or assignment so subsequent re-runs may not change it, **set old name** to record a rename, and **re-run with hint** such as "separate operating-model findings from technology findings".

**Downstream dependencies on commit.**

- Creates or updates `Theme` and `Initiative` records and sets `Finding.theme_id`.
- Theme membership counts and percentage shares are computed by the calculation engine and published in the findings playback deck. In the reference engagement these were rendered as per-theme opportunity counts and percentage shares across four themes, and the counts are derived, never typed.
- `Initiative` becomes the parent of `Opportunity`, so AI-11 generates opportunities inside a committed initiative and AI-12 uses the shared initiative as a similarity signal.
- `Initiative.wave` is set later by AI-15, but the initiative identity is fixed here.
- `Theme.replaces_theme_name` populates the theme-alias table. Any exhibit, conditional-format equivalent, or saved filter referencing a retired label resolves through the alias table rather than breaking, which is the defect being designed away where duplicated and typo'd theme names and formatting rules keyed to retired names coexisted.
- Re-clustering marks every dependent AI-11, AI-13, and AI-17 suggestion stale for moved findings.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

| Failure mode | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Theme names drift across runs and across artefacts, producing duplicates, near-duplicates, and typos. Directly observed in the reference engagement, where old and new theme names coexisted, one theme name carried a leading stray character, and another was misspelled in a parallel sheet. | `Theme.name` is a canonical record with a stable id. Every reference is by id, never by string. Names are normalised at write (trim, collapse whitespace, reject leading punctuation) and checked for near-duplicates against existing and retired names at a configured edit-distance threshold. Renaming writes an alias, never a second theme. |
| Every finding is assigned, including ones that belong nowhere, so the themes look tidier than the evidence supports. | `unassigned` is a first-class output and validation rejects a payload with zero unassigned findings when more than 5 percent of findings have `assignment_confidence` below the boundary threshold. The reviewer sees the unassigned list explicitly. |
| Cluster instability: a small change to the finding set reshuffles themes, invalidating the deck and the workshop cards. | `self_consistency` via Adjusted Rand Index gates confidence. Pinned themes and pinned assignments are honoured by re-runs. A re-run that would move more than a configured share of findings, default 15 percent, is presented as a re-clustering proposal requiring explicit confirmation rather than as ordinary suggestions. |
| Themes become technology categories ("data", "infrastructure") rather than investment arguments, which makes the later Board narrative impossible to write. | `strategic_question` is mandatory and validated as a question. A theme whose name matches a `CapabilityArea` name is rejected, because capability areas already exist as a separate axis and duplicating them destroys the theme's explanatory purpose. |

**Acceptance test.** Load a gold engagement with a committed finding set whose human-assigned theme structure is known, comprising 4 themes and 17 initiative buckets. Assert that: (1) the proposed theme count is within one of the gold count and the rationale is non-empty; (2) Adjusted Rand Index between proposed assignments and gold assignments is at least 0.60, which is the class B gate for this capability; (3) every finding appears exactly once across `assignments` and `unassigned`; (4) no proposed theme name equals a `CapabilityArea` name; (5) proposing a theme name within edit distance 2 of a retired name is rejected and offered as an alias instead; (6) pinning one theme and re-running leaves that theme's name, description, and pinned assignments byte-identical; (7) adding 5 new findings and re-running moves fewer than 15 percent of existing assignments, or else surfaces a re-clustering proposal; (8) theme counts and percentage shares rendered on the playback exhibit are computed from committed membership and change when a finding is moved.

### 8.8 AI-07 Contradiction and tension detection between sources

**Purpose.** Find places where sources disagree, and distinguish a factual contradiction that must be resolved from a structural tension that should be surfaced to leadership as a choice. Methodology row: Weeks 1-2, AI Enhancement "contradiction detection".

**Trigger.** On commit of any new `Finding` or `Evidence` batch, incrementally against the existing corpus. Full re-run on demand before any findings playback is generated.

**Input contract.**

| Input | Detail |
|---|---|
| `Finding[]` and `Evidence[]` | Full committed set with `capability_area`, `focus_areas[]`, `attributes` (named systems, counts, dates, owner role, documentation existence, stated consequence), `evidence[]`, and the originating `source_type` and `Stakeholder.function`. |
| Survey aggregates | Response distributions, including the split between self-reported strengths and self-reported opportunities, and free-text sentiment. |
| `SourceDocument` extracted structure | Declared plans, declared statuses, declared ownership, and declared dates, so a document's claim can be tested against an interview's claim. |
| `Benchmark[]` | External comparison points, so a self-assessment can be tested against a benchmark position. |
| Candidate pair set | Generated deterministically, not by the model: pairs of findings sharing a focus area, a named system, or an owner role, filtered to pairs whose embeddings are similar enough to be about the same thing (cosine >= 0.62) or whose structured attributes collide (same system, different owner; same metric, different value; same program, different date). |
| Limits | The model evaluates candidate pairs in batches of at most 40 pairs per call, 60k prompt tokens. Pair generation is capped at 5,000 candidates per full run, ranked by collision strength. |

**What the model must determine.** For each candidate pair or small group:

1. Whether a genuine conflict exists, or whether the two statements are compatible and merely differently scoped.
2. The conflict class: `factual` (a value, date, owner, or existence claim differs), `status` (one source says done, another says not started), `ownership` (two parties both claim or both disclaim), `priority` (two sources rank the same thing differently), `capability_self_assessment` (internal view differs from benchmark or survey), or `structural_tension` (both statements are true and in permanent conflict, such as maintaining stability with the same people needed to modernise).
3. For a `structural_tension`, the two poles named as a "X versus Y" pair, the mechanism that makes them conflict, and the consequence of leaving the tension unmanaged. The reference engagement published four such tensions on a findings-playback slide, each as a pole pair plus a short explanation, which is the output shape.
4. Severity: whether the conflict blocks an analytical step (a maturity level cannot be set, a score cannot be defended) or is informational.
5. Resolution route: which stakeholder role, document, or measurement would settle it, and whether it is settleable at all.
6. Which downstream records the conflict contaminates, so their confidence can be capped.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type AI07Payload = {
  conflicts: {
    candidate_conflict_id: string
    conflict_class: "factual" | "status" | "ownership" | "priority"
                  | "capability_self_assessment" | "structural_tension"
    parties: {
      finding_id: string | null
      evidence_ref: EvidenceRef
      position: string                  // <= 200 chars, what this side asserts
      source_type: "interview" | "document" | "survey" | "benchmark" | "workbook" | "prior_engagement"
      stakeholder_function: string | null
    }[]                                 // exactly 2 or more
    capability_area: string
    focus_areas: string[]
    what_conflicts: string              // the specific proposition in dispute
    severity: "blocking" | "material" | "informational"
    resolution_route: "interview_role" | "request_document" | "measure" | "leadership_decision" | "unresolvable"
    resolution_target: string           // role, document type, or metric
    contaminates: { entity: string, id: string }[]
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]
  }[]
  tensions: {
    candidate_tension_id: string
    pole_a: string                      // e.g. "Operational stability"
    pole_b: string                      // e.g. "Transformation speed"
    mechanism: string                   // why the two cannot both be maximised
    consequence_if_unmanaged: string
    supporting_finding_ids: string[]
    prevalence: { finding_count: number, distinct_source_count: number, distinct_function_count: number }
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]
  }[]
  pairs_evaluated: number
  pairs_dismissed_as_compatible: number
}
```

**Confidence and evidence.** A conflict requires at least one `EvidenceRef` per party, drawn from distinct `source_id`s. A `structural_tension` requires supporting evidence from at least three distinct findings across at least two distinct stakeholder functions, otherwise it abstains, because a tension asserted from one voice is an opinion rather than a structural condition. `evidence_sufficiency` is the ratio of distinct source types represented to the minimum for the class. `source_agreement` is inverted for this capability: high disagreement is the signal, so the factor is computed instead as the consistency of the k samples in identifying the same pair as conflicting. `field_confidence` is reported for `conflict_class`, `severity`, and `resolution_route` separately, because the existence of a conflict is often clear while its class is not.

**Human actions available.** Accept, edit, reject. No bulk accept. Capability-specific: **dismiss as compatible** with a recorded reason, which suppresses the pair in future runs unless its evidence changes; **reclassify** between conflict and tension; **promote tension to narrative**, which creates a `NarrativeMessage` of type `tension` for the findings playback; **assign resolution** to a role with a due date, creating an `ActivationTask`-style follow-up in the engagement plan; **resolve** with the winning position recorded and the losing evidence retained; **escalate to `Decision`** when the resolution is a leadership choice rather than a fact; and **re-run with hint** scoped to a focus area.

**Downstream dependencies on commit.**

- An unresolved `blocking` conflict on a focus area caps `source_agreement` at 0.6 for AI-09 on that focus area and for AI-13 on any opportunity citing the contaminated evidence, which is the mechanism that stops a disputed fact silently producing a confident score.
- Committed `tensions` create `NarrativeMessage` records that populate the "tensions beneath the surface" section of the findings playback, and are available to AI-17 as reasoning material.
- Resolutions write to `Evidence.status` (`superseded` for the losing position) and create `Decision` records where leadership chose.
- Resolution routes feed the interview plan and document request backlog, and AI-03 generates contradiction-resolution questions from open conflicts.
- Conflict density per capability area is a quality signal on the engagement dashboard and a prompt for additional fact-gathering before the maturity phase.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

| Failure mode | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| False positives from differently scoped statements, for example one source describing a pilot and another describing the enterprise estate. This is the dominant failure and it destroys reviewer trust quickly. | The candidate pair generator requires a structural collision (same named system, same focus area plus overlapping metric, or same program) rather than text similarity alone. The model must fill `what_conflicts` with a single proposition, and validation rejects a conflict where the two positions differ in scope qualifiers extracted from the quotes. `pairs_dismissed_as_compatible` is reported so reviewers can see the filter working. Dismissals are persistent. |
| A conflict is framed as a personal disagreement between two named leaders, which is both a personal-data problem and a relationship problem. | `parties[].stakeholder_function` is a function, never a person. `what_conflicts` and `position` are validated against the restricted name column. The narrative form of a tension names organisational forces, not people. |
| Genuine structural tensions are reported as factual contradictions and sent for resolution, wasting client time on something that cannot be resolved. | `structural_tension` requires the prevalence floor and a `mechanism` explaining why both poles are true. `resolution_route: "unresolvable"` is a valid and expected output. The harness tracks reclassification rate between conflict and tension as a specific calibration metric. |
| Quadratic blow-up: every finding compared to every other finding makes the capability unaffordable and slow. | Pair generation is deterministic, indexed, and capped at 5,000 ranked candidates, evaluated in batches of 40. Incremental runs compare only new findings against the existing corpus. Cost per run is reported in the manifest. |

**Acceptance test.** Seed a fixture containing: (a) two findings asserting different owners for the same named platform, (b) a document asserting a program is complete and an interview asserting it has not started, (c) a survey aggregate placing a capability among self-reported strengths while a benchmark places it as lagging, (d) five findings across three stakeholder functions all describing the same stability-versus-modernisation squeeze, and (e) two findings about the same system that are compatible because one describes a pilot scope. Assert that: (1) (a) is emitted as `ownership`, (b) as `status`, (c) as `capability_self_assessment`; (2) (d) is emitted as a single `tensions` entry with `prevalence.distinct_function_count >= 2` and a non-empty `mechanism`; (3) (e) is not emitted as a conflict and increments `pairs_dismissed_as_compatible`; (4) a tension supported by only one finding abstains; (5) committing (b) as `blocking` caps a subsequent AI-09 suggestion on the affected focus area at `confidence_band: "medium"` or lower; (6) no `position` or `what_conflicts` string contains a name from the restricted table; (7) dismissing (e) prevents its reappearance on the next incremental run while its evidence is unchanged.

### 8.9 AI-08 Firm precedent retrieval from anonymised prior engagements

**Purpose.** Surface structurally comparable material from the firm's prior engagements so that consultants reuse proven framing, taxonomies, anchors, and dependency patterns instead of rebuilding them, without ever exposing another client's data. Methodology row: Weeks 1-2 and later, AI Enhancement "retrieval of relevant Aberdeen precedents (future Armory integration)".

**Trigger.** Available on demand from any of: a `MaturityFocusArea`, a `Theme`, an `Initiative`, an `Opportunity`, a `Dependency`, a `Wave` plan, or a `ScoreDimension`. Also runs automatically at three points: on `Charter` creation (comparable engagement shapes), on entering the maturity phase (comparable focus-area sets and level distributions), and on entering sequencing (comparable wave structures).

**Input contract.**

| Input | Detail |
|---|---|
| Anchor entity | The record the consultant is working on, with its text fields, taxonomy position, and committed evidence. |
| `Engagement` profile | Industry, business model descriptor, revenue band, employee band, geography count, site count, and the declared scope areas. Used for comparability, not for claims. |
| Precedent library index | Anonymised prior-engagement records with the same entity shapes plus outcome metadata: what was proposed, what was accepted, what shifted after a workshop, what was sequenced into which wave, and what the client later decided. Client names, personal names, absolute currency amounts, and security-incident narratives are removed at library ingest. |
| Limits | Max 25 precedent records retrieved per call, 40k prompt tokens. Retrieval from the engagement index is not permitted in the same call, so that engagement facts and precedent facts cannot be conflated in one generation step. |

**What the model must determine.**

1. Which precedent records are genuinely comparable, with the comparability basis stated: same capability area, same focus-area definition, same structural condition (for example a single-person dependency on a core platform), or same taxonomy shape.
2. A comparability score and the dimensions on which the precedent differs, so the consultant can discount it.
3. What is transferable: an anchor definition, a focus-area definition, an initiative framing, a dependency pattern, a wave structure, a rubric calibration example, or a narrative message shape.
4. What is not transferable, stated explicitly. A prior engagement's score, cost, or level is never transferable as a value; only as a distribution or a range with the sample size attached.
5. Aggregate statistics where more than three comparable precedents exist: median current level for a focus area, the modal wave for an initiative type, the distribution of a dimension score for an opportunity type, each with n.
6. Where the precedent set is too thin, say so rather than generalising from one prior engagement.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type AI08Payload = {
  anchor: { entity: string, id: string }
  precedents: {
    precedent_id: string                 // library id, not a client identifier
    comparability_basis: ("same_capability_area" | "same_focus_area_definition"
                        | "same_structural_condition" | "same_taxonomy_shape"
                        | "same_industry" | "same_scale_band")[]
    comparability_score: number          // 0-1
    differs_on: string[]
    transferable: {
      artefact_type: "focus_area_definition" | "anchor_definition" | "initiative_framing"
                   | "dependency_pattern" | "wave_structure" | "rubric_calibration_example"
                   | "narrative_message_shape"
      content: string
      how_to_adapt: string
    }[]
    not_transferable: string[]           // e.g. "the level assigned there; different documentation baseline"
    evidence: EvidenceRef[]              // source_type must be "prior_engagement"
  }[]
  aggregates: {
    statistic: string                    // e.g. "median current level, integration architecture"
    value: number | string
    n: number
    dispersion: string | null            // e.g. "range 1-3"
  }[]
  sufficiency: {
    comparable_count: number
    verdict: "sufficient" | "thin" | "insufficient"
    note: string
  }
}
```

**Confidence and evidence.** Every precedent claim requires an `EvidenceRef` with `source_type: "prior_engagement"` and a `source_id` resolving to a library record. `evidence_sufficiency` is driven by `comparable_count`: below 3 comparable precedents the verdict is `thin` and confidence is capped at 0.55; with zero comparable precedents the capability abstains with `insufficient_evidence`. Aggregates with `n < 3` are forbidden by validation. `field_confidence` is reported per precedent and per aggregate. Confidence for this capability is explicitly about comparability, not about correctness of the precedent, and the review UI must label it that way.

**Human actions available.** Accept, edit, reject. Bulk accept at high confidence, because committing a precedent attaches a reference rather than a value. Capability-specific: **adopt artefact** (copies a focus-area definition, anchor text, or initiative framing into this engagement as a draft, always as an editable draft and never as a committed value), **cite as comparison** (attaches the aggregate to a `Benchmark` record for use in the findings playback), **mark not comparable** with a reason, which trains the comparability ranker, and **request library curation** when a precedent looks mis-anonymised.

**Downstream dependencies on commit.**

- Adopted artefacts seed `MaturityFocusArea` definitions, `ScoreDimension` anchor text, `Theme` archetypes, and `Dependency` pattern templates for this engagement, all as drafts requiring human commitment.
- Aggregates attached as `Benchmark` records become citable evidence for the external-benchmark exhibit and can be cited by AI-17 as comparative reasoning, always with `n` shown.
- Precedent dependency patterns are candidate inputs to AI-14 and are labelled as pattern-derived so that AI-14's confidence is capped when a dependency has no engagement-specific evidence.
- `not_transferable` entries are recorded as guardrail notes on the adopted artefact, so a later reviewer sees what was deliberately not carried over.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

| Failure mode | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| A prior client's identity, personnel, or incident history leaks through a precedent, which is a confidentiality breach with a paying client on the other end. | Anonymisation happens at library ingest, not at retrieval, and is verified by a scanner that blocks ingest on detection of organisation names, person names, email addresses, phone numbers, absolute currency values, and incident narratives. Retrieval runs against the anonymised index only. Every returned record is re-scanned before it reaches the prompt, and a detection blocks the response and raises a `security` `AuditEvent`. The engagement index and the library index are never queried in the same call. |
| Precedent values are adopted as this client's values, so a level, score, or cost from another engagement lands in this engagement's canonical fields. | `adopt artefact` may only copy definitions, framings, anchors, and patterns. The API rejects an adopt operation targeting `MaturityAssessment.current_level`, `OpportunityScore`, `CostEstimate`, or any numeric canonical field. Aggregates may only be attached as `Benchmark`, which is a comparison entity, never as an engagement value. |
| Superficial comparability: a match on industry alone produces precedents that mislead. | `comparability_basis` must contain at least one structural basis, not only `same_industry` or `same_scale_band`. Validation rejects a precedent whose basis array contains only demographic entries. `differs_on` is mandatory and must be non-empty. |
| Generalising from a single prior engagement, presented with unwarranted confidence. | `n >= 3` for any aggregate, `thin` verdict caps confidence at 0.55, `insufficient` abstains. The review UI renders `n` next to every aggregate and refuses to render an aggregate without it. |

**Acceptance test.** Build a precedent library fixture of 6 anonymised engagements, one of which is deliberately seeded with an un-anonymised organisation name, a person name, and an absolute currency figure. Assert that: (1) library ingest rejects the seeded record and raises a `security` `AuditEvent`, and the record never appears in retrieval results; (2) for an anchor `MaturityFocusArea` matching 4 library records, `aggregates` reports a median current level with `n: 4` and a dispersion string; (3) for an anchor matching 2 records, `sufficiency.verdict` is `thin` and `confidence <= 0.55`; (4) for an anchor matching 0 records, the capability abstains; (5) every `precedents[i].comparability_basis` contains at least one structural entry and `differs_on` is non-empty; (6) an attempt to adopt a precedent level directly into `MaturityAssessment.current_level` is rejected by the API; (7) all `evidence[].source_type` values equal `prior_engagement`; (8) a single call never contains chunks from both the engagement index and the library index, verifiable from `RetrievalManifest.retrieved`.

### 8.10 AI-09 Evidence-backed maturity scoring proposal
