### 8.31 AI-29 Audience-level rewriting (Weeks 10–12)

**Purpose.** Produce the same content at four defined audience levels, dropping detail by rule and rewriting within the surviving structure. Methodology row: Weeks 10–12, AI Enhancement "tailor detail to executive audience".

Grounding: the reference engagement produced the same underlying analysis at three observable densities. A 67-slide two-day working deck carried per-opportunity cards, dimension-level scoring, survey detail, and facilitation mechanics. A 23-slide execution-planning deck carried one slide per initiative for the seven initiatives needing near-term mobilisation, each with a why-it-matters line, a first-60-to-90-days block, workstreams, value created, and a takeaway, followed by firm qualifications and case studies. A 2-page recap email carried five themes, six next steps, no exhibits, no scores, no figures, and an explicit warning that rankings would shift. Those three artefacts define the drop rule.

**Trigger.** A consultant requests a `Deliverable` variant at a named level; or AI-34 assembles a pack at a named level; or a source `NarrativeMessage` changes and its downstream variants need regeneration.

**Input contract.** The full L1 content set: `NarrativeMessage[]` with bindings, `Exhibit[]` with markers, `Initiative[]`, `Opportunity[]` with scores, `Theme[]`, `Risk[]`, `Decision[]` (the asks), `ActivationTask[]`, `Milestone[]`, and the status of every source record (`proposed`, `accepted`, `committed`). Each content element carries a `detail_class`: `opportunity_row`, `score_dimension`, `initiative_detail`, `theme`, `storyline`, `ask`, `risk`, `exhibit`, `facilitation`, `caveat`, `qualification`. Also passed: the target `audience_level` and its policy row.

Audience level policy, expressed as allow-lists and caps so that the drop itself is deterministic and only the rewriting is a model job:

| Level | Target size | Allowed detail_class | Caps | Number precision | Currency allowed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L1 working** | up to ~70 slides, unbounded | all, including `facilitation`, `score_dimension`, `opportunity_row`, reviewer notes | none | 2 decimals (e.g. weighted score 4.23) | yes, point values |
| **L2 initiative** | 20–25 slides | `initiative_detail`, `theme`, `storyline`, `exhibit`, `ask`, `risk`, `caveat`, `qualification` | one slide per initiative, initiative count capped at the near-term mobilisation set; `exhibit` ≤ 12 | 1 decimal | yes, ranges only |
| **L3 board** | 10–14 slides | `storyline`, `theme`, `ask`, `risk`, `exhibit`, `caveat` | `storyline` ≤ 9, `exhibit` ≤ 6, `theme` ≤ 5, `ask` all, `risk` all | whole units with an explicit range and a basis label | yes, ranges with basis |
| **L4 recap email** | 2 pages | `theme`, `ask`, `caveat`, next steps | `theme` ≤ 5, next steps ≤ 6, `exhibit` = 0 | no scores, no figures | **no** |

Drops by class and level: `opportunity_row` and `score_dimension` drop at L2 (opportunity content rolls up to its initiative, dimension scores compress to the band label); `facilitation` drops at L2; `initiative_detail` drops at L3 except for wave 1; `qualification` drops at L3; every `exhibit` drops at L4.

**What the model must determine.**

1. The rewritten text for each surviving element at the level's density and reading level, respecting the caps.
2. When over a cap, which elements to merge, the merged text, and a `merge_loss` note stating what the merge removed.
3. `residual_notes[]`: a one-line note for any element of class `ask` or `risk` that a cap would drop, so that an ask or a risk can be compressed but never disappear.
4. The `caveat` sentence whenever any source record on the page has status `proposed` or `draft`, in the voice of the observed recap warning that rankings and scoring will shift with further work.
5. The rolled-up statement when opportunity rows collapse into an initiative, naming how many opportunities rolled up.
6. Nothing numeric. Numbers survive as binding tokens; the engine formats them to the level's precision policy. The model must not format a number.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type AudienceVariant = {
  deliverable_id: string; audience_level: "L1"|"L2"|"L3"|"L4";
  elements: {
    source_element_id: string; detail_class: string;
    rewritten_text: string;          // contains binding tokens, never literal numbers
    merged_from: string[];           // source element ids, when merged
    merge_loss: string | null;
    rollup: { rolled_up_count: number; from_class: string } | null;
  }[];
  dropped: { source_element_id: string; detail_class: string; rule: string }[];
  residual_notes: { source_element_id: string; detail_class: "ask"|"risk"; note: string }[];
  caveat: string | null;
  compliance: { element_counts: Record<string, number>; caps: Record<string, number>;
                within_caps: boolean; currency_tokens_present: boolean;
                unresolved_tokens: string[] };
};
```

**Confidence and evidence.** Raw confidence `= 0.40 × binding_survival (share of source bindings still resolvable in the rewritten text) + 0.30 × within_caps + 0.20 × residual_completeness + 0.10 × reading_level_target_met`. A variant is **invalid**, not merely low-confidence, when an `ask` or `risk` is dropped without a residual note, when a caveat is required and absent, when L4 contains a currency token, or when a binding token fails to resolve. Mandatory evidence: each rewritten element carries the `source_element_id`, and the variant carries the policy version applied.

**Human actions available.** Accept the variant; edit any element; restore a dropped element with an override reason (recorded as an `AuditEvent`, and the level's cap is then shown as exceeded rather than silently raised); regenerate at a different level; bulk-accept L2 element rewrites where the source element is `committed` and the rewrite changed no binding; L3 and L4 always require element-by-element review.

**Downstream dependencies.** On commit: creates a `Deliverable` variant and sets `NarrativeMessage.audience_variant` and `Exhibit.include_at_level`; the L4 variant is the recap email `Deliverable`. Every surviving binding stays on the AI-30 staleness watch list at every level, so a number change flags all four variants at once rather than only the one someone remembers to check.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

1. *Precision inflation.* A board figure rendered to the cent. Mitigation: the model emits tokens only; the engine formats per level policy; a literal numeral in `rewritten_text` fails validation.
2. *Missing caveat.* A draft-scored ranking presented as settled, the exact risk the reference engagement's recap warned about explicitly. Mitigation: the caveat is required whenever any source record is `proposed` or `draft`, enforced as a validity rule.
3. *Currency leaking into the email.* Mitigation: L4 policy forbids the currency class; `currency_tokens_present = true` at L4 rejects the variant.
4. *Silent loss of an ask.* Mitigation: `residual_notes` completeness is a validity rule, not a quality score.
5. *Compression that changes meaning.* Merging two initiatives into one line implies they are one programme. Mitigation: `merge_loss` is mandatory on every merge and surfaces in the reviewer's diff.

**Acceptance test.** Fixture L1 content set: 43 `opportunity_row` elements, 17 `initiative_detail` elements of which 7 are wave-1 near-term, 5 `theme`, 9 `storyline`, 3 `ask`, 4 `risk`, 14 `exhibit`, 6 `facilitation`, and 2 source records with status `proposed`. Render L2, L3, L4. Assert: (a) L2 has one slide per near-term initiative, no `opportunity_row` or `score_dimension` elements, and at most 12 exhibits; (b) L3 has at most 14 slides, at most 9 storyline elements, and no `qualification`; (c) L4 has at most 5 themes, at most 6 next steps, zero exhibits, and zero currency tokens; (d) all 3 asks and all 4 risks are represented at L3, and any dropped at L4 appear in `residual_notes`; (e) all three variants carry a non-null `caveat` because two sources are `proposed`; (f) every binding token in every variant resolves and `unresolved_tokens` is empty; (g) a variant with a literal `12.4` typed into an element is rejected; (h) manually dropping an ask without a residual note is rejected.

---

### 8.32 AI-30 Narrative staleness and number-consistency checking (Weeks 10–12)

**Purpose.** Guarantee that everything published matches the model underneath it, uses one canonical label set and one scoring model, and contains no content from another engagement. Methodology row: Weeks 10–12, AI Enhancement "ensure numbers and roadmap remain synchronized".

**This capability is deterministic.** All three check families are calculation-engine rules, and the result must be identical with the model provider disabled. The model only ranks violations by publication risk, drafts the fix instruction, and drafts the change note. Every known defect this capability targets was observed in the reference engagement's own artefacts, which is why the checks are specified as blocking rather than advisory.

**Trigger.** On any write to a bound entity field; on `Deliverable` assembly; on export or publish (blocking); and on a scheduled sweep before any governance checkpoint.

**Input contract.** All `NarrativeMessage` records with their `Binding[]`; all `Exhibit` records with their `data_query` and captions; the `Deliverable` element tree at every audience level; the canonical enum registry (horizon and wave labels, quadrant labels, priority bands, cost categories, t-shirt sizes); the active `ScoringModel` version and the list of superseded versions; the `ScoreDimension` storage schema; `AuditEvent` history for every bound entity; the `Engagement.id` of the deliverable and the roster of organisation and person names legitimately in scope; and the unit tolerance policy with its version.

**Check families.**

*Family A, binding revalidation.* For each `Binding`: recompute `entity.field` under `aggregation` and `scope_filter`; compare to `value_at_bind` within `tolerance`; on mismatch emit `stale_binding` with the token, old value, new value, delta, the changed source record, and the `AuditEvent` that changed it. Also emit `unresolvable_binding` when the entity or field no longer exists, and `hash_mismatch` when `source_hash` does not match the recomputed tuple.

*Family B, cross-artifact consistency.* Each rule below targets a defect observed in the reference engagement's artefacts.

| rule_id | Check | Defect it designs away |
|---|---|---|
| NC-01 | Every numeral in any deliverable element must lie inside a binding span or a verified `Exhibit` caption numeral. A free-text numeral is a violation by definition. | Deck numbers drifting from the workbook |
| NC-02 | Every horizon, wave, and quadrant label must be a member of the canonical enum; two distinct label strings mapping to the same enum value are both flagged | Three different names for the same horizon bucket |
| NC-03 | Every displayed score must derive from the active `ScoringModel` version; a value traceable to a superseded model is a violation | A second, incompatible scoring model living in hidden sheets |
| NC-04 | Every `ScoreDimension` value must have a numeric source column; a value derived by parsing a display string is a violation | Scores parsed out of display strings |
| NC-05 | Any two elements presenting the same `entity.field` must present the same value under the same rounding | Same number, two slides, two values |
| NC-06 | Every `Exhibit` caption numeral must appear in the current query result | Caption drift after a data change |
| NC-07 | Category totals shown alongside a sum must reconcile within 1% | Broken roll-ups |

*Family C, confidentiality and provenance.* Every deliverable element and every `Exhibit` must carry an `engagement_id`. An element whose `engagement_id` differs from the deliverable's is a `foreign_engagement_content` violation and blocks export. An element with **no** `engagement_id` is treated as foreign, not as clean, because that is how copied content arrives. A named-entity scan flags organisation and person names not on the engagement roster. Precedent-derived content lacking `anonymisation_cleared_at` is a violation. An `Exhibit` whose source resolves to an empty or unreadable artefact is flagged as `empty_source`, grounded in the zero-byte placeholder file found in the reference archive alongside its real deliverables.

**What the model must determine.** Only three things: (1) the publication-risk ranking of the open violations, with confidentiality violations first by policy and any deviation from the deterministic materiality order explained; (2) a fix instruction per violation, naming the element, the rule, and the specific edit or recompute needed; (3) a change note for the deck's revision history, describing what moved and why, with no numeral absent from the violation payload.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type ConsistencyReport = {
  deliverable_id: string; checked_at: string; policy_version: string;
  export_blocked: boolean; blocking_rule_ids: string[];
  violations: {                          // engine-authored
    violation_id: string; family: "A"|"B"|"C"; rule_id: string;
    severity: "blocking"|"warning";
    element_id: string | null; exhibit_id: string | null;
    binding_token: string | null;
    old_value: number | null; new_value: number | null; delta: number | null;
    changed_by_audit_event_id: string | null;
    detail: string;
  }[];
  ai_triage: {                           // model-authored
    violation_id: string; rank: number; publication_risk: "critical"|"high"|"medium"|"low";
    rank_reason: string; fix_instruction: string;
  }[];
  change_note_draft: string;
  model_disabled_equivalent: boolean;    // asserted by the test harness
};
```

**Confidence and evidence.** The violations carry no confidence; they are deterministic. The `AISuggestion` wrapping `ai_triage` derives confidence from `0.5 × numeric_containment_pass + 0.5 × (share of violations whose fix instruction names a valid element and rule)`. Mandatory evidence: each Family A violation carries the `AuditEvent` id that changed the source value; each Family B violation carries the canonical enum entry or `ScoringModel` version it was compared against; each Family C violation carries the offending `engagement_id` or the matched entity name span.

**Human actions available.** Fix the element or recompute; re-bind a stale headline at its new value (writes a new `value_at_bind` and an `AuditEvent`); remove foreign content; request an anonymisation clearance; accept a warning with a written rationale and an expiry; accept the change note. Blocking violations cannot be waived by any role in the MVP; export stays blocked until they clear.

**Downstream dependencies.** Blocks `Deliverable` export and publication while any blocking violation is open. Re-binding updates `NarrativeMessage.bindings`. Enum violations queue a data-cleanup task on the offending records. Family C violations create an `AuditEvent` and notify the engagement lead. The change note attaches to the `Deliverable` version history and feeds the "since last review" delta in AI-34.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

1. *Tolerance so wide that nothing goes stale.* Mitigation: tolerance is unit policy, versioned, changed only by an audited policy edit, and the report carries `policy_version` so a permissive run is visible after the fact.
2. *A page passing because it has no bindings at all.* Mitigation: NC-01 makes an unbound numeral a violation, so "no bindings" is a failure state rather than a clean sheet.
3. *Foreign content laundered by copy-paste that strips its tag.* Mitigation: a missing `engagement_id` is treated as foreign, so stripping the tag makes the violation worse rather than better.
4. *Score sourced from a superseded model surviving because it looks reasonable.* Mitigation: NC-03 compares the model version, not the plausibility of the value.
5. *Triage burying a confidentiality violation below a cosmetic one.* Mitigation: confidentiality violations rank first by policy; the model may not reorder them downward.

**Acceptance test.** Build a fixture `Deliverable` with 30 numerals, all bound. Then inject: two source value mutations beyond tolerance; one element carrying a different `engagement_id`; one element with no `engagement_id`; one horizon label `"Future Horizon"` while the canonical enum uses `"Sequence Later"`; one score traceable to a superseded `ScoringModel`; one `ScoreDimension` value whose only source is a parsed display string; one free-text numeral; one exhibit whose source artefact is zero bytes. Assert: (a) nine violations with the expected `rule_id`s and no others; (b) `export_blocked = true` with both Family C violations and the free-text numeral among `blocking_rule_ids`; (c) rerun with the model provider disabled and assert the `violations` array is byte-identical and `model_disabled_equivalent = true`; (d) `ai_triage` ranks both Family C violations above every Family A and B violation; (e) every numeral in `change_note_draft` appears in some violation payload; (f) widening the tolerance policy changes the result only after a policy `AuditEvent` exists; (g) re-binding one stale headline clears exactly that violation.

---

**Grounding note for the Ongoing capabilities (AI-31 to AI-34).** The reference engagement's file set ends at execution planning. It contains no status reports, no milestone log, no actual-spend records, no KPI actuals, and no risk register, so there is nothing in it to observe about in-flight tracking. Everything specified below for the *inputs* of the Ongoing phase is therefore derived from two sources and labelled accordingly: the methodology's Ongoing row, which names milestones, budgets, actual spend, KPIs, initiative status, risks, and decisions as inputs and monitoring, benefits tracking, dependency management, priority refresh, governance reviews, and leadership-view updates as activities; and the governance artefacts the reference engagement's execution-planning deck proposed standing up, namely a budget-forecast-and-spend process with a monthly tracker, a portfolio health scorecard, weekly status reporting, and a quarterly business review cadence. The numeric thresholds in AI-31 and the pack section list in AI-34 are inventions consistent with those two sources and are flagged inline as assumptions. The dependency graph, cost model, value model, capacity model, and scoring model these capabilities operate on are all observed in the reference engagement and are not inferred.

---

### 8.33 AI-31 Slippage detection and downstream impact forecasting (Ongoing)

**Purpose.** Detect where the roadmap is slipping against its approved baseline, forecast what that does downstream, and tell the leadership team which slips matter. Methodology row: Ongoing, AI Enhancement "detect slippage; forecast downstream impacts".

**Detection and forecasting are deterministic.** Variance detection is threshold arithmetic; downstream forecasting is schedule algebra over the dependency graph. The model ranks, hypothesises cause with evidence, names the decision now needed, and drafts the executive line. It does not compute a date.

**Trigger.** On ingestion of an `ActualsSnapshot`; on any `Milestone` status or forecast-date change; weekly on the status-reporting cadence; and before any governance review.

**Input contract.**

| Input | Fields | Grounding |
|---|---|---|
| `ActualsSnapshot` | `as_of`, `roadmap_item_id`, `pct_complete`, `spend_to_date_by_category`, `staffed_fte_by_skill`, `status_narrative`, `reported_by` | inferred from the Ongoing row inputs and the proposed monthly tracker and weekly status reporting |
| `Milestone` | `id`, `name`, `baseline_date`, `baseline_version`, `forecast_date`, `actual_date`, `roadmap_item_id`, `is_commitment` | inferred |
| `RoadmapItem` | `start_month`, `end_month`, `wave_id`, `priority_band`, planned S-curve | observed |
| `Dependency` | `predecessor_id`, `successor_id`, `type`, `reason`, computed `slack_days` | observed |
| `CostEstimate` + `CostLineItem` | plan by year and category | observed |
| `KPI` | `baseline`, `target`, `target_date`, actuals series | inferred |
| `Benefit` | ramp profile, annual value | observed |
| `Risk` | open risks per item | inferred |
| `Decision` | approved baselines and rebaseline decisions | observed |

Retrieval scope: current engagement, snapshots since the last detection run plus the full baseline. Limit: at most 200 items per run; narrative fields truncated to 2,000 characters each for the cause-hypothesis step.

Deterministic thresholds (**assumption**, configurable per engagement, defaults stated so an engineer can build against them):

| Signal | Amber | Red |
|---|---|---|
| Milestone date variance vs approved baseline | > 15 days or > 10% of remaining duration | > 30 days, or any successor's slack fully consumed, or a `is_commitment` milestone moves at all |
| Progress vs planned S-curve | 10–20 points behind | > 20 points behind |
| Spend vs phase-to-date plan | 10–20% over | > 20% over, or > 25% under with `pct_complete` on plan (a sign the work is not actually starting) |
| Staffing vs `ResourceDemand` | 10–25% under for one month | > 25% under, or under for two consecutive months |
| KPI trajectory | off the linear path to target by > 15% | off by > 30% or moving away from target for two periods |
| Snapshot freshness | 15–21 days old | > 21 days old, reported as `data_stale`, never as green |

Downstream forecast, computed by the engine: `downstream_slip(successor) = max(0, predecessor_finish_delta_days − successor.slack_days)`, propagated through the graph in topological order, with `hard_blocks` edges propagating fully and `soft_precedes` edges propagating at a declared factor. Benefit delay follows: `benefit_delay_months = ceil(downstream_slip_days / 30)` applied to the affected `Benefit` ramps, with the annual value at risk recomputed by the engine.

**What the model must determine.**

1. The ranking of slips by consequence, using deferred benefit, commitment breach, and successor exposure, with the reason for any deviation from the raw materiality order.
2. A `cause_hypothesis` per red slip, each requiring at least one `EvidenceRef` quote from a `status_narrative` or a `StakeholderFeedback` record, or else labelled `unevidenced`.
3. The decision now needed per red slip, with an owner role and a date, distinguishing a rebaseline request from a recovery action.
4. A three-sentence executive line per red slip, naming the milestone, the days, the affected successor, and the value at risk, with every numeral drawn from the engine result.
5. Which amber slips are early signals of the same underlying cause and should be handled as one.
6. No dates, no deltas, no forecasts of its own.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type SlippageReport = {
  engagement_id: string; run_at: string; snapshot_window: { from: string; to: string };
  data_quality: { stale_items: string[]; missing_snapshot_items: string[];
                  rebaselined_since_last_run: { item_id: string; decision_id: string }[] };
  slips: {                                     // engine-authored
    slip_id: string; roadmap_item_id: string; milestone_id: string | null;
    signal: "milestone_date"|"progress_curve"|"spend"|"staffing"|"kpi_trajectory";
    classification: "green"|"amber"|"red"|"data_stale";
    variance: { unit: "days"|"pct"|"points"|"fte"; value: number };
    baseline_version: string;
    downstream: { successor_item_id: string; slack_days: number;
                  forecast_slip_days: number; edge_type: string }[];
    value_at_risk: { benefit_id: string; benefit_delay_months: number;
                     annual_value_at_risk: number }[];
    commitment_breached: boolean;
  }[];
  ai_layer: {                                  // model-authored
    slip_id: string; rank: number; rank_reason: string;
    cause_hypothesis: { statement: string; evidence: EvidenceRef[]; unevidenced: boolean };
    decision_needed: { question: string; kind: "rebaseline"|"recovery_action";
                       owner_role: string; needed_by: string };
    exec_line: string;
    grouped_with: string[];
  }[];
};
```

**Confidence and evidence.** The variance figures and forecast slips carry no model confidence; they are deterministic. The `AISuggestion` wrapping `ai_layer` derives confidence from `0.35 × snapshot_freshness_score + 0.25 × cause_evidence_strength + 0.20 × dependency_reason_coverage + 0.20 × numeric_containment_pass`. Caps: **low** when the item's snapshot is `data_stale`; **medium** when the cause hypothesis is `unevidenced`. Mandatory evidence: for each red slip, the `ActualsSnapshot` id and the `Milestone` baseline record; for each cause hypothesis, a verifiable quote from a narrative field.

**Human actions available.** Accept a slip as reported; accept the executive line into the governance pack; accept the cause hypothesis or replace it; accept a `decision_needed` as a `Decision`; approve a rebaseline, which writes a new `baseline_version` and a `Decision` and resets variance measurement; mark a slip as expected and tolerated with a rationale; escalate to AI-33 for a resequencing proposal.

**Downstream dependencies.** On commit: updates `Milestone.forecast_date`, `RoadmapItem.status`, and `Wave.feasibility_flag`; recomputes `Benefit` ramp delays and the value at risk in the benefits-realisation view; flags affected `KPI`s at risk; creates `Risk` records for commitment breaches; feeds AI-33's input set and AI-34's health summary; every downstream date and value change triggers the AI-30 staleness sweep on bound narrative.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

1. *Silence read as health.* No snapshot arrives and the item shows green. Mitigation: the freshness threshold classifies stale items as `data_stale`, never green, and `data_quality.stale_items` is on the report face.
2. *Rebaseline laundering.* Slip disappears because the baseline moved. Mitigation: variance is always measured against the approved `baseline_version`; a rebaseline requires an approved `Decision` and appears in `rebaselined_since_last_run` for the next two reviews.
3. *Unevidenced cause attribution.* "Vendor delays" asserted with nothing behind it, which then shapes the leadership response. Mitigation: `unevidenced: true` is explicit and caps the band at medium; the reviewer sees the flag next to the hypothesis.
4. *Underspend read as good news.* Mitigation: the underspend-with-on-plan-progress red rule above treats it as a signal that work has not started.
5. *Slip storm.* Forty ambers on a large portfolio drown the two reds. Mitigation: `grouped_with` collapses shared-cause ambers, and the health summary in AI-34 shows reds first by rule.

**Acceptance test.** Fixture: 20 milestones, 30 dependency edges, snapshots dated three days ago. Slip one predecessor by 45 days where its successor has 20 days of slack and a `Benefit` with a known annual value. Assert: (a) the predecessor is classified red on `milestone_date`; (b) the successor's `forecast_slip_days` equals exactly 25; (c) `benefit_delay_months` equals 1 and the annual value at risk equals the hand-computed figure; (d) the `exec_line` names the milestone id and contains 45 and 25 and no numeral absent from the engine result; (e) rerun with the model disabled and assert the `slips` array is identical; (f) age the snapshot to 30 days and assert the item becomes `data_stale`, not green, and the band caps at low; (g) move the baseline without an approved `Decision` and assert variance is still measured against the approved baseline; (h) a cause hypothesis with no narrative quote is marked `unevidenced`.

---

### 8.34 AI-32 Emerging risk extraction from status narrative (Ongoing)

**Purpose.** Read the free text flowing through status reporting and governance minutes and surface risks that are not yet on the register, without inflating the register with restatements. Methodology row: Ongoing, AI Enhancement "surface emerging risks".

**Inference note.** The narrative sources are inferred from the methodology's Ongoing inputs and the weekly-status and QBR cadence the reference engagement proposed. The risk category enum is grounded in risk language observable in the reference engagement's own analysis (key-person dependency, capacity contention, vendor decision delay, integration collision, security exposure, data readiness, adoption, funding, governance delay, scope duplication).

**Trigger.** On ingestion of an `ActualsSnapshot` carrying a `status_narrative`; on ingestion of governance minutes; on new `StakeholderFeedback` since the last governance review; and on demand before a review.

**Input contract.** `ActualsSnapshot.status_narrative` and any attached notes; governance minutes documents via `SourceDocument`; `StakeholderFeedback` since the last review with its AI-24 labels; the full open and closed `Risk` register with `title`, `description`, `category`, `likelihood`, `impact`, `owner`, `closed_at`; the `Dependency` graph with computed slack; open `Decision`s with their needed-by dates; and `RoadmapItem` names and owners for entity resolution.

Retrieval scope: narratives dated since the last accepted extraction, capped at 150 documents or 200,000 characters per run, plus the complete risk register for deduplication regardless of date.

A deterministic pre-sweep runs first and is passed to the model as prompts to check, so the quiet risks are not left to text alone: successors whose `slack_days < 15` with no open `Risk`; `Decision`s past their needed-by date; items with two consecutive under-staffed months; skills with a single named person covering them; `CostEstimate`s with `basis = precedent_directional` inside wave 1.

**What the model must determine.**

1. Candidate `Risk` records: `title` of at most 90 characters, `description` of at most 80 words, `category` from the enum, and the affected entity ids.
2. `likelihood` 1–5 and `impact` 1–5, each with a rationale that cites the stated definition for the level chosen rather than asserting a number.
3. Whether the candidate duplicates or escalates an existing register entry. When it does, the output must be a merge carrying `existing_risk_id`, not a create.
4. Whether it is a risk or an already-materialised issue, since an issue belongs in the issues log with an owner and a date, not in the risk register with a likelihood.
5. The `leading_indicator` that would show the risk crystallising, and the period over which it should be watched.
6. `pre_sweep_dispositions`: for each deterministic pre-sweep prompt, either a risk candidate or an explicit statement of why it is not a risk.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type RiskExtraction = {
  engagement_id: string; window: { from: string; to: string }; source_count: number;
  candidates: {
    candidate_id: string; action: "create"|"merge"|"issue";
    existing_risk_id: string | null;              // required when action = "merge"
    title: string; description: string; category: string;
    affected_entity_refs: { entity: string; id: string }[];
    likelihood: 1|2|3|4|5; likelihood_rationale: string;
    impact: 1|2|3|4|5; impact_rationale: string;
    leading_indicator: { statement: string; watch_period: string; kpi_id: string | null };
    evidence: EvidenceRef[];                      // >=1, quote <=300 chars, verified
    dedupe: { nearest_existing_risk_id: string | null; similarity: number };
  }[];
  pre_sweep_dispositions: { prompt_id: string; prompt: string;
                            disposition: "candidate"|"not_a_risk"; reason: string;
                            candidate_id: string | null }[];
  unprocessed_sources: { source_id: string; reason: string }[];
};
```

**Confidence and evidence.** Raw confidence per candidate `= 0.35 × quote_strength (does the source state a consequence, or only a condition) + 0.25 × dedupe_certainty (1 − nearest similarity for creates, similarity for merges) + 0.20 × entity_resolution_confidence + 0.20 × corroboration (distinct sources naming the same risk)`. Caps: **low** when the only evidence states a condition without a consequence; **medium** when `dedupe.similarity` falls in the ambiguous band 0.55–0.75. Mandatory review regardless of confidence: any candidate with `impact >= 4`, any candidate with `action = "issue"`, and any candidate touching a `is_commitment` milestone. Those never bulk-accept. Mandatory evidence: at least one verified quote of at most 300 characters, verified by the engine as a substring of the cited source.

**Human actions available.** Accept a create into the `Risk` register with an owner; accept a merge, which updates the existing risk's likelihood, impact, or description and appends the new evidence; reclassify a create as a merge or an issue; edit likelihood or impact; reject with a reason code (`already_closed`, `not_a_risk`, `duplicate`, `insufficient_evidence`); accept a `leading_indicator` as a `KPI`.

**Downstream dependencies.** On commit: creates or updates `Risk` records with owners; risks touching schedule feed AI-31's exposure ranking and AI-33's improvement calculation; the risk register is a required section of the AI-34 pack and a mandatory node in the AI-27 storyline; a risk on a `Dependency` with low slack raises that item's `Wave` feasibility flag; accepted leading indicators become `KPI` records on the monitoring cadence.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

1. *Register inflation by restatement.* The same risk arrives every week in slightly different words. Mitigation: a mandatory dedupe pass against the full register, `action = "merge"` with `existing_risk_id` rather than a create, and the ambiguous-similarity band capped at medium so a human adjudicates.
2. *Resolved issues resurfacing as emerging risks.* Mitigation: the candidate's source date is compared against `Risk.closed_at`; a candidate whose evidence predates the closure is auto-rejected with the closure id shown.
3. *The quiet risk nobody wrote down.* An unstated dependency about to bind is invisible to text extraction. Mitigation: the deterministic pre-sweep, and `pre_sweep_dispositions` requires an explicit disposition for every prompt so a prompt cannot be ignored.
4. *Severity inflation to get attention.* Mitigation: `likelihood_rationale` and `impact_rationale` must cite the level definition; mandatory human review at `impact >= 4` means inflation costs the author review time rather than buying priority.

**Acceptance test.** Fixture: 25 narratives and 5 minutes documents spanning one month, containing 6 planted new risks, 4 restatements of existing register entries, 1 restatement of a risk closed two weeks earlier, and 3 deterministic pre-sweep conditions (one low-slack successor with no risk, one overdue decision, one single-person-covered skill). Assert: (a) 6 creates and 4 merges with the correct `existing_risk_id` for each merge; (b) zero creates for the closed risk, rejected with the closure id; (c) all three pre-sweep prompts have an explicit disposition; (d) every candidate carries at least one quote that verifies as a substring of its cited source; (e) every candidate with `impact >= 4` is routed to mandatory review and excluded from bulk accept; (f) a candidate whose only evidence states a condition without a consequence is banded low; (g) no `Risk` row is created before an accept call.

---

### 8.35 AI-33 Resequencing recommendation (Ongoing)

**Purpose.** When the roadmap has slipped or capacity has moved, propose alternative sequencings with quantified gains and losses, respecting what leadership has already committed to. Methodology row: Ongoing, AI Enhancement "recommend resequencing", supporting the activities "manage dependencies; refresh priorities".

**Same anti-silent-choice discipline as AI-21.** The output is at least two alternatives plus an explicit do-nothing baseline. `recommended` is not model-writable; only a human `Decision` selects.

**Trigger.** A red slip from AI-31; a new binding capacity constraint from AI-20; a refreshed `OpportunityScore` that changes a priority band; a budget change; or a consultant request before a governance review.

**Input contract.** The committed `RoadmapScenario` with its `RoadmapItem`, `Wave`, and start dates; the AI-31 `SlippageReport` with downstream forecasts; the AI-20 `CapacityAnalysis` with constraint windows; refreshed `OpportunityScore` and the active `ScoringModel`; the `Dependency` graph with slack and reasons; `CostEstimate` by year with `basis`, and remaining budget by year; `ValueCase` and `Benefit` ramps; the `Decision` log, with each decision's protected scope (items whose dates or scope the board has fixed); `Milestone` records with `is_commitment`; and the previous AI-33 proposal set with its dispositions, for the cooldown rule.

Retrieval scope: current engagement only. Limits: at most 60 items and 200 edges into context; at most 6 candidate move sets.

**What the model must determine.**

1. Two to five candidate move sets plus the mandatory do-nothing baseline. Each move is atomic: `{item_id, from_wave, to_wave, from_start, to_start, reason_code}` where `reason_code` is one of `clear_capacity_gap`, `absorb_predecessor_slip`, `respond_to_priority_change`, `respect_budget_year`, `unblock_successor`, `consolidate_duplicate_scope`.
2. For each candidate: what improves, quantified by the engine after re-running the models (capacity gap cleared in FTE-months, benefit recovered in months and annual value, red slips cleared, risks mitigated).
3. For each candidate: what worsens, quantified the same way (benefit deferred, risk exposure added, cost moved into a later year, milestones moved).
4. `constraint_compliance`: the constraints the candidate respects, and any it breaches, each breach naming the `Decision` id or `Milestone` id and the approval it would require.
5. `premise` of one sentence per candidate, and `does_not_answer`.
6. The comparison against do-nothing on the same metrics, so the cost of inaction is visible.

Engine validation, before anything is shown: topological order holds for all `hard_blocks` edges; the capacity model re-runs and the claimed gap change matches; the cost model re-runs and the claimed year movements match; the benefit ramps re-run and the claimed delays match. A candidate whose claims do not reproduce is dropped.

Churn control: a candidate must clear a `min_improvement` bar, defined as clearing at least one red slip, or clearing at least 1.0 FTE-month of capacity gap, or recovering at least one month of benefit. A move on the same item proposed and rejected within the last review cycle is suppressed unless an input changed materially, tracked by a hash of the item's inputs.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type ResequencingProposal = {
  scenario_id: string; triggered_by: "slippage"|"capacity"|"priority_refresh"|"budget"|"manual";
  baseline_do_nothing: {
    red_slips_open: number; peak_capacity_gap_fte: number;
    benefit_deferred_months_total: number; cost_by_year: Record<string, number>;
    milestones_breached: string[];
  };
  candidates: {
    candidate_id: string; premise: string;
    moves: { item_id: string; from_wave: number; to_wave: number;
             from_start: string; to_start: string; reason_code: string }[];
    engine_verified: boolean;
    improves: { capacity_gap_cleared_fte_months: number; red_slips_cleared: string[];
                benefit_recovered_months: number; annual_value_recovered: number;
                risks_mitigated: string[] };
    worsens: { benefit_deferred_months: number; annual_value_deferred: number;
               risks_added: string[]; cost_moved_by_year: Record<string, number>;
               milestones_moved: string[] };
    constraint_compliance: { respected: string[];
      breaches: { kind: "committed_decision"|"commitment_milestone"|"budget_cap"|"hard_dependency";
                  ref_id: string; approval_required: string }[] };
    meets_min_improvement: boolean;
    does_not_answer: string;
    recommended: null;
  }[];
  suppressed_by_cooldown: { item_id: string; last_rejected_at: string }[];
};
```

**Confidence and evidence.** Per candidate: raw confidence `= 0.30 × input_freshness (slippage and capacity run ages) + 0.25 × dependency_completeness + 0.25 × committed_cost_and_value_share for moved items + 0.20 × engine_verified`. Caps: **medium** when any moved item's cost is `precedent_directional`; **medium** when the slippage or capacity input is more than 14 days old; **low** when any moved item's `ValueCase` is unquantified, because the benefit recovery figure would then be unsupported. Mandatory evidence: the `SlippageReport` run id, the `CapacityAnalysis` run id, and for each breach the `Decision` or `Milestone` record.

**Human actions available.** Accept a candidate, creating a new `RoadmapScenario` version; edit a move set and revalidate; reject with a reason (feeding the cooldown); request board approval for a breach; accept do-nothing explicitly, which records a `Decision` that the slip is tolerated; mark one candidate as recommended, which is a human `Decision`.

**Downstream dependencies.** On accept: creates a new `RoadmapScenario` version rather than editing the committed one; updates `Wave` and `RoadmapItem` dates; a moved `is_commitment` milestone requires an approved rebaseline `Decision` before it takes effect; recomputes `Benefit` ramps, `KPI` dates, capacity utilisation, and the investment profile; triggers a full AI-30 staleness sweep across every bound `NarrativeMessage` and `Exhibit` caption at all four audience levels; feeds the decisions-required section of the AI-34 pack.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

1. *Broken dependency order.* Mitigation: topological validation on `hard_blocks` edges, plus engine re-verification of every claimed effect; unverified candidates are dropped rather than shown with a caveat.
2. *Churn.* A resequencing proposal every review cycle erodes trust in the plan. Mitigation: the `min_improvement` bar plus the cooldown suppression, with `suppressed_by_cooldown` reported so the suppression is visible rather than silent.
3. *Quietly moving a board-committed item.* Mitigation: `constraint_compliance.breaches` must name the `Decision` id and the approval required; a candidate with an unlisted breach fails engine validation because the protected-scope check runs independently of the model.
4. *Optimising capacity into a value hole.* A tidy resource curve that pushes the largest benefit out a year. Mitigation: `worsens.annual_value_deferred` is mandatory and computed by the engine, and the do-nothing baseline is always shown on the same metrics.

**Acceptance test.** Fixture: committed scenario with one red slip (45-day predecessor slip, 20-day successor slack), one binding 2.5 FTE capacity gap, one `Decision`-protected item, one `is_commitment` milestone, and 20 dependency edges of which 8 are `hard_blocks`. Assert: (a) at least two candidates plus the do-nothing baseline; (b) every shown candidate has `engine_verified = true` and passes topological validation; (c) each candidate reports both `improves` and `worsens` with non-zero quantities matching an independent recomputation; (d) any candidate that moves the protected item lists a `committed_decision` breach with that `Decision` id and the approval required; (e) all `recommended` fields are `null`; (f) the committed scenario's item dates are unchanged after generation; (g) rejecting a candidate and rerunning with unchanged inputs returns it under `suppressed_by_cooldown` rather than as a candidate; (h) a candidate clearing only 0.3 FTE-months has `meets_min_improvement = false` and is not shown.

---

### 8.36 AI-34 Governance review pack drafting (Ongoing)

**Purpose.** Draft the recurring governance pack as a delta against the previous period, with bound numbers, named decisions, and the red items surfaced rather than smoothed. Methodology row: Ongoing, AI Enhancement "automatically refresh executive and Board views", supporting the activities "conduct governance reviews; update leadership views".

**Inference note.** The section list below is an invention consistent with the governance artefacts the reference engagement's execution-planning deck proposed standing up: a monthly budget and spend tracker, a portfolio health scorecard, weekly status reporting, and a QBR cadence with quarterly improvement planning. The cadence itself and the existence of the pack come from the methodology's Ongoing row. Everything the pack reports on (roadmap, cost, value, risk, decisions, maturity) is observed.

**Trigger.** The governance cadence (weekly status, monthly tracker, or quarterly review, each with its own section subset); or on demand before an unscheduled leadership session.

**Input contract.** Everything since the previous pack: `ActualsSnapshot` set; `Milestone` status and the AI-31 `SlippageReport`; budget versus actual by initiative and by the six cost categories; `KPI` actuals against targets; `Risk` register deltas including AI-32 accepted candidates; the `Decision` log split into closed since last, open now, and needed next; the AI-33 `ResequencingProposal` set with dispositions; `ValueCase` and `Benefit` realisation to date; `ActivationTask` completion for the 90-day plan; the previous pack's element set and its bindings, so the new pack is a delta rather than a restatement; and the reporting coverage figure (share of active initiatives that submitted a snapshot).

Retrieval scope: current engagement, current period plus the previous pack. Limits: at most 200 items; narrative inputs summarised by AI-31 and AI-32 rather than re-read here.

Fixed section template (**assumption**, as noted above):

| # | Section | Required content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Portfolio health summary | every red item, the coverage caveat when applicable, the one-line position |
| 2 | Changes since last review | explicit delta list; unchanged metrics compressed to a "no change" line |
| 3 | Initiative status by wave | status per active item, with forecast dates |
| 4 | Financials versus plan | spend versus plan by year and category, open AI-19 blocking findings |
| 5 | Benefits realisation | benefits started, on track, delayed, with the delay in months |
| 6 | Risks and issues | new, escalated, closed, with owners |
| 7 | Decisions required | each with options, owner, and date needed |
| 8 | Next-period focus | at most five actions, each with an owner |

**What the model must determine.**

1. Which sections apply to this cadence, and for each, the content selected from the inputs.
2. Per section, an assertion headline with `bindings[]`, reusing the AI-27 binding contract exactly so AI-30 covers governance packs with no additional machinery. A section headline with no binding is invalid.
3. `delta_vs_previous` per section: what changed since the last pack. A section with no deltas must carry an explicit "no change" declaration rather than a restatement of last period's text.
4. The decisions required, each with an option set, an owner role, and a date needed. The AI does not set a recommendation; `recommendation` is null in model output and is filled by a named human.
5. Exhibit requests per section, handed to AI-28.
6. The audience level for the pack, handed to AI-29 (typically L2 for an operating review, L3 for a board review).
7. The coverage caveat sentence whenever reporting coverage is below 80%.

**Output schema.**

```ts
type GovernancePackDraft = {
  engagement_id: string; period: { from: string; to: string };
  cadence: "weekly"|"monthly"|"quarterly";
  reporting_coverage_pct: number; coverage_caveat: string | null;
  review_ready: boolean;                 // false when coverage < 80%
  sections: {
    section_no: 1|2|3|4|5|6|7|8; title: string;
    headline_template: string; headline_rendered: string; bindings: Binding[];
    body: string; takeaway: string;
    delta_vs_previous: { changed: { metric: string; from: unknown; to: unknown }[];
                         no_change_declared: boolean };
    exhibit_request: { intent: string; data_focus: string[] } | null;
    red_items_included: string[];
  }[];
  decisions_required: { question: string; options: string[]; owner_role: string;
                        needed_by: string; related_ids: string[];
                        recommendation: null }[];
  next_period_focus: { action: string; owner_role: string }[];   // <=5
  audience_level: "L2"|"L3";
};
```

**Confidence and evidence.** Per section: raw confidence `= 0.30 × input_freshness + 0.30 × reporting_coverage_pct + 0.25 × binding_health + 0.15 × delta_completeness`. Caps: the pack is not `review_ready` at all when coverage is below 80%, regardless of confidence; **medium** when any bound value derives from a `data_stale` item; **low** when the previous pack is unavailable, because a delta cannot then be verified. Mandatory evidence: each section carries `EvidenceRef`s for the `ActualsSnapshot` set it summarises and for the `SlippageReport` or `RiskExtraction` run it draws on; each decision carries the ids of the records that force it.

**Human actions available.** Accept a section; edit body and takeaway (numerals are bound and change only by recompute); reject and regenerate a section; accept `decisions_required` into the `Decision` log; set the recommendation on a decision, which records the human decision-maker; accept `next_period_focus` as `ActivationTask` records; publish, which runs the AI-30 blocking checks first.

**Downstream dependencies.** On commit: creates a `Deliverable` of type governance pack with its `NarrativeMessage` and `Exhibit` records; creates `Decision` records in `open` state with owners and dates; creates `ActivationTask` records for the next-period focus; refreshes the executive dashboard views; and adds every new binding to the AI-30 staleness watch list. The pack's own element set becomes the previous-pack baseline for the next period's delta.

**Failure modes and mitigations.**

1. *A green-looking pack with red items inside it.* Mitigation: every item classified red by AI-31 must appear in section 1; the validator compares `red_items_included` across sections against the `SlippageReport` and rejects the pack on any omission.
2. *Restatement instead of a delta.* Last period's text with a new date. Mitigation: `delta_vs_previous` is required per section, and a section with an empty `changed` list and `no_change_declared = false` is rejected.
3. *Decisions without owners or dates.* An ask nobody owns is not an ask. Mitigation: schema requires `owner_role` and `needed_by`; `recommendation` stays null in model output and is a separate human write.
4. *Thin reporting presented as a full picture.* Mitigation: `review_ready = false` below 80% coverage, with the caveat sentence at the top of section 1, and the pack cannot be published while `review_ready` is false without an explicit override recorded as an `AuditEvent`.

**Acceptance test.** Fixture: two consecutive periods; period two contains three changed metrics, one red slip, two newly accepted risks, one closed decision, one decision needed, 90% reporting coverage, and a previous pack with bindings. Assert: (a) all eight sections present for a quarterly cadence; (b) the red item appears in section 1's `red_items_included`; (c) sections whose metrics did not change carry `no_change_declared = true` and no restated body; (d) `delta_vs_previous.changed` lists exactly the three changed metrics with correct from and to values; (e) the decision required carries `owner_role` and `needed_by`, and `recommendation` is null; (f) every section headline has at least one binding and every numeral in every rendered headline lies inside a binding span; (g) dropping coverage to 70% sets `review_ready = false`, produces a non-null `coverage_caveat`, and blocks publish without an override `AuditEvent`; (h) removing the red item from section 1 causes the pack to be rejected.

FR ranges are reserved blocks within each module's hundred series. **Assumption:** the module sections (M6 to M9) number their requirements inside the blocks shown here, so that an AI capability and the functional requirements it serves stay adjacent in the document.

Acceptance rate is measured as defined in section 8.1: accepted plus edited-and-accepted `AISuggestion`s over total suggestions surfaced, excluding suggestions superseded by an input change before review. The rates for AI-21, AI-33, and AI-34 are deliberately low because those capabilities produce sets from which one option is chosen; the meaningful measure there is whether any option in the set advanced, which is stated in the table where it applies.

## 9. Integrations, Import and Export (FR-1200 to FR-1299)

This section covers everything that crosses the product boundary: what comes in from the firm's existing artifacts and the client's systems of record, and what goes out to the client. Two rules govern the whole section. Inbound, nothing is inferred silently; every inference is either recorded as a reversible transform or raised as a decision. Outbound, nothing is emitted that cannot be traced back to a `ModelSnapshot`.

### 9.1 Legacy workbook import (FR-1200 to FR-1219)

The commercial case for this sub-module is direct. Consultants already hold engagement workbooks of exactly the reference engagement's shape, they will not retype a 55-row scored register with 43 rows of narrative rationale into a new tool, and an import that only succeeds on clean files will never be used, because no such file exists. The reference engagement's two workbooks contained, between them, fifteen sheets, four of them hidden in one file and four in the other, and every one of the known defects listed in this PRD. The importer's job is not to read a tidy spreadsheet. It is to read that file and hand back a validation report that turns each defect into a decision a consultant can make in minutes.

#### 9.1.1 Detection and mapping

**FR-1200 — Import session.** The product MUST provide an import session that accepts one or more `.xlsx` files together, because in the reference engagement a formula in one workbook resolved against a sheet that existed intact only in the other. A session produces exactly one `LegacyImport` record holding the source files (retained byte-for-byte), the detected structure, every mapping decision, every transform applied, the validation report, and the resulting entity set. A session is re-runnable against the same sources and produces the same result given the same decisions.

**FR-1201 — Sheet role detection.** For every sheet in every file, including hidden and very-hidden sheets, the importer MUST propose a role from a closed vocabulary: `Readme`, `MaturityFrameworkDefinitions`, `MaturityAssessment`, `OpportunityRegister`, `OpportunityRegisterSuperseded`, `ScoringGuide`, `ThemeTaxonomy`, `ThemeDefinitions`, `PriorityHeatMap`, `EnumPickList`, `Scratch`, `Unknown`. Detection signals MUST include sheet name, the presence of a merged title row, freeze-pane position, autofilter range, column-header text matched against a role's expected header vocabulary, and formula shape. Every proposal carries a confidence and the signals that produced it.

- `AC-1201.1` Every sheet appears in the mapping UI with a proposed role, a row and column count, and its visibility state. No sheet may be omitted from the list, and no sheet may be imported or discarded without an explicit role assignment or an explicit `Scratch` marking.
- `AC-1201.2` A sheet whose proposed role is `Unknown` blocks completion of the import until the user assigns a role or marks it `Scratch` with a reason.

**FR-1202 — Header row and weight row detection.** The importer MUST NOT assume that row 1 is the header row. In the reference workbooks the register header row sat at row 4 in one file and rows 5 and 6 in another, with the dimension weights on a separate row above the header, a merged title spanning row 1, and data starting two rows below the header. Detection MUST use freeze panes, autofilter reference, the first row with a high ratio of non-empty short text cells, and the position of the first row whose cells match a data type pattern. Where a row above the header holds numeric values summing to 1.0 across the score columns, the importer MUST propose that row as the weight row and route those values into a candidate `ScoringModel`, not into the register.

- `AC-1202.1` The proposed header row, weight row, and first data row are shown as a highlighted preview over the actual sheet grid, and each can be corrected by clicking the correct row.
- `AC-1202.2` Weights detected from a weight row are imported into a `ScoringModel` draft and presented for confirmation against the product's configured weights. A mismatch is a decision line, not an overwrite.

**FR-1203 — Column mapping UI.** The importer MUST present, per sheet with an assigned role, a two-pane mapping between source columns and target fields. Each source column shows its header text, its detected type, its hidden state, its dominant formula pattern if any, the count of populated cells, and three sample values. Each proposed target field shows the entity and field name and whether the field is authored or derived. The user can remap, set to ignore, or route a column to a free-text `SourceNote` field.

- `AC-1203.1` A column whose header is populated but whose data cells are entirely empty is flagged `declared-but-empty` and defaults to ignore. Grounded: the master register declared a span or duration column with a full descriptive header and no values in any row, while the derived share copy carried the same field populated.
- `AC-1203.2` A hidden column whose formula pattern shows it is computed from a visible column MUST be classified as derived and MUST NOT be mappable to an authored field. It may be mapped only to a verification target used by FR-1206.
- `AC-1203.3` The mapping is saved as a named `ImportProfile` reusable across future imports of the same workbook lineage.

**FR-1204 — Derived fields are recomputed, never imported.** Any target field that the calculation engine of §7 computes MUST be recomputed from imported inputs and MUST NOT take its value from the source file. This applies at minimum to the per-dimension numeric score, the weighted score, the priority band, the quadrant axes, the quadrant label, the maturity gap, the maturity level label, and all theme and initiative rollups. Imported cached values for these fields are retained as `ImportedValue` for verification only.

- `AC-1204.1` After import, a verification table lists every row where the recomputed value differs from the imported cached value, with the delta and the defect that explains it. Grounded: in the reference maturity sheet the gap column and the level label column were both formulas over the current and target level, so both are reproducible; in the register the weighted score, band, quadrant axes and quadrant label were all formulas over the three numeric scores.
- `AC-1204.2` A difference that the report cannot attribute to a named defect is raised as a blocker, because it means the product's engine and the source's arithmetic disagree for an unknown reason.

**FR-1205 — Hidden sheet and hidden column handling.** Hidden and very-hidden sheets MUST be treated as first-class candidates, not as noise, and MUST NOT be imported by default. Grounded: in the reference file set, one hidden sheet held the only intact theme-to-initiative taxonomy that the visible registers depended on, a second hidden sheet held a superseded register on an incompatible identifier and score scale, a third held a five-value status pick list that the visible sheets used as an enum, and a fourth held a duplicate extract with a different column order. The correct treatment differs per sheet, so the importer requires one decision per hidden sheet: import under an assigned role, import as historical reference only, or discard as scratch with a recorded reason.

- `AC-1205.1` For each hidden sheet the report states what depends on it, computed by scanning visible-sheet formulas for references to that sheet name.
- `AC-1205.2` Discarding a hidden sheet that visible sheets reference is a blocker unless the referencing formulas are themselves being discarded.

#### 9.1.2 The validation report

**FR-1206 — Validation report structure.** The importer MUST produce a `ValidationReport` before any entity is written. Each line carries: a stable line ID, a severity of `Blocker`, `Decision`, `Warning`, or `Info`, a defect class from the closed list in FR-1207 to FR-1214, a precise locator (file, sheet, cell or range, row set), the observed condition in plain language, the candidate resolutions with one marked as the proposed default, and the decision state. The report is filterable by severity and defect class, sortable by sheet, exportable, and persisted with the `LegacyImport`.

- `AC-1206.1` The import cannot be promoted to an active `Engagement` while any line is severity `Blocker` or is severity `Decision` with state `undecided`. It may be saved and resumed indefinitely.
- `AC-1206.2` Every decision records actor, timestamp, chosen resolution, and optional note, and is written to the `AuditEvent` log.
- `AC-1206.3` The report opens with a summary line per defect class giving the count of affected rows, so a consultant can see the size of the job before starting it.

**FR-1207 — Defect class D1, prose-string scores.** The importer MUST detect score cells that carry a display string rather than a number and MUST extract the numeric score with confirmation. Grounded: every score cell in the reference registers held a single string combining the numeral, the anchor label, and a full sentence of anchor definition, for example a leading `4` followed by an anchor name and a sentence describing what that level means; the numeric value used by every downstream formula was recovered by taking the first character of that string and coercing it to a number.

Resolution mechanics:

1. Parse the leading integer token. Match the remaining text against the anchor definitions on the `ScoringGuide` sheet for that dimension using normalized similarity.
2. Emit a proposal of `(score, anchorLevel, residualProse)` where the residual prose is routed to the `ScoreRationale` field so no consultant writing is lost.
3. Require confirmation, individually or in bulk by identical string, where any of the following holds: no leading integer token; the leading integer is outside the configured scale; the leading numeric token is longer than one digit, because a single-character extraction silently truncates a two-digit value; the anchor text matches no guide anchor above threshold; or the same numeral maps to two different anchor texts elsewhere in the same column.
4. Auto-apply only where the leading token is a single digit inside the scale and the anchor text matches exactly one guide anchor above threshold, and record the auto-apply in the transform log with a one-click revert.

- `AC-1207.1` Cells whose string carries a numeral inconsistent with its anchor text (for example a leading `3` followed by the level-4 anchor sentence) are always confirmations, never auto-applies.
- `AC-1207.2` After import, no `Opportunity` numeric score field contains a string, and the anchor label and the rationale prose are separate fields.

**FR-1208 — Defect class D2, misaligned formula rows.** The importer MUST fingerprint the dominant formula pattern of every formula column, normalize it by row index, and flag every cell whose pattern diverges. Grounded: in the reference master register the priority-band column held the band conditional chain for the first 42 data rows and then, from a specific row onward, held the quadrant x-axis average formula instead, while the adjacent column held a bare reference to the risk score, so from that row down two columns produced values under the wrong headers.

- `AC-1208.1` The report states, per column, the dominant pattern, the count and list of divergent cells, and the first row at which divergence begins.
- `AC-1208.2` Candidate resolutions per divergent cell: recompute from the product engine and discard the source cell (proposed default), accept the imported cached value as an explicit override with a required reason, or exclude the row from import.
- `AC-1208.3` A column in which more than 20% of cells diverge is escalated to `Blocker`, because the column's intended meaning is no longer determinable from the file.

**FR-1209 — Defect class D3, broken external references.** The importer MUST detect any formula containing an external workbook reference, any cached `#REF!` or `#N/A` error, and any defined name resolving outside the file set. Grounded: the reference share workbook computed its weighted scores with a `SUMPRODUCT` whose weight range was an external reference into another workbook, and both registers resolved their theme column through a lookup against an externally referenced taxonomy sheet; the cached values survived the copy, the links did not.

- `AC-1209.1` For each broken reference the importer attempts resolution inside the current import session's file set by matching sheet name and range shape, and where it succeeds it proposes that resolution with the matched target shown.
- `AC-1209.2` Where resolution fails, the candidate resolutions are: supply the missing workbook and re-resolve, accept the cached value as a literal and mark the field `unverified`, or recompute the field from the product's own model (available where the field is derived).
- `AC-1209.3` A value accepted as an unverified literal is visibly marked as such wherever it appears and appears in the §12.2 unbasis'd-number count until replaced.

**FR-1210 — Defect class D4, duplicate and near-duplicate taxonomy names.** The importer MUST collect the distinct set of theme strings and initiative strings across every sheet in the session, cluster them by normalized similarity, and present each cluster with more than one member as a merge decision. Grounded: the reference file set contained four canonical theme names, one taxonomy row carrying a variant of one of those names with two leading words removed, a second sheet spelling the first theme with a typographical error and a different second word, a `Theme Definitions` sheet carrying an explicit column of retired names, and conditional-formatting rules across five sheets still keyed to four theme names that no longer appeared in any data cell.

- `AC-1210.1` Each cluster shows every member string, its occurrence count, the sheets it appears on, and whether it appears in a data cell, a header, a conditional-formatting rule, or a retired-name column.
- `AC-1210.2` Candidate resolutions per cluster: pick a canonical label and record the others as `ThemeAlias` records so historical exhibits and prior decks still resolve; split into two or more genuinely distinct `Theme` records; or map a member to an existing `Theme` in the target engagement.
- `AC-1210.3` No cluster is ever auto-merged, including clusters differing only by case or trailing whitespace, because a case difference in the reference file set coexisted with a genuine rename.
- `AC-1210.4` Theme or initiative strings that appear only in conditional-formatting rules and in no data cell are reported as `Info` with the recommendation to discard, and are never created as `Theme` records.

**FR-1211 — Defect class D5, discontiguous validation ranges.** For every column carrying a list validation, the importer MUST compute the validation's coverage against the populated data rows and report the uncovered rows. Grounded: the reference master register applied a two-value yes/no list validation to a set of ranges with several row gaps, leaving rows in the same column with no dropdown and therefore no enforcement.

- `AC-1211.1` The report states, per validated column, the enum members, the covered row count, the uncovered row count, the specific uncovered rows, and any existing value in the column outside the enum.
- `AC-1211.2` Candidate resolutions: adopt the enum for the whole column and list any out-of-enum values as sub-decisions (proposed default), declare the column free text, or ignore the column.
- `AC-1211.3` After import, an enum field is enforced across every row of the entity with no per-row exemption, and the product has no mechanism for partial enum coverage.

**FR-1212 — Defect class D6, prose typed into enum cells.** The importer MUST detect a column whose header or an adjacent legend declares a closed set of values but whose cells hold free prose, and MUST NOT discard the prose. Grounded: the reference heat-map sheet declared a three-value investment-type legend at the top of the sheet and gave the corresponding column that header, and every cell in that column instead held a two-sentence rationale explaining why the item mattered.

- `AC-1212.1` Detection triggers when a declared or inferred enum column has fewer than 20% of cells matching an enum member and a median cell length above 60 characters.
- `AC-1212.2` Candidate resolutions: retarget the column's content to a named free-text field with the target proposed by best match against the target entity's text fields (for the grounded case, the "why it matters" narrative field), and leave the enum unset; keep the enum and set values manually; or extend the enum with the observed distinct values where they are in fact short and repeated.
- `AC-1212.3` Retargeted prose is imported verbatim with a `SourceLocator` back to the original cell.

**FR-1213 — Defect class D7, alternate score scale in a hidden sheet.** The importer MUST detect any numeric score column whose observed values fall outside the declared scale and MUST NOT rescale automatically. Grounded: a hidden ranking sheet in the reference share workbook carried a score column with values of 8, 7, 5 and 4 while its own row labels quoted band boundaries expressed on a 1 to 5 scale, and its effort and value columns used single-letter codes not used anywhere in the visible registers.

- `AC-1213.1` The report states the declared scale, the observed minimum, maximum and distinct value set, and the count of rows outside the declared scale.
- `AC-1213.2` Candidate resolutions: import as a separate historical `ScoreSet` carrying its own declared scale and excluded from all current calculations and exhibits (proposed default); apply an explicit user-supplied mapping table from source value to target value, stored and shown wherever the mapped scores appear; or discard the column.
- `AC-1213.3` The product MUST NOT mix score sets on different scales in any calculation, chart, or export, and MUST refuse to compute a weighted score from inputs on more than one scale.

**FR-1214 — Defect class D8, competing identifier schemes.** The importer MUST mint its own canonical `Opportunity` identifiers and MUST preserve every identifier found in the sources as an `ExternalRef` carrying scheme name, value, and source locator. Grounded: the reference visible registers had no identifier column at all, so an opportunity's identity was the pair of its initiative text and its opportunity text, while a hidden sheet used a prefixed sequential scheme over a smaller set of items that did not reconcile one-to-one with the visible rows.

- `AC-1214.1` Where two sheets in the session appear to describe the same opportunity set under different schemes, the importer produces a reconciliation table with three sections: proposed matches with a similarity score and the matched fields, rows present only in the primary sheet, and rows present only in the secondary sheet.
- `AC-1214.2` Every proposed match requires confirmation. Confirmed matches create one `Opportunity` with two `ExternalRef` records. Unmatched secondary rows are imported as separate `Opportunity` records with status `Superseded` unless the user links or discards them.
- `AC-1214.3` Identity based on a text pair is never used as a durable key after import. The canonical identifier is stable across renames, and renaming an opportunity does not break any reference to it.

**FR-1215 — The importer never silently guesses.** Every inference the importer makes MUST be materialized in one of exactly two places: the transform log, holding auto-applied transforms each with a plain-language description, the affected cell range, and a one-click revert; or the validation report, holding every ambiguity as a line requiring a decision. There is no third path. The importer MUST NOT drop a row, drop a column, coerce a type, normalize a string, merge two values, rescale a number, or resolve a broken reference outside those two mechanisms.

- `AC-1215.1` The conditions in the following list MUST be decisions and MUST NOT be auto-applied under any confidence: any theme or initiative name merge; any cross-scheme identifier match; any score scale mapping; any acceptance of an imported cached value over a recomputed one; any hidden sheet import or discard; any enum extension; any row exclusion.
- `AC-1215.2` The count of auto-applied transforms and the count of decisions are both shown on the import summary, and a consultant can review the full transform log as a list before promotion.
- `AC-1215.3` A completed import produces a signed `ImportManifest` stating source file hashes, the profile used, every decision with its chosen resolution, every transform, and the resulting entity counts. The manifest is retained for the life of the engagement.

**FR-1216 — Import-time confidentiality triage.** On import the product MUST run the classification scan of FR-1310 across all imported text and MUST report what it found before the data becomes generally visible: person names, email addresses, telephone numbers, currency amounts, credential-shaped strings, threaded review comments with named authors, and any content matching the security-sensitive classes of FR-1314. Grounded: the reference workbooks carried a confidentiality marking on their introduction sheet, threaded reviewer comments naming delivery staff and asking each other to validate specific scores, contact details, named individuals identified as sole incumbents for critical systems, an inventory of security tooling with coverage gaps, a reference to a historical security incident, and currency figures.

- `AC-1216.1` The triage output lists each finding class with a count and a sample, and offers per class: import and classify at the stated level, import and immediately redact, or exclude from import.
- `AC-1216.2` Threaded comments import as `Comment` records with authorship preserved and classified `PersonIdentifying`, so they can never leave the engagement through a client-facing export (FR-1304).
- `AC-1216.3` A source cell containing a named individual described as a sole point of failure creates the corresponding risk statement at role level and records the individual link separately, subject to FR-1313.

**FR-1217 — Maturity sheet import specifics.** For a sheet with role `MaturityAssessment`, the importer MUST map to the `MaturityAssessment` structure of §5: capability area, focus area, current level as an integer, target level as an integer, current-state summary, rationale, evidence text, gaps text, next steps, priority-to-fix, and review status. Grounded: the reference sheet held 28 focus areas grouped under 8 capability areas, with the gap and the level label as formulas and the level scale defined on a separate framework sheet.

- `AC-1217.1` Gap and level label are recomputed per FR-1204 and are not importable.
- `AC-1217.2` The framework definition sheet, where present, is imported as a candidate `MaturityFramework` and matched against the registered frameworks; a level-count or level-name mismatch is a decision.
- `AC-1217.3` Multi-fact current-state cells, where the source packed several distinct observations into one cell with an internal separator, are split into candidate `Finding` records with the separator shown and the split offered for confirmation. Grounded: the reference current-state cells packed six or more separate observations into a single cell with a repeated delimiter.

**FR-1218 — Unparseable and empty sources.** The importer MUST report any file it cannot parse, including zero-length files, password-protected files, and files whose extension does not match their content, as an explicit report line. It MUST NOT skip them silently. Grounded: the reference archive contained a zero-byte presentation file sitting inside the final deliverable folder.

**FR-1219 — Import rollback.** A promoted import MUST be reversible for a configurable window (default 7 days) provided no `ModelSnapshot` has been issued from it, and the reversal MUST remove exactly the entities the import created, leave anything created since untouched, and be recorded in the audit log.

### 9.2 Interview and transcript ingestion (FR-1220 to FR-1229)

**FR-1220 — Supported inbound formats.** The product MUST accept, as sources for a `Transcript`: audio files in `wav`, `mp3`, `m4a`, `aac`, `flac`, `ogg` up to 4 hours and 500 MB each; video files in `mp4`, `mov`, `webm` with audio extracted; transcript exports in `vtt`, `srt`, `txt`, `docx`, and the JSON transcript exports of the common meeting platforms (Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Google Meet); and typed notes as pasted text, `md`, `docx`, or direct entry in the interview workspace. Each source records its format, duration where applicable, and the tool that produced it.

**FR-1221 — Speaker attribution is mandatory.** Every utterance in a `Transcript` MUST carry a speaker label, and every distinct speaker label MUST be resolved to a `Stakeholder`, to a consultant `User`, or explicitly to `Unattributed` before the transcript can be used as a source of `Evidence`.

- `AC-1221.1` For diarized audio, the product presents each machine label (`Speaker 1`, `Speaker 2`) with its total speaking time and three sample utterances, and the consultant maps it in one screen.
- `AC-1221.2` For platform exports that already carry display names, the product proposes a match against the engagement's `Stakeholder` list and requires confirmation of each match.
- `AC-1221.3` `Evidence` derived from an `Unattributed` utterance carries `attribution = unknown`, is excluded from any per-stakeholder aggregation such as stakeholder priorities and sentiment by role, and is visibly marked in the evidence list.
- `AC-1221.4` Speaker labels are classified `PersonIdentifying` and are subject to the redaction operation of FR-1312.

**FR-1222 — Transcript locator.** A `TranscriptLocator` MUST be a structured, stable, machine-resolvable value with the shape below, and every `Evidence` record sourced from a transcript MUST carry one. The product MUST render it as a human-readable string and MUST make it clickable, opening the transcript scrolled to the span with the span highlighted and, where audio is retained, the player seeked to `startMs`.

```json
{
  "sourceId": "src_9f3c…",
  "transcriptVersion": 2,
  "segmentIndex": 147,
  "startMs": 2841200,
  "endMs": 2859000,
  "charStart": 18422,
  "charEnd": 18734,
  "speakerLabel": "S2",
  "stakeholderId": "stk_41b…",
  "display": "Interview 7, 47:21, VP Infrastructure"
}
```

- `AC-1222.1` Re-transcription or manual correction of a transcript creates a new `transcriptVersion`. Existing `Evidence` continues to resolve against the version it cited, and the UI marks it "cited version differs from current" with a one-click re-anchor that shows the diff of the cited span.
- `AC-1222.2` A locator whose span can no longer be resolved renders as a broken-citation state and counts toward the §12.2 integrity metrics. It never renders as plain text with the citation dropped.
