- `AC-1222.3` Locators are valid for typed notes as well, using `charStart` and `charEnd` with `segmentIndex` and the millisecond fields null.

**FR-1223 — Transcription is a reviewed step.** Machine transcription MUST be treated as a draft. The interview workspace MUST show the transcript alongside the audio with confidence shading on low-confidence spans, allow inline correction, and require the transcript to be marked `Reviewed` before it can be cited in a client-facing artifact. Uncorrected transcripts may be used for internal synthesis and are marked as such on any derived `Finding`.

**FR-1224 — Interview metadata.** Every `Transcript` MUST record the linked `Interview` (date, interviewer, interviewee list, capability areas in scope, guide version used), a consent flag stating whether the interviewee was informed of recording, and an audio-retention choice per FR-1311. An interview with the consent flag unset cannot have its audio retained beyond the transcription job.

**FR-1225 — Typed notes parity.** Typed notes MUST produce the same downstream object set as a transcript: a source, addressable spans, speaker attribution where the note-taker recorded it, and `Evidence` with locators. The product MUST NOT create a second-class path for interviews that were not recorded, because in the reference engagement a substantial part of the fact base came from functional deep dives and strategy discussions that produced notes rather than recordings.

### 9.3 Document ingestion (FR-1230 to FR-1239)

**FR-1230 — Document type vocabulary and per-type extraction contract.** The product MUST support the document types the methodology names as Weeks 1 to 2 inputs, and for each type MUST define which structured records extraction is expected to yield. Extraction MUST NOT be a generic "read the file and see what happens" operation; each type has a target record set, and the extraction result is scored against that target so coverage gaps are visible.

| Document type | Accepted formats | Extraction expectation | Structured records yielded |
|---|---|---|---|
| Strategy deck or document | `pptx`, `pdf`, `docx` | The list of named strategic goals or priorities, each with its verbatim statement and a slide or page locator, plus the strategy's own time horizon | `StrategicObjective` (name, verbatim statement, horizon, locator), `Evidence` |
| Project or initiative list | `xlsx`, `csv`, `pptx` | One record per in-flight or proposed project with name, owner, status, start and end, funded state | `ExistingInitiative`, plus candidate links to `Initiative` |
| Application landscape | `xlsx`, `csv`, `pdf` | One record per application with name, business capability served, owner, hosting, lifecycle or end-of-support date, integration count | `Application`, `RiskFlag` for any end-of-support date inside the roadmap horizon |
| Budgets | `xlsx`, `csv` | Cost lines by category and fiscal year with capital and operating split, and the budget's own basis year | `BudgetLine` only. No `CostEstimate` and no `ValueCase` is ever created from a budget document |
| Org charts | `pptx`, `pdf`, `xlsx`, `csv` | Person, title, function, reporting line, vacancy state | `Stakeholder` candidates, `OrgUnit`, `RiskFlag` for a named single-incumbent role subject to FR-1313 |
| Architecture | `pdf`, `pptx`, `vsdx`, images | Platform inventory, integration patterns and their transport, stated architectural constraints and standards | `Application`, `Constraint`, `Evidence`. Unparseable diagrams are retained as `Exhibit` with a manual annotation task |
| Vendor information | `xlsx`, `pdf` | Vendor, product, contract type, term start and end, renewal or notice date, spend presence | `Vendor`, `ContractRef`. Contract currency values extract only with confirmation and classify `Restricted` |
| Prior assessments | `pptx`, `pdf`, `xlsx` | Previously assessed capability areas with prior level, prior recommendation, and assessment date | `PriorAssessmentFinding`, mapped to focus areas but never merged into the live `MaturityAssessment` |
| Survey instrument or results | `xlsx`, `csv` | Question set, response set, respondent function | `SurveyInstrument`, `SurveyResponse` (see 9.4) |
| Firm precedent material | any | Handled only through the anonymized precedent path of FR-1302, never as a client-engagement source | `PrecedentRecord` |

**FR-1231 — Extraction output contract.** Every extracted record MUST carry: the target entity and field values, a confidence in `[0,1]`, a `SourceLocator` (file, page or slide, bounding region or character span), and the verbatim span the value was read from. A record below the configured confidence threshold (default 0.7) enters the extraction review queue and is not written to the model until reviewed.

- `AC-1231.1` Clicking any extracted value opens the source at the locator with the span highlighted. This holds for `pdf` page regions, `pptx` shapes, and `xlsx` cells.
- `AC-1231.2` The extraction result screen shows, per document, the target record set for its type, the count found per target, and the targets with zero records, so a strategy deck from which no named goal was extracted is visibly a gap rather than a silent success.

**FR-1232 — Extraction never creates an Opportunity.** Document extraction MUST NOT create `Opportunity` records. Opportunities originate from maturity gaps and findings through AI-11 with consultant confirmation, or from direct authoring. Extraction may create `Finding` candidates and `RiskFlag` records that feed that path.

Rationale: the reference register's opportunities each carried a recommended action written as a directive and a "so what" statement written for an executive reader, neither of which exists in a source document. An opportunity is a consulting judgment, and letting extraction mint them would fill the register with restated document contents that then get scored.

**FR-1233 — OCR and scanned documents.** Scanned `pdf` files MUST be OCR'd, the OCR confidence retained per page, and any page below threshold flagged. `Evidence` from an OCR'd span carries the OCR confidence in addition to the extraction confidence.

**FR-1234 — Document request register linkage.** Every ingested document MUST be linkable to a line on the M1 document request list, and the request list MUST show requested, received, outstanding, and declined-with-reason states. AI-01 consumes this register to identify what is missing. An engagement cannot pass the M2 exit criteria with outstanding requests that have neither a received document nor a recorded reason.

**FR-1235 — Ingestion is idempotent and de-duplicating.** Re-uploading a byte-identical file MUST be detected by content hash and MUST offer to link to the existing source rather than create a duplicate. A near-duplicate (same name, different hash) MUST be offered as a new version of the existing source, preserving locators against the prior version per AC-1222.1.

### 9.4 Survey capture (FR-1240 to FR-1249)

Grounded: the reference engagement ran a survey whose results were played back in the onsite deck as a respondent count, a breakdown of respondents across eight functional areas including one area with zero respondents, coded strength themes across four categories, a "tensions beneath the surface" synthesis, and a word cloud. That is a distribution, a coding, and three exhibits, and all of it was assembled by hand.

**FR-1240 — Survey instrument.** The product MUST provide a `SurveyInstrument` builder supporting question types: single-select Likert on a configurable 1 to 5 or 1 to 7 scale with labelled anchors, single-select from a list, multi-select with an optional maximum, ranked ordering, numeric, and free text. Every instrument MUST include a respondent-function question whose option list is the engagement's own capability area or functional area list, so results can be broken down against the structure the assessment already uses. Instruments are versioned; editing an instrument after distribution creates a new version and responses record the version they answered.

**FR-1241 — Distribution and completion tracking.** The product MUST distribute a survey by per-respondent tokenized link, track invited, started, completed and declined per invitee against the `Stakeholder` list, support reminders, and support an anonymous mode in which the token is not stored against a `Stakeholder` and only the respondent-function answer is retained.

- `AC-1241.1` A survey can be marked anonymous only before distribution, and the mode is displayed on every view of its results.
- `AC-1241.2` Completion rate is shown as completed over invited, per functional area.

**FR-1242 — Results as a distribution object.** Survey results MUST be represented as a `SurveyResultDistribution` computed by the calculation engine, not as a static chart. For each question it MUST hold: `n`, response count per option, percentage per option, mean and median for ordered scales, standard deviation, and the same set broken down by respondent function. The distribution is a citable, bindable object that exhibits and narrative bind to, so a survey figure on a slide is a binding, not a typed number.

- `AC-1242.1` A breakdown cell with a count of zero MUST be represented and displayed as zero, not omitted. Grounded: the reference playback showed one functional area with zero respondents, which is itself a finding about coverage, and an exhibit that silently drops empty categories would have hidden it.
- `AC-1242.2` Any exhibit built from a distribution recomputes when a late response arrives, and every deliverable bound to it is marked stale per AI-30.
- `AC-1242.3` The distribution records the survey's own `n` and instrument version, and any narrative citing a survey figure resolves to both.

**FR-1243 — Free-text coding to evidence.** Free-text answers MUST become `Evidence` records with a `SourceLocator` into the response, attributed to the respondent's function and, where the survey is not anonymous and the reader holds the permission, to the `Stakeholder`. Coding free text into `Finding` candidates uses the same clustering path as interview synthesis, and a survey-derived finding records that its evidence is self-reported.

**FR-1244 — Small-cell handling.** Any breakdown cell whose `n` is below a configurable threshold (default 3) MUST display the count but MUST suppress attribution of free-text quotes to that cell for any user who does not hold the `SeeSurveyIdentity` permission, and MUST never expose it to a `ClientGuest`. This prevents a two-person function's answers from being individually identifiable in a client-facing playback.

**FR-1245 — Findings playback binding.** The survey distribution, its coded themes, and its tension pairs MUST be available as bindable exhibit sources to the findings playback builder in M2 and to the deliverable builder in M8, so the playback deck's survey pages are generated from the distribution rather than assembled by hand.

### 9.5 Workshop and whiteboard integration (FR-1250 to FR-1259)

Grounded observation: the reference engagement ran its priority and urgency activities on a collaborative whiteboard over a two-day onsite. Activity 1 gave each group a card set drawn from the register, with the initiative in bold and the opportunity in italic and a detail expander, and asked each group to move its top five into a column inside ten minutes, after which the consultants revealed their own calculated ranking and the room reconciled. Activity 2 assigned an urgency level per card from a dropdown. Activity 3 added dependencies from a dropdown, milestones, business value, and a t-shirt size on a six-point scale with defined effort, duration and risk per size. Activity 4 placed items on the roadmap timeline as a full group. The output then reached the register by hand: a threaded comment in the master workbook records that a column was added and populated from the whiteboard, and the post-onsite recap warned recipients that the rankings on the deck would shift as the team continued to incorporate the notes captured on the board. That hand-carry is the defect. The workshop produced a client-owned judgment that then existed in two places, in a form that no calculation could see.

**FR-1250 — In-product facilitation mode.** The product MUST support running the priority, urgency, effort and dependency activities inside the product, against the live register, through the M4 workshop console and workshop board screens. Requirements specific to the integration boundary: cards are generated from the current register scope with initiative and opportunity rendered distinctly and a detail expander showing recommended action and linked findings; group membership, per-group card sets, activity timer, and activity state are session objects; participant inputs write to `Opportunity.clientRank`, `clientUrgency`, `clientEffort`, `clientDependencies` and `clientNotes` with `WorkshopSession` provenance on every value; the facilitator reveal step discloses the calculated band and rank alongside the group's selection and records both without either overwriting the other; and the session produces a `WorkshopSession` record that any later `Decision` can cite.

**FR-1251 — Whiteboard import path.** The product MUST support importing workshop output produced on an external collaborative whiteboard. Accepted inputs: a board export in the vendor's JSON or CSV form (Miro and FigJam board exports at minimum), or a hand-prepared CSV of card title, frame or column name, and per-field values. The import uses the same mapping-and-validation machinery as FR-1200 to FR-1215.

- `AC-1251.1` Frames, columns and swimlanes on the board map to target fields through a mapping UI, so a column named for a horizon maps to `clientHorizon` and a column named for a top-five selection maps to `clientRank`.
- `AC-1251.2` Cards match to `Opportunity` records by title similarity with a confirmation step; unmatched cards become validation-report decisions offering match-to-existing, create-new, or discard.
- `AC-1251.3` Sticky notes and free comments attached to a card import as `Comment` records with the board locator retained, so the "notes captured through the board discussions" become part of the record rather than a follow-up task.
- `AC-1251.4` A card carrying a value outside the target field's enum (for example an urgency label the product does not have) is a decision, resolved by mapping to an existing member or extending the enum.

**FR-1252 — Client judgment and calculated score are separate fields.** `clientRank`, `clientUrgency`, `clientEffort` and `clientHorizon` MUST be stored as distinct fields from the calculated score, band, quadrant and horizon. Neither may overwrite the other, and no calculation may silently substitute one for the other. Divergences are surfaced to the M4 reconciliation screen, which owns the resolution workflow and the requirement that a material divergence produces a `Decision` record. This section's requirement is only that both values arrive in the model, attributed, with session provenance, and that the import cannot merge them.

**FR-1253 — MVP choice.** For the MVP, the whiteboard import path (FR-1251) is in scope and the in-product facilitation mode (FR-1250) is deferred to v1.1.

Reasoning. The facilitation mode is a real-time multi-user collaborative application in its own right, requiring presence, concurrent editing, conflict resolution, timers, projector and participant views, and a tolerance for twenty people on unfamiliar conference wifi. Its failure mode is a stalled activity in front of an executive room during a paid onsite, which is the single worst place for this product to be new. Consultants already have a whiteboard tool that those participants have used before, and the workshop happens once per engagement. The import path, by contrast, removes the actual observed defect at a small fraction of the cost: the board output lands in the register as attributed data with provenance instead of being retyped into a spare column, and the divergence between the room's ranking and the calculated ranking becomes a visible, resolvable list rather than a warning sentence in a recap email. Building the import first also produces the field structure and reconciliation surface that the facilitation mode needs, so no work is wasted.

### 9.6 PowerPoint export (FR-1260 to FR-1269)

**FR-1260 — Template binding.** A `DeckTemplate` MUST be a registered `.pptx` template file with a declared inventory of slide layouts and, per layout, named placeholders. All content binding MUST address layouts and placeholders by name, never by shape index or position. Grounded: the reference decks were built on a small set of named layouts and named shapes, and index-based binding breaks the moment the firm's template team reorders a master.

- `AC-1260.1` Template registration parses the file, lists every layout and placeholder with its name and type, and fails registration with a specific error if a layout required by any bound `SlideSpec` is missing or if a layout has duplicate placeholder names.
- `AC-1260.2` Templates are versioned. A `Deliverable` records the template ID and version it was rendered with, and regeneration uses that version, not the latest (FR-1332).
- `AC-1260.3` A template can be validated against the full `SlideSpec` catalogue on demand, producing a compatibility report, so a brand refresh is checked before an engagement depends on it.

**FR-1261 — Placeholder mapping and bound values.** A `SlideSpec` MUST map each placeholder to exactly one of: a binding expression over the `ModelSnapshot`; an `Exhibit` reference; an authored `NarrativeMessage`; or static template text. Every bound value MUST record its source path and the resolved value at render time.

- `AC-1261.1` A binding that fails to resolve renders as a visible unresolved marker and raises a blocking export error. It never renders as an empty placeholder or as the last known value.
- `AC-1261.2` Every number appearing on a slide is either a bound value or is flagged in the §12.2 unbasis'd-number count. There is no path for a consultant to type a figure directly into an exported deck through the product.
- `AC-1261.3` Text overflow is detected at render time by measuring against the placeholder box and reported per slide, because a silently overflowing executive slide is a delivery defect.

**FR-1262 — Native chart versus image rendering.** Exhibits MUST render as native PowerPoint charts wherever the exhibit's data is tabular and its type maps to a supported chart type, and as vector images plus a data appendix otherwise.

| Exhibit type | Rendering | Data carried |
|---|---|---|
| Score or count by category, stacked composition, trend | Native chart (bar, stacked bar, line) with embedded worksheet | Exact plotted values in the embedded worksheet |
| Value versus urgency bubble or scatter | Native bubble chart with embedded worksheet | Point values plus the label field |
| Maturity heatmap grid, roadmap swimlane timeline, quadrant map with per-point labels, dependency graph, word cloud | Vector image (rendered to EMF or high-resolution PNG fallback) | A companion appendix slide or a hidden data table, plus full alt text, plus the exhibit's data hash in the manifest |

- `AC-1262.1` The product MUST NOT emit third-party charting add-in objects, and MUST NOT emit an image-only exhibit whose underlying data is not carried somewhere in the exported package. Grounded: across the reference deck set of 130 slides there were roughly 66 embedded third-party charting objects carrying an opaque "do not delete" data payload, only 4 native chart objects, and over 250 flat images; the deck's numbers were therefore unreadable to anything but a human eye, which is the mechanism by which deck figures drifted from the workbook.
- `AC-1262.2` Every native chart's embedded worksheet values MUST equal the snapshot values byte-for-byte after formatting, verified by a post-render check that reads the emitted chart back and compares.
- `AC-1262.3` Every exhibit, native or image, carries alt text generated from its bound data description, for FR-1360.

**FR-1263 — Every exported deck records its snapshot.** Every exported deck MUST record, in OOXML custom document properties: `snapshotId`, `engagementId`, `deliverableId`, `templateId`, `templateVersion`, `calcEngineVersion`, `scoringModelVersion`, `exportedAt`, `exportedBy`, and `manifestHash`. It MUST additionally carry a visible provenance token, by default a short snapshot reference in the title-slide footer, configurable per template but not removable.

- `AC-1263.1` Given only an exported file, a consultant can paste its snapshot reference into the product and open the exact snapshot it was built from.
- `AC-1263.2` A deck exported from a snapshot that has since been superseded is identifiable as such in the product's deliverable list, with the count of model changes since.

**FR-1264 — No foreign content in an issued deliverable.** An issued `Deliverable` MUST contain only slides generated for this engagement from the bound snapshot, plus firm content drawn from a `FirmContentLibrary` whose items are explicitly marked reusable and client-neutral. A `Deliverable` MUST have a working area whose slides are never included in an issued export, and issuing MUST run the cross-client scan of FR-1304.

Grounded: the reference file set contained a working planning deck of 33 slides whose last ten were a holding area of reusable and other-client material, including another named client's platform estate and taxonomies, alongside a cleaned 23-slide version. Both files sat in the same final deliverable folder with near-identical names, distinguished only by a date in one filename. The product's answer is to make the distinction structural rather than a matter of which file someone attaches: the working area exists in the model, cannot be issued, and issuing scans for content whose provenance is another engagement.

- `AC-1264.1` An export whose content includes an `Exhibit` or `NarrativeMessage` whose provenance is another `Engagement` is blocked, not warned.
- `AC-1264.2` A `FirmContentLibrary` item that fails the confidentiality scan cannot be included in any export until remediated.
- `AC-1264.3` Issued deliverables are named by the product from engagement, deliverable type, version and snapshot reference, so two files cannot differ only by a hand-typed date.

**FR-1265 — Export manifest.** Every deck export MUST produce a machine-readable `ExportManifest` listing every slide with its `SlideSpec`, every bound value with its source path and resolved value, every exhibit with its type, rendering mode and data hash, every scan finding with its resolution, and every warning. The manifest is retained with the `Deliverable`, is downloadable, and is the input to the regeneration check of AC-1332.1.

### 9.7 Excel export (FR-1270 to FR-1279)

**FR-1270 — Client-shareable workbook.** The product MUST generate a client-shareable `.xlsx` workbook mirroring the register and the scoring model, with a fixed sheet set: `Introduction` (engagement, snapshot reference, generation date, confidentiality classification, contents guide), `Scoring Guide` (dimensions, weights, per-level anchor labels and definitions, band thresholds, all read from the `ScoringModel` version in the snapshot), `Opportunity Register` (one row per in-scope `Opportunity`), `Maturity Assessment` (one row per focus area), `Taxonomy` (theme, initiative, sequence, description, and any aliases), and `Method` (per FR-1272).

- `AC-1270.1` The workbook contains no hidden sheets, no hidden columns, and no hidden rows.
- `AC-1270.2` Each data sheet is a real Excel table object with a single header row at the top of the table, an autofilter, and frozen headers.
- `AC-1270.3` Every column declared in the header has data in at least one row, or is omitted. The export never ships a declared-but-empty column.
- `AC-1270.4` The numeric score, the anchor label, and the rationale prose occupy three separate columns per dimension. The export never writes a combined numeral-plus-label-plus-sentence string into a score cell.
- `AC-1270.5` Enum columns carry a whole-column list validation covering every data row, with no gaps, and no cell holds a value outside its enum.

**FR-1271 — Generated, not hand-maintained.** The workbook MUST be generated on demand from a snapshot and MUST NOT be an editable artifact that the product later re-imports as a source of truth. Regenerating from the same snapshot produces a byte-identical file (FR-1332). The workbook records its snapshot reference in document properties and on the `Introduction` sheet.

**FR-1272 — Derived values as values, with a documented formula statement.** All derived values MUST be written as static values with explicit number formats, and the `Method` sheet MUST state, for each derived column, the exact formula, its inputs, and the parameters actually applied to this snapshot.

The `Method` sheet MUST contain at minimum: the weight vector in force (Financial Impact 0.40, Risk if Deferred 0.35, Strategic Alignment 0.25 for the reference model), the weighted-score expression, the band thresholds (4.5, 3.75, 2.8) with band names, the quadrant axis definitions and the quadrant threshold (3.5) with quadrant names, the maturity framework name, level count and level labels, the gap definition, the calculation engine version, and the snapshot reference. Each statement is rendered in the notation defined in §7 so a client analyst can reproduce any number in the file with a calculator.

- `AC-1272.1` No cell in the exported workbook contains a formula that references another workbook, another file, or an external defined name.
- `AC-1272.2` No cell in the exported workbook derives a number by parsing a string.
- `AC-1272.3` The taxonomy required to interpret the register is present in the file, so the workbook is self-contained. Grounded: neither reference workbook was self-contained, and the only intact theme-to-initiative taxonomy existed as a hidden sheet in the derived share copy while the master resolved its theme column through a broken external reference to it.
- `AC-1272.4` Conditional formatting, where applied, is keyed to the values actually present in the exported snapshot and to nothing else. Grounded: the reference workbooks carried conditional-formatting rules across five sheets keyed to four theme names that had been retired mid-engagement and appeared in no data cell.

**FR-1273 — Share-copy filtering.** Generating a client-facing workbook MUST run the confidentiality scan of FR-1304 and MUST omit fields classified internal-only unless the exporting user explicitly includes them and confirms. Omitted by default: internal comment threads and their authors, internal status and reviewer assignment, `Restricted` content per FR-1314, contract and cost values not published to the client, `AISuggestion` records and confidences, and any field naming an individual as a risk. The `Introduction` sheet MUST state the count of fields and rows withheld, so the client copy is honest about being a subset.

Grounded: the reference client-shareable workbook carried the delivery team's own threaded review comments across into the client-facing file, including one asking whether an opportunity was a duplicate of another and two recording a mid-engagement rename, each naming individual staff.

**FR-1274 — Why the export does not reproduce live formulas.**

The export deliberately ships values plus a written method rather than a live formula model. The reason is that in the reference engagement every single analytical defect was a formula defect. The numeric score that drove the whole prioritization was reconstructed by taking the first character of a display string, so a two-digit value or an edited label would have silently changed the answer. The weights were hard-coded into a `SUMPRODUCT` against a cell range rather than held as a named model, so nothing prevented a row from being weighted against the wrong range. The priority band conditional chain stopped matching its own column part-way down the register, so the last rows reported a different quantity under the band header. The theme column resolved through a lookup into another workbook, which broke the moment the file was copied for sharing, leaving cached values with no live derivation. Conditional formatting was keyed to names that no longer existed. Every one of those failures is invisible to a reader and survives being emailed.

A live-formula export recreates all of them, in a file the product cannot see, cannot version, and cannot correct, and it invites a client analyst to edit an input and get an answer that the system of record does not hold. The product's contract is therefore explicit: the system of record computes, the export reports, and the export states precisely how each number was computed so any figure can be independently reproduced. Where the client wants to test an alternative, the answer is a `RoadmapScenario` in the product (M5), which recomputes the whole model consistently and records the premise, not a formula in a spreadsheet that diverges the moment it is saved.

**FR-1275 — Internal working export.** A separate internal-variant workbook MAY include the withheld fields for delivery-team use. It MUST carry the confidentiality classification of its most sensitive field on every sheet header, MUST be watermarked internal, and MUST be excluded from any client share link.

### 9.8 Written narrative and PDF export (FR-1280 to FR-1289)

**FR-1280 — Written narrative export.** The product MUST render a `NarrativeExport` from `NarrativeMessage` records in a chosen structure, with a `SessionRecap` structure provided out of the box modelled on the reference engagement's post-onsite recap: an opening acknowledgement, N key themes each as a bolded heading plus two to four sentences, a numbered committed-next-steps list with owner and time window per step, a provisional-figures caveat block, and a closing. Output formats: Markdown, HTML suitable for pasting into an email client, and `.docx`.

Grounded: the reference recap carried five key themes and six numbered next steps, and an explicit caveat that the rankings and scoring on the workshop deck would shift as the opportunity inventory was cleaned up and the board notes incorporated.

- `AC-1280.1` Every theme and every next step is a model object (a `Theme` summary or an `ActionItem` with owner and due window), not text typed at export time. Editing the recap edits the model.
- `AC-1280.2` The caveat block is generated, not written: it lists, automatically, every figure in the narrative whose source `Opportunity` or `MaturityAssessment` is not in a `Reviewed` state, and every scenario referenced whose status is not `Agreed`. If nothing is provisional, the block is omitted.
- `AC-1280.3` An internal variant includes evidence locators under each theme; the client variant does not.
- `AC-1280.4` The narrative export MUST NOT embed a recipient list, a distribution list, or any email address in the artifact. Grounded: the reference recap survived into the deliverable set as a printed mail client page carrying the full addresses of roughly thirty recipients across both organizations. Recipients are a property of the send action, recorded in the audit log, not content of the document.

**FR-1281 — PDF export.** Any `Deliverable` MUST render to PDF with: selectable text, a document outline matching its section structure, tagged headings and tagged tables for accessibility, alt text on every image, embedded fonts, the same snapshot properties as FR-1263 in the PDF metadata, and the visible provenance token. PDF/A-2b conformance is required for issued client deliverables.

- `AC-1281.1` A PDF rendered from a deck snapshot and the deck itself present identical figures, verified by comparing bound values in both manifests.

### 9.9 API surface (FR-1290 to FR-1299)

**FR-1290 — Internal API.** The product MUST expose an authenticated, versioned, engagement-scoped JSON HTTP API sufficient for the product's own clients and for the export and import flows above: read a `ModelSnapshot` and its entities; list register rows with derived values; list `MaturityAssessment` rows; create an import session and upload sources; read a `ValidationReport` and post decisions; trigger an export and poll its status; download a `Deliverable` and its `ExportManifest`; read the `AuditEvent` stream for an engagement. Every call is engagement-scoped by the token, rate-limited, and audit-logged.

**FR-1291 — Precedent source adapter.** The product MUST define one outbound integration interface for firm precedent, with exactly two operations, and MUST route AI-08 and AI-18 through it and nowhere else:

```
searchPrecedent(query: PrecedentQuery) -> PrecedentRecord[]
getPrecedentRecord(id: string) -> PrecedentRecord
```

`PrecedentRecord` is the anonymized shape defined in FR-1302. In the MVP the only implementation is the product's own precedent store; the interface exists so the firm's knowledge library can be substituted later without changing any AI capability code. The adapter MUST NOT be able to return non-anonymized content: the return type has no field for it, and the adapter validates every returned record against the anonymization schema before it reaches a prompt.

**FR-1292 — No public API in the MVP.** The MVP MUST NOT ship a public API, partner OAuth, client-tenant API tokens, or outbound webhooks. Reason: no external consumer exists yet, the data model will still move through v1.1, and a published surface would freeze it. Client-side systems integration (ITSM, PPM, ERP, finance) is out of scope for the MVP entirely; the inbound path for those systems is a file export handled by 9.1 and 9.3.

---

## 10. Non-Functional Requirements (FR-1300 to FR-1399)

### 10.1 Confidentiality and data segregation (FR-1300 to FR-1309)

This is the highest-stakes requirement set in the PRD. The reference engagement's two working artifacts, in a folder labelled as the final deliverable set, carried between them: a confidentiality marking on the introduction sheet; the names, work email addresses and a direct telephone number of roughly thirty individuals across two organizations; named single points of failure, including the sole incumbent responsible for the platform through which every order, shipment and invoice passed; a reference to a historical ransomware incident with an attributed cause; an inventory of security tooling with named coverage gaps and unremediated findings; currency figures for committed programs; and internal review threads in which delivery staff questioned each other's scores. One of those two workbooks was the copy prepared for sharing with the client. A third file in the same folder carried another client's platform estate.

Every requirement below exists because that combination of contents and that pattern of file handling is normal, not exceptional.

**FR-1300 — Per-engagement data isolation.** Every persisted record of every entity MUST carry an `engagement_id`, and all data access MUST pass through a layer that requires an explicit engagement scope. A query constructed without an engagement predicate MUST be rejected by that layer rather than merely avoided by convention. Object storage keys MUST be namespaced by engagement. Search and vector indexes MUST be partitioned by engagement.

- `AC-1300.1` A schema test asserts that every table holding engagement content has the column, non-nullable, indexed, and covered by a row-level policy.
- `AC-1300.2` A test asserts that constructing any repository query without a scope raises at build or request time, and that the rejection is logged as a security event per FR-1373.
- `AC-1300.3` Files uploaded to engagement A are not retrievable by any authenticated request scoped to engagement B, including by direct object key.

**FR-1301 — Hard prohibition on cross-engagement retrieval.** No retrieval, keyword search, embedding lookup, summarization input, fine-tuning corpus, or AI prompt MAY include content from an `Engagement` other than the one in scope. The only permitted cross-engagement information path in the entire product is the anonymized `PrecedentRecord` store accessed through FR-1291.

- `AC-1301.1` For every AI capability, prompt assembly is covered by a test that fails if any assembled source carries a different `engagement_id` than the request scope.
- `AC-1301.2` An integration test asserts that a retrieval call scoped to engagement A cannot return a chunk from engagement B under any query, including a query that is a verbatim string from engagement B.
- `AC-1301.3` No model is fine-tuned or otherwise trained on engagement content. Capability improvement uses the evaluation harness of FR-1371 over permitted, anonymized material only.

**FR-1302 — Anonymization pipeline for precedent records.** A `PrecedentRecord` MUST be produced from a source `Engagement` by a deterministic, re-runnable pipeline with an explicit field contract.

Stripped, without exception:

- Client legal name, trading names, brand names, site names, and every alias recorded on the engagement's alias list.
- All person data: names, titles held by a single identifiable person, email addresses, telephone numbers, usernames.
- Security incident specifics: incident type, date, affected systems, attack vector, remediation state.
- Security tooling inventory: product names, coverage, and identified gaps.
- Absolute currency figures, contract values, and budget lines.
- Dates finer than a calendar quarter.
- File names, folder paths, document titles, and system or environment names.
- Internal comment threads and reviewer identities.
- Verbatim quotations longer than a configured length (default 15 words).
- Any string matching the engagement's own PII and confidential-information register produced by FR-1216.

Retained, because it is what makes precedent useful:

- Industry, revenue band as a band, employee-count band, count of operating sites as a band.
- Capability area and focus area on the firm's standard taxonomy.
- Current and target maturity level, and the gap.
- Opportunity title generalized to a capability statement, plus its dimension scores and band.
- T-shirt size, duration band, and sequence position within its wave.
- Dependency shape (the pattern of typed dependencies, not the named systems).
- Cost as a normalized band with the currency and basis year, and the count of contributing engagements behind that band.
- The generalized form of the recommended action.

- `AC-1302.1` The pipeline is deterministic: the same source snapshot and the same pipeline version produce an identical candidate record.
- `AC-1302.2` A candidate record is blocked from release if any retained field matches any entry on the source engagement's alias list or PII register, or if any retained free-text field fails the person-name and organization-name detectors.
- `AC-1302.3` A `PrecedentRecord` is never linked, in any user-visible or API-visible way, to its source `Engagement`. The link exists only in an internal provenance table readable by `FirmAdmin` and `PrecedentSteward` and is required for FR-1303 review and for withdrawal.
- `AC-1302.4` Cost bands MUST be derived from at least three contributing engagements before they can be surfaced by AI-18, so a band cannot be reverse-engineered to a single client's figure.

**FR-1303 — Precedent release requires recorded permission and two-person approval.** An `Engagement` MUST carry a `PrecedentPermission` value of `Permitted`, `PermittedWithRestrictions` (with the restrictions recorded as text and as field-level exclusions), or `NotPermitted`, sourced from the client contract and recorded with the contract reference and the date. Release requires: a proposal by the engagement lead, and an approval by a distinct user holding the `PrecedentSteward` role who reviews the field-level diff between source and candidate.

- `AC-1303.1` An engagement marked `NotPermitted` cannot produce a candidate record at all; the action is unavailable, not merely warned.
- `AC-1303.2` The proposer and the approver MUST be different users. Self-approval is rejected.
- `AC-1303.3` Released records are immutable. Correction is a new version, and the prior version is withdrawn and removed from retrieval within 60 seconds of withdrawal.
- `AC-1303.4` The audit log holds proposer, approver, timestamp, pipeline version, and the full field-level diff reviewed.
- `AC-1303.5` A client withdrawal of permission triggers withdrawal of every record derived from that engagement, and the operation reports which precedent-derived figures in other live engagements cited those records.

**FR-1304 — Export-time confidentiality scan.** Every artifact leaving the product, by download, share link, or email, MUST pass a confidentiality scan before it is made available. The scan runs over rendered content, including speaker notes, chart-embedded worksheets, document properties, hidden columns, alt text, and the export manifest.

Detectors and dispositions:

| Detector | Disposition | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Content whose provenance is another `Engagement`, or a string matching another engagement's alias list | Block | The reference engagement shipped another client's slides inside a working deliverable deck |
| An individual named as a single point of failure, risk, or capability gap without the FR-1313 confirmation | Block | |
| `Restricted` content (security incident specifics, security tooling inventory) in a client-external artifact | Block | |
| Credential-shaped strings (keys, tokens, connection strings, passwords) | Block | |
| Unresolved binding, unverified imported literal, or stale narrative binding | Block | Overlaps §12.2; an export cannot carry a number the product cannot vouch for |
| Person names matched against the engagement `Stakeholder` list or a general name detector | Warn | Named stakeholders legitimately appear in some internal artifacts |
| Email addresses, telephone numbers, personal URLs | Warn | |
| Currency amounts in an artifact whose classification does not permit them | Warn | |
| The client's own confidentiality markings detected in imported content | Warn, and propagate the marking to the export | |

- `AC-1304.1` An export cannot proceed while any `Block` finding is unresolved. Resolution means removing or reclassifying the content, not dismissing the finding.
- `AC-1304.2` Every `Warn` finding requires an explicit per-finding acknowledgement recording actor, timestamp and reason, and the acknowledgement set is retained with the `Deliverable`.
- `AC-1304.3` The scan result is stored as part of the `Deliverable`, is visible on the deliverable record, and a deliverable with no scan record cannot be marked issued.
- `AC-1304.4` Scan latency is inside the export budgets of FR-1345, and a scan failure blocks the export rather than being skipped.

**FR-1305 — AI processing boundary.** Engagement content sent to a model provider MUST be sent under a contract prohibiting training on it, with provider-side retention disabled. The provider, model identifier, endpoint region, and retention setting MUST be recorded on every `AISuggestion`. Content classified `Restricted` per FR-1314 MUST be excluded from every prompt by default; a consultant may include it per request with a recorded reason, and that inclusion is audit-logged and surfaced on the resulting suggestion.

*Assumption (A-13): that a zero-retention, no-training deployment is available to the firm on the models the capabilities require. If it is not, capabilities that require sending client narrative content must be gated behind a per-engagement client permission, and that changes the MVP scope.*

**FR-1306 — Encryption and key handling.** Data MUST be encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3 minimum) and at rest, with object storage server-side encrypted and database volumes encrypted. Per-engagement encryption keys are deferred to v1.1; the MVP assumption is a single firm tenant with logical isolation per FR-1300, stated as A-04.

### 10.2 Personal data handling (FR-1310 to FR-1319)

**FR-1310 — Field-level classification.** Every field in the schema MUST carry a classification from the closed set `Public`, `ClientConfidential`, `PersonIdentifying`, `Restricted`. The classification is stored data, queryable, and drives export filtering, client-guest visibility, prompt assembly, and scan behaviour.

`PersonIdentifying` includes at minimum: `Stakeholder` name, title, email, telephone, and photo; transcript speaker labels; `Comment` authorship; survey respondent identity; interview attendee lists; org-chart person records; `AuditEvent` actor; and any free-text field in which the name detector has produced a hit, which is recorded as a field-level flag on that specific record rather than on the schema.

- `AC-1310.1` A migration that adds a field without a classification fails the build.
- `AC-1310.2` The classification of every field is inspectable in the product by an administrator, and a report lists all `PersonIdentifying` and `Restricted` fields with their record counts per engagement.

**FR-1311 — Retention.** The product MUST implement configurable retention with the following defaults, and MUST purge by real deletion of the stored object with a tombstone in the audit log, never by a visibility flag:

| Class | Default retention | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Interview audio and video | 90 days from transcription, or delete-on-transcription if chosen per FR-1224 | Requires the consent flag to be retained at all |
| Transcripts and uploaded source artifacts | Engagement close plus 24 months | Client contract may shorten |
| Engagement model data and issued deliverables | Engagement close plus 7 years | Deliverables are the firm's professional record |
| `AuditEvent` log | 7 years | Append-only per FR-1330 |
| `AISuggestion` records including prompts and outputs | Engagement close plus 12 months | Needed for §12.3 evaluation |
| `PrecedentRecord` | Indefinite | Already anonymized; withdrawn on permission change per AC-1303.5 |

- `AC-1311.1` A client-requested early deletion can be executed at engagement level, produces a certificate listing what was deleted and what was retained under a stated legal or professional basis, and cannot be executed by a single user without a second approver.
- `AC-1311.2` Retention is enforced by a scheduled job whose runs are audit-logged, and a failed purge raises an alert rather than silently retrying forever.

*The 90-day, 24-month and 7-year figures are defaults chosen to be defensible, not derived from the reference material, and are recorded as assumption A-15 pending the firm's own records-retention policy and its client contract templates.*

**FR-1312 — Redact a named individual across an engagement.** Given a `Stakeholder`, the product MUST provide a single operation that replaces that individual's identity everywhere in the `Engagement` with a stable pseudonymous role label (for example, "the sole systems programmer for the core platform"), across: the `Stakeholder` record; transcript speaker labels; `Evidence` quote text and attribution; `Finding`, `Opportunity`, `MaturityAssessment` and `NarrativeMessage` free-text fields; `Comment` bodies and authorship; and generated content already materialized into the model.

- `AC-1312.1` The operation produces a preview listing every location, entity, field and character span it will change, and requires confirmation. It never runs blind.
- `AC-1312.2` The replacement label is stable, so two mentions of the same individual remain recognizable as the same person by role, and the label is editable before confirmation.
- `AC-1312.3` The operation completes within 60 seconds at the target scale of FR-1340.
- `AC-1312.4` After redaction, a full-text search for the individual's name anywhere in the engagement returns zero results outside the audit log and previously issued snapshots.
- `AC-1312.5` Already-issued `Deliverable` records and immutable snapshots are not altered. Instead they are listed as containing pre-redaction content, and the engagement lead is prompted to decide per deliverable whether to reissue from a post-redaction snapshot or to recall.
- `AC-1312.6` The whole operation is one `AuditEvent` with the full change set.

**FR-1313 — No generated content names an individual as a single point of failure.** Generated client-facing content MUST NOT name an individual as a single point of failure, a risk, a performance problem, a capability gap, or a dependency. The generator MUST emit the role-level formulation by default: not the person's name but the role, the fact that it has a single incumbent, and the consequence.

Grounded: the reference maturity framework definition sheet and the register's rationale text both named individuals as sole incumbents, and those rows flowed into the client-shared copy of the workbook. The finding is correct and belongs in the assessment. Naming the person in a document that circulates to twenty of their colleagues is a different act, and it should require a human to choose it.

- `AC-1313.1` A consultant may override to name the individual only through an explicit per-instance confirmation that records actor, timestamp, and a stated reason.
- `AC-1313.2` The confirmation is bound to the exact generated sentence. Regenerating or materially editing the sentence invalidates the confirmation and requires it again.
- `AC-1313.3` The confidentiality scan of FR-1304 blocks export of any unconfirmed instance, detected by cross-referencing text against the engagement's `Stakeholder` names within a configurable proximity of the risk vocabulary.
- `AC-1313.4` The role-level formulation retains an internal-only link to the `Stakeholder`, so the analysis does not lose the fact, and that link is `PersonIdentifying`.

**FR-1314 — Restricted classes.** Security incident records, security tooling inventory (product, coverage, identified gap, remediation state), unremediated vulnerability findings, and credential-shaped strings MUST be classified `Restricted`. `Restricted` content MUST be: visible only to users holding the `SeeSecuritySensitive` permission; entirely excluded from `ClientGuest` views; excluded from all client-external exports; excluded from `PrecedentRecord` candidates; and excluded from AI prompts by default per FR-1305.

- `AC-1314.1` A finding derived from `Restricted` content MAY be expressed at a generalized level ("no executive-level forum reviews accepted security risk"), and that generalized statement is not itself `Restricted`. The derivation link records the `Restricted` source and is visible only to permitted users.
- `AC-1314.2` A `MaturityAssessment` rationale or an `Opportunity` narrative that quotes `Restricted` detail inherits the classification of the quote, and the product warns at authoring time rather than at export time.
- `AC-1314.3` `Restricted` content is excluded from the client-shareable Excel export unconditionally, with the withheld count stated per FR-1273.

### 10.3 Access control and client-guest access (FR-1320 to FR-1329)

**FR-1320 — Roles.** The product MUST implement the roles `FirmAdmin`, `EngagementLead`, `Consultant`, `Analyst`, `PrecedentSteward`, `ClientGuest`, assigned per `Engagement` except `FirmAdmin` and `PrecedentSteward`, which are firm-level. Permissions are additive and least-privilege; the detailed matrix lives in §4's cross-cutting requirements and is not restated here. The `SeeSecuritySensitive` and `SeeSurveyIdentity` permissions are separately grantable and are not implied by any role except `EngagementLead`.

**FR-1321 — Client-guest capability boundary.** A `ClientGuest` MUST be able to:

- View `Deliverable` versions explicitly shared with them, and only those versions.
- View a published `RoadmapScenario` view within their `StakeholderView` scope.
- View the register within their scope, limited to `Public` and `ClientConfidential` fields.
- View `Decision` records explicitly marked client-visible.
- Submit structured feedback against an `Opportunity`, `Initiative`, or scenario: a position (support, concern, oppose, need more information), a free-text comment, and an optional proposed change.
- Download client-facing exports that have been shared with them.

A `ClientGuest` MUST NOT be able to see, under any circumstances: any draft or unpublished snapshot; internal `Comment` threads; `AISuggestion` records, confidences, or the fact that a value was AI-proposed; `Evidence` attribution to a named individual; `Restricted` content; another stakeholder's feedback; `CostEstimate` or `ValueCase` values not explicitly published; the `AuditEvent` log; the precedent library; the scoring model's internal calibration views; or anything belonging to any other `Engagement`.

- `AC-1321.1` A `ClientGuest` session that requests a resource outside this boundary receives a not-found response, not a forbidden response, so the existence of out-of-scope objects is not disclosed.
- `AC-1321.2` A `ClientGuest` can only ever read a snapshot marked `Published`. There is no code path by which a draft becomes visible to a guest.

**FR-1322 — Stakeholder-specific views are enforced server-side.** A `StakeholderView` MUST be a named, persisted scope definition (filters over business area, theme, initiative, workstream, plus explicit include and exclude lists). When a scoped user requests any resource, the server MUST resolve their view and apply it as a query predicate. Scope MUST NOT be implemented by returning a full payload and hiding rows in the client.

- `AC-1322.1` The response to a scoped request MUST NOT contain out-of-scope data in any form, including list rows, record counts, aggregates, chart series, exhibit images, tooltip payloads, export files, and export manifests.
- `AC-1322.2` For every list and aggregate endpoint, a test asserts that the response to a scoped token is byte-identical to the response to the same request made against a database that physically contains only the in-scope rows. This is the definition of correct scoping, and it is testable.
- `AC-1322.3` Aggregates shown to a scoped user are computed over the scoped set. Any figure that is inherently engagement-wide (total investment, total opportunity count, enterprise maturity average) is either suppressed or explicitly labelled as an engagement-wide figure, and the choice is a property of the exhibit, not a runtime accident.
- `AC-1322.4` Exports produced for a scoped user contain no out-of-scope record anywhere, including hidden columns, speaker notes, chart-embedded worksheets, alt text, document properties, and manifests. Grounded: the leak surface that matters is exactly the one the reference workbooks demonstrated, where the sensitive material sat in hidden sheets and threaded comments rather than in the visible grid.
- `AC-1322.5` A scoped user's view definition is visible to them in plain language ("you are seeing 41 of 312 opportunities, filtered to Distribution and Supply Chain"), because a silently filtered view invites a client to conclude the roadmap is smaller than it is.

**FR-1323 — Sharing and links.** `Deliverable` share links MUST be per-recipient, expiring (default 30 days), revocable individually, and audit-logged on every access with recipient identity, timestamp and IP. Public unauthenticated links MUST NOT exist. Every download of a client-facing artifact records the recipient.

**FR-1324 — Authentication.** The product MUST support SSO via SAML or OIDC for firm users with enforced MFA, and email-verified magic-link or OIDC authentication for `ClientGuest` users. Session inactivity timeout defaults to 12 hours for firm users and 2 hours for guests. Failed-authentication and permission-denial events are logged as security events.

### 10.4 Auditability and reproducibility (FR-1330 to FR-1339)

**FR-1330 — Append-only audit log.** The product MUST maintain an append-only `AuditEvent` log capturing at minimum: every field mutation (entity type, entity ID, field, before value, after value, actor, timestamp, request ID, and the `AISuggestion` ID where the change came from accepting a suggestion); every read of `Restricted` content; every export with its scan result; every share-link access; every precedent proposal, approval and withdrawal; every permission change; every import decision; every retention purge; and every rejected unscoped-query attempt.

- `AC-1330.1` The application role holds `INSERT` and `SELECT` only on the audit store. `UPDATE` and `DELETE` privileges are revoked at the database level, so append-only is enforced by the database rather than by application discipline.
- `AC-1330.2` Deletion of engagement data writes a tombstone event recording what was deleted, by whom, and under what basis. It does not remove the prior events.
- `AC-1330.3` For every entity type, a test replays that entity's event stream from creation and asserts the result equals its current state. An entity that cannot be reconstructed from its events is a defect.
- `AC-1330.4` The log is queryable by entity, actor, time range and event type, and is exportable per engagement as signed JSONL.

**FR-1331 — Snapshot immutability.** A `ModelSnapshot` MUST capture the complete computed state of an `Engagement`: every entity and field value; the `ScoringModel` version including weights, anchor definitions and band thresholds; the quadrant definition and threshold; the maturity framework version; the taxonomy version including aliases; the calculation engine version; and a content hash of every referenced source artifact and `Exhibit`.

- `AC-1331.1` Snapshots are immutable and content-addressed. No operation modifies a snapshot; superseding one creates a new one.
- `AC-1331.2` Taking a snapshot completes within 5 seconds at the target scale, so it can be done on every deliverable issue, on every phase gate, and on demand.
- `AC-1331.3` A snapshot records its parent snapshot, so the change history between two deliverables is computable.
- `AC-1331.4` Deleting a snapshot is impossible while any `Deliverable` references it.

**FR-1332 — Byte-identical regeneration.** Given a `ModelSnapshot` ID and the `DeckTemplate` version recorded on the `Deliverable`, regeneration MUST produce an artifact byte-identical to the one originally issued, for decks, workbooks, PDFs and narrative exports.

This requires, and the implementation MUST provide:

- Deterministic ordering everywhere: explicit sort keys on every collection rendered, no reliance on set or map iteration order.
- No timestamps written into the artifact other than those recorded in the snapshot itself.
- Fixed seeds for any layout algorithm with a random component (dependency graph layout, word cloud placement).
- Pinned font and rendering library versions, recorded on the `Deliverable`, with old versions retained and selected by the snapshot rather than by the current default.
- Normalized OOXML packaging: fixed ZIP entry order, fixed entry timestamps, stable part naming, stable relationship IDs.
- No AI call at render time. All generated text and captions MUST be materialized into the model and captured in the snapshot before the snapshot is taken, so rendering is a pure function.

- `AC-1332.1` A regression suite regenerates a corpus of at least 20 stored deliverables and asserts an identical SHA-256 for each.
- `AC-1332.2` A rendering-library or font upgrade that would break byte-identity is caught by that suite and is handled by retaining the prior renderer, not by relaxing the requirement.
- `AC-1332.3` Any issued deliverable can be regenerated from its snapshot for as long as the snapshot is retained under FR-1311, and a regeneration attempt that fails raises an incident.

**FR-1333 — Provenance of every displayed number.** Every derived number displayed anywhere in the product MUST be inspectable down to its inputs and, where the input is a judgment, to the `Evidence` behind it, through the basis inspector described in M6. A number with no resolvable basis is displayed with an explicit unbasis'd marker and counts toward §12.2.

### 10.5 Performance targets (FR-1340 to FR-1349)

**FR-1340 — Target scale.** The product MUST meet the latency targets below at the following per-engagement scale, and the firm-level concurrency below:

| Dimension | Target scale | Reference engagement observed |
|---|---|---|
| `Opportunity` records | 500 | 43 scored plus 12 operating-model, in two sheets, with a further 27 in a superseded hidden sheet |
| `Initiative` records | 60 | 17 |
| `Theme` records | 8 | 4 |
| `RoadmapScenario` records | 8 | 1 published sequence, with alternatives discussed but not modelled |
| `Stakeholder` records | 40 | roughly 30 named across the delivery and distribution lists; 21 survey respondents |
| Source documents | 200 | 8 files in the final set, with an unknown but larger number of upstream inputs |
| `Transcript` records | 60 | executive interviews plus functional deep dives across a two-month window |
| `Evidence` records | 3,000 | roughly 53 catalogued pain points, each linked to one or more opportunities |
| Maturity focus areas | 40 under 10 capability areas | 28 under 8 |
| `Deliverable` records | 20 | 4 decks (130 slides), 2 workbooks (15 sheets), 1 recap |
| Concurrent active engagements | 50 | n/a |
| Concurrent users | 30, rising to 60 during a workshop | n/a |

The target scale is set at roughly nine times the reference register, three and a half times its initiative count, and an order of magnitude above its document count. That headroom is deliberate, for four reasons that are observable rather than speculative. First, the engagement's own committed next steps included breaking larger opportunities into more actionable roadmap components, which increases row count without adding scope. Second, a product register accumulates what a spreadsheet discards: rejected candidates, superseded rows, merged duplicates and their history. The reference file set already carried 55 live rows plus 27 superseded rows in a hidden sheet plus a 69-row older register, which is 150 rows of real history compressed into "55 opportunities". Third, the reference client operated eight distribution centres and a single core platform; a client with more business units enters with proportionally more in-flight programs. Fourth, evidence density grows faster than opportunity count once evidence is a first-class record rather than a comma-separated list of pain-point numbers in a cell.

*The target scale is traceable to the reference engagement as set out above. The latency figures in FR-1341 to FR-1346 are not: no timing was observable in the source artifacts, so they are engineering targets chosen so that every high-frequency interaction in the observed workflow (score a row, change a weight, filter the register) is faster than the equivalent action in a spreadsheet, and every low-frequency batch operation completes inside a coffee break. They are stated numerically so they can be tested and argued with, and they are recorded as an assumption of this section rather than as an inference from the evidence.*

**FR-1341 — Register view latency.** The `Register tree` and `Bulk scoring and triage` views MUST render a 500-row register with all derived columns in ≤ 1.5 s p95 to first meaningful paint from a warm cache and ≤ 3.0 s p95 cold. Subsequent sort, filter, group and column-reorder operations MUST complete in ≤ 500 ms p95 without a server round trip where the data is already loaded. Grouping by theme and initiative, switching band and quadrant filters, and toggling the unscored filter MUST NOT refetch.

- `AC-1341.1` Rendering is virtualized; scroll remains at 60 fps on the reference client machine specification.
- `AC-1341.2` Keyboard-driven scoring (enter a score, advance to the next unscored cell) MUST have an input-to-visible-update latency of ≤ 100 ms p95, because the observed workflow scores dozens of rows in one sitting and any perceptible lag per cell makes the product slower than the spreadsheet it replaces.

**FR-1342 — Recalculation latency.** A full recomputation of every derived value for a target-scale engagement (per-dimension scores, weighted scores, bands, quadrant axes and labels, initiative and theme rollups, maturity gaps and rollups, sequencing feasibility flags, and cost and capacity rollups where present) MUST complete in ≤ 2.0 s p95 server-side, with the UI consistent within ≤ 3.0 s p95.

- `AC-1342.1` A single field edit MUST propagate to every dependent derived value and every open view in ≤ 300 ms p95, by incremental recomputation over the dependency graph rather than a full pass.
- `AC-1342.2` A change to a weight, a band threshold, or the quadrant threshold, which touches every row, MUST complete inside the 2.0 s full-recalculation budget and MUST present the before-and-after band and quadrant movement summary within that same budget. This matters because the reference workbook's weights were hard-coded into formulas, so nobody could see what a weight change would do; being able to see it in two seconds is the feature.
- `AC-1342.3` No recalculation blocks editing. The model remains writable while a recomputation is in flight, and the result is consistent.

**FR-1343 — Scenario diff latency.** A diff of two `RoadmapScenario` records over 500 opportunities and 60 initiatives, reporting adds, drops, horizon moves, sequence moves, owner changes, dependency violations introduced and resolved, and cost and capacity deltas where present, MUST compute in ≤ 1.5 s p95 and MUST render progressively so the first differences appear in ≤ 500 ms.

**FR-1344 — AI suggestion latency budgets by capability class.** Every AI capability MUST be assigned to a latency class with the budgets below. Budgets are measured from user action to first useful output.

| Class | Capabilities | p50 | p95 | Interaction mode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inline single item | AI-13 (one opportunity), AI-17 (one row), AI-26 (one statement), AI-29 (one paragraph) | 2 s | 5 s | Synchronous, streamed, cancellable |
| Interactive multi item | AI-09 (one focus area), AI-10, AI-11 (one gap), AI-16, AI-19 (one initiative), AI-24 (one feedback item), AI-25, AI-28 | 5 s | 12 s | Synchronous with progress, cancellable |
| Batch analytical | AI-01, AI-06, AI-07, AI-12, AI-14, AI-15, AI-20, AI-21, AI-23, AI-30, AI-31, AI-32, AI-33 | 60 s | 180 s | Asynchronous job, partial results streamed, notify on completion |
| Long-form generation | AI-03, AI-04 (one 90-minute transcript), AI-05 (one document), AI-22, AI-27, AI-34 | 90 s | 300 s | Asynchronous, draft appears progressively |
| Retrieval-grounded estimation | AI-08, AI-18 | 8 s | 20 s | Synchronous with progress; retrieval latency reported separately |

- `AC-1344.1` No AI call blocks a save, a navigation, or a recalculation. The model is always editable while a suggestion is pending.
- `AC-1344.2` A capability exceeding twice its p95 budget is cancelled server-side and recorded as an `abstention` with reason `timeout`, not left pending. A silent hang is worse than a declared failure.
- `AC-1344.3` Batch and long-form jobs survive a page reload and a session change, and their results arrive in the notification centre.

**FR-1345 — Export latency.** A 40-slide deck export MUST complete in ≤ 30 s p95; the client-shareable workbook in ≤ 10 s p95; a PDF in ≤ 20 s p95; a narrative export in ≤ 5 s p95. All exports are asynchronous with progress and a durable downloadable result. Regeneration from a snapshot MUST meet the same budgets.

**FR-1346 — Import and ingestion latency.** A legacy import of the reference shape (2 workbooks, 15 sheets, roughly 150 register rows across live and superseded sheets, 28 maturity rows) MUST produce a complete `ValidationReport` in ≤ 60 s p95. Transcription MUST complete within 10 minutes per 60 minutes of audio p95. Extraction of a 60-slide deck MUST complete within 5 minutes p95. All are asynchronous with progress.

**FR-1347 — Measurement.** Every budget above MUST be instrumented in production, reported on the reliability dashboard of FR-1372, and alerted on breach of p95 over a rolling 1-hour window. A budget that is not measured is not a requirement.

### 10.6 Reliability, backup, and the consequence of data loss (FR-1350 to FR-1359)

*The availability, RPO and RTO figures below are chosen targets, not observations, and are calibrated to one observable fact about the engagement shape: work is concentrated into a fixed 12-week window with immovable client dates, so the cost of unavailability is not spread evenly and a four-hour outage on a workshop morning is not equivalent to a four-hour outage in week two.*

**FR-1350 — Availability.** The product MUST achieve 99.5% availability per calendar month measured over the firm's working window (07:00 to 21:00 local to the firm's primary office, Monday to Friday), with planned maintenance outside that window and capped at 4 hours per month. An engagement MUST be able to register blackout windows (onsite workshop days, board presentation days) during which no deployment occurs.

**FR-1351 — Backup and recovery.** RPO MUST be ≤ 15 minutes and RTO ≤ 4 hours for full service restoration. Point-in-time recovery to any minute within the last 35 days MUST be supported. Backups MUST be encrypted, stored in a second region, and restore-tested at least quarterly with the test result and the measured restore time recorded. Object storage holding source artifacts and issued deliverables MUST be versioned, so an overwritten or deleted artifact is recoverable.

- `AC-1351.1` A quarterly restore drill restores a full engagement into an isolated environment and verifies that a stored deliverable regenerates byte-identically per AC-1332.1. A restore that produces data but cannot reproduce a deliverable is a failed drill.

**FR-1352 — The consequence of losing an engagement's data mid-delivery, and what follows from it.**

Losing an engagement's data during delivery is the product's worst possible failure, and it is worse than the equivalent failure in most business software, for three specific reasons. First, the lost material cannot be reconstructed from anywhere else. The client's own systems hold none of it: interview synthesis, evidence-to-finding links, the scoring judgments and their rationale, the workshop's captured priorities, and the decision history exist only in this product. Second, it lands against a fixed date. A transformation engagement runs to a twelve-week calendar with an executive or board audience whose diary will not move, so there is no recovery by working late over a quarter. Third, the failure mode is not "the tool is down for a day", it is "the engagement reverts to spreadsheets mid-flight with a partial dataset", which reintroduces every defect this product exists to remove, at the worst moment, in front of the client.

The requirements that follow from this are therefore hard, not aspirational:

- `AC-1352.1` The RPO and RTO of FR-1351 are hard requirements. A breach is a P1 incident with a mandatory written post-incident report to the affected engagement lead within 24 hours and to firm leadership within 72 hours.
- `AC-1352.2` Every `Engagement` MUST support a one-click complete local escape hatch, downloadable at any time by the `EngagementLead`: the generated workbook of FR-1270 plus a full JSON dump of every entity, every field, every evidence locator, every decision, every comment, and every snapshot reference, plus the original uploaded source files. The dump is documented well enough that the engagement could be continued in a spreadsheet if it had to be.
- `AC-1352.3` The product MUST prompt for an escape-hatch download before every client-facing milestone (findings playback, workshop, deliverable issue) and record whether one was taken.
- `AC-1352.4` The product MUST never be the only copy of a client-supplied source artifact. Uploaded originals are retained byte-for-byte and re-downloadable for the life of the engagement plus the retention window.
- `AC-1352.5` No destructive operation (engagement delete, bulk row delete, import rollback, retention purge) is available without a typed confirmation, a preview of exactly what will be removed, and a recovery window.

**FR-1353 — Graceful degradation.** If the AI provider is unavailable, every non-AI function MUST continue to work, affected capabilities MUST show an explicit unavailable state, and no save path MAY depend on an AI call. If export rendering is unavailable, the model MUST remain editable and export requests MUST queue and complete when service returns. If the transcription service is unavailable, uploads MUST still be accepted and queued.

**FR-1354 — Data integrity guards.** The product MUST run a continuous integrity canary that, per engagement, recomputes a sample of derived values and asserts they match the stored values, and alerts on any mismatch. Grounded: silent divergence between a stored number and its formula is exactly the reference workbook's failure mode, and the product should detect it in minutes rather than at deliverable review.

### 10.7 Accessibility and browser support (FR-1360 to FR-1369)

*The WCAG level and the browser matrix are conventional choices for an enterprise web product rather than inferences from the evidence, and are assumed accordingly. Only AC-1360.1 is grounded, and it is grounded directly.*

**FR-1360 — Accessibility.** All consultant and client-guest screens MUST meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Specifically required: full keyboard operability of the register grid, the roadmap board, the dependency graph and the quadrant chart, including scoring and drag-equivalent operations; a visible focus indicator throughout; text contrast of at least 4.5:1 and non-text contrast of 3:1; programmatic names and roles on every control; and no meaning conveyed by colour alone.

- `AC-1360.1` Every priority band, quadrant, maturity level, status and score magnitude carries a text label or a distinct shape in addition to its colour, in the UI and in every export. Grounded: the reference workbooks encoded band, maturity level and score magnitude in colour-scale fills and cell colours, which is unavailable to a colour-blind reader and is lost entirely the moment a value is copied out of the cell.
- `AC-1360.2` Exported PDFs are tagged with a reading order, and every exported exhibit carries alt text (AC-1262.3).
- `AC-1360.3` Accessibility is verified by automated checks in CI plus a manual keyboard-and-screen-reader pass on the register, roadmap, and quadrant screens before each release.

**FR-1361 — Browser support.** The product MUST support the current and immediately previous major versions of Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox on desktop at viewport widths of 1280px and above. A read-only responsive layout MUST be provided on tablet for the roadmap, register and deliverable views. Authoring on mobile is out of scope. Internet Explorer and legacy Edge are not supported. When the facilitation mode of FR-1250 ships, it additionally targets tablet in participant mode.

### 10.8 Observability (FR-1370 to FR-1379)

**FR-1370 — AI interaction logging.** For every `AISuggestion` the product MUST log: capability ID, model ID and version, prompt template version, the IDs and content hashes of every input record and retrieved chunk (identifiers and hashes, not raw content), the structured output payload, the self-reported confidence, the evidence citations emitted, latency, token counts, provider cost, and the outcome from the closed set `accepted_unchanged`, `accepted_edited`, `rejected`, `abstained`, `expired`, `cancelled`. For `accepted_edited` it MUST log the field-level diff and a normalized edit magnitude. For `rejected` it MUST require a reason from the closed set `wrong`, `not_evidenced`, `miscalibrated`, `out_of_scope`, `duplicate`, `style`, `too_generic`. It MUST also log time-to-decision and whether the evidence panel was opened before the decision.

- `AC-1370.1` Every metric defined in §12.3 is computable from these fields alone, with no additional instrumentation.
- `AC-1370.2` Suggestion content stays inside its engagement. The cross-engagement metrics layer stores only IDs, hashes, numbers and enumerated values, so evaluation never becomes a back-door cross-engagement content store, and FR-1301 is not weakened by the observability requirement.

**FR-1371 — Evaluation harness.** The product MUST maintain a versioned evaluation set per capability class, built only from material on engagements with recorded permission and passed through the anonymization pipeline of FR-1302, with a held-out portion. Running the harness on a prompt or model change MUST report, per capability, acceptance proxy, citation compliance, abstention rate, calibration (for score-proposing capabilities, the distribution of proposed against final values), and regression against the previous version.

- `AC-1371.1` A prompt or model change that regresses citation compliance, or that regresses calibration beyond a stated tolerance, cannot ship.
- `AC-1371.2` The prompt template version is recorded on every suggestion, so a production behaviour change is always attributable to a specific version.

**FR-1372 — Dashboards.** The product team MUST have the following dashboards, each with the stated purpose and the stated decision it supports:

| Dashboard | Contents | Decision it supports |
|---|---|---|
| AI capability health | Per capability: volume, acceptance rate, edit rate, median edit magnitude, abstention rate, citation compliance, blind-accept rate, p50 and p95 latency, cost per accepted suggestion, 8-week trend | Which capabilities to improve, which to gate, which to withdraw |
| Engagement integrity | Per engagement: open validation errors, unbasis'd numbers, stale narrative bindings, taxonomy violations, broken citation locators, days since last snapshot, deliverables issued from a superseded snapshot | Which engagement needs intervention before it issues something wrong |
| Delivery funnel | Engagements by phase, elapsed days per phase against the 12-week reference, artifacts generated in-product versus assembled outside it, escape-hatch downloads taken | Whether the product is actually shortening the engagement, or being worked around |
| Adoption | Weekly active consultants, client-guest sessions, decisions logged, feedback items submitted in-product versus by email, refresh cycles completed, 90-day survival | Whether the living-roadmap thesis is real |
| Reliability and cost | Availability, error budget consumption, p95 against every FR-134x budget, failed exports, failed scans, rejected unscoped-query attempts, AI spend per engagement | Whether to spend on performance, reliability, or model cost |

**FR-1373 — Operational telemetry.** Every request MUST carry a request ID and an engagement ID in structured logs. Distributed traces MUST cover the import, recalculation, export and AI paths end to end. Alerts MUST fire on error-rate breach, p95 breach of any FR-134x budget, failed export, failed confidentiality scan, failed retention purge, integrity-canary mismatch, and any rejected unscoped query. The last of these MUST be routed as a security signal, not as an application error, because it means code attempted to read across an engagement boundary.

**FR-1374 — Logging hygiene.** Application logs MUST NOT contain `PersonIdentifying` or `Restricted` field values, client narrative content, or prompt content. Logs carry identifiers and hashes. Log retention is 90 days.

---

## 11. MVP Scope and Build Sequence

### 11.1 Scope table
